Own-work draft; status: independently checked proof; F0124_C20 version 1. For 0<p<16/17, theta=(1-p)/p>1/16, independent iid fair sign scenery and the exact maximal-cut interval gas, consider constant full words on odd lengths l. Condition on center +1 and every interval variable OTHER than the whole-word interval being vacant. This event has positive finite-volume probability. The whole interval then has conditional occupation probability h_l(theta)/(1+h_l(theta)), since the only remaining sets have weights 1 and h_l. Confined-loop contributions force h_l to infinity through odd l, so this probability tends to one. No summable length-only occupation profile can bound EVERY partial conditional distribution. This rules out extending universal all-history independent interval domination through p<16/17; it does not prove bad configurations. Keeping competing intervals, restricting exploration histories, or controlling rare adverse histories in aggregate may still work. No assertion is made at p=16/17.

exact maximal-cut positive interval expansion
constant full color words including center +1
finite conditional event with all competing interval variables vacant

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:691a4c750e6ef517bcddbbcef877e4a72ddda8e7f56739c0bedbf39be8a7f57b","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/69/691a4c750e6ef517bcddbbcef877e4a72ddda8e7f56739c0bedbf39be8a7f57b.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:a798a30ac3673c427a7b1d3a20a3f5fd2b925000b8e105ec4f1b5f6d995c5a2d","bundle_entry_key":"supercritical-kappa-common-hessian","bundle_id":"population.t362-supercritical-kappa-004","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"optimization; random reshuffling; supercritical condition number; optimal constant step","draft":"w732/bundle_004.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.randomreshuffling:common-hessian-random-reshuffling-supercritical-condition-number-stability-edge-optimizer","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Target 1: supercritical condition number and the stiff stability edge

Status: proof draft (unaudited). No novelty or full-T362 claim.

## Statement

Take the common-Hessian model of C001, with mu=1, fixed n>=2, deterministic x0!=0 and y0, and fixed zero-sum component linear terms of mean squares s1>=0 and s2>0. Epoch permutations are fresh, independent and uniform, shared across coordinates. Set T=nK. Suppose kappa=kappa_T satisfies

    kappa*log(T)/T -> c,   4<c<infinity.

Let P_T(eta) denote expected final-epoch function error and A=x0^2/2. Then

    min_{eta>=0} P_T(eta) ~ A*exp(-4T/kappa).              (1)

Every sequence of global minimizers satisfies

    eta_T = 2/kappa + o(1/T).                            (2)

In particular log(min P_T)/log T -> -4/c. Equation (1), rather than A*T^(-4/c), retains subleading dependence of kappa_T: the ratio assumption alone does not justify replacing the exponential by that power with relative error o(1).

## Exact input, inherited from C001

For q=kappa*eta and W_n(q)=sum_{0<=i<j<n}((1-q)^i-(1-q)^j)^2, the stiff-coordinate variance satisfies

    P_T(eta) >= [s2*q^2*W_n(q)/(2(n-1)*kappa)]
                   *sum_{r=0}^{K-1}(1-q)^(2nr).          (3)

Always W_n(q)>=q^2, by the pair (0,1). The flat deterministic term is exactly A*(1-eta)^(2T). For 0<q<2 the stationary stiff variance is (s2/kappa)*J_n(q), where

    J_n(q)=q^2*W_n(q)/[2(n-1)(1-(1-q)^(2n))].

The actual finite-horizon stiff variance is this stationary quantity times 1-(1-q)^(2T). All objective contributions are nonnegative; correlations of the two coordinate noises introduce no mixed objective term.

## Upper bound

1. Put ell=log T, delta=ell^(-2), and choose q_c=2-delta, eta_c=q_c/kappa. For large T, 0<q_c<2 and eta_c->0. Since n is fixed, W_n stays bounded near 2; expansion of the fixed polynomial denominator at 2 gives J_n(2-delta)=O(delta^-1). Explicitly 1-(1-delta)^(2n)~2n*delta, with a positive leading coefficient. The stiff variance is therefore

    O(1/(kappa*delta))=O(ell^3/T).                       (4)

The stiff deterministic contribution is at most (kappa*y0^2/2)*exp(-2*delta*T).

2. Since T/kappa~ell/c and T/kappa^2->0, the flat deterministic term is

    A*(1-eta_c)^(2T)
      = A*exp(-4T/kappa)
          *exp(2*delta*T/kappa + O(T/kappa^2))
      = A*exp(-4T/kappa)*(1+o(1)).                       (5)

The flat variance is O(eta_c^3)=O(kappa^-3) by the settled fixed-n scalar variance estimate. This is an upper bound on the finite-horizon contribution, because its stable geometric multiplier is bounded by the stationary one.

3. Let B_T=A*exp(-4T/kappa). Its logarithm divided by ell tends to -4/c. Since c>4,

    (ell^3/T)/B_T ->0,   kappa^-3/B_T ->0,
    [kappa*exp(-2T/ell^2)]/B_T ->0.

For example the logarithm of the first ratio divided by ell tends to -1+4/c<0. The third ratio has a dominant negative term -2T/ell^2, while all its other logarithmic terms are O(ell). Thus (4)-(5) prove

    min P_T <= B_T*(1+o(1)) ->0.                        (6)

## Global lower bound and optimizer localization

4. The exact error is a continuous coercive polynomial by (3) and W_n(q)>=q^2; hence global minimizers exist. Fix ANY sequence eta_T of them and write q_T=kappa*eta_T. Eventually q_T<3. Indeed if q_T>=3 along a subsequence, the last summand of (3) gives

    P_T(eta_T) >= [s2*q_T^4/(2(n-1)*kappa)]
                       *(q_T-1)^(2n(K-1))
                >= const * 2^(2(T-n))/kappa ->infinity,

contradicting (6). This uses kappa~cT/ell, and K->infinity; no small-step assumption is made.

5. If 2<q_T<3, let epsilon=q_T-2 in (0,1). The same last-summand bound gives

    P_T(eta_T) >= [8*s2/((n-1)*kappa)]
                         *(1+epsilon)^(2(T-n)).

Since log(1+epsilon)>=epsilon/2 for epsilon in [0,1], and P_T(eta_T)<=1 eventually by (6),

    epsilon*(T-n) <= log kappa + O(1).

Consequently, whether q_T>2 or q_T<=2,

    q_T <= 2 + O(log kappa/T).                          (7)

The implied constant can be chosen uniformly over all global minimizers. This bounds possible unstable overshoot using noise amplification, not an assumed step-size cap.

6. From q_T<3, eta_T=q_T/kappa->0 and uniformly

    log[(1-eta_T)^(2T)] = -2q_T*T/kappa + O(T/kappa^2).

Because T/kappa^2->0 and log kappa/kappa->0, (7) implies

    P_T(eta_T) >= A*(1-eta_T)^(2T)
       >= A*exp(-4T/kappa-o(1))
       = B_T*(1-o(1)).                                 (8)

Combined with (6), this proves (1).

7. The same transient comparison, now using the relative upper bound (6), gives

    exp(2*(2-q_T)*T/kappa+o(1)) <= 1+o(1).

Thus limsup (2-q_T)*T/kappa<=0. Bound (7) also gives liminf (2-q_T)*T/kappa>=0, since its possible negative part is O(log kappa/kappa)->0. Hence (2-q_T)*T/kappa->0, exactly (2). The proof applies to every sequence of global minimizers; it assumes neither uniqueness nor a local optimizer.

## Scope and least-trusted steps

This extends named target 1 to the parameter interval c>4, beyond C004's c in (0,4). The transition c=4 remains unpaid: the logarithmic variance cost in (4) is no longer negligible relative to the candidate transient, so this proof does not cover it. No assertion is made for s2=0, x0=0, growing n, a general finite-sum Hessian, or a full minimax last-iterate RR rate.

Independent audit should focus on steps 5-7 (unrestricted-step overshoot and the relative lower bound). Prior-art context is inherited from the C001 primary sources and the bounded literature query recorded with C004. No priority conclusion is drawn from that search. [Lemma 4 of arXiv:2609.03750, '\bf Pullback Measure Attractors, Zero-Noise Limits, and Moderate Deviations for 2D Stochas'] Let \( B_0 \subset B \subset B_1 \) be Banach spaces, with \(B_0\) and \(B_1\) reflexive and \(B_0\) compactly embedded in \(B\). Let \( p \in (1, \infty) \) and \( \alpha \in (0, 1) \) be given. Let \( \mathfrak X \) be the space
	\[

[Theorem thm:mainThm of arXiv:2604.07711, 'Central Limit Theorem for Random Partial\\ Sphere Coverings in High Dimensions'] Let \(\alpha\in\bigl(0,(2\log(2/c_1))^{-1}\bigr)\) with $c_1$ as in (equation eq:VarLowBd of the paper), and let \(d=d(N)\geq 2\) be a sequence of dimensions such that $d(N)\leq \alpha\log N$ for all sufficiently large \(N\). For each \(N\), let \(X_1,\ldots,X_N\) be independent random points on \(\mathbb{S}^{d-1}\) with distribution \(\sigma\), and define
    \[
    V_N:=\sigma\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^N C_N(X_i)\right),\qquad W_N:=\frac{V_N-\mathbb{E}[V_N]}{\sqrt{\var(V_N)}}.
    \]
    Then there exists an absolute constant \(C>0\), such that
    \[
    d_K(W_N,\mathcal N(0,1))\leq C\,N^{\alpha\log(2/c_1)-1/2}
    \]
    for all sufficiently large \(N\).
    In particular,
    \[
    W_N\stackrel{d}{\longrightarrow}\mathcal N(0,1)
    \qquad\text{as }N\to\infty.
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem cellsep of arXiv:2604.07183, 'Stopping on the last success with unknown odds: asymptotic minimax optimality of the plug-'] Let~$p\in[p_0,1)$ and~$m=m(p)$, and set~$\Delta_-:=p-\frac{1}{m+1}$ and~$\Delta_+:=\frac1m-p$. Then $m\le M_0$,
$$
\Delta_-+\Delta_+=\frac{1}{m(m+1)}
,
\quad
\textrm{ and}
\quad
\max\{\Delta_-,\Delta_+\}\ \ge\ \frac{1}{2M_0(M_0+1)}=:c_1(p_0)>0
.
$$
Moreover, for any~$q\in(0,1)$ and any integer~$i\ge2$, $m(q)=m+i$ forces $|q-p|\ge c_0(p_0):=1/\{(M_0+1)(M_0+2)\}$, and so does~$m(q)=m-i$.

Take long virtual knot diagrams $D_{1}$ and $D_{2}$ representing $K_{1}$ and $K_{2}$, respectively.

[Lemma lem:boundary-construction of arXiv:2509.04333, 'The limiting law of the Discrete Gaussian level lines'] Fix $n \geq 1$, and let $R$ be an $\ell_1 \times \ell_2$ rectangle, where $\ell_1, \ell_2 \gg (\log L)^6$. Let $\Lambda_{9L/10} \subset V \subset \Lambda$, and $0 \leq k \leq H-n$. Suppose that, w.h.p.\ under $\pi_{V}^k$, $R$ is contained in the interior of $\mathfrak{L}_{n-1}$ and that there are two points $A, B$ on the sides of $\partial R$ with the top arc of $\partial R$ from $A$ to $B$ in the interior of $\mathfrak{L}_n$, such that if $d$ is the distance from $\{A, B\}$ to the top or bottom of $R$, then $\sqrt{\ell_1}(\log L)^2 \leq d$. 

        Then there exists a $\pi^k_V$-measurable distribution on connected regions $Q\subset R$ with marked boundary conditions $\xi$ satisfying  (it:Q-simp-conn,it:dist-Q-R-bdy,it:good-boundary-points,it:Q-bc-arc of the paper)
        below, such that the following holds. If $\ensuremath{\mathcal A}_1$ is the area of the interior of $\mathfrak{L}_n$ intersected with~$Q$, and $\ensuremath{\mathcal A}_2$ is the area above the $(H+1-n)$ level line in $Q$ under $\pi^\xi_Q$, then $\ensuremath{\mathcal A}_2 \subset \ensuremath{\mathcal A}_1$ w.h.p.\ under $\pi^k_V$.        
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item $Q$ is simply connected,

            \item $\dist(\partial Q, \partial R) \leq \log L$,

            \item There exists $A', B' \in \partial Q$ such that ${\ensuremath{\mathscr C}}(\overline{A'B'}) \subset Q$, $\ensuremath{\mathcal Y}^{\blacktriangleleft}(A')$ does not intersect the left side of $Q$, $\ensuremath{\mathcal Y}^{\blacktriangleright}(B')$ does not intersect the right side of $Q$, and $\max\{d(A, A'), \dist(B, B')\} \leq 2(\log L)^5$.

            \item  The boundary conditions $\xi$ assigns height $H+1-n$ on the top arc from $A'$ to $B'$, and $H-n$ on the bottom arc.
        \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 7 of arXiv:2608.17509, '2608.17509'] Let \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\subset\mathbb R\) be bounded pairwise disjoint Borel
sets, set \(A_j:=B_j\times I_a\) and \(A:=\bigcup_{j=1}^m A_j\). Let \(K_A\)
be the integral operator on \(L^2(A,\mathrm dA)\) with kernel
\(K_{\mathbb H}\) restricted to \(A\times A\). Then \(K_A\) is a positive
trace-class contraction, \(0\le K_A\le \operatorname{Id}\). Moreover, for
\(s=(s_1,\ldots,s_m)\in\mathbb C^m\), define
\[
        g_s(z):=\sum_{j=1}^m(s_j-1)\mathbf 1_{A_j}(z),
        \qquad z\in A,
\]
and let \(M_{g_s}\) be multiplication by \(g_s\) on \(L^2(A,\mathrm dA)\).
Then \(M_{g_s}K_A\) is trace class and
\begin{equation}

        \mathbb E\left[\prod_{j=1}^m s_j^{\#(Z\cap A_j)}\right]
        =
        \det\left(\operatorname{Id}+M_{g_s}K_A\right),
\end{equation}
where the determinant is the Fredholm determinant on \(L^2(A,\mathrm dA)\).

body:
Let $\kappa \ge 0$ be a kernel supported in $[-a, a]$ with $\int\kappa = 1$ and moments $m_k = \int t^k \kappa(t)\,dt$, and let $H_\kappa(x) = \pi^{-1}\,\mathrm{PV}\!\int \kappa(t)/(t - x)\,dt$. For $|x| > a$ no principal value is needed and $H_\kappa(x) = -\pi^{-1}\sum_{k \ge 0} m_k\, x^{-(k+1)}$, the series converging absolutely; for a symmetric kernel the odd moments vanish. For the Epanechnikov kernel $\kappa(x) = \tfrac{3}{4\sqrt5}(1 - x^2/5)^+$ ($a = \sqrt5$): $m_2 = 1$, $m_4 = 15/7$, so $H_\kappa(x) = -\pi^{-1}(x^{-1} + x^{-3} + \tfrac{15}{7}x^{-5}) + O(x^{-7})$. Its closed form $-\tfrac{3x}{10\pi} + \tfrac{3}{4\sqrt5\pi}(1 - x^2/5)\log|\tfrac{\sqrt5 - x}{\sqrt5 + x}|$ is the same function, but in floating point its two $O(x)$ terms cancel to leave the $O(1/x)$ value with absolute rounding error of order $\varepsilon |x|$: the error exceeds the value once $|x| \gtrsim \varepsilon^{-1/2}$, and the three-term series is accurate to $10^{-7}$ from $|x| = 30$ on, so a numerically sound evaluation switches to the series there.
kappa nonnegative, integrable, compactly supported in [-a, a]
the moment series is used only for |x| > a (outside the support)

[Theorem MH2p1 of arXiv:2511.15893, 'On a Class of Dynamical Poisson-Voronoi Tessellations'] Suppose there are two types of stations with intensities $\lambda_1, \lambda_2$ and speeds $v_1> v_2$. Let $\lambda_1+\lambda_2=\lambda$. Then we have:

\begin{enumerate}[(i).]
\item  The pure handover frequencies are 
\begin{equation}
     \Lambda_l= \frac{4v_l\sqrt{\lambda}}{\pi}\left(\frac{\lambda_l}{\lambda}\right)^2, \text{ for }l=1,2.
\end{equation}
\item   The mixed handover frequencies satisfies the relations $\Lambda^{(1)}_{1,2}=\Lambda^{(2)}_{2,1}$ and $\Lambda^{(2)}_{1,2}=\Lambda^{(1)}_{2,1}$.
\item  For $k=1,2$,
\begin{align}
\Lambda^{(k)}_{2,1}&= 4\lambda_1\lambda_2v_1v_2\int_{0}^{\infty}\left[\int_0^{h_1}\int_{t^*}^\infty e^{-\lambda\pi\hat h^2_k(t, h_1, h_2)}  \,{\rm d}t \, {\rm d}h_2  +\int_{h_1}^{\infty}\int_{0}^{\infty} e^{-\lambda\pi\hat h^2_k(t, h_1, h_2)}\,{\rm d}t \, {\rm d}h_2 \right] {\rm d}h_1 ,
\end{align}
\end{enumerate}

where $\hat h^2_k$ as in ((eq:HO_distance1 of the paper)), being a function of $t, h_1, h_2$.

\iffalse
\[
\hat h_k^2= v_1^2 \left(\frac{v_2^2 t+ (-1)^k \Delta^{\frac{1}{2}}}{v_1^2-v_2^2}\right)^2\!\! +h_1^2 \text{ and } \Delta= v_1^2v_2^2 t^2- (h_1^2-h_2^2)(v_1^2-v_2^2).
\]

The last two expressions are functions of $t, h_1, h_2$, determined in ((eq:HO_distance1 of the paper)) and ((eq:Delta of the paper)), respectively.
\fi
title: Handover frequency: two-speed case

[Proposition prop:concentHtheo2 of arXiv:2411.10235, '\textbf{Smooth transport map via diffusion process}'] There exists  $0<C_\star<C_2$ such that if $t\in [0,1)$  and $x\in \mathbb{R}^d$ satisfy \begin{equation}
1-t^2\leq C_\star^{-1}\log(\epsilon^{-1})^{-C_\star} \text{ and } \|tx\|^2\leq 1-C_2^{-1}\log(\epsilon^{-1}+1)^{-K},
\end{equation}
then for all $i,j\in \{1,...,d\}$ we have
    $$\int H(y,x)_i^2 dp^{t,x}(y)\leq C(1-t^2)$$
    and 
    $$\int \left(H(y,x)^{\otimes2}_{ij}- \int H(z,x)^{\otimes2}_{ij}dp^{t,x}(z)\right)^2dp^{t,x}(y)\leq C(1-t^2)^{2}.$$
title: Proposition prop:concentHtheo2 of arXiv:2411.10235

body: FIRES WHEN an attempt record's obstruction field contains a phrase like 'as I recall their first-moment section' or 'if their estimate is stated for bulk boxes only'. WHAT HAPPENED: the first pass at Kalai's Conjecture 8 reduced both inequalities to a single box estimate for the spectral sample and then declared the whole weight of the argument to rest on whether Garban, Pete and Schramm actually prove it - 'as I recall their first-moment section' - and flagged the row as a partial result for that reason, expecting a second-moment input to be needed. Reading the paper showed the estimate is their Lemma 3.2 (3.4), which follows in ONE LINE from the conditional-variance identity P[S intersect B nonempty] = E[Var(f | bits outside B)] and needs no second-moment input whatsoever. CONDITION OF FAILURE: an obstruction whose only evidence is recall. A recalled citation is a hypothesis about the literature with the same status as a hypothesis about the mathematics, and it costs one paper fetch to settle. The same pass also over-worried the boundary boxes; the half-plane three-arm bound handles them.

body: [Corollary 31 of arXiv:2608.07239, 'Unified framework for asymptotically uniform iterative construction of generalised random '] The total number of MISs in a $2$-uniform graph $G$ is given by the formula $$\frac1{\alpha(G)!}\prod_{t=1}^{\alpha(G)}\left(\ell(G)\binom{t}{2}+t\right)=\prod_{t=1}^{\alpha(G)}\left(\frac{\ell(G)}{2}(t-1)+1\right).$$ In particular, if $\ell(G)=2$, this simplifies to $\alpha(G)!$, and if $\ell(G)=4$, this simplifies to $(2\alpha(G)-1)!!=\tfrac{(2\alpha(G))!}{2^{\alpha(G)}\alpha(G)!}$.

\[
 q_\beta\in(0,1),\qquad c_\beta\in(0,1),
\]
and a nonnegative function
\[
 \rho_\beta\in C^\infty([0,q_\beta))

such that
\begin{equation}
 \mu_\beta(\dd s)
 =\rho_\beta(s)\dd s+c_\beta\delta_{q_\beta}(\dd s),
\end{equation}
where the density term is understood to be zero on
$[q_\beta,1]$. Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 \supp\mu_\beta=[0,q_\beta].
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\end{enumerate}

[Definition def:flatly_parallel of arXiv:2607.02410, 'Polynomial mixing for polygonal side matchings'] Let $e_{1} = \{A,B\},e_{2} = \{C,D\} \in C_{\mathrm{cross}}$ be two chords which do not cross each other. The chords partition the sides of $P \setminus \{A,B,C,D\}$ into three disjoint sets: 
	\begin{itemize}
		\item The set $I^{e_1}$ of sides which are separated from $e_2$ by $e_1$.
		\item The set $I^{e_2}$ of sides which are separated from $e_1$ by $e_2$.
		\item The set $I^{e_1,e_2}$ of sides which are between $e_1$ and $e_2$.
	\end{itemize}
	The chords $e_{1}$ and $e_{2}$ are said to be \textit{flatly parallel} if every chord with an endpoint in $I^{e_1,e_2}$ has both endpoints in $I^{e_1,e_2}$, and none of those chords intersect each other.
title: Definition def:flatly_parallel of arXiv:2607.02410

body: A sunflower (or Delta-system) with r petals is a collection of sets S_1, ..., S_r such that the pairwise intersection S_i intersect S_j is the same set Y (the core) for every pair i not equal to j. The classical sunflower lemma: if F is a family of finite sets, each of size at most k, with |F| > k! (r-1)^k, then F contains a sunflower with r petals. [Erdos and Rado (1960) (1960); see Jukna, Extremal Combinatorics]
title: Sunflower Lemma (Delta-System Lemma, Classical Bound)

A probability distribution with characteristic function \phi(t) is said to satisfy Cramér's Condition (C) if \limsup_{|t| \to \infty} |\phi(t)| < 1. [Lemma 13 of arXiv:2603.28093, 'Random Stability of Random Variables'] Take infinitely divisible random variables $N = 0, 1, 2, \ldots$ and $X$ on the real line. Pick a $k = 2, 3, \ldots$ and decompose 
$$
N = M_1 + \ldots + M_k,\quad X = Y_1 + \ldots + Y_k
$$
into $k$ independent copies of $M$ and $Y$, respectively. Then $X$ is $N$-stable if and only if $Y$ is $kM$-stable. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 13 of arXiv:2603.28093

[Lemma le5 of arXiv:2411.10235, '\textbf{Smooth transport map via diffusion process}'] If a probability density $p$ is compactly supported, then for all $t\in [0,1)$ its associated velocity field $V$ from (equation eq:V of the paper) satisfies
$$V\in L^1\Big([0,t],W^{1,\infty}_{loc}(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbb{R}^d)\Big)\text{ and } \frac{V}{1+\|x\|}\in L^1\Big([0,t],L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbb{R}^d)\Big).$$
In particular there exists a unique solution for all $t\in [0,1)$ to the equation
    $$\partial_t X_t(x) =V(t,X_t(x)), \quad X_0(x)=x.$$
title: Lemma le5 of arXiv:2411.10235

[Cor 8 of arXiv:2510.26207, 'A combinatorial perspective on the Kemeny constant and more'] For all $n\geq 0$, all $u\in V$,
  \ben
  \bK^{\geq 1,(n)}(1)/n! 
  &=& \sum_{s=0}^{n\wedge (|V|-1)}  \sum_{v\in V} \frac{\E_u\l({\sf Fac}_{n-s}(\tau^{\geq 1}_v)\r)}{(n-s)!}  \;  \frac{\pi^{(s)}_v(1)}{s!}.
\een

In particular,  for $n=1$, for all $u\in V$,
\ben
\bK^{\geq 1,(1)}(1)   &=& \sum_{v\in V} \E_u(\tau_v^{\geq 1})\pi_v + \sum_{v\in V}\pi^{(1)}_v(1), 
\een
so that ${\bf Q}^{\geq 1}(u)=\sum_{v\in V} \E_u(\tau_v^{\geq 1})\pi_v$ does not depend on $u$ (this is the Kemeny theorem). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:PR3 of arXiv:2509.16541, 'Two-stage Bootstrap Percolation'] Fix an integer $s \geq 1$ and consider the box $A = [-\lfloor q^{-s} \rfloor, \lfloor q^{-s} \rfloor]^2$.
    Initially, each vertex $x \in A$ is in state $2$ with probability $q$ and is in state $1$ otherwise.
    Let the state-$2$ vertices perform the internal bootstrap percolation on state-$1$ vertices in $A$.
    Then in the final configuration of these dynamics, all the maximal connected sets of state-$2$ vertices have $\ell^\infty$-diameter at most $16s$ with probability at least $1 - c_0q^s$, where $c_0 = c_0(s)$ is a constant.

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Same structure as C0050: contour relations plus Morera give holomorphy of subsequential limits; identify the missing a priori bounds. Result: Smirnov's parafermionic observable for the honeycomb SAW at the critical weight satisfies the discrete contour relation (sum around each hexagon vanishes) but is not discretely holomorphic (only half the Cauchy-Riemann relations), the same deficit as for FK with q not 2. Any subsequential limit of the normalised observable that is tight and locally bounded is holomorphic by Morera (the contour relations pass to the limit) with boundary modulus determined by the spin 5/8 and the boundary conditions; the function (Phi')^{5/8} is the unique such function with the prescribed singularity at a and normalisation at b. Hence Conjecture 3.6 reduces to (i) tightness/local boundedness of F_delta(a, z)/F_delta(a, b) away from a and b and (ii) control near the marked points. (i) would follow from the Beurling-type estimate that a SAW from a to z in the domain has weight comparable to the two-point function in the bulk, i.e. from an RSW-type theory for the critical SAW, which is unavailable (there is no RSW for SAW, unlike FK with q in [1,4]). So the obstruction is specific: SAW lacks the crossing estimates that make the FK reduction work. Obstruction: No RSW-type crossing estimates for critical SAW; tightness of the observable ratio is not available.

Own-work draft; F0124_C15 version 1; status: independently checked proof. For a two-sided nearest-neighbor iid walk with 0<p<1 and independent iid fair sign scenery, assume the exact positive maximal-upward-cut interval expansion. If every length-l interval coefficient, including all four endpoint types and both center signs, is bounded by a finite nonnegative beta_l with sum_{l>=2}l beta_l<infinity, every exterior configuration is good. No smallness of this sum is required. Put c=product_{l>=2}(1+beta_l)^(-l)>0 and T(R)=sum_{l>R}l beta_l. For exterior words agreeing at 0<|t|<=n, at every outer radius m>=n their central conditional probabilities differ by at most 2[(1-c)^floor(n/R)+floor(n/R)T(R)] for integer R>=2. Choosing R=n/k(n) rounded down with k(n) tending sufficiently slowly to infinity makes the bound vanish. All four raw interval coefficients are bounded by the constant-word WHOLE no-cut coefficient h_l(theta), theta=(1-p)/p, so sum l h_l(theta)<infinity is sufficient. Raw coefficient domination is valid before normalizing by a word-dependent partition. This criterion alone verifies no additional drift range.

body:
[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2607.25645, 'Estimates of the total variation distance between laws of Sobolev mappings on Gaussian spa'] Let $k\in \mathbb{N}$, $p\ge 2k$, $b>0$, and set
\[
q:=\frac{p}{p-2k+1}.
\]
Then, for every mapping $f=(f_1,\ldots,f_k)$ with $f_j\in W^{2,p}(\gamma)$ and
\[
\max_{1\le j\le k}\|f_j\|_{\dot W^{2,p}(\gamma)}\le b,
\]
one has
\[
\sigma_f(t)\le
128k b^{2k-1}\, t\, \bigl(h_{\gamma,q}(\Delta_f,\varepsilon)\bigr)^{1/q}
+\gamma(\Delta_f\le 2\varepsilon)
\quad \forall\, t,\varepsilon>0.
\]

If, in addition,
\[
\gamma(\Delta_f\le \varepsilon)\le a\varepsilon^\varkappa
\quad \forall\, \varepsilon>0
\]
for some $\varkappa\in(0,q)$, then
\[
\sigma_f(t)\le
512 k^\alpha (1-\alpha)^{-\alpha} a^{\alpha/\varkappa} b^{(2k-1)\alpha}\cdot t^\alpha
\quad \forall\, t>0,
\]
where
\[
\alpha:=\frac{p\varkappa}{p+\varkappa(2k-1)}.
\]

[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2604.08127, 'Asymptotics of Brownian occupation measures \\ with unusually large intersections'] For any $d \ge 1$, $p \ge 2$ such that $d(p-1) < 2p$ and any $0 < \gamma < \frac{2p}{d(p-1)}$, the distribution $\widehat{\mathbb{P}}_t^{\otimes p} \circ (\widetilde{L}_t^{\otimes p})^{-1}$ under the Gibbs measure \eqref{eq:mutual-gibbs-measure} satisfies an LDP in $\widetilde{\mathcal{X}}^{\otimes p}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ with good rate function
    \[
    \mathcal{I}_{d, p, \gamma}^{\mathrm{Gibbs}}(\xi^{\otimes p}) = \begin{cases}
    \displaystyle \mathcal{I}(\xi^{\otimes p}) - p\biggl(\sum_{i \in I} \Big\| \prod_{j=1}^p \psi_i^j \Big\|_2^2 \biggr)^{\gamma/p} + p \cdot \rho_{d, p, \gamma} & \text{if } \mathcal{I}(\xi^{\otimes p}) < \infty\\
    \infty & \text{otherwise},
    \end{cases}
    \]
    where $\mathcal{I}(\cdot)$ and $\rho_{d, p, \gamma}$ are defined in \eqref{eq:rate-function} and \eqref{eq:mutual-tilted-var}, respectively. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:hill-moment of arXiv:2608.08375, 'Algebraic formulas for first-passage times of Markov processes in the linear framework: ge'] With the same assumptions as at the start of this section, choose $z \in Z$. Let $W$ be as defined in the statement of Lemma~(cor:hill-2 of the paper) and let $\Omega$ be as defined in the statement of Theorem~(thm:hill-moment-Z of the paper). Then the $r$-th moment of the conditional FPT from $u$ to $z$ is given by,
\[
\begin{split}
    \mu^{(r)}_{c,u,z}(G) = r! \sum_{(i_1, \dotsc, i_r) \in \Omega}{\left( \prod_{j=0}^{r-1}{\frac{\psi_{i_{j+1}|i_j,u} \, x_{i_{j+1}}^*(\mathcal{H}_u[G])}{\sum_{z' \in Z}{\sum_{k \in W , k \to_G z'}{\ell(k \to_G z') \, x_k^*(\mathcal{H}_u[G])}}}} \right)} \\
    \times \left( \frac{\sum_{k \in W: k \to_G z}{\ell(k \to_G z) \, \psi_{k|i_r,u} \, x_k^*(\mathcal{H}_u[G])}}{\sum_{k \in W: k \to_G z}{\ell(k \to_G z) \, x_k^*(\mathcal{H}_u[G])}} \right) \,.\qquad\qquad\quad
\end{split}
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Conservative weighted-distance fluctuations in heavy-tailed configuration models structural reduction Result: For nonnegative weights, a path sum is at least its maximum edge, so the FPP distance dominates the minimax path value. The latter is exactly the smallest level t at which the two vertices are connected using edges of weight at most t. This follows by comparing the same path family under the two objectives. Check: A connection at level t supplies a path with every edge at most t, and any path with maximum edge at most t supplies such a connection; taking infima proves the minimax/percolation identity. Obstruction: The lower bound tracks the largest obstruction but discards accumulated small costs. In the conservative regime infinitely many layers can contribute, so the minimax comparison does not determine centered sum fluctuations.

[Definition of arXiv:2411.07157, 'Rough differential equations in the flow approach'] Given $\underline{\tau}, \underline{\sigma} \in \boldsymbol{\mathfrak{T}}$, we call a bijection $f: N(\underline{\tau}) \rightarrow N(\underline{\sigma})$ an \textit{isomorphism} from $\underline{\tau}$ to $\underline{\sigma}$ if $f\big(r(\underline{\tau})\big) = r(\underline{\sigma})$, and if the induced mapping $\vec{f}: E(\underline{\tau}) \rightarrow \big(N(\underline{\sigma})\big)^{(2)}$ given by $e = \{v,\bar{v}\} \mapsto \vec{f}(e) = \{f(v),f(\bar{v})\}$ is in fact a bijection between $E(\underline{\tau})$ and $E(\underline{\sigma})$. 

We write $\mathrm{Iso}(\underline{\tau},\underline{\sigma})$ for the collection of isomorphisms from $\underline{\tau}$ to $\underline{\tau}'$ and use the shorthand $\mathrm{Aut}(\underline{\tau}) \eqdef \mathrm{Iso}(\underline{\tau},\underline{\tau})$ for the \textit{automorphism group} of $\tau$. 
We say $\underline{\tau}$ and $\underline{\sigma}$ are isomorphic if there exists an isomorphism between them, and denote by $\mathfrak{T}$ the set of isomorphism classes of elements of $\boldsymbol{\mathfrak{T}}$. 
An element of $\mathfrak{T}$ is called an \textit{unlabelled rooted tree}, or just a tree. 

We write $\circ = \{ \circ_{r}: r \in \N\}$ as the isomorphism class of labelled trees with a single node.
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2411.07157, 'Rough differential equations in the flow approach'

[Theorem recentering of arXiv:2606.29622, 'Affine Structure of the Brownian Signature'] Let $\bm{p} \in \mathcal{B}$ and $\mathbb{X} \in G\,$. Assume that $\mathbb{E}[\exp(\bracket{\bm{p}}{\sigX[] \otimes \sigW[t,T]})] \neq 0$ for all $t \in [0\,,T]\,$. Then
    $$
    \mathbb{E}\left[\exp (\bracket{\bm p}{\sigX[] \otimes \sigW[t,T]}) \right] =  \exp  (\bracket{\bm \psi_t^{\sigX[]}}{{\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{\varnothing}}}})\,, \quad t \in [0, T]\,,
    $$
    where $\bm{\psi}_t^{\sigX[]}$ is a solution to the recentered Riccati equation (equation eq:Riccati_recentered of the paper). In particular, if $\mathbb{E}[\exp(\bracket{\bm{p}}{\sigW[T]}) \,|\, \mathcal{F}_t] \neq 0\,$ a.s., for all $t \in [0, T]$, we have
    $$
\mathbb{E}\left[\exp\left(\bracket{\bm p}{\sigW[T]}\right)\,\Big\vert \,\mathcal F_t\right] = \exp\left(\bracket{\bm \psi_t^{\sigW[t]}}{{\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{\varnothing}}}}\right) \,, \quad t \in [0, T]\,.
    $$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm Result2 of arXiv:2609.01350, 'New classes of trace-form permutation polynomials and their compositional inverses'] Let $q=2^m$, $m>1$ $c_1, c_2, c_3, \gamma \in \mathbb F_{q^2}$. Then
$$f_2(x)=x+\gamma {\rm Tr}_{q}^{q^2} (c_1 x+ c_2 x^2+ c_3 x^3+ c_3x^{q+2}+x^{2q-1}),$$
is a permutation polynomial of $\mathbb F_{q^2}$ if and only if one of the following holds,
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\gamma=0$,
\item $\gamma \in \mathbb F_{q}^*$, $c_2, c_3 \in \mathbb F_{q}$ and $1+\gamma{\rm Tr}_q^{q^2}(c_1)=\gamma$. 
\item $\gamma \in \mathbb F_{q^2} \setminus \mathbb F_{q}$, $m$ is odd, $\gamma^{2q-1} \in \mathbb F_q$, ${\rm Tr}_q^{q^2}(c_2\gamma^q)=0$, $c_3=0$ and $1+{\rm Tr}_q^{q^2}(c_1\gamma)=\gamma^{2q-1}$,
\end{enumerate}

[Definition 19 of arXiv:2609.02017, 'Optimal girth-dependent bounds for the Bethe approximation of the permanent'] The auxiliary directed network $\mc{N}$ has a source $\mathbf s$, a
sink $\mathbf t$, and a node $(v,e,\sigma)$ for every incidence
$v\in e$ and every $\sigma\in\{+,-\}$. Its arcs are of the following
three types.

\begin{itemize}
\item For every $e\in E$, the {traversal arcs} are
\[
(e_L,e,+)\longrightarrow(e_R,e,+)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
(e_R,e,-)\longrightarrow(e_L,e,-).
\]

\item For every pair of distinct edges $e,f\ni v$, the {transfer arcs} are
\[
(v,e,-)\longrightarrow(v,f,+),
\qquad v\in L,
\]
and
\[
(v,f,+)\longrightarrow(v,e,-),
\qquad v\in R.
\]

\item The {source and sink arcs} are
\[
\mathbf s\longrightarrow(v,e,+),
\qquad v\in L,
\]
and
\[
(v,e,+)\longrightarrow\mathbf t,
\qquad v\in R.
\]
\end{itemize}
title: Definition 19 of arXiv:2609.02017

[Thm 54 ({\cite{C70}*{Theorem 2}}) of arXiv:2609.03836, 'Koszul Orlik--Solomon Algebras from Non-supersolvable Arrangements'] A collection $\Fc$ of subsets (called ``blocks'') of the ground set of a matroid $M$ of rank $r$ is the set of rank $r$ flats of an erection of $M$ if and only if 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item each block spans $M,$
        \item each block is $(r-1)$-closed,
        \item each basis of $M$ is contained in a unique block.
    \end{enumerate}
Here, a subset $S\subseteq M$ is said to be $k$-closed if the closure of any $k$-element subset of $S$ lies in $S$.

[Lemma lem:realize of arXiv:2608.28007, 'Exact Risk Ratios for Weighted Data Selection in Linear Regression'] Let $s_i>0$ with $\sum_is_i=1$ and let nonzero vectors $d_i\in\mathbb{R}^d$ satisfy
$\sum_is_id_i=0$ and $M=\sum_is_id_id_i^{\top}\succ0$. Set
\[
v_i=M^{-1/2}d_i,\qquad \eta_i=\sqrt{Ns_i},\qquad \xi_i=\eta_iv_i .
\]
Then $\{(\xi_i,\eta_i)\}$ satisfies the three identities
(equation eq:threeid of the paper); moreover $\eta_i^2=Ns_i$, each $v_i$ spans the image of
the ray of $d_i$ under the invertible map $M^{-1/2}$, and
$\ip{v_i}{v_j}=d_i^{\top}M^{-1}d_j$. Linear dependences among the $d_i$
transfer verbatim to the $v_i$; since $g_i=Ns_iv_i$ with $s_i>0$, a
dependence $\sum_ic_id_i=0$ becomes $\sum_i(c_i/s_i)\,g_i=0$, so circuit
supports, coefficient signs and positive spanning properties transfer to
the gradients after this positive rescaling of coefficients.

body: In mathematics, specifically in group theory, the concept of a semidirect product is a generalization of a direct product. It is usually denoted with the symbol . There are two closely related concepts of semidirect product:an inner semidirect product is a particular way in which a group can be made up of two subgroups, one of which is a normal subgroup. an outer semidirect product is a way to construct a new group from two given groups by using the Cartesian product as a set and a particular multiplication operation.

[Defn def:TSAW of arXiv:2603.17858, 'Decay of correlations and zeros for the hard-core model'] Given a graph $G=(V,E)$ and a vertex $v$, the \emph{tree of self avoiding walks} is the tree $T_{\mathrm{SAW}(G,v)}$ obtained from $(G,v)$ as follows.
    Fix a total ordering of the vertices of $G$.
    We define the tree $T_{\mathrm{SAW}(G,v)}$ recursively. 
    If the component of $G$ containing $v$ consists of a single vertex $v$, then $T_{\mathrm{SAW}(G,v)}=\{v\}$.
    In case the component of $G$ containing $v$ consists of more than $1$ vertex, let $v_1,\ldots,v_d$ denote the neighbours of $v$ in $G$.
    Let for $i=1\ldots d$, $G_i$ be the graph obtained from $G$ by removing $v,v_1,\ldots,v_{i-1}$ from $G$.
    Denote for $i=1,\ldots, d$, $T_i=T_{\mathrm{SAW}(G_{i},v_{i})}$.
    Then $T_{\mathrm{SAW}(G,v)}$ is defined as the tree obtained from the disjoint union of the $T_i$ adding a vertex $v$ connecting it to each of the $v_1,\ldots,v_d$.
title: The tree of self avoiding walks

[Proposition 2 of arXiv:2607.18186, 'Small Counterexamples to the Gaussian Moments Conjecture'] For every $A\in\C[z]$ and $m\geq1$,
\begin{equation}
  \E\bigl(A(Z_2)P_4^m\bigr)
  =m!\,[z^m]A(z)(1+z)^{m-1}.
\end{equation}
In particular,
\[
  \E(P_4^m)=0,
  \qquad
  \E(Q_4P_4^m)=m!
  \qquad(m\geq1).
\]

[Lemma 29 (Low Orders of Residue Subfields imply Explicit Numerators) of arXiv:2609.00974, 'On Algebraic Integrability\\ of Vector Fields \\ with Rational Function Coefficients\\ tha'] Let $k$ be a field. Let $f\in k[x]$ be a separable irreducible polynomial over $k$ of degree $d$ with roots $a_1,\ldots,a_d$.  Let $h\in k[x]$ be a polynomial of degree $<d$.
    Then the field $L\coloneqq k\left(\frac{h(a_1)}{f'(a_1)},\frac{h(a_2)}{f'(a_2)} ,\frac{h(a_3)}{f'(a_3)}, \ldots, \frac{h(a_d)}{f'(a_d))}\right)$
    satisfies $(L:k) \le 2$ if and only if:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $(L:k) =1$, and $h=cf'$ for some $c\in k$.
        \item $(L:k) = 2$, and $f=g\cdot \overline{g}$ factorizes over $L$ into two conjugate factors, 
        \\and there is $c\in L\setminus k$ such that $h=cg' \overline{g}+ \overline{c}g\overline{g}'$.
    \end{enumerate}

body:
[Thm 5 (Bethuel's interior theorem) of arXiv:2609.00739, '2609.00739'] Let $D\subset\subset\R^2$ be a bounded smooth domain, and let $v_j$ solve
\begin{equation}
 -\eps_j\Delta v_j+\frac{1}{\eps_j}\nabla V(v_j)=0
 \quad\text{in }D,
\end{equation}
where $\eps_j\to0$ and
\[
 \cE_{\eps_j}(v_j;D)\leq M.
\]
After passing to a subsequence, there exist a closed countably
$1$-rectifiable set $S_D\subset D$ and Radon measures
$\upnu_D$, $\upzeta_D$, and $\upmu_{D,i\ell}$,
$i,\ell\in\{1,2\}$, such that
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 \left[\frac{\eps_j}{2}\abs{\nabla v_j}^2
       +\frac{1}{\eps_j}V(v_j)\right]\dd x
 &\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}\upnu_D,\\
 \frac{1}{\eps_j}V(v_j)\dd x
 &\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}\upzeta_D,\\
 \eps_j\,\partial_i v_j\cdot\partial_\ell v_j\dd x
 &\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}\upmu_{D,i\ell}
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
as Radon measures locally in $D$, and the following properties hold.

\begin{enumerate}[label=$(\theenumi)$]
\item There exists a locally constant map
\[
 v_\star:D\backslash S_D\to\Sigma
\]
such that
\[
 v_j\to v_\star
 \quad\text{locally uniformly in }D\backslash S_D.
\]

\item The limiting measures are concentrated on $S_D$ and admit the
representations
\begin{equation}
 \upnu_D=e_D\,\cH^1\llcorner S_D,
 \quad
 \upzeta_D=\Uptheta_D\,\cH^1\llcorner S_D,
 \quad
 \upmu_{D,i\ell}
 =m_{D,i\ell}\,\cH^1\llcorner S_D.
\end{equation}
For every $K\subset\subset D$, there exist constants
$0<c_K\leq C_K<+\infty$ such that
\begin{equation}
 c_K\leq e_D,\Uptheta_D\leq C_K,
 \quad
 \abs{m_{D,i\ell}}\leq C_K
\end{equation}
for $\cH^1$-almost every point of $S_D\cap K$.

\item At $\cH^1$-almost every $x\in S_D$, let $\tau(x)$ be a unit
vector spanning the approximate tangent line $T_xS_D$, and set
$n(x):=\tau(x)^\perp$.  In the frame $(\tau,n)$, the limiting densities
satisfy the vectorial discrepancy relations
\begin{equation}
 e_D=m_{D,nn},
 \quad
 2\Uptheta_D=m_{D,nn}-m_{D,\tau\tau},
 \quad
 m_{D,n\tau}=0.
\end{equation}
Equivalently, the limiting stress--energy tensor
\begin{equation}
 T_D:=\upnu_D I_2-\upmu_D
\end{equation}
has the representation
\begin{equation}
 T_D=2(\tau\otimes\tau)\upzeta_D.
\end{equation}

\item The rectifiable varifold determined by the potential-energy measure,
\[
 \mathbf V_D:=\Vbold(S_D,\Uptheta_D),
 \quad
 \norm{\mathbf V_D}=\upzeta_D,
\]
is stationary in $D$:
\begin{equation}
 \delta\mathbf V_D(X)
 =
 \int_{S_D}
 (\tau\otimes\tau):DX\,
 \Uptheta_D\,\dd\cH^1
 =0
 \quad
 \forall X\in C_c^1(D;\R^2).
\end{equation}

\item There exists a set $N_D\subset S_D$ with
$\cH^1(N_D)=0$ such that, for every $x\in S_D\backslash N_D$, there are
$r_x>0$, a line $L_x$ through $x$, and a constant $\Uptheta_x>0$ for
which
\begin{equation}
 \cH^1\left(
 (S_D\mathbin{\triangle}L_x)\cap B_{r_x}(x)
 \right)=0,
 \quad
 \upzeta_D\llcorner B_{r_x}(x)
 =
 \Uptheta_x\,
 \cH^1\llcorner
 \left(L_x\cap B_{r_x}(x)\right).
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}

If A = V Lambda V^-1 with Lambda diagonal, every eigenvalue mu of A + E satisfies dist(mu, spec A) <= kappa(V) ||E||, where kappa(V) = ||V|| ||V^-1|| in the spectral norm. If every eigenvalue of A has modulus at least rho > 0, the relative distance to the nearest eigenvalue is at most kappa(V) ||E|| / rho. (F. L. Bauer and C. T. Fike, 1960.)

[Definition 4 (Stochastic domination) of arXiv:2608.29872, 'Local Laws and Outlier Eigenvalues for Spiked Separable Covariance Matrices'] (i) Let
\[\xi=\left(\xi^{(n)}(u):n\in\bb N, u\in U^{(n)}\right),\quad \zeta=\left(\zeta^{(n)}(u):n\in\bb N, u\in U^{(n)}\right)\]
be two families of non-negative random variables, where $U^{(n)}$ is a parameter set depending on $n$. We say that $\xi$ is stochastically dominated by $\zeta$, uniformly in $u$, if for any fixed (small) $\epsilon>0$ and (large) $D>0$, 
\[\sup_{u\in U^{(n)}}\bb P\left[\xi^{(n)}(u)>n^\epsilon\zeta^{(n)}(u)\right]\le n^{-D}\]
holds for large enough $n\ge n_0(\epsilon, D)$, denoted by $\xi\prec\zeta$. Throughout this paper, the stochastic domination will always be uniform in all parameters that are not explicitly fixed (such as matrix indices, and $z$ that takes values in some compact set). Note that $n_0(\epsilon, D)$ may depend on quantities that are explicitly constant, such as $\tau$ in Assumption \ref{assm_big1} and \eqref{assm_gap}. If for some complex family $\xi$ we have $|\xi|\prec\zeta$, then we will also write $\xi \prec \zeta$ or $\xi=\OO_\prec(\zeta)$.
\medskip

\noindent (ii) We extend the definition of $\OO_\prec(\cdot)$ to matrices in the weak operator sense as follows. Let $A$ be a family of random matrices and $\zeta$ be a family of nonnegative random variables. Then $A=\OO_\prec(\zeta)$ means that $\left|\left\langle\mathbf v, A\mathbf w\right\rangle\right|\prec\zeta \| \mathbf v\|_2 \|\mathbf w\|_2 $ uniformly in any deterministic vectors $\mathbf v$ and $\mathbf w$. Here and throughout the following, whenever we say ``uniformly in any deterministic vectors", we mean that ``uniformly in any deterministic vectors belonging to certain fixed set of cardinality $n^{\OO(1)}$".

\medskip

\noindent (iii) We say that an event $\Xi$ holds with high probability if $\mathbbm{1}_{\Xi^c}\prec0$, or equivalently, for any constant $D>0$, $\mathbb P(\Xi)\ge 1- n^{-D}$ for large enough $n$.

[Prop Hitting versus escape to infinity and boundary behavior at $0$ and at infinity of arXiv:2606.06187, 'How to Study Reflected Brownian Motion in a Quadrant via Kernel Functional Equations?\\ \m'] Assume that $\alpha \geqslant 1$ and $\mu\neq 0$.
The events $\{T=\infty\}$ and $\{Z_t  \to \infty\}$ coincide almost surely, i.e.,
\[
\mathbb{P}\big(T=\infty,\; Z_t \not\to \infty\big)=0
\quad \text{and} \quad
\mathbb{P}\big(T<\infty,\; Z_t \to \infty\big)=0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
h^0(0)=1-h^\infty(0)=1,
\qquad
\lim_{z\to\infty} h^0(z)=1-\lim_{z\to\infty}h^\infty(z)=0.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def.standard_extremal of arXiv:2603.11043, 'An asymptotically optimal bound for the concentration function of a sum of independent int'] Let $\alpha \in (0,1]$.
    We call a (probability) measure $\mu$ \emph{standard extremal} for $\alpha$ if it is the distribution of $X + i$ where $i$ is an integer and 
    
    $X \sim \nu_\alpha$ or $-X \sim \nu_\alpha$,
    i. e. the support of $\mu$ is an interval and the smallest atom, whenever it is unique, is on one of the endpoints of the interval. We denote the set of standard extremal measures for $\alpha$ by $\mathrm{SE}(\alpha)$.
   
   

    Any measure which is 
    standard extremal for some $\alpha$ will be called
    
    \emph{standard extremal}.

body:
Let $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu)$ be a probability space, $T: X \to X$ measure-preserving (not necessarily invertible), $A \in \mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A) > 0$, and $n_A(x) = \min\{n \ge 1 : T^n x \in A\}$ the first return time (finite for a.e. $x \in A$ by Poincare recurrence; set $n_A = \infty$ where no return occurs). Then, in general,
$$\int_A n_A\,d\mu = \mu\Big(\bigcup_{j \ge 0} T^{-j} A\Big),$$
the measure of the set of points whose forward orbit ever meets $A$. In particular $\int_A n_A\,d\mu \le 1$ always, so $n_A$ is integrable over $A$ for EVERY positive-measure set in a probability-preserving system, ergodic or not. If $T$ is ERGODIC, the union has full measure and
$$\int_A n_A\,d\mu = 1, \qquad\text{i.e.}\qquad \frac{1}{\mu(A)} \int_A n_A\,d\mu = \frac{1}{\mu(A)}:$$
the mean return time to $A$, with respect to the normalised measure $\mu_A = \mu(\cdot \cap A)/\mu(A)$, is exactly $1/\mu(A)$. The induced (first-return) map $T_A = T^{n_A}$ on $A$ preserves $\mu_A$. When $T$ is invertible and ergodic, $(X, \mu, T)$ is isomorphic mod 0 to the tower (Kakutani skyscraper) over $(A, \mu_A, T_A)$ with height $n_A$, of total mass $\int_A n_A\,d\mu / \mu(A)$ in units of $\mu_A$; for non-invertible $T$ the tower map $(x, j) \mapsto T^j x$ is in general only a factor map (for the doubling map with $A = [0, 1/2)$ it is many-to-one).

WHERE IT FAILS. (1) Without ergodicity the mean return time can be strictly less than $1/\mu(A)$: if $A$ is itself invariant then $n_A = 1$ on $A$ and $\int_A n_A = \mu(A) < 1$. (2) In an infinite measure space $\int_A n_A\,d\mu$ can be infinite even for a conservative ergodic $T$ (in fact for an ergodic conservative infinite-measure system it is always infinite for sets of finite positive measure), so 'mean return time $= 1/\mu(A)$' is a finite-measure statement. (3) The lemma controls only the MEAN of $n_A$: no bound on its variance or tail follows; $n_A$ need not be in $L^2$.
mu is a probability measure
T is measure-preserving, not necessarily invertible
mu(A) > 0
the value 1/mu(A) for the mean return time requires ergodicity; the general identity does not

[Proposition 11 of arXiv:2606.23896, 'The one-point Schreier Poisson boundary of Thompson's group \(F\)'] Under the coding \(\partial T=\{0,1\}^{\mathbb N}\), the
harmonic measure \(\nu\) is the Bernoulli product measure with weights

\[
p_0=2-\sqrt2,
\qquad
p_1=\sqrt2-1.
\]

That is, for every cylinder

\[
[\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_k]
=
\{\xi\in\partial T:\xi_j=\varepsilon_j,\ 1\le j\le k\},
\]

one has

\[
\nu([\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_k])
=
\prod_{j=1}^k p_{\varepsilon_j}.
\]

If there exists a constant alpha > 0 such that x^T * mu(t, x) + ((p - 1)/2)*||sigma(t, x)||^2 <= alpha*(1 + ||x||^2) for all x in R^d, then: (i) for 0 < p < 2 with X_0 in L^2, E[||X_t||^p] <= (1 + E[||X_0||^2])^(p/2) * exp(p*alpha*t); and (ii) for p >= 2 with X_0 in L^p, E[||X_t||^p] <= 2^((p - 2)/2) * (1 + E[||X_0||^p]) * exp(p*alpha*t).
One-sided monotonicity condition holds with constant alpha > 0

[Theorem t:alph0finreset of arXiv:2607.10708, 'A class of Markov processes with resetting and applications to cybersecurity'] Suppose $\alpha=0$. Then, $\mathbb P^x(T_A<\infty)=1$ for all $A$ if and only if one of the following conditions is violated for some $A<\infty$:
\begin{enumerate} \setlength{\itemsep}{0.75em}
\item $\sum_{n=1}^\infty \mathbb P^x(\ell(n,Z_n)>A)<\infty$.
\item $\sum_{n=1}^\infty \mathbb E^x[\ell(n,Z_n);\ell(n,Z_n)>A)]<\infty$.
\item $\sum_{n=1}^\infty \mathbb{V}^x[\ell(n,Z_n);\ell(n,Z_n)>A)]<\infty$,
where $\mathbb{V}^x$ stands for variance under $\mathbb P^x$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let mu be a log-supermodular measure on a finite distributive lattice (mu(x)mu(y) <= mu(x join y) mu(x meet y)), and let f, g both be nondecreasing (or both nonincreasing). Then E_mu[f g] >= E_mu[f] E_mu[g] after normalizing mu to a probability measure. Increasing events are positively correlated under such measures; product measures on the cube are the basic example.

Let n ≥ 1, 0 < α < n, and 1 < p < q < ∞ with 1/q = 1/p − α/n. Define the Riesz potential I_α f(x) = ∫_{R^n} |x − y|^{α−n} f(y) dy. Then there is C = C(n,α,p) with ‖I_α f‖_{L^q(R^n)} ≤ C ‖f‖_{L^p(R^n)} for all f ∈ L^p(R^n). The endpoints fail: for p = 1 only the weak-type bound ‖I_α f‖_{L^{n/(n−α),∞}} ≤ C‖f‖_{L¹} holds, and for q = ∞ (that is, p = n/α) the strong inequality is false. In one dimension the case n = 1, α = 1 − 2/q, p = q' is the form used to sum the Duhamel integral in the non-endpoint Strichartz argument.
0 < α < n
1 < p < q < ∞ with 1/q = 1/p − α/n (so also α < n/p)

[Lemma lm-iff of arXiv:2411.15401, 'The reference interval in higher-order stochastic dominance'] Let $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$ with $a<b$, and let $\mathcal V_1$ and $\mathcal V_2$ be two closed convex cones of real-valued functions on $[a,b]$.
Suppose that $\succsim_1$ and $\succsim_2$ are two orderings on $\mathcal X_{[a,b]}$, which satisfy for $X,Y\in\mathcal X_{[a,b]}$ and $i\in\{1,2\}$, $X\succsim_i Y$ if and only if $\mathbb{E}[u(X)]\ge \mathbb{E}[u(Y)]$ for all $u\in\mathcal V_i$. Then, the orderings $\succsim_1$ and $\succsim_2$ are equivalent if and only if $\mathcal V_1=\mathcal V_2$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let X be a nonnegative random variable (or f a nonnegative measurable function on a measure space, integrated against the measure) and a > 0. Then P(X >= a) <= E[X] / a. More generally, if phi: [0, infinity) -> [0, infinity) is nondecreasing and phi(a) > 0, then for any real random variable X, P(X >= a) <= E[phi(X^+)] / phi(a), and for any X and a > 0, P(|X| >= a) <= E|X|^p / a^p for every p > 0 (Markov applied to |X|^p). The bound is attained: for X taking the value a with probability m/a and 0 otherwise (0 < m <= a), E X = m and P(X >= a) = m/a.
X >= 0 almost surely for the basic form (no moment assumption beyond E X, which may be infinite - then the bound is trivial)

        \dtv{\mathbb{W}(n, m, q, p, d)}{ \ \mathbb{M}(n, m, p)} = o(1)

For exact algorithms on N bits, expected distinct query cost equals the sum of coordinate revealments, but no universal K bounds every revealment by K times cost/N. Fixed-order OR on fair bits has first revealment 1 and cost 2*(1-2^(-N)). Also any exact algorithm of cost o(N) can be padded by querying a fixed bit first, retaining cost at most the original cost plus one and revealment 1 at that bit. Thus a sublinear crossing query budget alone does not justify a uniform average-revealment premise.
All hypotheses and scope restrictions in the statement apply.

[Definition 26 (Flower domain) of arXiv:2605.30030, 'Critical exponents for planar random-cluster model with cluster-weight~$q=4$'] Fix~$R \geq 1$ and a configuration~$\omega$ on $\Z^2$. The \emph{inner flower domain} on~$\Lambda_R$ is obtained as follows. 
Write~$\calI$ for the union of all interfaces\footnote{Here, we consider interfaces as the closure of the space contained between the primal and dual edges.} between the primal and dual edges contained in~$\Ann(R,3R/2)$ that start on~$\partial \Lambda_{3R/2}$; these may end on~$\partial \Lambda_{3R/2}$ or on~$\partial \Lambda_{R}$. Write~$\calF_{\rm in}$ for the closure of the connected component of~$\Lambda_R$ in~$\bbR^2 \setminus \calI$. 

The \emph{outer flower domain} on~$\Lambda_{2R}$ is the closure of the infinite connected component~$\calF_{\rm out}$ of~$\bbR^2 \setminus \calJ$, 
where~$\calJ$ denotes the union of all interfaces in~$\Ann(3R/2,2R)$ that start on~$\partial \Lambda_{3R/2}$.

\item If $\iota_h^+>0$, then $\phi_h^+(\hat{b}'_{h}) = 0$.
\item If $\iota_h^{\pm} = 0$ or $\rho_{h,j}^{\pm} = \theta_{h,h}$ for every $j \in [\iota_h^\pm]$, then $\phi_h^{\pm,[1]}(z) = 0$.
\end{enumerate}

[Corollary cor:addition-type-frequency of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Fix $h\geq2$ and $k\geq3$.  For a strictly increasing
$a=(a_1,\ldots,a_k)$, let $\mathsf T_h(a)$ be the equivalence relation on
$\mathcal U_{h,k}$ defined by
\[
 u\sim_{\mathsf T_h(a)}v
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 u\cdot a=v\cdot a.
\]
Equivalently, after quotienting the forced permutation symmetries, this is
O'Bryant's weak type of the $h$-fold addition table
[OBryant2025].
Let $\mathfrak T_{h,k}$ be the finite set of types realized by strictly
increasing integer $k$-tuples.  For $\mathsf T\in\mathfrak T_{h,k}$, put
\[
 r(\mathsf T)=\dim_{\mathbb R}
 \operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}
 \{u-v:u\sim_{\mathsf T}v\}
\]
and
\[
 F^{(k)}_{h,\mathsf T}(q)=
 \#\left\{A\in\binom{[q]}k:\mathsf T_h(A)=\mathsf T\right\}.
\]
Then $F^{(k)}_{h,\mathsf T}(q)$ is a quasipolynomial in $q-1$, valid for
every positive integer $q$, of degree exactly $k-r(\mathsf T)$.  In
particular, there is an effectively computable
$c_{h,k,\mathsf T}\in\mathbb Q_{>0}$ such that
\begin{equation}
 F^{(k)}_{h,\mathsf T}(q)
 =c_{h,k,\mathsf T}q^{k-r(\mathsf T)}
  +O_{h,k,\mathsf T}\!\left(q^{k-r(\mathsf T)-1}\right).
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 F^{(k)}_{h,n}(q)=
 \sum_{\substack{\mathsf T\in\mathfrak T_{h,k}\\
 |\mathcal U_{h,k}/\mathsf T|=n}}
 F^{(k)}_{h,\mathsf T}(q).
\end{equation}
Hence summing over weak types with $n$ equivalence classes recovers
Theorem~(thm:rank-frequency of the paper).

[Definition def:regvar of arXiv:2607.18505, 'A Vector Space Approach to Heavy Tailed Analysis'] A real-valued random variable $X$ is regularly varying with tail index $\alpha>0$ if there exists a regularly varying function $b(s)=s^\alpha L_b(s)$, and nonnegative real numbers $\kappa_+, \kappa_{-}$, with $\kappa_++\kappa_{-} > 0$ such that for all $x>0$
    	\[
    	\lim_{s\rightarrow \infty} b(s) P(X>sx) = \kappa_+ x^{-\alpha},  \tag{1.2.1}
    	\]
    	\[
    	\lim_{s\rightarrow \infty} b(s) P(X<-sx) = \kappa_{-} x^{-\alpha}.   \tag{1.2.2} 
    	\]

body: [campaign status: candidate_full_solution - author-checked, unrefereed] Aldous and Janson, The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree II (arXiv:2303.02529), Open Problem 14 (pp. 54-55) asks to prove that L_n, the expected drawn length of DTCS(n) under their recursion (73) l(chi_m) = l(chi_i) + l(chi_{m-i}) + 2 + |h(chi_{m-i}) - h(chi_i)|, grows roughly like n log^4 n. Our result (id P0340, 2026-09-08): the drawn length is Theta(n), so the conjecture is FALSE. For every full binary tree the drawn length is at most the sum of all leaf depths, because the increment 2 + |h_R - h_L| is at most n_L + n_R (a full binary tree with k leaves has height at most k-1); with the authors' own Theorem 3 (the expected depth of a random leaf is asymptotic to (1/(2 zeta(2))) log^2 n = 3 pi^-2 log^2 n) this gives E[drawn length] <= n E[leaf depth] ~ (3/pi^2) n log^2 n = o(n log^4 n). The heuristic's error is a missing factor m: their heuristic (75) uses n a(n,m) as the mean count of size-m subclades where the correct count is (n/m) a(n,m); with the wrong count the conjecture is reproduced exactly, with the right one the scale sum converges (sum log^3 m / m^2) instead of diverging (sum log^3 m / m). Verification as the source words it: machine-checked in P0340.lean, together with the exact decomposition drawn(T) = sum of internal subtree heights + height(T); simulation gives L_n/n = 4.71, 4.78, 4.84, 4.83, 4.86 at n = 10^3 to 4 x 10^5 - flat across a 400x range while log^4 n grows 12x - with the sampler validated first against the paper's own clade counts and leaf-depth law. Prior art not cleared. DTCS(n), the discrete critical beta-splitting tree of Aldous and Janson drawn length defined by their recursion (73)

[Definition of arXiv:2606.29622, 'Affine Structure of the Brownian Signature'] Let $(X_t)_{t \geq 0} = (X^0_t\,, X^1_t)_{t \geq 0}$ be a two-dimensional continuous semimartingale. For $0 \leq s \leq t\,$, the Stratonovich signature of $X$ over $[s,t]$ is the element $\sigX[s,t] \in T((\mathbb{R}^2))$ whose components are given by
    $$
    \sigX[s,t]^{{\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{i_1...i_n}}}} := \int_{s \leq t_1 \leq \ldots \leq t_n \leq t} \circ dX^{i_1}_{t_1}\circ \ldots \circ dX^{i_n}_{t_n}\,, \quad i_1\,,...\,, i_n \in \{0\,,1\}\,,
    $$
    and $\sigX[s,t]^{{\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{\varnothing}}}} := 1\,$. {We also use the shorthand notation $\sigX[t] := \sigX[0,t]$.}
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2606.29622, 'Affine Structure of the Brownian Signature'

body: Let P be the transition matrix of an irreducible, aperiodic Markov chain on a finite state space S with unique stationary distribution pi. Define d(n) = max_{x in S} ||P^n(x, .) - pi||_TV, where ||mu - nu||_TV = (1/2) sum_{y in S} |mu(y) - nu(y)| is total variation distance. For epsilon in (0, 1/2), the total-variation mixing time is t_mix(epsilon) = min{n >= 0 : d(n) <= epsilon}; the unqualified mixing time t_mix denotes t_mix(1/4). [standard, e.g. Levin and Peres, Markov Chains and Mixing Times]
title: Total-Variation Mixing Time of a Finite Markov Chain

body: [Prop hpcgen of arXiv:2412.09535, 'Local limit theorem for joint subgraph counts'] If $n$ is $(p, \pm)$-HPC, then $p$ must be rational. Fix a deterministic nearest-neighbor environment omega on Z^d. For a nonzero direction l let A_l be the event that X_n dot l tends to positive infinity, and let q(x)=P_x^omega(A_l). Assume inf_x q(x)=c>0. Then q(x)=1 for every starting site x.

Proof. With F_n the natural path filtration, removal of the first n steps does not change A_l. The Markov property consequently gives P_x^omega(A_l | F_n)=q(X_n). Since A_l belongs to F_infinity, Levy's upward theorem gives q(X_n) -> 1_{A_l} almost surely. Each q(X_n)>=c. The limit cannot be zero, hence A_l has probability one. This proves the claim for any x. Ellipticity is unnecessary for this particular implication.

Single hardest gap at this checkpoint: infer a path-uniform positive escape floor (or another exclusion of convergence to zero) from the exact iid environment assumptions without assuming the conclusion. A pointwise positive harmonic q is not automatically bounded away from zero on an infinite state space.

Let (B, ||.||) be a Banach space continuously and COMPACTLY embedded in a Banach space (B_w, |.|_w), and let L be a bounded operator on both. Suppose there are constants n_0, 0 < theta < 1 and C with ||L^{n_0} g|| <= theta ||g|| + C |g|_w for all g in B, and suppose L has bounded powers on B_w. Then L is QUASI-COMPACT on B: its spectrum outside the disc of radius theta^{1/n_0} consists of finitely many eigenvalues of finite multiplicity, and the rest of the spectrum lies in that disc. Hennion's refinement identifies the essential spectral radius as the limit of ||L^n||_{ess}^{1/n}, bounded above by the limit of the n-th root of the contraction coefficients in the Lasota-Yorke inequalities.
COMPACTNESS of the embedding of B into B_w is essential - continuity alone is not enough.
Quasi-compactness by itself does not give mixing or a spectral gap: one still has to show the peripheral eigenvalue 1 is simple and the rest of the peripheral spectrum is absent, which needs a topological hypothesis such as topological exactness or aperiodicity.

[Definition def:stopping-times of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix a real number $\lambda \in (0,1)$ and a send sequence $\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$. Let $j_0$ be a
sufficiently large integer.  
Let  
$\Psi_0$ be the initialising state with
$j^{\Psi_0} = j_0$ and $\tau^{\Psi_0} = \tau_0$.  
Let $\mathrm{hls}$ be  
the $\Psi_0$-backoff bounding rule from Definition~(def:backoff-bounding-rule of the paper).
Let $V$ be a volume process from~$\Psi_0$ with transition rule~$\mathrm{hls}$, send sequence~$\overline{p}$ and birth rate~$\lambda$. 
For any
$t \geq \tau_0$,  
let   $\newsym{T-t}{sequence of times - Def~(def:stopping-times of the paper)}{T(t) = \{\tau_0,\ldots,t\}}$ and define the following stopping times (which could possibly have the value~$\infty$).
\begin{align*}
\newsym{trans}{next change of state - Def~(def:stopping-times of the paper)}{\mathrm{trans}({t})} &= \min\{t' > {t} \mid \Psi(t') \neq \Psi({t})\},\\
\newsym{back}{next back transition - Def~(def:stopping-times of the paper)}{\mathrm{back}(t)} &= \min \{ t' > {t} \mid  
\Psi(t' - 1) \rightarrow 
\Psi(t') \mbox{ is a back transition} 
\},\\
\newsym{exit}{next exit from loop - Def~(def:stopping-times of the paper)}{\mathrm{exit}({t})} &= \min\{t' > {t} \mid \textup{type}^{\Psi(t')}  \notin \{\textup{refilling},\textup{stabilising}\}\},\\
\newsym{backexit}{min of $\mathrm{back}(t)$ and $\mathrm{exit}(t)$ - Def~(def:stopping-times of the paper)}{\mathrm{back}\textnormal{-}\mathrm{exit}(t)} &= \min \{\mathrm{back}(t),\mathrm{exit}(t)\}.
\end{align*}
title: Definition def:stopping-times of arXiv:2602.21315

[Theorem 3 (Range convergence) of arXiv:2607.24561, 'Range convergence and sharp one-arm asymptotics\\for the critical percolation cluster in h'] Consider critical nearest-neighbour bond percolation on $\Z^d$ with $d\geq 11$. For every $\eps>0$, conditionally on the event $\{\mu_n(\R^d)>\eps\}$, the pair
$\bigl(\mu_n,\ n^{-1}\mathcal C\bigr)$ converges in distribution to $(\mu,\supp\mu)$ under the
conditioned canonical measure $\mathbb{N}_{0,\lambda/\mathfrak a}(\,\cdot\mid\mu(\R^d)>\eps)$, with $\mathfrak a,\lambda$ as in \eqref{eq:guiding-kp}), jointly in $\cM\times\mathcal K(\R^d)$. In particular the rescaled cluster $n^{-1}\mathcal C$
converges in distribution to the range of super-Brownian motion in the Hausdorff metric on the
space $\mathcal K(\R^d)$ of compact sets. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 8 (XY model) of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] Fix $d\in\Z_{\geq 1}$ and $\beta\in\R_{\geq 0}$.
    For any domain $\Lambda$ and $\zeta:\Z^d\to\S^1$,
    the \emph{XY model} on $\Lambda$ with boundary condition $\zeta$
    at inverse temperature $\beta$ is the probability measure  on $\sigma\in(\S^1)^\Lambda$ given by
    \[
        \diff\mu_{\XYM,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta(\sigma) = \frac1{Z_{\XYM,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta} e^{-\beta H_{\XYM,\Lambda}^\zeta(\sigma)} \diff\sigma,
    \]
    where $Z_{\XYM,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta$ is the normalising constant,
    $\diff\sigma$ the Haar measure, and
    \[
        H_{\XYM,\Lambda}^\zeta(\sigma) := \sum_{\substack{\{x,y\}\subset\Lambda\\x\sim y}} |\sigma_x-\sigma_y|^2/2 + \sum_{\substack{x\in\Lambda,\,y\in\Lambda^c\\x\sim y}} |\sigma_x-\zeta_y|^2/2.
    \]
    The \emph{critical inverse temperature} is defined as the largest $\beta_c=\beta_c(d)\in(0,\infty)$
    such that $\mu_{\XY,\Lambda_n,\beta}^{+1}[\sigma_0]$ decays exponentially fast in $n$
    for any fixed $\beta\in[0,\beta_c)$.
    Classical arguments based on correlations inequalities imply the existence of an infinite-volume Gibbs measure with $+1$ boundary conditions at inverse temperature $\beta\geq 0$, that we refer to as $\mu^{+1}_{\XY, \beta}$.
    The label $\XYM$ is omitted from notations when it is clear from the context.
title: XY model

[Lemma lem:arnold of arXiv:2604.28068, 'Mean-square Stability and Bifurcations for Dissipative SDEs'] Let ${\widetilde{Y}}$ be a solution of the SDE (equation eq:sdeLinMult of the paper). Then the following holds:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item The mean vector $M(t):=\expect{{\widetilde{Y}}(t)}$, $t\geq 0$, is the unique solution of the ODE
        \[
            M'(t)=AM(t)+\Lambda,
        \]
        with initial value $M(0)={\widetilde{Y}}(0)$.
        \item The second moment matrix $P(t):=\expect{{\widetilde{Y}}(t){\widetilde{Y}}(t)^T}$, $t\geq 0$, is the unique nonnegative definite symmetric solution of the equation
        \begin{multline}
            P'(t)=AP(t)+P(t)A^T+\Lambda M(t)^T+M(t)\Lambda^T
            \\+\sum_{i=1}^{m}\left(B_i P(t)B_i^T+B_i M(t)\Gamma_i^T+\Gamma_i M(t)^T B_i^T+\Gamma_i\Gamma_i^T\right),
        \end{multline}
        with initial value $P(0)={\widetilde{Y}}(0){\widetilde{Y}}(0)^T$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.18557, 'Randomly Permuted Orthogonal Products and Fast Dimension Reduction'] There exists a universal constant \(C>0\) such that the following
	holds. Let \(N\geq d\ge C\), \(0<\eps<C^{-1}\), and let
	\(X\subseteq \R^d\) with \(|X|=N\). Then there
	exists an ORA-based random linear map
	\(\Phi:\R^d\to\R^m\), with \(m\le C\eps^{-2}\log N\), such that
	\[
	(1-\eps)\norm{x}_2
	\le
	\norm{\Phi x}_2
	\le
	(1+\eps)\norm{x}_2
	\qquad
	\text{for every }x\in X,
	\]
	with probability at least \(2/3\). Moreover, \(\Phi x\) can be computed in time
	\[
	O\left(
	d\log d+
	\min\left\{
	d\log d\log N,\,
	\eps^{-2}(\log N)^2(\log\log N)^2(\log d)^4
	\right\}
	\right)
	\]
	using \(O(1)\) additional working memory. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.18557

[Lemma 214 (Integral inequalities for the below-top-order vorticity- and entropy gradient-controlling quantities) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] Let $0 \leq N \leq \Ntop$, and recall that the $L^2$-controlling quantities
	$\fluxcontrolVort_{ N}$, 
	$\fluxcontrolGradEnt_{ N}$,
	$\cdots$, are defined in
	Defs.\,\ref{D:MAINCOERCIVE} and\,\ref{D:SUMMEDL2CONTROLLINGQUANTITIES}.
	Then by making the constant $\varsigma_0$ from Lemma\,\ref{L:PRELIMINARYBELOWTOPORDERL2ESTIMATESFOREIKONALFUINCTIONQUANTITIES} (see also Remark\,\ref{R:SMALLNESSCONSTANTFORBELOWTOPORDERACOUSTICVARIABLES}) potentially even smaller, the following integral inequality holds for

	\begin{align}   
		\begin{split}
			& \fluxcontrolVort_{N}(\ubar,u)
			+
			\fluxcontrolGradEnt_{N}(\ubar,u) + \blowuprateoftransportWRTnumberofcommutations(N) \left( \bulkcontrolVort_N(\ubar,u) + \bulkcontrolGradEnt_N(\ubar,u) \right)\\
			& \ \   \lesssim
			\initialsmall^2
				+ 
			\int_{\ubar' = \leftubar}^{\ubar} \frac{1}{|\ubar'|^{0.13}} 
			\left\lbrace 
				\fluxcontrolVort_{\leq N}(\ubar,u')

				+
				\fluxcontrolDivGradEnt_{\leq N}(\ubar,u')
			\right\rbrace
			\, \rmd \ubar' 
		+
		\int_{u' = \moreinterestingu_1}^u
			\left\lbrace
				\;{\leq N}(\ubar,u')
				+
				\fluxcontrolDivGradEnt_{\leq N}(\ubar,u)
			\right\rbrace
		\, \rmd u'
			\\
	& \ \
		+
		\int_{u' = \moreinterestingu_1}^u 
			\left\lbrace
				\fluxcontrolVort_{\leq N+1}(\ubar,u')
				+
				\fluxcontrolGradEnt_{\leq N+1}(\ubar,u')
			\right\rbrace
		\, \rmd u'	
			+
		(1 + \varsigma_0^{-1})\fundbootsmall^2 
		\int_{\ubar' = \leftubar}^{\ubar}	\totalfluxcontrolvelocity_{[1,N]}(\ubar',u) 
		\, \rmd \ubar' \\

	\end{split}
	\end{align}

[Theorem 5 (McLeish, 1974) of arXiv:2604.07579, 'Topology of Percolation Clusters: Central Limit Theorems beyond the Lattice'] Let $\{X_{r,j}\}_{r \geq 1, 1 \leq
      j \leq b_r}$ be a martingale difference array with respect to filtrations
      $\{\mathcal{F}_{r,j}\}$, satisfying:
      \begin{enumerate}
        \item $\max_{1 \leq j \leq b_r}|X_{r,j}|$ is uniformly bounded in
          $L_{2}$-norm;

        \item $\max_{1 \leq j \leq b_r}|X_{r,j}|$ converges in probability
          to $0$; and

        \item $\sum_{j=1}^{b_r}X^{2}_{r,j}$ converges in probability to $1$.
      \end{enumerate}
      Then, denoting $S_{r}= \sum_{j=1}^{b_r}X_{r,j}$, $S_{r}$ converges in
      distribution to $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 11 (Stochastic Gronwall's inequality) of arXiv:2607.18862, 'Tamed Euler Schemes for Singular SDEs with Multiplicative L\'{e}vy Noise'] Let $\eta_t$, $V_t$ be nonnegative, nondecreasing processes, with $\eta_t$ being a càdlàg process. Let $A_t^i (i=1,2)$ be continuous, nondecreasing,  $\sF_t$-adapted processes such that $A_0^i=0 (i=1,2)$. Furthermore, let $M_t$ be $\sF_t$-local martingale with $M_0=0$. Suppose that there exists a constant $\theta\in (0,\infty)$  such that, with probability one,
	\be 
	\eta_t\leq \bigg(\int_0^t\eta_s^{1/\theta}dA_s^1\bigg)^{\theta}+\int_0^t\eta_sdA_s^2+M_t+V_t,~~\forall t\geq 0.
	\ee
	Then for any $0<p<1$ and  any bounded stopping time $\tau$, we have 
		\ce 
	\mE \eta_{\tau}^p\leq \bigg(\mE \exp\bigg[\frac{p}{1-p}(2^{1/\theta+1} \theta^{1/\theta}A_\tau^1+A_\tau^2)\bigg]\bigg)^{1-p}(\mE V_{\tau})^p, ~\mbox{when}~ \theta\leq 1
	\de 
	and 
	\ce 
	\mE \eta_{\tau}^p\leq \bigg(\mE \exp\bigg[\frac{p}{1-p}(\theta^{1/\theta} (A_\tau^1)^\theta+A_\tau^2)\bigg]\bigg)^{1-p}(\mE V_{\tau})^p, ~\mbox{when}~ \theta> 1.
	\de

[Theorem 20 (Perfect reduction of the parabolic bar complex) of arXiv:2609.01882, '\textbf{Coxeter Descents and Parabolic Homotopy Colimits}\\[2mm] \large A Hochster-type de'] Let $(W,S)$ be a finite Coxeter system, $r=|S|$, and $N=\ell(w_0)$. The based complex $\BK(W)$ admits a unit acyclic matching whose only critical generators are
\[
  [e;\varnothing]\quad\text{in degree }0,
  \qquad
  \xi_{w_0}\quad\text{in degree }2N+r-1.
\]
Consequently its algebraic Morse complex is
\begin{equation}
  \BK(W)_{\mathrm{Morse}}\cong\Z[0]\oplus\Z[2N+r-1]
\end{equation}
with zero differential.

[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2606.21591, '\textbf{Equal probabilities maximize the expected deficit\\ in the siblings of the coupon '] Fix $N\ge 2$ and an integer $j\ge 2$. For every $\mathbf{p}\in\mathcal{P}_N$ with $\mathbf{p}\ne\mathbf{u}$,
write $\mathbf{q}(\theta)=\mathbf{u}+\theta(\mathbf{p}-\mathbf{u})$, $\theta\in[0,1]$, for the segment from
$\mathbf{u}$ to $\mathbf{p}$. Then
\[
\frac{d}{d\theta}\,\mathbb{E}[U_j^N]\bigl(\mathbf{q}(\theta)\bigr)<0
\qquad\text{for every }\theta\in(0,1].
\]
In particular $\mathbb{E}[U_j^N]$ is strictly decreasing along this segment, so
\[
\mathbb{E}[U_j^N](\mathbf{p})<\mathbb{E}[U_j^N](\mathbf{u})\qquad\text{for all }\mathbf{p}\in\mathcal{P}_N\setminus\{\mathbf{u}\},
\]
and the uniform vector is the unique maximizer of $\mathbb{E}[U_j^N]$ on $\mathcal{P}_N$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2606.21591

[Lem 9 of arXiv:2605.20115, 'Moment bounds on correctors for the degenerate random conductance model'] Let  $a$ satisfy \eqref{eq.mombd-a} for some $\gamma\ge d+1$.
There exist a vector field $\phi=\{\phi_i\}_{1\le i \le d}$ and a tensor field $\sigma=\{\sigma_{ijk}\}_{1\le i,j,k\le d}$ with the following properties. For each $1\le i,j,k\le d$, $\phi_i$ solves \eqref{eq.corrector} and $\sigma_{ijk}$ solves \eqref{eq.flux}. The gradient fields are stationary (that is, their laws are invariant under translations), have some finite moments, and have zero mean: $\expec{\nabla \phi_i}=\expec{\nabla \sigma_{ijk}}=0$, and 

\[
\sum_{i=1}^d \expecb{a |\nabla \phi_i|^2}^\frac12+\sum_{i=1}^d \expecb{|\nabla \phi_i|^\frac{2\gamma}{\gamma+1}}^\frac{\gamma+1}{2\gamma} + \sum_{i,j,k=1}^d \expecb{|\nabla \sigma_{ijk}|^\frac{2\gamma}{\gamma+1}}^\frac{\gamma+1}{2\gamma} \,\lesssim \, \Gamma.
\]

Moreover, the correctors grow sub-linearly at infinity:
\begin{equation}
\lim_{n\to+\infty} \frac1n \fint_{B_{n}} |(\phi_i,\sigma_{ijk})|=0,
\end{equation} 
where $\fint_{B_{n}}$ denotes the average on the ball $B_n$ of size $n$ (see notation for details). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 9 of arXiv:2605.20115

Let $U\subset\mathbb R^n$ be bounded, open and connected, $T>0$, and let $u\in C^2_1(U_T)\cap C(\overline{U_T})$ satisfy $u_t-\Delta u=0$ in $U_T$. If there is a point $(x_0,t_0)\in U_T$ (so $x_0\in U$, $0<t_0\le T$) with $u(x_0,t_0)=\max_{\overline{U_T}}u$, then $u$ is constant on $\overline{U_{t_0}}=\overline U\times[0,t_0]$. Nothing is asserted for $t>t_0$. The same conclusion (constancy on $U\times(0,t_0]$) holds for subsolutions $u_t+Lu\le0$ of a uniformly parabolic nondivergence operator with $c\equiv0$ and continuous bounded coefficients (Nirenberg), and for $c\ge0$ provided the maximum is nonnegative. The minimum version follows by applying the theorem to $-u$.

[Defn def:VSSM of arXiv:2603.17858, 'Decay of correlations and zeros for the hard-core model'] The hard-core model on a family $\mathcal{G}$ of bounded degree graphs satisfies
    \emph{very strong spatial mixing (VSSM)} at a parameter $\lambda>0$ if there
    exist constants $\alpha\in[0,1)$ and $C>0$ such that for all $G=(V,E)\in\mathcal{G}$, any induced subgraph $H$ of $G$ and $v\in V(H)$, and for all boundary conditions $\sigma,\tau:S_{T_{\mathrm{SAW}(H,v)}}(v,\ell)\to\{0,1\}$ we have
    \begin{equation}
        \abs{R_{(T_{\mathrm{SAW}(H,v)},\sigma,v}(\lambda)-R_{(T_{\mathrm{SAW}(H,v)},\tau,v}(\lambda)}\le C\cdot \alpha^{\ell}\quad \text{for all }\ell\in \mathbb{N}.
        
    \end{equation}
    
    We refer to $\alpha$ as the \emph{rate of VSSM}.

body: In number theory, Dirichlet's theorem, also called the Dirichlet prime number theorem, states that for any two positive coprime integers a and d, there are infinitely many primes of the form a + nd, where n is also a positive integer. In other words, there are infinitely many primes that are congruent to a modulo d. The numbers of the form a + nd form an arithmetic progression
title: Dirichlet's theorem on arithmetic progressions

Let $U$ be a linear subspace of $\mathbb{R}^M$ with $\dim U \le d$, and let $r(U)$ be the number of open coordinate orthants of $\mathbb{R}^M$ that $U$ meets. Then $r(U) \le 2\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}\binom{M-1}{j}$. If $U$ lies inside a coordinate hyperplane then $r(U)=0$. If $\dim U = d$ and the $M$ coordinate functionals restricted to $U$ are in general position, meaning every $d$ or fewer of them are linearly independent, then equality holds. Equivalently, $M$ points in general position in $\mathbb{R}^d$ admit exactly $2\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}\binom{M-1}{j}$ homogeneously linearly separable dichotomies.

[Lemma lem:finite-energy-potential of arXiv:2608.02459, 'Response Calculus for Spectral Simplicity\\ and Joint Eigenvalue Densities'] Let $\nu,\eta\in\mathcal M_{\rm fe}(D)$.  Then $I_D(|\nu|,|\eta|)<\infty$, so the mutual Green
energy $I_D(\nu,\eta)$ is well defined.  For each
$\sigma\in\{\nu,\eta\}$ there is a unique $U_D\sigma\inH$ characterized by
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal E(U_D\sigma,v)=\int_D\widetilde v\,d\sigma,
 \qquad v\inH.
 
\end{equation}
Its quasi-continuous representative is
\begin{equation}
 \widetilde{U_D\sigma}(z)
 =\int_DG_D(z,w)\,\sigma(dw)
 \qquad\text{for $\mathcal E$-q.e. }z\in D,
 
\end{equation}

addition,
\begin{align}
 I_D(\nu,\eta)

 \\
 |I_D(\nu,\eta)|
 &\le I_D(\nu)^{1/2}I_D(\eta)^{1/2},
 \\
 \|U_D\nu\|_{H}^2
 &=I_D(\nu),
 \qquad
 \langleU_D\nu,f\rangle_{H}=\int_D\widetilde f\,d\nu,
 \quad f\inH.
 
\end{align}

Let $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu)$ be a probability space, $T: X \to X$ measure-preserving (not necessarily invertible), $A \in \mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A) > 0$, and $n_A(x) = \min\{n \ge 1 : T^n x \in A\}$ the first return time (finite for a.e. $x \in A$ by Poincare recurrence; set $n_A = \infty$ where no return occurs). Then, in general,
$$\int_A n_A\,d\mu = \mu\Big(\bigcup_{j \ge 0} T^{-j} A\Big),$$
the measure of the set of points whose forward orbit ever meets $A$. In particular $\int_A n_A\,d\mu \le 1$ always, so $n_A$ is integrable over $A$ for EVERY positive-measure set in a probability-preserving system, ergodic or not. If $T$ is ERGODIC, the union has full measure and
$$\int_A n_A\,d\mu = 1, \qquad\text{i.e.}\qquad \frac{1}{\mu(A)} \int_A n_A\,d\mu = \frac{1}{\mu(A)}:$$
the mean return time to $A$, with respect to the normalised measure $\mu_A = \mu(\cdot \cap A)/\mu(A)$, is exactly $1/\mu(A)$. Equivalently, the induced (first-return) map $T_A = T^{n_A}$ on $A$ preserves $\mu_A$ and $(X, \mu, T)$ is recovered from $(A, \mu_A, T_A, n_A)$ as a tower of total mass $\int_A n_A\,d\mu / \mu(A)$.

WHERE IT FAILS. (1) Without ergodicity the mean return time can be strictly less than $1/\mu(A)$: if $A$ is itself invariant then $n_A = 1$ on $A$ and $\int_A n_A = \mu(A) < 1$. (2) In an infinite measure space $\int_A n_A\,d\mu$ can be infinite even for a conservative ergodic $T$ (in fact for an ergodic conservative infinite-measure system it is always infinite for sets of finite positive measure), so 'mean return time $= 1/\mu(A)$' is a finite-measure statement. (3) The lemma controls only the MEAN of $n_A$: no bound on its variance or tail follows; $n_A$ need not be in $L^2$.
mu is a probability measure
T is measure-preserving, not necessarily invertible
mu(A) > 0
the value 1/mu(A) for the mean return time requires ergodicity; the general identity does not

PROOF (UNAUDITED); novelty unverified. Conditional on a completed network past, fix q,r in [0,1], c in [-1,1], and an integer n>=1. Let (X_i,Y_i) be independent paired standard Gaussians of correlation c, fresh conditional on that past. Set Qnew=n^-1 sum_i tanh(sqrt(q)X_i)^2 and Rnew=n^-1 sum_i tanh(sqrt(r)Y_i)^2. Put e=q-r, T=qr(1-c), B=e^2+8T, and a=1-(q+r)/12. Then E[(Qnew-Rnew)^4|past] <= a^4 e^4 + 18 e^2 B/n + 1079 B^2/n^2. In particular when q=r this is at most 69056 q^4(1-c)^2/n^2. This is a one-step positive-moment component, not a closed depth-uniform rate. No Lean certificate is claimed.
q,r,c measurable with respect to completed past; q,r in [0,1], c in [-1,1]
n independent fresh paired standard Gaussian rows conditional on past; n>=1 integer
