[Definition 7 (Markov kernel) of arXiv:2608.03353, '\bfseries A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence\\[2mm] \Large via Asymptotic Equivale'] A \emph{Markov kernel} on $(\XX,\XXA)$ is a map
\[
  T : \XXA \times \XX \longrightarrow [0,1], \qquad (A,x) \longmapsto T(A \mid x),
\]
such that
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep,topsep=3pt]
  \item for every $x \in \XX$, the map $T_{x} : \XXA \to [0,1]$ is a probability measure;
  \item for every $A \in \XXA$, the map $T(A \mid \cdot\,) : \XX \to [0,1]$ is measurable.
\end{enumerate}
The \emph{$n$-step kernels} are defined recursively by
$T^{0}(A \mid x) := \ind_{A}(x)$ and
\[
  T^{n+1}(A \mid x) := \int_{\XX} T^{n}(A \mid z)\, T(\dd z \mid x)
  \qquad (n \in \Nz,\ A \in \XXA,\ x \in \XX),
\]
each of which is again a Markov kernel.
title: Markov kernel

\[

    \qquad\text{on }\Omega_A
\]
for every $z\in Z$.

body:
Read the ladder result (every consistent cleaner ties inside the long-only stack; floors and linear shrinkage lose) through the entrywise bound. Unconstrained minimum variance depends on $\hat\Sigma^{-1}$, so its error is governed by the SPECTRUM of $\hat\Sigma$: the ratio $q = M/n$, the bulk edge, the near-null directions - the territory of random-matrix cleaning, where the Ledoit-Peche oracle, its analytical estimate and NERCOME differ from the sample covariance by design. The long-only plug-in's excess risk is bounded by twice the ENTRYWISE error $\varepsilon = \max_{ij}|\hat\Sigma_{ij} - \Sigma_{ij}|$, which is $O(\sqrt{\log M/n})$ for the sample covariance and of the same order for every consistent estimator (a consistent nonlinear shrinkage moves the eigenvalues by $O(n^{-1/2})$ relative, hence the entries by the same order) - so all of them obey the same bound and, on the well-conditioned active submatrix, produce the same weights. A fixed floor $f\sigma^2$ on the small eigenvalues, or a linear shrinkage $\rho(\mu I - \hat\Sigma)$, is a BIAS of size $f\sigma^2$ (or $\rho|\mu - \Sigma_{ii}|$) in the entries spanned by those directions that does not vanish with $n$; it cannot tighten the bound and it displaces the plug-in wherever an active member has weight in a floored direction. With case weights $s_i$ (the per-sample relative metric $s_i = 1/\|y_i\|^2$) the bound holds with $n$ replaced by the effective sample size $n_{\mathrm{eff}} = (\sum s_i)^2/\sum s_i^2$, which a few tiny-norm cases can make much smaller than $n$: that is why the relative-metric fit overfits without the constraint and why the long-only form still pays a little at very small $n$. Measured on the EMIT pool (2026-09-05, seed 101): the bound holds on every output of Y1/Y2/Y4 at n = 932 and of Y2/Y4 at n = 60, and is loose by one to three orders of magnitude (median $2arepsilon$ over the oracle risk 10-1000 against a realised excess of 0.02-0.5 at full calibration) - it delivers finiteness and the right dependence, not a tight number; the unconstrained plug-in on the same matrices carries weights of median absolute size 68,000 on Y1 and 1,800 on Y2; the effective sample size of the $1/\|y\|^2$ weighting is 150 of 932 rows on Y2 (615 on Y1) and 8.7 of 60 in the $n = 60$ arm.
the cleaners compared are consistent for the population covariance (sample, eta-RIE without floor, LW2020, NERCOME)
the ensemble error covariance is rank-deficient in practice (members near-collinear), so the unconstrained plug-in has near-null sample directions

Proof (unaudited), exact off-policy TD example. Two states share feature 1, gamma=1/2, zero rewards, target always chooses L; behavior chooses L with probabilities 1/2 and 1/4 in states 1 and 2. Transitions, independent of action conditional on state, have P=[[3/4,1/4],[1/4,3/4]]. The update is e_next=(1-alpha rho/2)e, rho=pi(a|s)/mu(a|s). For iid tuples from the uniform stationary state distribution, A=1/2, mean stability is exactly 0<alpha<4, and homogeneous mean-square stability is exactly 0<alpha<4/3. For the actual behavior trajectory, mean stability is still exactly 0<alpha<4, while homogeneous mean-square stability is exactly 0<alpha<r, with r the unique root of 2r^3-6r^2+r+4=0 in (6/5,121/100). Stability is required for every corresponding finite-moment initial law; replay initial errors are independent of the iid samples. Threshold endpoints are excluded. At alpha=5/4 replay has second-moment multiplier 59/64 but the trajectory moment matrix has det(I-K)=-35/1024 and is unstable.

[Thm Fn_StandardPath of arXiv:2609.01458, 'Confluence relations for $q$-analogues of multiple zeta values'] Let $n\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $u\in\mathcal{F}^{n}$.
Let 
\[
\operatorname{Std}(u)=(u_{0},u_{1},\dots,u_{l})
\]
be the standard path from $u(z)$ to $u(zq)$. Then $u_{0},\dots,u_{l}$
are formal $q$MPLs. Furthermore, for $i=1,\dots,l$, the elements
$u_{i-1}$ and $u_{i}$ are adjacent and 
\[
D(u_{i-1},u_{i})\in\mathbb{Q}\mathcal{F}^{n}\otimes(\mathbb{Q}e_{0}\oplus\mathbb{Q}e_{q^{-n}})+\mathbb{Q}\mathcal{F}^{n+1}\otimes(\mathbb{Q}e_{0}\oplus\mathbb{Q}e_{q^{-(n+1)}}).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm Fn_StandardPath of arXiv:2609.01458

body: [Thm 10 (Convergence of f.d.d's for the entire flow of initial data) of arXiv:2510.22155, 'Random walks in space-time random media in all spatial dimensions: the full subcritical fl'] Fix $n\in \mathbb N$. For $1\le j \le n$, let $\mathfrak H^N_j(t,\phi)$ be as in \eqref{hn}, but where the subscript now corresponds to different good sequences of initial conditions $\mathfrak H^N_j(0,\bullet)$, all of which are deterministic and converging weakly to some initial measures $\mathfrak H_j$ $(1\le j \le n$) as $N\to \infty$. Then in all of Theorems \ref{main1}, \ref{main2}, and \ref{main3}, the entire tuple $(\mathfrak H^N_1, ..., \mathfrak H^N_n)$ converges in law in the topology of $C([0,T], X)^n$. The limit is given by the natural coupling of the solutions of the stochastic PDEs written in those theorems. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Convergence of f.d.d's for the entire flow of initial data

[1 15 of arXiv:2607.12303, 'Marginal Stationary Distributions and Convergence Rates of Higher Order Markov Chains'] {(\rm Hopf's inequality, see \cite{Hop63})} Suppose that $A=[a_{ij}]$ is a positive square matrix.  Let 
$$
\gamma = \max _{i,j} a_{ij}, \  \ \ \  \delta = \min_{i,j} a_{ij} .
$$  
If $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$ other than  $\rho(A)$, then 
$$
|\lambda| \leq \frac{\gamma-\delta}{\gamma+\delta} \rho(A).
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: 1 15 of arXiv:2607.12303

body:
[Lemma eq:two-L-conservation of arXiv:2609.00645, 'Global persistence of nearly radial concentrated vortices in a bounded domain'] Under the hypotheses of (thm:two-vortex of the paper), define
\[
  \mathcal L(t)
  :=\sum_{i=1}^2\mathcal P(\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0}^*)
  -\mathcal E(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})-W_*.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal L(t)=\mathcal L(0)
  \qquad (t\in\mathbb R),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{align}
  \mathcal L(t)
  ={}&d_\varepsilon(t)
  +\sum_{i=1}^2\mathcal R(\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,t})
  +\mathcal I(\zeta_{1,\varepsilon,t},\zeta_{2,\varepsilon,t})
  -W_*.
  
\end{align}
Moreover, there exist $\varepsilon_{\rm init},C_{\rm init}>0$, depending
only on $D,\rho$, and $\mathbf a_{*,i},\kappa_i,M_i,R_i$, $i=1,2$, such that
\begin{align}
  \mathcal L(0)
  \leq d_\varepsilon(0)
  +\mathcal W(\mathbf a_\varepsilon)
  -W_*+C_{\rm init}\varepsilon
 \leq C_{\rm init}\eta^{(2)}_{\varepsilon,0}
  
\end{align}
whenever $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_{\rm init}$.

body:
[Theorem 8 (Bulk, real Wishart) of arXiv:2511.12623, 'The eigenvector bead process'] We recall Convention~\ref{conv:inverse-stieltjes-branches}. 
Fix $E \in \bigl((1-\sqrt{q})^2,(1+\sqrt{q})^2\bigr)$ and define the anchor index
\[
i_N(E) \;:=\; \min\bigl\{\,k \in \{1,\dots,N\}\ :\ \lambda^{(N)}_{k} \ge E\,T\,\bigr\}.
\]
We recall the notation for the Marčenko–Pastur density $\rho_{\mathrm{MP}}$ (see Equation~\ref{eq:MP-law}).
Then the overlaps satisfy
\begin{equation}
\Omega^{(N)}_{\,i_N(E)+u,\;i_N(E)+v}
\;\mathrel{\underset{N\to\infty}{\overset{d}{\sim}}}\;
\frac{g_v}{\,S_{\mu,\,g^2}^{-1}(h)_u - \mu_v\,}\,
\sqrt{\bigl(S_{\mu,\,g^2}^{-1}\bigr)'(h)_u},
\qquad 
h
\;=\;
-\,\frac{E + q - 1}{2E}
\cdot
\frac{1}{2\pi\rho_{\mathrm{MP}}(E)}\,.
\end{equation}

\noindent
Here $(\mu_u)_{u \in \mathbb{Z}}$ follows the sine\(_1\) point process, 
and $(g_u)_{u \in \mathbb{Z}}$ are i.i.d.\ real Gaussian random variables 
$g_u \sim \mathcal{N}(0,1)$, independent of $(\mu_u)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Bulk, real Wishart

[Prop calc2ptsum of arXiv:2604.15146, 'Renormalised two-point functions of CLE$_4$ gaskets'] Given the equivalence from Proposition (prop:2ptNestedCLE of the paper), we have the following representations:
\begin{eqnarray*}
\nonumber
 (\varepsilon_1 \varepsilon_2)^{-1/8}\mathbb{P}(E^{\rm nest}_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}(z_1, z_2))+o(1) 
 &=& (\varepsilon_1 \varepsilon_2)^{-1/8}\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} \mathbb{P}(E^{2\lambda n}_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}) + o(1),
 \\
 &=& C_{\rm nest}
 \CR(z_1,D)^{-1/8}\CR(z_2,D)^{-1/8}\frac{\theta_3(q^{1/2})}{\theta_2(q^{1/4})},
\end{eqnarray*}
\begin{eqnarray*}
\nonumber
(\varepsilon_1 \varepsilon_2)^{-1/8}\mathbb{P}(E^{\rm odd}_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}(z_1, z_2))+o(1)
&=& (\varepsilon_1 \varepsilon_2)^{-1/8}\sum_{n \in 2\mathbb{Z}} \mathbb{P}(E^{2\lambda n}_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2})+ o(1) 
\\&=& \dfrac{1}{2}C_{\rm nest}
\CR(z_1,D)^{-1/8}\CR(z_2,D)^{-1/8}\frac{\theta_3(q^{1/8})}{\theta_2(q^{1/4})},
\end{eqnarray*}
\begin{eqnarray*}
\nonumber
(\varepsilon_1 \varepsilon_2)^{-1/8}\mathbb{P}(E^{\rm even}_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}(z_1, z_2))+o(1)
&=&
(\varepsilon_1 \varepsilon_2)^{-1/8}\sum_{n \in 2\mathbb{Z}+1} \mathbb{P}(E^{2\lambda n}_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}) + o(1)
\\
&=&
\dfrac{1}{2}C_{\rm nest}
\CR(z_1,D)^{-1/8}\CR(z_2,D)^{-1/8}\frac{\theta_4(q^{1/8})}{\theta_2(q^{1/4})}.
\end{eqnarray*}
Further, the right hand sides of these formulas are, 
up to explicit constants, equal to 
$$\Big\langle:\exp\Big(i\sqrt\frac{\pi}{2}\Phi_D(z_1)\Big):~
:\exp\Big(-i\sqrt\frac{\pi}{2}\Phi_D(z_2)\Big):
\Big\rangle = \CR(z_1,D)^{-1/8}\CR(z_2,D)^{-1/8}\exp(\frac{\pi}{2}G_D(z_1,z_2)),$$
$$\Big\langle:\cos(\sqrt\frac{\pi}{2}\Phi^D(z_1))::\cos(\sqrt\frac{\pi}{2}\Phi^D(z_2)):\Big\rangle,$$
and
$$\Big\langle:\sin(\sqrt\frac{\pi}{2}\Phi^D(z_1))::\sin(\sqrt\frac{\pi}{2}\Phi^D(z_2)):\Big\rangle,$$
respectively. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop calc2ptsum of arXiv:2604.15146

body: [Corollary cor:partialperm of arXiv:2609.03081, 'Non-attacking rook placements on crossword grids'] Suppose $G$ is an $n \times n$ partial permutation grid. Then $G$ admits a rook placement if and only if the number of across words in $G$ is equal to the number of down words in $G$, if and only if the total number of black squares in columns $1$ and $n$ is equal to the total number of black squares in rows $1$ and $n$.

Let X_1, X_2, ... be i.i.d. with E[X_1] = 0 and E[X_1^2] = sigma^2 < infinity, and let S_n = X_1 + ... + X_n. Then almost surely limsup_{n -> infinity} S_n / sqrt( 2 n log log n ) = sigma and liminf_{n -> infinity} S_n / sqrt( 2 n log log n ) = - sigma. Consequently the set of limit points of S_n / sqrt(2 n log log n) is exactly the interval [-sigma, sigma], and the sequence oscillates: it comes arbitrarily close to both endpoints infinitely often and does not converge. STRASSEN'S CONVERSE: if limsup_n |S_n| / sqrt( 2 n log log n ) < infinity with positive probability, then E[X_1] = 0 and E[X_1^2] < infinity, so the two-moment hypothesis is exactly right and not merely convenient. The theorem sits strictly between the strong law, which says S_n/n -> 0, and the central limit theorem, which describes S_n/sqrt(n) in distribution but says nothing about the almost sure oscillation; in particular the CLT does NOT imply that S_n/sqrt(n) is almost surely bounded, and indeed it is not - the iterated logarithm is the correct almost sure envelope. [Hartman and Wintner (1941); Strassen (1966); see Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, 5th ed., Theorem 8.5.2]

the constant sqrt(2) inside the normalisation is not adjustable; it is the correct almost sure envelope

[Theorem 10 of arXiv:2607.17662, 'On the Strong Law of Large Numbers under Sublinear Expectations'] Given a sublinear expectation space $(\Omega, \mathcal{H}, \mathbb{E})$ where $\mathbb{E}$ is lower-continuous and $V$ is the induced capacity, let $\mathcal{P}$ be the family of probability measures representing $\mathbb{E}$. Let $\{X_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of independent and identically distributed non-negative random variables in $\mathcal{H}$. Suppose that the following integrability condition holds:
		\[
		\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \sup_{Q \in \mathcal{P}} \int_k^{k+1} x \, \mathrm{d}F_{Q}(x) < \infty,
		\]
		where $F_{Q}(x) = Q(X_1 \le x)$ is the distribution function of $X_1$ under $Q$. 
		
		Then, for $S_n = \sum_{i=1}^n X_i$, we have
		\[
		V \left( \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{S_n}{n} > \mathbb{E}[X_1] \ \cup \ \liminf_{n \to \infty} \frac{S_n}{n} < -\mathbb{E}[-X_1] \right) = 0.
		\]
title: Theorem 10 of arXiv:2607.17662

[Lemma 44 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] Let
\[
 (X,g_i(s))\longrightarrow (Z,g_\infty(s)),\qquad s<0,
\]
converge smoothly in spacetime on an exhaustion of a complete smooth
limit, and suppose that \(p_i\to p_\infty\) in the correspondence at
time \(-1\).  Assume
\[
 K_0:=1+\sup_{Z\times[-1-1/8,-1]}|\Rm(g_\infty(s))|<\infty,
\]
choose
\[
 0<\rho\le \min\left\{\frac14,\frac1{\sqrt8},
 (4K_0)^{-1/2}\right\},
 \qquad I_\rho=[-1-\rho^2,-1],
\]
and fix an integer \(N\).  Suppose that
\[
 d_{g_i(-1)}(y_{i,k},p_i)\le R_N,
 \qquad 1\le k\le N,
\]
where \(R_N\) is independent of \(i\).  After an \(N\)-dependent
subsequence, one convergence image contains the worldline tracks over
\(I_\rho\) of all the balls \(B_{g_i(-1)}(y_{i,k},\rho)\).  On their
union,
\begin{equation}
 |\Rm(g_i(s))|_{g_i(s)}\le 2K_0\le\rho^{-2}.
\end{equation}
The convergence domain and index threshold may depend on \(N\), but
\(\rho\) does not.

[Proposition prop:brownian-os of arXiv:2609.02829, 'Quantitative explosion and percolation of the divisible sandpile'] Fix $T>0$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$. The value process
		$s\mapsto \mathcal D_h(T-s,B_s)$ has a right-continuous modification. With
		this modification, the first time at which the value vanishes,
		\[
			\tau_h^*\coloneqq \inf\{0\leq s\leq T:\mathcal U_h(T-s,B_s)=0\}\leq T\, ,
		\]
		is optimal and is dominated by every optimal stopping time. In particular,
		\[
			\mathcal U_h(T,x)
			=
			\sup_{0\leq\tau\leq T}\bigl(h(T,x)-\mathbf E_x^{\rm BM} h(T-\tau,B_\tau)\bigr)
			=
			h(T,x)-\mathbf E_x^{\rm BM} h(T-\tau_h^*,B_{\tau_h^*})\, .
		\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 5 (Odlyzko bound) of arXiv:2606.25204, 'Exponential Rank Bounds for Random Matrices'] Let \(U=(U_1,\ldots,U_n)\) have independent real coordinates.  Suppose that
for some \(\lambda\in(0,1)\),
\[
   \sup_{x\in\R}\PP\{U_i=x\}\leq \lambda
   \qquad\text{for every }i.
\]
Then for every affine subspace \(W\subseteq\R^n\) of codimension \(r\),
\[
   \PP\{U\in W\}\leq \lambda^r.
\]

body: [Theorem 22 of arXiv:2609.03875, 'Measure theory without infinities'] Let $\mathcal K$ be a $\delta$-ring, $\mf A$ be an HTM, and $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ be $\mf A$-valued premeasures such that $\mathcal K\subset D_{\mu_1}\subset \sigma(\mathcal K)$, $\mathcal K\subset D_{\mu_2}\subset\sigma(\mathcal K)$, and $\mu_1|_{\mathcal K}=\mu_2|_{\mathcal K}$. Then $\mu_1 \asymp \mu_2$. If $\mu_2$ is a measure, then it is an extension of $\mu_1$. If $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ are both measures, then $\mu_1=\mu_2$.

[Definition def1 of arXiv:2411.05534, 'Inverse problems for stochastic partial differential equations'] Assume $x_0\in S$ and $ K$ is a nonnegative number. 
Given the hypersurface $S$, it is said to  satisfy the outer
paraboloid condition with $K$ at $x_0$ if there exists a

body:
[Lemma 36 of arXiv:2609.02808, 'Minimizers of Laplace eigenvalues under a lower curvature bound'] Let $e\in\{0,D\}$ with $\varphi(e)=0$ and fix $\mu\in\R$, and consider
$(\varphi u')'+\mu\varphi u=0$ in the quasi-derivative sense
$u,\varphi u'\in AC_{\mathrm{loc}}(0,D)$. Then $e$ is limit-circle non-oscillatory
\textup{(LCNO)} in the sense of \cite[\S7.3]{Zettl}; the limit
$\lim_{t\to e}\varphi(t)u'(t)$ exists for every solution; and the solutions for which it
vanishes form a one-dimensional space, each nontrivial member having a finite nonzero
limit at $e$. Finally, the operator $\mathsf L_\varphi$
associated with the closed form $(\mathcal E,H^1(\varphi))$ is self-adjoint with the
separated domain
\[
D(\mathsf L_\varphi)=\bigl\{u\in D_{\max}:\ \lim_{t\to e}\varphi(t)u'(t)=0
\ \text{ at each endpoint } e\in\{0,D\}\bigr\}.
\]

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2606.23099, 'Path-dependent Affine Processes'] If $X$ is an affine process on $S$, then for all $0 \leq T' \leq T$, there exist
    $\C$- and $\ccM([0,T], \C^d)$
    
    -valued functions $\phi(t,T',\mu)$ and $\Psi(t,T',\mu)$, satisfying $(i)$ and $(ii)$ of Definition~\ref{def:path-dependent-affine}, such that
    \begin{align}
        E[e^{ \, \mu \cdot X_{[0,T']} } \mid \ccF_t] = \exp\bigl( \phi(t,T',\mu) + \Psi(t,T',\mu) \cdot X_{[0,t]} \bigr)
    \end{align}
    for all $0 \leq t \leq T'$ and all $\mu \in \cU(T')$.
title: Lemma 4 of arXiv:2606.23099

body: Let (M_n)_{n >= 0} be a martingale with respect to a filtration (F_n) with M_0 = 0 and increments X_i = M_i - M_{i-1} satisfying |X_i| <= R almost surely for every i. Let W_n = sum_{i=1}^n E[X_i^2 | F_{i-1}] be the predictable quadratic variation. Then for every n and all t, sigma^2 > 0, P(M_n >= t and W_n <= sigma^2) <= exp(- t^2 / (2 (sigma^2 + R t / 3))). [Freedman (1975); see Tropp, An Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities]
title: Freedman's Inequality (Martingale Bernstein Concentration)

body: [Abstract of arXiv:2609.03968, 'A one-parameter family of local-time conditioned processes : the generalized Brownian...'] We construct and characterize the one-parameter family of real-valued processes that allow to recover the law of a Brownian loop-soup of any intensity on the real line conditionally on its occupation time field. These processes generalize the Brownian burglar constructed by Warren and Yor (that corresponds to our process in the limiting case where the intensity vanishes and there is just one Brownian motion). These processes are closely related to the Bass-Burdzy flow and recent work of A\"id\'ekon, Hu and Shi on the stochastic Jacobi flow. Our approach uses a formalism, building on the notion of driver processes, where one considers the evolving object to be the line that we ``stretch", instead of the burglar itself and its remaining occupation time. This leads to a characterization of these (generalized) Brownian burglars by simple natural axioms. It also allows to treat ``negative intensities'' and provides fairly direct derivations of several properties of the burglars, and in particular a ``target-independence/locality" property at the special intensity where the local time is the square of a Gaussian Free Field.
title: Abstract of arXiv:2609.03968: A one-parameter family of local-time conditioned processes : the generalized Brownian...

[Lemma O-cobc-lQ of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let $V,W$ be finite dimensional inner product spaces. Then
    \[
    \textbf{\textup{O}}(V,W)\smashp_{{\textup{O}}(V)}{-}\colon\cat{$\bm{({\textup{O}}(V)\times G)}$-Top}_*\to \cat{$\bm{({\textup{O}}(W)\times G)}$-Top}_*
    \]
    is left Quillen for the $\mathcal G_{{\textup{O}}(V),G}$-model structure on the source and the $\mathcal G_{{\textup{O}}(W),G}$-model structure on the target.
    \begin{proof}
        It is clear that this functor is a left adjoint. By the explicit description of the generating (acyclic) cofibrations, it will then suffice to show that ${\textbf{\textup{O}}(V,W)\smashp_{{\textup{O}}(V)}({\textup{O}}(V)\times G)_+/\Gamma_{H,\varphi}}\cong \textbf{\textup{O}}(V,W)\smashp_\varphi G_+$ is cofibrant in the $\mathcal G_{{\textup{O}}(W),G}$-model structure on $\cat{$\bm{({\textup{O}}(W)\times G)}$-Top}_*$ for any $H\subset {\textup{O}}(V)$ and $\varphi\colon H\to G$.

        By Proposition~(prop:O-mapping-CW of the paper), $\textbf{\textup{O}}(V,W)$ is an $({\textup{O}}(W)\times H)$-CW complex with free $H$-action outside the basepoint, hence cofibrant in the $\mathcal G_{{\textup{O}}(W),H}$-model structure. To complete the proof it then suffices to observe that
        \[
            {-}\smashp_\varphi G_+=\varphi_!\colon\cat{$\bm{({\textup{O}}(W)\times H)}$-Top}_*\to \cat{$\bm{({\textup{O}}(W)\times G)}$-Top}_*
        \]
        is left Quillen for the graph model structures by Example~(ex:graph-restr-rQ of the paper).
    \end{proof}

[Lemma 8 (mass control of compensator measures) of arXiv:2605.11783, 'Stability of Compensated Jump Integrals under Quadratic Variation Convergence'] Let $X$ and $\{X^n\}_{n\ge1}$ be c\`adl\`ag processes on $[0,t]$ with jump measures
$\mu,\mu_n$ and compensators $\nu,\nu_n$, respectively, and assume that
\[
[X^n-X]_t \to 0 \quad \text{a.s.}
\]
and let
\[
\mathcal{A}:=\{(s,\omega): s\le t,\ \nu(\omega,\{s\},\mathbb R)>0\},
\qquad
\mathcal{A}_n:=\{(s,\omega): s\le t,\ \nu_n(\omega,\{s\},\mathbb R)>0\}.
\]
For every \(r>0\), there exists a family of stopping times $\{\theta_{q,k,\ell,n}\}_{q,k,\ell,n\in\N}$,  depending on \(r\), such that
\[
\{s\in \mathcal{A}_n\cap [0,\theta_{q,k,\ell,n}): |\Delta X^n_{s}|>L(r,k)\}
=
\{s\in \mathcal{A}\cap [0,\theta_{q,k,\ell,n}): |\Delta X_{s}|>L(r,k)\}
\quad \text{a.s.}
\]

For every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $k_0$ such that for all $k\ge k_0$
there exists $\ell_0=\ell_0(k,\varepsilon)$ such that for all $\ell\ge \ell_0$
there exists $q_0=q_0(\ell,\varepsilon)$ such that for all $q\ge q_0$,
\[
\sup_{n\ge \ell}\P(\theta_{q,k,\ell,n}\le t)<\varepsilon.
\]

Moreover,
\[
\sum_{s\le t}
\sup_{n\ge\ell}\bigl(1_{\{\cdot<\theta_{q,k,\ell,n}\}}\bigr)_{s-}
\left(
\int_{|x|>L(r,k)}\nu_n(\{s\},dx)
+
\int_{|x|>L(r,k)}\nu(\{s\},dx)
\right)
<\infty
\qquad \textsf{a.s.}
\]

[Lemma lem:lcp-canonical-boundary-gmc of arXiv:2608.02459, 'Response Calculus for Spectral Simplicity\\ and Joint Eigenvalue Densities'] There exist a deterministic sequence $\varepsilon_j\downarrow0$, a Borel set
\[
 \Omega_{\rm GMC}^{\partial}\subsetX_{\rm C},
 \qquad
 \mathbb P_{\rm C}(\Omega_{\rm GMC}^{\partial})=1,
\]
and a measurable map
\begin{equation}
 X_{\rm C}\ni x\longmapsto M_x^{\partial}
 \in\mathcal M_{\rm fin}^+(\mathbb T).
 
\end{equation}
They satisfy the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=0pt,topsep=0.35em,parsep=0pt,partopsep=0pt]
\item For every $x\in\Omega_{\rm GMC}^{\partial}$,
\[
 M_{x,\varepsilon_j}^{\partial}\Longrightarrow M_x^{\partial},
\]
where $\Longrightarrow$ denotes narrow convergence of finite measures.
\item For the coordinate field $h$, $M_h^\partial$ agrees almost surely with
subcritical boundary GMC.
\item If $f\in C^\infty(\mathbb T)\capH$ and
$x,x+f\in\Omega_{\rm GMC}^{\partial}$, then
\begin{equation}
 M_{x+f}^{\partial}=e^{\kappa f}M_x^{\partial}.
 
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}

[Corollary pushforwardofbicausalwiener of arXiv:2412.02948, 'Causal transport on path space'] Assume the SDEs (equation eqn:firstsde of the paper) and (equation eqn:2ndsde of the paper) have strong solutions satisfying  pathwise uniqueness, given by the Ito maps $F^{\sigma,b} : \deln{\mathcal{W}^d, \mathcal{F}_1} \rightarrow \deln{\mathcal{W}^d, \mathcal{F}_1}$ (resp. $F^{\overline{\sigma}, \overline{b}})$. Then all 
    bicausal couplings $\pi \in \Pi_{bc}\deln{\mu^{\sigma,b}_z, \mu^{\overline{\sigma}, \overline{b}}_{\tilde{z}}}$ between the  solutions of the SDEs  may be obtained by pushing forward bicausal Wiener couplings $\hat{\pi} \in \Pi_{bc}\deln{\mathbb{W}^d,\mathbb{W}^d}$ with the Ito maps $\deln{F^{\sigma,b}, F^{\overline{\sigma}, \overline{b}}}$:
    \[
    \Pi_{bc}\deln{\mu^{\sigma,b}_z, \mu^{\overline{\sigma}, \overline{b}}_{\tilde{z}}} = \cbr{\del{F^{\sigma,b}, F^{\overline{\sigma}, \overline{b}}}_{\#}\hat{\pi} : \hat{\pi} \in \Pi_{bc}\deln{\mathbb{W}^d, \mathbb{W}^d}}.
    \]

[Proposition 5 of arXiv:2506.10476, 'Construction of ergodic \textsc{idla} forests in $\mathbb{Z}^d$'] {(Global upper bound)}

For any $L\geq 1$, for any $\varepsilon > 0$ and $\alpha \in (1-1/d,1)$, there exists a positive constant $C = C(d,n,\varepsilon,\alpha,L)$ such that for all integers $M > 1$,
\[
\mathbb{P}\left(\Over^{\dagger}_{\alpha}(M, n, \varepsilon)\right) \leq \frac{C}{M^L} ~.
\]
In particular, with probability $1$, there exists a (random) level from which $A^{\dagger}_n[\infty] \cap \mathbb{Z}_M^c$ is included in the cone $\mathscr{C}_{\varepsilon}^{\alpha}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 7 (Triangular-array conditioned bridge invariance principle) of arXiv:2609.02257, 'Aperiodic random walks: uniform estimates, local limits and invariance principles'] Under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:killed-local-limits}, define
the right-continuous step process
\[
 \widehat S_N(u)
 :=
 \frac{A_N+S_N(\lfloor r_Nu\rfloor)}
      {\sigma_N\sqrt{r_N}},
 \qquad 0\le u\le t .
\]
Under \(\mathbf Q_{N;A_N,B_N,L_N}^{+}\), the process
\(\widehat S_N\) converges in \(D([0,t])\), equipped with the \(J_1\)
topology, to the Brownian bridge of length \(t\) from \(h_0\) to \(h_1\),
conditioned to stay nonnegative. When exactly one endpoint is zero, this is
the corresponding
\(\mathrm{BES}(3)\) bridge, interpreted by time reversal if the terminal
endpoint is zero; when both endpoints are zero it is the normalized
Brownian excursion of length \(t\).

[Proposition prop:affine-gaussian-poc of arXiv:2607.00149, '\bf Uniform-in-time Propagation-of-Chaos for\\ Stein Variational Gradient Descent'] Let $Y_1(0),\ldots,Y_N(0)$ be i.i.d. with law $\widetilde\mu_0$.  Assume that
\[
        \mathbb E \exp\{\alpha \|Y(0)\|^2\}<\infty,
\quad
        \operatorname{Cov}(Y(0))\ge c_0 I_d
\]
for some $\alpha>0, c_0>0$.  Let $\widetilde\mu_t$ and $\widetilde\mu_t^N$ be the
mean-field and particle solutions for the kernel (equation eq:affine-kernel of the paper).
Then there is a constant
$
        C=C\bigl(d,c_0,\alpha,\mathbb E e^{\alpha\|Y(0)\|^2}\bigr)<\infty
$
such that
\[
        \mathbb E\left[\sup_{t\ge0}\, D_2^2\bigl(
        (\widetilde m^N(t),\widetilde S^N(t)),
        (\widetilde m(t),\widetilde S(t))
        \bigr)\right]
        \le
        C N^{-1}.
\]

body:
In the optimal stopping problem for (X, S), the smooth fit conditions and the diagonal Neumann condition w_s(s, s) = 0 define a first-order non-linear ordinary differential equation for candidate boundary functions s -> g(s). The optimal stopping boundary s -> g_*(s) is the maximal solution among all solutions to this differential equation that stay strictly below the diagonal (g(s) < s for all s > 0).
Infinitesimal generator L has distinct positive and negative characteristic roots
Obstacle R satisfies C^1 regularity on S

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The heat diffusion equation, $\dot{\varphi}=\alpha\Delta\varphi$ with $\alpha>0$, with initial condition $\varphi(x,0)=f(x)$, has as solution the function
$$\varphi(x,t)=\int_{\mathbb R^N}K_t(x-y)f(y)dy$$
where the function $K_t:\mathbb R^N\to\mathbb R$, called heat kernel, given by
$$K_t(x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{(4\pi\alpha t)^N}}\,e^{-||x||^2/4\alpha t}$$
is the standard solution, coming from the initial data $f=\delta_0$, Dirac mass at $0$.

[Theorem 128 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Consider data specifying a master problem. Assume Conditions 1.,2.,3. of Assumption~\ref{Assumptions_Theta} for these data, and additionally assume the existence of a constant $C > 0$ for which the distance between any pair of points in $\bigcup_{h = 1}^{H} \big\{\hat{a}_h^{\mathfrak{m}},\alpha_h,\beta_h,\hat{b}^{\mathfrak{m}}_h\big\}$ is larger than $\frac{1}{C}$ and the absolute value of all these points is smaller than $C$. Then, the master problem \eqref{eq_Master_equationpre} has a unique solution
 \begin{equation}
 
 \forall h \in [H]\quad \forall z \in \amsmathbb{C} \setminus \amsmathbb{A}_h^{\mathfrak{m}}  \qquad F_h(z) = \Op_h\big[\boldsymbol{E}\,;\,\boldsymbol{\kappa}\big](z).
 \end{equation}
 For any $h \in [H]$, the solution operator $\Op_h$ is linear in $\boldsymbol{E}$ and $\boldsymbol{\kappa}$, depends smoothly on the parameters $\boldsymbol{\Theta}$ and $\boldsymbol{\alpha},\boldsymbol{\beta}$, and depends on the segments $(\amsmathbb{A}_g^{\mathfrak{m}})_{g = 1}^{H}$ and the domains $(\amsmathbb{M}_g)_{g = 1}^{H}$ only through the domain of definition (the precise meaning is explained in Chapter~\ref{Chapter_SolvingN}).

 Besides, it is continuous in the following sense. For any $2H$-tuple of compact subsets $(\amsmathbb{K}_g,\amsmathbb{K}_g^-)_{g = 1}^{H}$ such that
 \[
 \forall g \in [H]\qquad \amsmathbb{K}_g^- \subset \mathring{\amsmathbb{K}}_g \subset \amsmathbb{K}_{g} \subset \amsmathbb{C} \setminus \amsmathbb{A}_g^{\mathfrak{m}},
 \]
 there exists a constant $C' > 0$ depending only on these compacts and the constants in the assumptions such that, for any $\boldsymbol{E},\boldsymbol{\kappa}$ as in (iv)-(v), we have
 \begin{equation}
\max_{h \in [H]} \sup_{z \in \amsmathbb{K}_h} \big|\Op_h\big[\boldsymbol{E}\,;\,\boldsymbol{\kappa}\big](z)\big| \leq C' \cdot \Big( \max_{h \in [H]} \sup_{z \in \amsmathbb{K}_h^-} |E_h(z)| + |\!|\boldsymbol{\kappa}|\!|_{\infty}\Big).
\end{equation}
Besides, if $E_h(z)$ is holomorphic in $\amsmathbb{M}_h$ for each $h \in [H]$, then
\[
\forall h \in [H]\qquad \Upsilon_h[\boldsymbol{E}\,;\,\boldsymbol{0}] = 0.
\]

[Lemma 14 (Entire parameter dependence) of arXiv:2607.26377, '\textbf{Entire Logarithmic Signatures\\ of Bounded-Variation Paths in Finite Dimensions}'] Let $q,r\geq1$ and $T_0>0$, write $I=I_q$, let $\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_r:[0,T_0]\to\C$ be continuous bounded-variation paths, and let $K_1,\ldots,K_r:[0,T_0]\to M_q(\C)$ be continuous. Write
\[
\norm{K_j}_{\infty}=\sup_{0\leq s\leq T_0}\norm{K_j(s)}.
\]
For $u=(u_1,\ldots,u_r)\in\C^r$, let $V^u$ solve
\[
\dd V_s^u
 =V_s^u\sum_{j=1}^r u_j K_j(s)\dd\xi_j(s),
\qquad
V_0^u=I.
\]
Then $u\mapsto V_{T_0}^u$ is entire on $\C^r$.
Its Picard series converges absolutely and locally uniformly, and
\begin{equation}
\norm{V_{T_0}^u}
 \leq
 \exp\!\left(
   \sum_{j=1}^r
   \abs{u_j}\,\norm{K_j}_{\infty}\,
   \Var(\xi_j;[0,T_0])
 \right).
\end{equation}
All mixed derivatives may be computed term by term from the Picard series.

Own-work draft; status: independently checked proof; F0124_C13 version 1. For a two-sided nearest-neighbor iid walk with P(X_t=+1)=p in (27/28,1], independent iid fair {-1,+1} scenery, and Y_t=C_{S_t}, every exterior configuration is good. For p<1 set theta=(1-p)/p, alpha=3theta^(1/3)<1, S=alpha(2-alpha)/(1-alpha)^2, c=exp(-S), and T_R=alpha^R[(R+1)/(1-alpha)+alpha/(1-alpha)^2]. For n>=4 choose R=floor(sqrt(n)), N=floor(n/R). If two exterior words agree at 0<|t|<=n, their central conditional probabilities at any outer radius m>=n differ by at most 2[(1-c)^N+N T_R], which tends to zero; the bound can be capped at one. At p=1 the record is iid. The exact maximal-cut-block expansion is a positive hard-core interval gas. A no-cut block of L steps has at least L/3 backward steps, giving a uniform activity bound alpha^L. Its occupation probability under EVERY partial conditioning is <=alpha^L/(1+alpha^L). A sequential coupling explores occupied intervals from changed exterior activities; its failure requires a chain in an independent dominating interval field reaching the center. One-dimensional uncovered points bound that event. Actual Gibbs interval occupations are not assumed independent. This is a restricted regime; the full p>4/5 range and the low-drift side are not settled and no novelty is asserted.

The sentence 'the naive guess rho^D proportional to r_D(x)^2 fails unless Z^D(D) is a.s. constant' is too strong: if Z^D = xi mu with xi a random scalar and mu deterministic, then Z^D(dx)/Z^D(D) = mu(dx)/mu(D) is deterministic and E[Z^D(dx)/Z^D(D)] = E Z^D(dx)/E Z^D(D) although Z^D(D) is random. The correct statement: rho^D differs from the normalised intensity E Z^D(dx)/E Z^D(D) exactly when the total mass Z^D(D) is not independent of the normalised measure Z^D(dx)/Z^D(D); for the DGFF extremal measure this independence fails (the mass and the shape are coupled through the Gibbs-Markov structure), so rho^D is not r_D(x)^2 dx normalised, but the argument in A001 does not prove that and the question stands. Key identity: rho^D = E[Z(dx)/Z(D)] equals E Z(dx)/E Z(D) iff the total mass is independent of the normalised measure (sufficient direction), not iff the mass is constant. [Definition def:antiHN of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] An \textbf{ascending-phase filtration} of an object $E\in\cA$ is a filtration 
    \[
    0=E_0\subset E_1\subset E_2\subset\cdots\subset E_n=E
    \]
    such that $0\neq A_i\coloneqq E_i/E_{i-1}$ are semistable for $i=1,\ldots,n$ with strictly ascending phases $\phi(A_1)<\phi(A_2)<\cdots<\phi(A_n)$. We write $E_{\leq\phi}\coloneqq E_k$, where $k=\max\left(\{0\}\cup\{i\mid\phi(A_i)\leq\phi\}\right)$ and regard the collection $(E_{\leq\phi})_\phi$ as an ascending $[0,1]$-filtration of $E$.

    If $E,F\in\cA$ are equipped with ascending-phase filtrations $(E_{\leq\phi})_\phi$, $(F_{\leq\phi})_\phi$, then a morphism $f\colon E\to F$ is said to be \textit{compatible} if it is filtration preserving, i.e.\ $f(E_{\leq\phi})\subseteq F_{\leq\phi}$.
title: Definition def:antiHN of arXiv:2609.00978

[Corollary 12 of arXiv:2609.03191, 'On lifting representations and actions on curves of the metacyclic groups $C_{p^s}\rtimes '] Suppose that $R$ contains $R_s$. Let $b\in\llbracket1,p^s\rrbracket$. Then the following properties hold.

\medskip
{\bf (1)} For each subset $\Lambda\in\mathcal P_b(\Xi_s)$, there exists a unique $R[H]$-module $\mathcal U(b;\Lambda)$ up to isomorphisms which is a lift of $U(b)$ and we have 
$$\kappa_{\mathcal U(b;\lambda)\otimes_R B}(\zeta)=\begin{cases}1\quad {\rm if}\quad \zeta\in\Lambda\\
0\quad {\rm if}\quad \zeta\notin\Lambda.\end{cases}$$ 
We have $\mathcal U(b;\Lambda)\cong R[x]/\bigl(\prod_{\zeta\in\Lambda} (x-\zeta)\bigr)$.

\smallskip
{\bf (2)} The isomorphism classes of lifts of $U(b)$ to $R$ are the $\mathcal U(b;\Lambda)$s with $\Lambda\in\mathcal P_b(\Xi_s)$.

\smallskip
{\bf (3)} The $R[H]$-module $\mathcal U(p^s-1;\Xi_s^{\ast})$ is the unique lift of $U(p^s-1)$ to $R$ with $r_{\mathcal U(p^s-1;\Xi_s^{\ast})}=0$ up to isomorphisms. Moreover, $\mathcal U(p^s-1;\Xi_s^{\ast})$ is uniquely defined over $R_0$, i.e., there exists a unique lift $\mathcal U_0(p^s-1;\Xi_s^{\ast})$ of $U(p^s-1)$ to $R_0$ up to isomorphisms with $\mathcal U_0(p^s-1;\Xi_s^{\ast})\otimes_{R_0} R\cong \mathcal U(p^s-1;\Xi_s^{\ast})$.

    Let $A$ and $D$ be subsets of $S$.
    The pair $(A,D)$ is called an \emph{asymptotically disjoint pair} (denoted by $A\pitchfork_\mathcal{E} D$) if any (equivalently, all) of the following equivalent conditions hold:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item the set $A\cap E[D]$ is bounded in $S$ for any $E\in \mathcal{E}$.
        \item the set $E[A]\cap D$ is bounded in $S$ for any $E\in \mathcal{E}$.
        \item the set $E[A]\cap E[D]$ is bounded in $S$ for any $E\in \mathcal{E}$.
        \item the set $E[A]\cap F[D]$ is bounded in $S$ for any $E,F\in \mathcal{E}$.
    \end{enumerate}

[Proposition prop_1445 of arXiv:2605.10479, 'Poisson approximation of random lattices'] Suppose that $\lambda = { \rm Vol }_n(S) \leq n/30$. Then
	with probability of at least $1 - C e^{-cn}$, the set $L \cap S$
	consists of at most $n/10$ vectors, and these vectors are linearly independent.
	Here, $c, C > 0$ are universal constants.

body: [Lemma of arXiv:2605.02226, 'Finitely Dependent Processes on Subshifts'] If $ (X_g)_{g \in G} $ is an iid process and if $ (Y_g)_{g \in G} $ is a $r$-block factor of $ (X_g)_{g \in G} $ for some $ r \in \mathbb{N}$, then $ (Y_g)_{g \in G} $ is a shift-invariant $(2r+1)$-dependent process.

[Lemma lem:ulmc-cross-reg of arXiv:2506.23062, 'Shifted Composition IV\@: \\ Toward Ballistic Acceleration for Log-Concave Sampling'] For $q \geqslant 2$, if $h \lesssim \gamma^{-1} \wedge \gamma/\beta \wedge 1/(\beta^{1/2} q^{1/2})$, for $\hat{\boldsymbol{P}}{}' = \hat{\boldsymbol{P}}{}^{\mathsf{ULMC}}$,
    \begin{align}
        \mathsf{R}_q(\delta_{x,p} \hat{\boldsymbol{P}}{}' \mathbin{\|} \delta_{\bar x,
        \bar p} \boldsymbol{P})
        &\lesssim \frac{\norm{x-\bar x}^2}{\gamma h^3} + \frac{\norm{p-\bar p}^2}{\gamma h} + \frac{\beta^2 h^3 q}{\gamma}\,\norm p^2 + \beta^2 dh^4 q + \frac{\beta^2 h^5 q}{\gamma}\,\norm{\nabla V(x)}^2\,.
    \end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm31 of arXiv:2605.16160, 'Revisiting Toeplitz and Hankel random matrices via $*$-convergence of circulant-type matri'] Let $S_n$ be a skew-circulant matrix. Then the following hold:\vskip5pt

    \noindent (i) If the entries $\{s_j\}$ satisfy Assumption I, then $n^{-1/2}S_n$ as an element of $*$-probability space $(\mathcal{M}_n,n^{-1}\mathbb{E}\text{Tr})$ converges to a 
    
    standard complex Gaussian variable.\vskip5pt

    \noindent (i) If $\{s_j\}$ satisfy Assumption II, then the ESD of $n^{-1/2}S_n$ converges weakly in probability
    
    to a bivariate Gaussian distribution with mean $0$, and covariance matrix $\Sigma$
    which is diagonal with entries $1/2$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm31 of arXiv:2605.16160

Own-work draft; independently checked proof; T232-w704-C009 v2. Reviewer urn:mb-agent:d6ca7a10ae76247b PASS, 21 Oct 2026; exact reviewed snapshot and receipt in worker folder. Historical proof_text status is superseded. Post-review scope notes are separate; novelty/priority unverified. Let Sigma be symmetric positive definite and M invertible, both 2x2. Let zbar=(bbar;abar) be a nonzero balanced rank-one factor path converging to a nonzero critical factor zstar. Let s>0 be the residual singular value, Lstar=[[0,-Gstar],[-Gstar^T,0]], and v its unit s-eigenvector. For an actual width-w factor flow split z=(b;a), X=(V;W), B=[b,V], A=[a,W]^T, Z=zz^T+XX^T. There are a sufficiently small endpoint neighborhood and sufficiently narrow h>0 such that the following holds after a fixed sufficiently late reference time: if ||z(0)-zbar(0)||<=C epsilon, c0 epsilon<=||v^T X(0)||F<=c1 epsilon with fixed 0<c0<=c1, and ||(I-vv^T)X(0)||F<=h||v^T X(0)||F, then later times t_epsilon give p_epsilon=||v^T X(t_epsilon)||F->0, ||z(t_epsilon)-zstar||=O(p_epsilon^2), ||X(t_epsilon)||F=O(p_epsilon), and liminf v^T Z(t_epsilon)v/||Z(t_epsilon)-zstar zstar^T||F>0. Only convergence of the reference is needed, using diagonal thresholds. The strict spectral bound max eigenvalue(DF(zstar))<s follows because the active Jacobian is Lstar minus the positive semidefinite product-response operator and its top residual vector has nonzero product response. The endpoint need not minimize over rank-one products. Audit/scope: Local alignment including convergence-only diagonal choice independently checked. No effective data-uniform small-initialization bound is supplied. Published G.2 local-minimum hypothesis and the selected forward endpoint remain separate obligations; no general-data second-step theorem yet.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:b830bb5e54b1c1e61f4dfbb2852f822462e59f60ce02a8ab30eb6a83f5b2ba47","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/b8/b830bb5e54b1c1e61f4dfbb2852f822462e59f60ce02a8ab30eb6a83f5b2ba47.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:62b37a0e5b3f43f2b597c9eb36466623aae3077347358d7d6bad31f4eae5889b","bundle_entry_key":"nonminimal-cone-gram-alignment","bundle_id":"population.t232-square-two-gaussian-second-step-chain-20261020","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"deep linear networks; asymmetric factorization; saddle-to-saddle dynamics","draft":"w704/bundle_004.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.deep_linear_networks:nonminimal-cone-gram-alignment","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# T232 Target 1: local Gram alignment near a possibly nonminimal rank-one endpoint

Status: proof draft (unaudited). The conclusion is local alignment. Applying Li-Luo-Lyu G.2 afterwards still requires its local-minimum hypothesis, or a separately proved extension; this file does NOT remove that theorem hypothesis by assertion.

## Statement
Let Sigma be symmetric positive definite, M invertible, both 2x2. Suppose the balanced rank-one first path zbar(t)=(bbar;abar) converges exponentially to a nonzero critical factor zstar=(bstar;astar), with ||zbar(t)-zstar||<=C exp(-lambda t), lambda>0, after choosing a local time origin. The critical endpoint need not minimize the loss over rank-one products. Put Gstar=(bstar astar^T-M)Sigma, Lstar=[[0,-Gstar],[-Gstar^T,0]], and s=sigma_1(Gstar)>0. Let v be its unit positive eigenvector. Let an actual width-w>=2 family at this local time zero satisfy
  ||z_epsilon(0)-zbar(0)||<=C0 epsilon,
  c0 epsilon<=||v^T X_epsilon(0)||F<=c1 epsilon,
  ||(I-vv^T)X_epsilon(0)||F<=h||v^T X_epsilon(0)||F,
where h is a sufficiently narrow fixed cone and the reference time origin is chosen sufficiently late so its remaining endpoint distance is small.

Then for some beta in (0,1) there are positive times t_epsilon with p(t_epsilon)=epsilon^beta, Z_epsilon(t_epsilon)->Z1=zstar zstar^T, and
  liminf v^T Z_epsilon(t_epsilon)v / ||Z_epsilon(t_epsilon)-Z1||F>0.
No balance-defect smallness hypothesis is needed beyond the stated active matching: the actual active column may lie on a nearby conserved-balance leaf.

## 1. The active Hessian grows strictly slower than the frozen inactive mode
The residual Gstar has rank one because Gstar astar=0 and Gstar^T bstar=0 with both factors nonzero; Gstar cannot vanish since M has rank two. Thus Lstar has eigenvalues s,0,0,-s, with simple top s and v perpendicular to zstar.

Let F(z)=(-G a;-G^T b) be the rank-one factor field and Jact=DF(zstar). If T maps an increment xi=(delta_b;delta_a) to delta_b astar^T+bstar delta_a^T, direct differentiation gives the symmetric-matrix identity
  Jact=Lstar-T^* S T,
where S maps a product increment P to P Sigma in the Frobenius inner product. S is positive definite and therefore T^* S T is positive semidefinite. It follows that r=largest eigenvalue(Jact)<=s. The inequality is STRICT: if equality held, a maximizing unit vector would have to belong to both the simple s-eigenspace of Lstar and the kernel of T. But for v=(p;q)/sqrt(2), its residual singular vectors satisfy p perpendicular to bstar and q perpendicular to astar, and
  T v=(p astar^T+bstar q^T)/sqrt(2)
has Frobenius norm squared (||astar||^2+||bstar||^2)/2>0. Positive-definite Sigma forbids its S-norm from vanishing. Hence r<s. The factor-scaling kernel gives r>=0.

Choose rplus with r<rplus<s. By symmetry and continuity, DF(z) has largest eigenvalue at most rplus throughout a small convex neighborhood of zstar. For actual/reference active factors in that neighborhood, the difference e=z_epsilon-zbar obeys the one-sided comparison
  D^+ E<=rplus E+C||X||F^2, E=||e||.
Here the feedback term is exactly -H(VW^T)z_epsilon and is bounded quadratically. This comparison uses the full ACTIVE derivative; it does not replace it by frozen inactive transport.

## 2. Cone growth and active forcing
Choose h>0 and eta>0 sufficiently small that
  eta(1+h)^2<h s,
  a=s-eta(1+h)>rplus,
  b=s+eta(1+h).
As long as the reference is sufficiently near zstar and E,||X|| are small, the exact dormant generator differs from Lstar by at most eta. The same symmetric cone calculation as in C005 gives q<=h p, a p<=p'<=b p, and ||X||F^2<=(1+h^2)p^2.

Since 2a>rplus, variation of constants with p(u)<=p(t)exp(-a(t-u)) gives
  E(t)<=C0 epsilon exp(rplus t)+C1 p(t)^2,
  C1=C(1+h^2)/(2a-rplus).
The distance of the actual active factor from zstar is therefore bounded by
  C exp(-lambda t)+C0 epsilon exp(rplus t)+C1 p(t)^2.       (A)

## 3. Choose an arrival scale that dominates BOTH active errors
Choose
  0<beta<min{lambda/(lambda+2b),(a-rplus)/(2a-rplus)}.
Both thresholds are positive. Stop when p reaches epsilon^beta. The growth bounds imply
  [(1-beta)log(1/epsilon)-log c1]/b <= t_epsilon
       <=[(1-beta)log(1/epsilon)-log c0]/a.
These estimates yield
  exp(-lambda t_epsilon)/epsilon^(2beta)
     =O(epsilon^[lambda(1-beta)/b-2beta])->0,
  epsilon exp(rplus t_epsilon)/epsilon^(2beta)
     =O(epsilon^[1-rplus(1-beta)/a-2beta])->0.
Until that threshold the active discrepancy is at most a constant times
  epsilon^[1-rplus(1-beta)/a]+epsilon^(2beta),
which tends to zero; the reference is already in a small endpoint neighborhood. Also ||X||<=sqrt(1+h^2)epsilon^beta. Thus, by continuation, the trajectory cannot leave the neighborhood before p hits the threshold, and the lower growth bound ensures that this happens. This verifies the assumptions used for the cone and active comparison on the entire stopping interval.

At the stopping time (A) gives ||z_epsilon-zstar||=O(epsilon^(2beta)), while ||X||F^2=O(epsilon^(2beta)). Therefore ||Z_epsilon-Z1||F<=C2 epsilon^(2beta), and positivity gives
  v^T Z_epsilon v=(v^T z_epsilon)^2+||v^T X||F^2>=epsilon^(2beta).
The asserted strong relative Gram alignment follows. QED, subject to independent review.

## Relation to the Gaussian family and remaining theorem gap
C008 supplies the required O(epsilon) active matching on every fixed first-escape shifted compact interval. C006 supplies normalized dormant matching, and C003 supplies its late unstable cone for any nonzero critical endpoint. If the canonical rank-one path is known to converge exponentially, these lemmas therefore produce strong Gram alignment even at a non-best rank-one endpoint.

This is NOT yet a general-data second-step theorem. G.2, as published, assumes a rank-constrained local minimum, which this extension deliberately does not assume. One must prove that the Gram Jacobian has the same simple dominant rate 2s and justify the local escape theorem under that checked hypothesis; one must also identify the selected rank-two orbit's forward endpoint without relying on energy below the globally best rank-one loss. Those are two further obligations, not consequences of an alignment inequality alone.

## 4. Convergence alone suffices for existence of an aligned arrival
The exponential reference assumption is needed only for the explicit power threshold in Section 3. For existence of suitable arrival times it can be removed altogether. Assume merely zbar(t)->zstar. Start late enough so the reference remains in the chosen local neighborhood for all future times. Sections 1-2 are unchanged and still give
  E(t)<=C0 epsilon exp(rplus t)+C1 p(t)^2, a>rplus.
For a fixed sufficiently small threshold delta>0, stop at p=delta. Before that stop, the upper stopping-time bound gives
  epsilon exp(rplus t)<=C delta^(rplus/a) epsilon^(1-rplus/a)->0.
Thus for all sufficiently small epsilon the local continuation is valid until this stop, since C1 delta^2 is small. Its stopping time tends to infinity as epsilon->0. At the stop the reference endpoint error tends to zero, and the homogeneous actual-reference error tends to zero as well, whereas the feedback is bounded by C1 delta^2.

Choose delta_n decreasing to zero. For each n choose epsilon_n decreasing strictly to zero, with epsilon_n<delta_n^n, so that for every epsilon<=epsilon_n the stop at p=delta_n is valid and both the reference tail and the homogeneous active error are at most delta_n^2. Set n(epsilon)=max{n:epsilon<=epsilon_n} for epsilon sufficiently small, and use the stop at delta_n(epsilon). All comparison constants are uniform for thresholds in the one fixed local neighborhood. Then n(epsilon)->infinity,
  ||Z_epsilon-Z1||F<=C delta_n(epsilon)^2,
  v^T Z_epsilon v>=delta_n(epsilon)^2.
These give convergence to Z1 and the same uniform positive relative-alignment lower bound. The condition epsilon_n<delta_n^n ensures the stopping times tend to infinity and initial p0 is below the threshold for large n. This is a diagonal choice of actual arrival times, not an interchange of infinite-time and small-initialization limits.

Accordingly the LOCAL EXISTENCE conclusion is valid with convergence alone; exponential convergence additionally gives the explicit epsilon^beta construction stated earlier. DISTINCT CONJECTURE. In a simply connected planar domain with two marked boundary points, approximate the domain by a mesh-delta honeycomb subdomain and sample a self-avoiding walk between nearby boundary points with probability proportional to x_c to the number of visited vertices, where x_c=1/sqrt(2+sqrt(2)). Conjecture 1.5 and Section 3.3 of Bauerschmidt, Duminil-Copin, Goodman and Slade predict convergence as delta tends to zero to chordal SLE(8/3). This is a variable-length two-endpoint ensemble; the cited conjecture does not itself settle Grimmett's uniform fixed-length origin-started question.
Simply connected domain
Two distinct marked boundary points
Critical fugacity x_c=1/sqrt(2+sqrt(2))
Mesh-delta honeycomb domain approximation

[Lem 172 (eighth moment bounds for $X^{\RomII}$, $X^{\trunc,\RomII}$, and $X^{\frozen,\RomII}$) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $(a(q_d):0\le d\le \dmax)$
and $(a^\frozen(q_d):0\le d\le \dmax)$
be sampled as in Definition~\ref{d:rerand}.
For $N$ large enough, we have
	\[
	\E\bigg[\bigg(
	\sum_{\ell=a}^{b-1} 
	\Delta X^{\RomII}(q_d,a(q_{d+1}))
	\bigg)^8\bigg]
	\le L^{O(1)} (q_b-q_a)^4
	\]
for all $0\le a\le b\le \dmax$. The same bound holds 
with $\Delta X^{\trunc,\RomII}(q_d,a(q_{d+1}))$
or $\Delta X^{\frozen,\RomII}(q_d,a^\frozen(q_{d+1}))$
in place of $\Delta X^{\RomII}(q_d,a(q_{d+1}))$.

\begin{proof}
Let $\Delta_d$ be as in Remark~\ref{r:fourth.mmt}. We first define the (high probability) events
	\beq
	E_d\equiv \bigg\{
	\frac{\|\bar{\bg}(q_d)\|^2}{N} \le 2
	\bigg\} \in \cFt(q_d)\,,\quad
	E_\star=\bigcap_{d=a}^{b-1} E_d\,.
	\eeq
It follows using Lemma~\ref{l:y.subgaus} (with $\cFt(q_d)$ in place of $\cG(q_d)$, as discussed above) that, for any $\vartheta\in\R$,
	\[
	\ind\{E_d\}
	\E\Big[ \exp(\vartheta \Delta_d) \,\Big|\,\cFt(q_d)\Big]
	\le \ind\{E_d\}
	\exp \bigg\{ L^{O(1)} \delta
	\vartheta^2 \frac{\|\bar{\bg}(q_d)\|^2}{N} 
	\bigg\}
	\le \exp\Big(L^{O(1)} \delta\vartheta^2\Big)\,.
	\]
Recall that $\Delta_{a,b} \equiv \Delta_a + \ldots + \Delta_{b-1}$. Then
	\begin{align*}
	&\E\Big[ \exp( \vartheta \Delta_{a,b})
		\ind\{E_\star\} \,\Big|\,
		\cFt(q_{b-1})\Big]
	=\E\bigg[ \exp\bigg( \vartheta\sum_{d=a}^{b-1} \Delta_d\bigg)
		\ind\{E_\star\}
		\,\bigg|\,
		\cFt(q_{b-1})\bigg] \\
	&\qquad=
	\bigg\{ \exp\bigg( \vartheta\sum_{d=a}^{b-2} \Delta_d\bigg)
	\prod_{d=a}^{b-2} \ind\{E_d\}\bigg\}
	\cdot
	\ind\{E_{b-1}\}
	\E\Big[ \exp(\vartheta \Delta_{b-1})
		\,\Big|\,
		\cFt(q_{b-1})\Big]\\
	&\qquad\le
	\bigg\{ \exp\bigg( \vartheta\sum_{d=a}^{b-2} \Delta_d\bigg)
	\prod_{d=a}^{b-2} \ind\{E_d\}\bigg\}
	\cdot \exp\Big(L^{O(1)} \delta\vartheta^2\Big)\,.
	\end{align*}
Applying the same argument recursively gives
	\[
	\E\Big[ \exp( \vartheta \Delta_{a,b})
	\ind\{E_\star\}\Big]
	\le \exp\Big(L^{O(1)} (b-a) \delta \vartheta^2\Big)
	\le \exp\Big(L^{O(1)} (q_b-q_a) \vartheta^2\Big)
	\]
It follows by a Chernoff bound (using only $\P(E_\star)\ge1/2$)
	\[
	\P( |\Delta_{a,b}| \ge y \,|\,E_\star)
	\le 2 \exp\bigg( -\frac{y^2}{4 L^{O(1)} (q_b-q_a)}\bigg)\,,
	\]
and integrating this bound gives (cf.\ \eqref{e:subgaus.mmt})
	\[
	\E\Big[ (\Delta_{a,b})^8 \,\Big|\, E_\star\Big]
	\le \int_0^\infty 8y^{7}
	\P( |\Delta_{a,b}| \ge y \,|\,E_\star)\,dy
	\le L^{O(1)} (q_b-q_a)^4\,.
	\]
On the event $(E_\star)^c$ we can use the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality to bound
	\[
	\E\Big[ (\Delta_{a,b})^8 ; (E_\star)^c\Big]
	\le \Big( \E[(\Delta_{a,b})^{16}] \P(( E_\star)^c) \Big)^{1/2}
	\le \frac{L^{O(1)} (q_b-q_a)^4}{\delta^{O(1)}\exp(\Omega(N))}\,,
	\]
where the bound on $\E[(\Delta_{a,b})^{16}]$ follows very similarly to \eqref{e:weak.fourth.mmt.bound}. This is negligible since we assume  $\delta\gg 1/N$ (see Assumption~\ref{a:params}), and the claim follows.  It is straightforward to verify that the same argument applies with $X^{\trunc,\RomII}$ or $X^{\frozen,\RomII}$ in place of $X^{\RomII}$.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Test the weakest form, pairwise negative edge correlation, on small graphs exactly, and examine the q -> 0 limits. Result: At q -> 0 with p -> 0 appropriately the model becomes the uniform spanning tree, which is negatively associated (Feder-Mihail / Lyons determinantal), and at q = 1 the model is a product measure; the conjecture is that negative association holds for all 0 < q < 1, and even the pairwise statement Cov(omega_e, omega_f) <= 0 is open. On a single cycle of length n one can compute exactly: the random-cluster measure on the cycle with edge weight w = p/(1-p) gives the configurations 'all n edges' weight w^n q, 'n-1 edges' weight w^{n-1} q (n choices), and generally k edges missing (k >= 1) weight w^{n-k} q^k; two edges e, f are both open iff neither is among the missing ones; the covariance can be written in closed form and is <= 0 for q <= 1 by a direct check of the sign of a polynomial in w and q (the missing edges form a 'positive' k-dependent weight with q^k which is log-concave in k for q <= 1... ). I did not carry out the closed-form check in this batch; the cycle is the first non-trivial test case because on trees the model is a product measure. Recorded as the concrete next computation: verify Cov(omega_e, omega_f) <= 0 on cycles and on the theta graph for q in (0,1) symbolically. Obstruction: Even pairwise negative correlation lacks a general argument; the Feder-Mihail route needs a matroid-like structure absent for q in (0,1).

[Lemma 18 of arXiv:2609.02065, '\textbf{From Bowditch's question to Goldman's conjecture for type-preserving representatio'] \cite[Lemma 2.11]{ryu}
    Let $m: \SL\times \SL
    \to \SL$ be defined by $m(A,B) = AB$.
    Let $U$ be an open subset of $\SL$, and let 
    
    $\Par$ be the subset of $\SL$ consisting of the parabolic matrices.
    \begin{enumerate}[(1)]
        \item The restrictions of $m$ to 
        $U\times U$, $\Par\times U$, and $U\times \Par$ are submersions.
        
        
    
        \item At $(A,B)\in \Par\times \Par$, the differential $dm_{(A,B)}$ of the restriction   
    $m: \Par\times \Par
    \to \SL$ is surjective if and only if $A$ and $B$ do not commute. 
    
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 26 of arXiv:2605.02430, '\textbf{Scaling limit of the range of tree-valued branching random walks in random environ'] (\textbf{Real trees}) 
Let $(T, d)$ be a metric space; it is a {\it real tree} {if and only if} the following holds true.

\smallskip

\noi
\textbf{(a)} For any $\sigma_1, \sigma_2 \! \in\!  T$, there is a unique isometry 
$f:[0,d(\sigma_1,\sigma_2)] \! \rightarrow \! T$ such
that $f(0)\!=\! \sigma_1$ and $f(d(\sigma_1,\sigma_2))\! =\! \sigma_2$. Then, we set 
$\lgeo \sigma_1,\sigma_2\rgeo \! :=\! f([0,d (\sigma_1,\sigma_2)])$. 

\smallskip

\noi
\textbf{(b)} For any continuous injective function 
$g: [0, 1] \! \rightarrow \! T$, such that $g(0)=\sigma_1$ and $g(1)=\sigma_2$,  $g([0,1]) \! = \! \lgeo \sigma_1,\sigma_2\rgeo$. \cq
title: Definition 26 of arXiv:2605.02430

body: For any graph G (loops dropped, parallel edges allowed) with V vertices, E edges and b bipartite connected components: F(G) := SUM_{x in {-1,+1}^V} 2^{cut(x)} <= 2^{E-V+2b} 3^{V-b}, equivalently Z(G) = F/(2^V (3/2)^E) <= (4/3)^{E-V+b}. Equality holds exactly on forests. Interpretation: Z is the factor by which dependence among edge-cut indicators inflates E[2^cut] over independence, and the bound is (4/3)^{cycle rank - [non-bipartite]} per component.

[Cor Jackson_integral_qMPL of arXiv:2609.01458, 'Confluence relations for $q$-analogues of multiple zeta values'] Let $d\geq1$. When $x_{1},\dots,x_{d}$
are constant with respect to $z$, we have
\begin{align*}
\int\frac{\mathrm{Li}_{q;k_{1},\dots,k_{d}}(x_{1},\dots,x_{d-1},x_{d}z)}{z}d_{q}z & =\mathrm{Li}_{q;k_{1},\dots,k_{d-1},k_{d}+1}(x_{1},\dots,x_{d-1},x_{d}z),\\
\int\frac{\mathrm{Li}_{q;k_{1},\dots,k_{d}}(x_{1},\dots,x_{d-1},x_{d}z)}{z-a^{-1}}d_{q}z & =-\mathrm{Li}_{q;k_{1},\dots,k_{d},1}(x_{1},\dots,x_{d-1},x_{d}a^{-1},az),\\
\int\frac{1}{z-a^{-1}}d_{q}z & =-\mathrm{Li}_{q;1}(az),
\end{align*}
where $a\in\mathbb{C}^{\times}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cor Jackson_integral_qMPL of arXiv:2609.01458

body: Theorem (campaign status: audited-pass): Pointwise form (S7): if for some fixed c > 0 one has 4^ell/(ell*log n) >= c (tag 35), then 2*ell >= log_2 log n + log_2 ell - O_c(1) (36) and hence ell >= (1/2)log_2 log n + (1/2)log_2 log log n - O_c(1) (37). Equivalently and unambiguously (38): ell <= (1/2)log_2 log n + (1/2)log_2 log log n - omega(1) implies 4^ell = o(ell log n). Notes: QUANTIFIER CORRECTION, required by S7: S6's tag (32) as written is wrong for oscillating sequences. Failure of the little-o condition only yields c > 0 and an INFINITE SUBSEQUENCE on which (35), hence (37), holds - not the threshold at every index. Cite the pointwise (35) or the subsequence form, never (32) unqualified.

body:
[Theorem 19 of arXiv:2608.19832, 'Sharp Convex Concentration for Symmetric Random Tensors with Subgaussian Coordinates'] Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent and assume
\[
 \E X_i=0,\qquad \E X_i^2=1,\qquad \abs{X_i}\le K.
\]
Let $L>0$, let $f:H_d\to\R$ be convex and $L$-Lipschitz, and put
$Z=f(X^{\otimes d})$. Then, for every $d\ge1$ and
$0\le t\le c_KLn^{d/2}$,
\begin{equation}
 \Pp\{\abs{Z-\E Z}>t\}
 \le C\exp\left(-\frac{c_Kt^2}{L^2d^2n^{d-1}}\right).
\end{equation}
The variance scale $d^2n^{d-1}$ is sharp for nontrivial moderate deviations.
This already holds for one fixed bounded marginal law with an absolute support
bound.

body: The PROBABILISTS' Hermite polynomials He_n are defined by He_n(x) = (-1)^n e^{x^2/2} d^n/dx^n e^{-x^2/2}, equivalently by the generating function exp(t x - t^2/2) = sum_{n >= 0} t^n He_n(x)/n!. The first few are He_0 = 1, He_1 = x, He_2 = x^2 - 1, He_3 = x^3 - 3x. They satisfy He_n' = n He_{n-1}, the three-term recursion He_{n+1}(x) = x He_n(x) - n He_{n-1}(x), and the orthogonality relation E[ He_m(Z) He_n(Z) ] = n! times the Kronecker delta, for Z standard Gaussian. Hence { He_n / sqrt(n!) } is an ORTHONORMAL BASIS of L^2 of the standard Gaussian measure on R, and the normalised basis satisfies the derivative relation d/dx ( He_n/sqrt(n!) ) = sqrt(n) ( He_{n-1}/sqrt((n-1)!) ). The PHYSICISTS' Hermite polynomials H_n(x) = (-1)^n e^{x^2} d^n/dx^n e^{-x^2} are orthogonal with respect to the weight e^{-x^2} instead, and the two families are related by H_n(x) = 2^{n/2} He_n( sqrt(2) x ), equivalently He_n(x) = 2^{-n/2} H_n( x / sqrt(2) ). Constants such as the sharp constant in the Gaussian Poincare inequality or the coefficients in a chaos expansion depend on which family is meant, so the convention must be stated. In several variables one takes products He_alpha(x) = prod_i He_{alpha_i}(x_i) over a multi-index alpha, with orthogonality E[He_alpha He_beta] = alpha! delta_{alpha beta} where alpha! = prod_i alpha_i!. [standard; e.g. Nualart, The Malliavin Calculus and Related Topics, 2nd ed., Section 1.1]

body: In mathematical analysis, the inverse function theorem gives sufficient conditions for a function to have an inverse function. The essential idea is that if the best linear approximation to the function at a point is invertible, then with sufficient regularity assumptions, the function should also be invertible near that point. In its simplest form, the theorem states that if a real function f is differentiable in an open interval, with a continuous derivative, then in a neighborhood of any point where the derivative is not zero, f has an inverse function. The inverse function is also continuously differentiable, and the inverse function rule expresses its derivative as the multiplicative inverse of the derivative of f.
title: Inverse function theorem

Let patience D and E be independent mean-one exponentials and service X=D+E, with joint density f(x,y)=exp(-x) on x>y>0. A customer entering service after waiting w has X conditional on D>w distributed as w+Gamma(2,1). At service age a, its hazard is0 if a<w and (a-w)/(1+a-w) if a>w. Thus two customers of the same current service age can have different completion hazards because their entry waiting times differ. Check: Memorylessness gives D conditional on D>w equal to w plus a fresh exponential independent of E. The Gamma(2,1) survival function is (1+t)*exp(-t), yielding the stated hazard. The joint density integrates to1 and has precisely this conditional law. Obstruction: The unmarked service-age measure alone cannot close the dynamics. An augmented measure retaining entry-wait or residual-service marks can supply a martingale representation, but its tightness, boundary flux and uniqueness of the limit remain to be proved. body:
[Theorem 21 (Exact aggregate-density formula) of arXiv:2609.01116, 'Vector-Carleson, Calder\'on, and Poisson--Atomic Criteria for\\ Generalized Hilbert Operat'] For every $K\ge1$,
\[
 \boxed{\Ccal_K(X)^2=\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}
 A_\lambda\gamma_K(\lambda),\qquad
 \Ccal_\infty(X)^2=\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}A_\lambda.}
 \tag{7.3}
\]
There is $c_p>0$ such that
\[
 c_p\delta_K(\lambda)^2\le1-\gamma_K(\lambda)
 \le\delta_K(\lambda)^\alpha.
 \tag{7.4}
\]
Consequently $\Ccal_K(X)\uparrow\Ccal_\infty(X)$, including an infinite
limit. All statements remain valid for coordinate tails.

[Lemma L:alpha0-tail of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Take $n/2 \le m \le n$. For any $\epsilon \in (0, 1)$ we have the bound
$$
\mathbb{P}(W(1, 1; n, m) < \mu(n, m) - \epsilon n) \le 2\exp\left(- c \epsilon^3 n^2 \right),
$$
where $c>0$ is a universal constant.
Moreover, for any $\alpha_0 \in (0, 1/2)$, $\alpha \in [\alpha_0, 1/2 - n^{-1/3}]$, and $\epsilon \in (0, 1)$ with $\mu_\alpha(n, m) - \epsilon n \ge \mu(n, m)$, we have 
$$
\mathbb{P}(W(1, 1; n, m) < \mu_\alpha(n, m) - \epsilon n) \le 2\exp\left(-  \frac{c\epsilon^2 n}{1/2 - \alpha} \right).
$$
where $c > 0$ is a constant depending on only on $\alpha_0$.

[Definition 11 (Generated tree, see Figure \ref{fig:generated_tree}) of arXiv:2605.09459, 'Multipoint connectivity in the branching interlacement process'] Let $T$ be a finite planar tree with more than $n$ vertices, and $v_1,\dots,v_n$ distinct vertices of $T$. The \textbf{tree generated by $v_1,\dots,v_n$ in $T$} is the tree $T\langle v_1,\dots,v_n\rangle$ with vertex set
  \[
    \{v_1,\dots,v_n\} \cup \{v_i \wedge v_j, i \neq j\},
  \]
  and where two vertices are connected by an edge if the geodesic between the two in $T$ does not contain any other vertex of $T\langle v_1,\dots,v_n\rangle$.

[Lemma 14 of arXiv:2608.26662, 'Boundary–Moment Universality and Curvature Corrections in Random Geometric Graphs on Riema'] Assume $d\ge2$.  Use the displacement coordinates
$z=z_1$ and
$w=z_1-z_2$.
We set
$a=\ind_{\{|z|\le1\}}$,
$b=\ind_{\{|z-w|\le1\}}$,
$c=\ind_{\{|w|\le1\}}$,
and
$\widehat H_{\mathfrak h}(z,w)
:=
\overline{\mathfrak h}(a,b,c)$.
Then
\[
\widehat H_{\mathfrak h}\in BV_c(\R^{2d})
\]
holds. 
Moreover, for every
$\varphi\in C_c^1(\R^{2d};\R^d)$, we have
\begin{align}
\int_{\R^{2d}}
\varphi\cdot dD_w\widehat H_{\mathfrak h}
={}&
\int_{\R^d}\int_{\{|z-w|=1\}}
\Delta_b\mathfrak h(a,c)\,
\varphi(z,w)\cdot(z-w)
\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}(w)\,dz
\\
&-
\int_{\R^d}\int_{S^{d-1}}
\Delta_c\mathfrak h(a,b)\,
\varphi(z,w)\cdot w
\,d\sigma(w)\,dz,
\notag
\end{align}
where
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta_b\mathfrak h(a,c)
&:=
\mathfrak h(a,1,c)-\mathfrak h(a,0,c)\\
&=
\lambda_P(a+c)+(\lambda_K-3\lambda_P)ac,
\end{aligned}
\]
and
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta_c\mathfrak h(a,b)
&:=
\mathfrak h(a,b,1)-\mathfrak h(a,b,0)\\
&=
\lambda_P(a+b)+(\lambda_K-3\lambda_P)ab.
\end{aligned}
\]
The two measures on the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:BV-jump-measure}
are mutually singular; consequently, each of them is supported in
$\operatorname{supp}\widehat H_{\mathfrak h}$.

[Definition 23 of arXiv:2609.02105, 'Contact fundamental forms and \\ adjoint varieties'] Let $S \subset U(\fh)^*$ be a contact symbol system on the graded Heisenberg algebra $\fh$.
Regarding $U(\fh)^*$ as the space of  polynomial functions on the Heisenberg group $\sH$, the subspace $S \subset U(\fh)^*$ is a linear system of  regular functions on the affine variety $\sH$. This gives rise to a morphism $\Phi_S: \sH \to \BP S^*$. Let $Z^S \subset \BP S^*$ be the closure of the image of $\Phi_S$. We call it the {\em Heisenberg-symmetric variety} determined by the contact symbol system $S \subset U(\fh)^*$.

[Definition def:FKG-ratio of arXiv:2505.02685, 'On the Spectral Expansion of Monotone Subsets of the Hypercube'] Fix a monotone set $A\subseteq\{0,1\}^{n}$ with at least 2 elements. We define the \emph{approximate FKG ratio} of the poset $A$ to be
$$\delta(A):=\min\left\{0,\inf_{f,g\in \mathsf{mono} _{A}\setminus \mathsf{const}_{A}}\frac{\Covs{A}{f}{g}}{\sqrt{\Vars{A}{f}\cdot\Vars{A}{g}}}\right\},$$
where $f$ and $g$ range over all non-constant monotone increasing functions from $A$ to $\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$. Here, $\Covs{A}{f}{g}$ stands for the covariance of the random variable pair $(f(x),g(x))$ where $x$ is a uniformly random element of $A$.
title: Approximate FKG ratio

[Lemma lem:certificate of arXiv:2608.30254, 'Exact Recovery Thresholds for Weighted Data Selection\\ in Vector-Valued Linear Regression'] Let $c\in\mathbb{R}^N_{\ge0}$ have support $S$ with $c_i>0$ on $S$. If
\begin{equation}
  \sum_{i\in S}c_iM_i=0
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  \operatorname{span}\{x_i:i\in S\}=T ,
\end{equation}
then $A(F_c)=W^\circ$; in particular the selection realizes the full-data
optimal loss, and the ratio is $1$ (also when $L^{\star}_{D}=0$, by the $0/0$
convention).

Own-work draft; independently checked proof. For a two-tail decoder using an m-valued left-tail message, v-epsilon <= sqrt(m)(rho(n)+p rho(2n))/2+rho(n)sqrt(v)/2, where p=P(A), v=p(1-p). No upper bound on message alphabet or observation-window length is implied by finite-state X. Here A is a coordinate-zero event, epsilon is the decoder error, n>=1; the m message cells form a partition of the distant left tail and the right-tail decision can depend on the cell. If rho(n)->0, fixed 0<p<1 and epsilon_n->0 force m_n=Omega(rho(n)^(-2)) wherever rho(n)>0.

body:
[Corollary 66 of arXiv:2608.12947, 'Branch-stationary max-stable fields on rooted trees'] For \(v\in K\), define
\begin{equation}
  \Psi_{K,v}(x)
  =
  \E*{
    Z_v^\alpha\omega_{K,v}(x,Z)
  },
  \qquad x\in(0,\infty)^K.
  
\end{equation}
Then
\[
  0
  \leq
  \Psi_{K,v}(x)
  =
  \E*{
    \omega_{K,v}(x,\Theta^{[v]})
  }
  \leq1,
  \qquad
  \Psi_{K,v}(cx)=\Psi_{K,v}(x),
  \quad c>0,
\]
and
\begin{equation}
  \ell_K(x)
  =
  \sum_{v\in K}x_v\Psi_{K,v}(x).
  
\end{equation}
The field \(\eta\) is branch-stationary if and only if
\begin{equation}
  \Psi_{aK,av}(x^a)
  =
  \Psi_{K,v}(x),
  \qquad
  a\in\mathcal T,\quad
  v\in K,\quad
  x\in(0,\infty)^K,
  
\end{equation}
for every non-empty finite \(K\subset\mathcal T\). If \(Z\) satisfies (equation 17 of the paper) and
\(\Theta=\Theta^{[\varnothing]}\), then
\begin{equation}
  \Psi_{K,v}(x)
  =
  \E*{
    \Theta_v^\alpha
    \omega_{K,v}(x,\Theta)
  }.
  
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:nogradient of arXiv:2510.22778, 'Free denoising diffusion models'] Let $f\in C^{1}(\mathbb{R})$ with $f>0$. Suppose the spectral flow of (equation eq:opsde of the paper) is, for
every initial law, the $m$-mobility Wasserstein gradient flow of an energy
\[
  E[\mu]=\int W\,\mathrm{d}\mu+\tfrac12\iint K(x,y)\,\mathrm{d}\mu(x)\mathrm{d}\mu(y),
  \qquad K\ \text{symmetric and }C^{2}\ \text{off the diagonal},
\]
with a continuous mobility $m>0$, that is
$\partial_{t}\mu+\partial_{x}\big(\mu\,m\,\partial_{x}\tfrac{\delta E}{\delta\mu}\big)^{-}=0$
reproduces (equation eq:opvelocity of the paper). Then $m$ and $f$ are both constant. In particular,
for non-constant $f$ the flow is not a Wasserstein gradient flow of
any such energy, and the convexity method of Section~(sec:inequalities of the paper) does not
apply.

[Theorem 7 of arXiv:2608.19179, 'A random walk on $p$-groups with a symmetric perfect pairing'] Suppose $M$ is symmetric and non-singular. Then $\Delta_S$ satisfies
   \[
   \Delta_S \Big[ \Ker(M) \Big]=
   \Ker 
   \begin{mat}{ccc|c}
   & & & *\\
   & M& &\vdots\\
   & & & *\\ \hline
   * & \hdots & * & *
   \end{mat} \hspace{1in} \text{ for all } \, M
   \]
   where the entries denoted by $*$ are uniformly random variables, that are independent, subject to the symmetry condition. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Attempt to derive g_alpha from the PWIT recursive distributional equation for the resolvent at z, then differentiate in z. Result: The density is g_alpha(r) = (1/2pi) Delta_z of the log-potential U(z) = -integral log|z-w| dmu_alpha(w), and U is expressed through the limit of the singular-value law of the shifted operator on the PWIT, whose Stieltjes transform satisfies a fixed-point equation in a 2x2 matrix-valued function with alpha-stable-type nonlinearity (as in Bordenave-Caputo-Chafai). The z-dependence enters only through the off-diagonal entries; at z = 0 the equation closes on a single positive stable random variable, which is why g_alpha(0) is explicit. For z not 0 the fixed point involves a two-parameter family of stable laws (radial and angular parts), and I could not reduce it to a scalar equation; the isotropy only removes the angular variable of z, not of the recursion. Tail check: the stated tail r^{2(alpha-1)} e^{-alpha r^alpha/2} is consistent with the expected behaviour that eigenvalues of modulus r come from rows with an exceptionally large entry of size r^alpha, whose density in the stable domain is r^{-alpha-1} ... the exponential factor indicates instead a large-deviation of a sum of alpha-stable variables of the Poisson-Dirichlet type. No closed form. Obstruction: The matrix-valued PWIT fixed point does not reduce to a scalar equation away from z = 0.

Let $\{\mu_n\}_{n\ge 1}$ be a family of $\mathcal P(\mathcal S)$-valued random probability measures defined on a common probability space $(\Omega,\mathscr{F},\P)$ (i.e. each $\mu_n$: $(\Omega,\mathscr{F}) \to (\mathcal P(\mathcal S), \mathcal{B}\bigl(\mathcal{P}(\mathcal S),\Gamma\bigr))$ is a measurable function, where $\mathcal{B}\bigl(\mathcal{P}(\mathcal S),\Gamma\bigr)$ denotes the Borel $\sigma$-field on $\mathcal P(\mathcal{S})$ generated by $\Gamma$). We say that $\mu_n$ converges weakly in probability to a measure $\mu \in  \mathcal P(\mathcal S)$, if for all $U \in \Gamma$ containing $\mu$, we have $$\P(\mu_n \in U) \rightarrow 1.$$

body:
Let f be a C^1 diffeomorphism of a compact Riemannian manifold M and mu an f-invariant Borel probability measure. Since M is compact, log of the norm of Df and of Df^{-1} are bounded, hence integrable, so Oseledets' multiplicative ergodic theorem applies: for mu-a.e. x there are finitely many numbers lambda_1(x) > lambda_2(x) > ... > lambda_{k(x)}(x) (the LYAPUNOV EXPONENTS at x) and a Df-invariant splitting of the tangent space

  T_x M = E_1(x) + ... + E_{k(x)}(x),   Df_x E_i(x) = E_i(f x),

such that for every nonzero v in E_i(x) the limit of (1/n) log |Df^n_x v| as n -> +-infinity exists and equals lambda_i(x). The functions x -> lambda_i(x) and the multiplicities dim E_i(x) are measurable and f-invariant, and if mu is ergodic they are constant almost everywhere; the subspaces E_i(x) are measurable and Df-equivariant, Df_x E_i(x) = E_i(fx). The splitting is in general only MEASURABLE, not continuous, and the convergence is not uniform in x.

Two structural facts that every application uses. (1) TEMPEREDNESS: any measurable positive function that is subexponential along orbits -- such as the angle between the Oseledets subspaces, or the norm of the change to Lyapunov (adapted) coordinates -- can be chosen tempered, meaning (1/n) log of its value at f^n x tends to 0; this is what lets one build Lyapunov charts in which Df is uniformly contracting on the negative-exponent bundle at the cost of a chart size that shrinks subexponentially along the orbit. (2) PESIN BLOCKS: for each l one collects the points where the Oseledets estimates hold with uniform constants depending on l; the resulting sets Lambda_l are COMPACT (after discarding a null set and restricting the subbundles continuously), increase in l, exhaust a full-measure set, and carry uniform hyperbolic-like estimates. They are NOT f-invariant -- an orbit wanders between blocks -- which is exactly why non-uniformly hyperbolic statements are local-and-measurable rather than uniform.

A point x is called (non-uniformly) hyperbolic when no exponent at x is zero; the stable bundle E^s(x) is the sum of the E_i(x) with lambda_i(x) < 0 and the unstable bundle the sum of those with lambda_i(x) > 0. Zero exponents are the obstruction: nothing in this framework says anything about directions with zero exponent.
M is a compact Riemannian manifold and f a C^1 diffeomorphism of M
mu is an f-invariant Borel probability measure (compactness makes the Oseledets integrability condition automatic)
the exponents and multiplicities are measurable and f-invariant, constant a.e. when mu is ergodic; the subspaces are measurable and Df-equivariant
the Oseledets splitting is measurable, generally not continuous, and the Pesin blocks are not invariant

body:
The gcd of two positive integers a >= b is computed by repeated division: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a mod b), terminating when the remainder is 0, at which point the last nonzero remainder is gcd(a, b). Running the steps backward (the extended Euclidean algorithm) produces integers x, y with ax + by = gcd(a, b) (Bezout coefficients). It runs in O(log min(a,b)) division steps.
a, b positive integers

[Definition of arXiv:2505.12187, 'Speeding up quantum Markov processes through lifting'] We say that
    a QMS $\mathcal{P}_t = \exp(t \mathcal{L})$ with a full-rank invariant state is \emph{ergodic} if the convergence in (equation eq:ergodic of the paper) holds, equivalently, $\mathcal{N}(\mathcal{L}) = \mathcal{F}(\mathcal{L})$. 
    We say that $\mathcal{P}_t$ is \emph{primitive} if it admits a unique full-rank invariant state $\sigma$.

Own-work draft, C007 version 2, proof (unaudited); priority not established. For every m>=1 and 0<eta<=1, consider the depth-three mean-field model h_i=sigma(w_i x), z_j=m^(-1)sum_i B_ji h_i, f=m^(-1)sum_j a_j sigma(z_j), with sigma(z)=z/[4(1+z^2)]. Data have x=1 and y Bernoulli(1/2). Every w_i,a_j,B_ji is initially 1/4; these point-mass random variables are independent iid within each array and independent between arrays and runs. Train all layers by one simultaneous half-squared-loss SGD step, with learning-rate multipliers m on a,w and m^2 on B, using independently sampled labels in the two runs. Let L(theta)=E[(f_theta-y)^2/2]. For any compatible permutation P define H_m=sup_{0<=t<=1}[L((1-t)theta^A+tP theta^B)-(1-t)L(theta^A)-tL(theta^B)]_+. Then E inf_P H_m>=eta^2/160000000. All arrays remain constant within a run, so every permutation fixes the endpoints. The width-independent scalar reduction F=a sigma(b sigma(w)) has f0=17/18500 and grad F=(78625,78591,69345)/21390625 at (1/4,1/4,1/4). Along the sampled-update segment, its population risk has second derivative <=-1/10000000; independent labels differ with probability 1/2, giving the bound. The activation and its first two derivatives are globally bounded by 1. This rules out a universal width-only replacement for independent SGD noise in this finite-horizon class. A positive excess above the larger endpoint loss, a prescribed nondegenerate initialization, or low-risk converged endpoints is not established.

body:
Let f be in L^1_loc(R^d). Then for Lebesgue-almost every x, (1/|B(x,r)|) integral_{B(x,r)} |f(y) - f(x)| dy -> 0 as r -> 0; such an x is called a Lebesgue point of f. In particular the averages of f over shrinking balls converge to f(x) for a.e. x. The result persists if balls are replaced by any family of sets U_r shrinking NICELY to x, meaning U_r is contained in B(x,r) and |U_r| >= c |B(x,r)| for a fixed c > 0 (cubes centred at x, for instance). It FAILS for families of arbitrary eccentricity: in R^2 there is an integrable f whose averages over rectangles centred at x with sides parallel to the axes and both side lengths tending to 0 fail to converge at almost every x, because the strong maximal function is not of weak type (1,1). The a.e. exceptional set genuinely depends on f and cannot be taken empty. [standard; e.g. Stein and Shakarchi, Real Analysis, Chapter 3, Corollary 1.5 and Section 1.4]
f in L^1_loc(R^d), Lebesgue measure
averaging sets shrink nicely to x (bounded eccentricity); unbounded eccentricity breaks the theorem

body: [Theorem 18 (Morse transfer from induced subcomplexes) of arXiv:2609.01882, '\textbf{Coxeter Descents and Parabolic Homotopy Colimits}\\[2mm] \large A Hochster-type de'] For each $D\subseteq S$, the unit matchings in Lemmas~\ref{lem:conereduction} and \ref{lem:descentclosure} give an explicit algebraic Morse reduction of the $D$-relative pair to the suspended augmented chains of $\sd\mathcal K_D$. Consequently any unit acyclic matching on $\sd\mathcal K_D$ may be applied as a second algebraic Morse reduction, shifted one degree upward. If $\mathcal K_D\ne\{\varnothing\}$ and the chosen matching has a critical vertex, the augmentation generator can be cancelled with the suspension of one such vertex; the remaining critical generators represent the shifted reduced Morse complex of $\sd\mathcal K_D$.

[Lemma modifiedEP9.6 of arXiv:2506.10448, 'Hitting probabilities and the Ekstr\"om--Persson conjecture'] Let $\mu$ and $\theta$ be probability measures on a separable metric space $X$, let 
$(V_k)_{k=1}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of Borel subsets of $X$ such that $0<\mu(V_k)<1$ for
every $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $\underline r$ be a sequence of positive numbers tending to $0$.
Suppose that there exists a number $s>0$ such that 
\begin{equation}
f_{\theta}(\underline{\rho})=s_2(\underline{\rho})
\end{equation}
for every sequence $\underline{\rho}=(\rho_k)_{k=1}^\infty$ of radii with 
$s_2(\underline{\rho})\leq s$. Assume also that
there exists a constant $C$ such that, for every $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and every $x\in \spt \theta$,
\[
\theta(B(x,2r_k))\leq C\mu_{V_k}(B(x,r_k))
\] 
where $\mu_{V_k}:=\mu(V_k)^{-1}\mu_{|_{V_k}}$.
If there exists $t\in\mathopen]0,s\mathclose[$ such that 
\[
\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\mu(V_k)r_k^t=\infty,
\]
then $f_{\mu}(\underline{r})\geq t$.
