[Proposition l:covasymstatfindiffsobolev of arXiv:2411.08848, 'Stationary random measures: Covariance asymptotics, variance bounds and central limit theo'] Let ${\mathcal X}$ be a stationary random measure and let ${\mathcal X}_L$ denote the scaled random measure defined by ${\mathcal X}_L(A)={\mathcal X}(LA)$ for $L \geq 1$. Assume that $\int |z^{\gamma}||{\bf K}|(\mathrm{d} z) < \infty$ for $|\gamma|\le 2k+1$. Let $f,g\in L^1\cap H^k$ functions on $\mathbb{R}^d$ for some $k\ge 0$ (with the convention that $H^0=L^2$).  Then,
\begin{enumerate}
\item $L^{-d} \mathrm{Cov}({\mathcal X}_L(f),{\mathcal X}_L(g))  \to Q_0^{{\bf K}}(f,g)$ as $L\to \infty$.

\item If $\lambda_D + I(0) = 0$ and $I(\alpha)=0$ for  $1\le |\alpha|< 2k$, then
$L^{-d+2k} \mathrm{Cov}({\mathcal X}_L(f),{\mathcal X}_L(g)) \to Q_{2k}^{{\bf K}}(f,g)$.

\item If $\lambda_D + I(0)= 0$ and $I(\alpha)=0$ for  $1\le |\alpha|\le 2k$, then $\mathrm{Cov}({\mathcal X}_L(f),{\mathcal X}_L(g))=O(L^{d-2k-1})$  if one of  $f$ or $g$ is in $C_b^{2k+1}$  (functions with bounded, continuous partial derivatives of order $2k+1$).
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition l:covasymstatfindiffsobolev of arXiv:2411.08848

For real Gaussian phase retrieval, rotate the fixed unit signal to e_1, so y_i=a_{i1}^2. The leave-one-out trajectory deletes observation l from the loss while retaining the denominator m and uses an initialization independent of all observations. It is independent of a_l. In a second trajectory replace each first coordinate a_{i1} by xi_i |a_{i1}| with fresh independent Rademacher signs xi_i; retain the other coordinates and labels. This random-sign trajectory is independent of the original first-coordinate signs. A third auxiliary trajectory combines both changes and has both independence properties. Bounds comparing these three trajectories with the original trajectory transfer concentration estimates to the original dependent iterates. The comparison bounds, not exact independence of the original iterates, are the essential step. Sections 4.4–4.6 establish these comparisons in the polylogarithmically oversampled setting of the main theorem.

For a measure space (X, mu) and measurable sets A, B, d_mu(A, B) = mu(A symmetric difference B), possibly infinite. For an increasing sequence E_1 in E_2 in ... with increments D_k = E_{k+1} minus E_k and union E, d_mu(E_m, E_n) = sum_{k=m}^{n-1} mu(D_k) for m <= n and d_mu(E_m, E) = sum_{k >= m} mu(D_k). Hence the following are equivalent: the sequence is d_mu-Cauchy; sum_{k >= m} mu(D_k) < infinity for some m; d_mu(E_m, E) < infinity for some m; d_mu(E_n, E) -> 0. Consecutive distances tending to zero are not enough: under the measure with weight 1/k at the point k, the chain E_n = {1, ..., n} has d(E_n, E_{n+1}) = 1/(n+1) -> 0 but is not Cauchy.

body: Let M be a compact, oriented, boundaryless smooth surface with Gaussian curvature K and area element dA. The Gauss-Bonnet theorem states that the integral over M of K dA equals 2 pi chi(M), where chi(M) is the Euler characteristic of M; for instance a topological sphere always has total curvature 4 pi, whatever its metric. If M has a piecewise-smooth boundary with geodesic curvature k_g and exterior angles theta_i at its corners, the formula generalizes to: integral of K dA over M, plus integral of k_g ds over the boundary, plus the sum of the theta_i, equals 2 pi chi(M). Due to Carl Friedrich Gauss and Pierre Ossian Bonnet.
title: Gauss-Bonnet theorem

[Definition of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] Define $\cC_\star(Q)$ to be the quasi-abelian category over $\mathbf k$ whose objects are given by:
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
    \item for each $i\in Q_0$ a finite-dimensional $\bR/\Gamma$-graded vector space $V_i$ over $\mathbf k$, 
    \item for each $a\in Q_1$ an increasing $\bR$-filtration $\cF^{a^-}$ on $V_{s(a)}$, compatible with the grading,
    \item for each $a\in Q_1$ a decreasing $\bR$-filtration $\cF^{a^+}$ on $V_{t(a)}$, compatible with the grading.
\end{enumerate}
Morphisms are collections of linear maps $V_i\to V_i'$ compatible with the gradings and filtrations.

[Proposition prop:complexZero of arXiv:2608.18320, 'Asymptotics for Beta-Splitting Trees via Homogeneous Fragmentations and Meromorphic Potent'] Let $\beta>0$ be noninteger and let $      \beta=n_\beta+\theta_\beta$ with $       n_\beta=\lfloor\beta\rfloor$.

If $n_\beta$ is even, then $f_\beta$ has exactly $n_\beta$
nonreal zeros, counted with multiplicity. They occur in conjugate pairs.

Suppose that $n_\beta$ is odd. Let $q_\beta$ be the number of zeros
of $f_\beta$ in the upper half-plane, counted with multiplicity, and,
for $0\leq k\leq n_\beta+1$, let $M_k(\beta)$ be the total
multiplicity of the real zeros of $f_\beta$ in $\mathcal I_k$. Then
each $M_k(\beta)$ is odd and
\begin{equation}
        2q_\beta
        +
        \sum_{k=0}^{n_\beta+1}
        \left[M_k(\beta)-1\right]
        =
        n_\beta+1.
\end{equation}
In particular, $f_\beta$ has at most $n_\beta+1$ nonreal zeros,
counted with multiplicity.

Consequently, for every noninteger $\beta>0$, only finitely many zeros
of $f_\beta$ are nonreal or multiple. All the remaining zeros are real
and simple.

[Theorem 1 ($J$-stable criterion, see Theorem 1.1 of Song~\cite{Song}) of arXiv:2608.29736, '2608.29736'] Let $(M^n,\omega)$ be a compact K\"ahler manifold of complex
 dimension $n\geq 2$. Let $\chi$ be another K\"ahler form. Suppose that the pair $(\chi,\omega)$ is $J$-stable, that is,
  $\displaystyle\int_M \left(\chi^n-n\chi^{n-1}\wedge\omega\right)\geq 0,$ and for any $p$-dimensional subvarieties $V\subset M$ with $1\leq p\leq n-1$, \(
    \displaystyle\int_V \left(\chi^p-p\chi^{p-1}\wedge\omega\right)>0.\)
    Then there exists a smooth function $u$ such that  $\chi_u$ is a K\"ahler form and satisfies the cone condition $$\chi_u^{n-1}-(n-1)\chi_u^{n-2}\wedge\omega>0.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: $J$-stable criterion, see Theorem 1.1 of Song~\cite{Song}

[Lem 251 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] If $\bX:\R^{N'}\to\R^N$ is $L$-Lipschitz, and $\bg$ is a standard gaussian in $\R^{N'}$, then $\bX(\bg)-\E[\bX(\bg)]$ is subgaussian with variance proxy $2L^2$.
(As a result, Lemma~\ref{l:sg.norm.bound} applies with $\sigma^2=2L^2$.)

\begin{proof}
Recall from \cite[Thm.~1.3.4]{MR2731561} that if the function $F: \R^N\to\R$ is $L$-Lipschitz, and $\bg$ is a standard gaussian in $\R^N$, then
    \[
    \E \exp\bigg\{
     s\Big( F(\bg)-\E f(\bg)\Big)\bigg\}
    \le \exp(s^2 L^2)
    \]
for all $s\in\R$, i.e., the random variable $F(g)-\E F(g)$ is subgaussian
with variance proxy $2L^2$. As a consequence we have the subgaussian tail bound
    \beq
    \P\bigg(
    \Big|  F(\bg)-\E f(\bg) \Big| \ge t
    \bigg)
    \le 2 \exp\bigg\{ -\frac{t^2}{4L^2}
    \bigg\}
    \eeq
for all $t\ge0$. Now suppose $\bX:\R^{N'}\to\R^N$ is $L$-Lipschitz. If $\theta$ is a unit vector in $\R^N$, then it is easily seen that $\bg\mapsto (\theta,\bX(\bg))$ is $L$-Lipschitz. It follows from \eqref{e:lip.subgaus} that the scalar random variable $(\theta,X(\bg)-\E[X(\bg)])$ is subgaussian with variance proxy $2L^2$, as claimed.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 13 of arXiv:2607.02434, 'A Topological Formula for \\ Potts Lattice Gauge Theory Correlations'] Let $\Lambda\subset \Z^d$ be a box and let $q\in\N+1,\,$$\beta \in [0,\infty),$ and $p = 1-e^{-\beta}.$ Consider the couplings on $C^{i}\paren{\Lambda;\Z\paren{q}}\times \set{0,1}^{X^{\paren{i+1}}}$ by
\[K^{\mathbf{f}}\paren{f,P} \propto \prod_{\sigma \in X^{\paren{i+1}}}\brac{\paren{1-p}I_{\set{\sigma \notin P}} + p I_{\set{\sigma \in P,\delta f\paren{\sigma}=1}}}\]
and
\[K^{\mathbf{w}}\paren{f,P} \propto I_{\delta f\mid_{\partial \Lambda} =1}\prod_{\sigma \in X^{\paren{i+1}}}\brac{\paren{1-p}I_{\set{\sigma \notin P}} + p I_{\set{\sigma \in P,\delta f\paren{\sigma}=1}}}\,.\]

Then for $\#\in\set{\mathbf{f},\mathbf{w}},$ 
\begin{itemize}
    \item The first marginal of $K^{\#}$ is
    $\nu^{\#}_{\Lambda,\beta,q,i}.$ 
    \item The second marginal of $K^{\#}$ is
    $\mu^{\#}_{\Lambda,p,\Z_q,i+1}.$ 
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:topo of arXiv:2604.15146, 'Renormalised two-point functions of CLE$_4$ gaskets'] Let $z_1, \dots, z_n$ be distinct points in $D$. Let $A \subseteq D$ be a closed connected set not containing any of the $z_j$, such that $D \setminus A$ has countably many connected components,  the boundary of each connected component is a Jordan curve, and for every $\varepsilon > 0$ only finitely many of these curves have diameter more than 
$\varepsilon$. 

Let $\widehat A$ be the set obtained as follows: we take the connected components $O_j$ of $z_j$ in $D \setminus A$, the connected component $O_0$ whose boundary is $\partial D$ and set 
$\widehat A := \overline{D \setminus \bigcup_{j=0}^n O_j}$.

Then there exists a closed path $\gamma \subseteq A$ with $\sum_{j=1}^{n}
\indx_{\gamma}(z_j) \text{ odd}$ if and only if there exists a closed path $\widehat \gamma \subseteq \widehat A$ with $\sum_{j=1}^{n}
\indx_{\widehat \gamma}(z_j) \text{ odd}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:topo of arXiv:2604.15146

[Theorem 6 (Output-space deletion bound) of arXiv:2608.30261, 'Estimating Population-Risk Curves Along Nonconvex Gradient Flows from the Training Sample'] Fix a realized sample, $\cH\subset[0,T]\times\Lambda$, and a nonempty set of
evaluation inputs $\varnothing\ne\mathcal X_{\rm ev}\subseteq\mathcal X$.
Suppose the identities in \cref{thm:kernel-mismatch} hold for every
$i\in[n]$, $(t,\lambda)\in\cH$, and $x\in\mathcal X_{\rm ev}$.
Suppose there are finite nonnegative constants $A_{\rm tr}$ and
$D_{\rm dyn}$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{\substack{1\leq i\leq n,\ (t,\lambda)\in\cH\\0\leq s\leq t}}
 \operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{z\in\mathsf Z}^{|h_i|}
 \|a_s^\lambda(z)\|\leq A_{\rm tr},
 \qquad
 \|\mathcal K^{\rm ch,\lambda}-\mathcal K^{\rm res,\lambda}\|
       _{\infty,\op;\mathcal X_{\rm ev},\mathbf h}\leq D_{\rm dyn}.
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{\substack{1\leq i\leq n,\ (t,\lambda)\in\cH\\x\in\mathcal X_{\rm ev}}}
 \|f_{\theta_{-i,t}^\lambda}(x)
     -f_{\theta_t^\lambda+d_{i,t}^\lambda}(x)\|
 \leq\frac{2T}{n}A_{\rm tr}D_{\rm dyn}.
\end{equation}
If $x_i\in\mathcal X_{\rm ev}$ for every $i\in[n]$ and
$\varphi(\cdot,y_i)$ is continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of the
line segment joining $f_{\theta_t^\lambda+d_{i,t}^\lambda}(x_i)$ and
$f_{\theta_{-i,t}^\lambda}(x_i)$ for every $i$ and $(t,\lambda)\in\cH$, define
\[
 \bar a_{i,t}^{\rm out,\lambda}
 =\int_0^1\nabla_f\varphi\!\left(
 f_{\theta_t^\lambda+d_{i,t}^\lambda}(x_i)
 +u\{f_{\theta_{-i,t}^\lambda}(x_i)
      -f_{\theta_t^\lambda+d_{i,t}^\lambda}(x_i)\},y_i
 \right)\,\dd u.
\]
If, for a finite $A_{\rm ev}\geq0$,
$\|\bar a_{i,t}^{\rm out,\lambda}\|\leq A_{\rm ev}$ uniformly over
$1\leq i\leq n$ and $(t,\lambda)\in\cH$, then
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{(t,\lambda)\in\cH}
 |\Score_n^{\LOO}(t,\lambda)-\widetilde\Score_n(t,\lambda)|
 \leq\frac{2T}{n}A_{\rm ev}A_{\rm tr}D_{\rm dyn}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.26692, 'Many Facets in Random Polytopes from Product and Log-Concave Measures'] There exists
\[
 0<\eta<\min\{1,x^*/4\}
\]
with the following property.  For every fixed $0<a<b<r^*$ there are constants
$c,C>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$ and every
$x\in[-\eta,\eta]^n$ satisfying
\[
 an\leq\Lambda_{\mu_n}^*(x)\leq bn,
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
 q_n(x)\geq c\frac{e^{-\Lambda_{\mu_n}^*(x)}}{\sqrt n}.
\end{equation}
Moreover, if
\[
 H_x^+=\{y:\ip{\nabla\Lambda_{\mu_n}^*(x)}{y-x}\geq0\},
\]
then
\begin{equation}
 \mu_n(H_x^+)\leq C\frac{e^{-\Lambda_{\mu_n}^*(x)}}{\sqrt n}.
\end{equation}

On Z^4 let p_n be the full-space discrete-time nearest-neighbor SRW kernel, g_T(x)=sum_{n=0}^T p_n(x), sigma_T^2=sum_x g_T(x)^2, and let xi_z be independent standard Gaussians. Define Y_T(x)=sum_z g_T(x-z)xi_z/sigma_T and H_T(x)=1{Y_T(x)>=sqrt(2 log T)}, h_T=E H_T(0). For every fixed a>0, with graph radius R_T=floor(a h_T^(-1/4)), liminf_{T->infinity} log[sum_{0<|x|<=R_T} E(H_T(0)H_T(x))/h_T]/log T >= 2/3. Thus this comparison field violates bounded Palm clustering at mean spacing. It is not a parking process and has no active-particle field. Novelty: UNCHECKED exact comparison statement; KNOWN Gaussian tail method. Status: independently checked proof.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:50be63e3013cb3562a8ba8fd7e9e7888f0410e491ed6b9d4e15fc85d4f2b3816","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/50/50be63e3013cb3562a8ba8fd7e9e7888f0410e491ed6b9d4e15fc85d4f2b3816.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:a31d174696b39217c23e18b76d86886c8a46b0b980c4086414d1bd398b3b5ce2","bundle_entry_key":"i0005-c11","bundle_id":"population.i0005-palm-reductions-and-comparisons-004","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"interacting particle systems and comparison fields","draft":"w661/bundle_004.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.particle-hole:four-dimensional-logarithmic-gaussian-hole-clustering-benchmark-draft","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# I0005-C11 v2: a logarithmic Gaussian comparison fails bounded Palm clustering

Status: proof (unaudited). Novelty: UNCHECKED exact comparison statement;
KNOWN Gaussian density method and SRW kernel estimates. This is not a
claim about the actual parking field.

Let p_n be the full-space, discrete-time, uniform nearest-neighbor SRW
kernel on Z^4. For integer T>=2 put g_T(x)=sum_{n=0}^T p_n(x). Let
(xi_z) be independent standard real Gaussian variables, and define

    Y_T(x) = sum_z g_T(x-z) xi_z / sigma_T,
    sigma_T^2 = sum_z g_T(z)^2.

The sums are finite. Each Y_T(x) is standard normal, and the field is
stationary. Define H_T(x)=1{Y_T(x)>=sqrt(2 log T)}, h_T=E H_T(0), and
R_T=floor(a h_T^(-1/4)) for a fixed a>0. Then

    liminf_{T->infinity} log[ sum_{0<|x|_1<=R_T}
                  E(H_T(0)H_T(x))/h_T ] / log T >= 2/3.

In particular this field violates C9's bounded Palm clustering hypothesis
for every a>0. There is no active-particle field or parking dynamics in
this construction; it does not refute any claim concerning that dynamics.

## Covariance and the graph-ball scale

By symmetry and the semigroup property,

    C_T(x):=sum_z g_T(z)g_T(z-x)
           =sum_{n=0}^{2T} w_{T,n} p_n(x),

where w_{T,n}=n+1 for n<=T and w_{T,n}=2T-n+1 for T<n<=2T.
The uniform heat-kernel bound p_n(x)<=C n^(-2) shows that the tail
T<n<=2T contributes O(1), uniformly in x. The first part is exactly
the kernel of I0005-C1 v1. Consequently, with c=4/pi^2,

    C_T(x)=c log_+(T/(1+|x|_2^2))+O(1),
    sigma_T^2=c log T+O(1).

All constants are independent of x and T. The positive covariance kernel
here is the convolution square of g_T; no assertion of positive
definiteness for an arbitrary truncated semigroup polynomial is needed.

Mills' estimate follows directly by integrating the normal density: for
v>0, phi(v) v/(v^2+1)<=P(Z>=v)<=phi(v)/v. Thus

    h_T=(1+o(1))/(2 sqrt(pi log T) T).

It follows that R_T=T^(1/4+o(1)). In the annulus
R_T/2<=|x|_1<=R_T, norm equivalence gives |x|_2=T^(1/4+o(1)), uniformly.
Therefore

    rho_T(x):=E[Y_T(0)Y_T(x)]=1/2+o(1)

uniformly on this annulus. In particular rho lies in [1/3,2/3] eventually.

## Uniform bivariate tail estimate

Let (Z,W) be standard jointly Gaussian with correlation rho in [1/3,2/3]
and put v=sqrt(2 log T). The implication Z,W>=v => Z+W>=2v and the
Gaussian exponential-moment bound give

    P(Z,W>=v)<=exp(-v^2/(1+rho)).

For a matching logarithmic lower bound, integrate the joint density over
[v,v+1/v]^2. Its area is 1/v^2. On that rectangle the density exponent is

    (z^2-2rho zw+w^2)/(2(1-rho^2))
                  <=v^2/(1+rho)+C,

with one uniform C because rho stays in the stated compact interval.
The density prefactor is uniformly bounded below by a positive constant.
Hence

    P(Z,W>=v)>=c v^(-2) exp(-v^2/(1+rho)).

For rho_T(x)=1/2+o(1), these bounds imply

    E[H_T(0)H_T(x)]=T^(-4/3+o(1))

uniformly throughout the annulus.

## Palm summation

The number of annulus sites is a positive constant times R_T^4,
up to a lower-order boundary error, hence T^(1+o(1)). Also
h_T^(-1)=T^(1+o(1)). Keeping only this annulus in the nonnegative sum
gives

    sum_{0<|x|_1<=R_T} E[H_T(0)H_T(x)]/h_T
                    >=T^(1+1-4/3+o(1))=T^(2/3+o(1)).

This proves the claimed liminf and divergence.

## What the comparison excludes

The full-space G*G obstruction in the parking source resembles the
logarithmic covariance used here. By contrast the interlacement benchmark
C10 uses a single Green function and has bounded Palm counts. Neither
comparison identifies the actual parking field. They show that decay of
the one-hole intensity and a reference to random-walk Green functions do
not, by themselves, imply C9's Palm bound. The stopping dynamics must be
used in any valid transfer theorem.

Sources: I0005-C1 v1 (exact periodic SRW asymptotic, both auditors PASS);
I0005-C1 periodic local-CLT expansion also supplies the uniform heat-kernel bound.
Lawler--Limic Theorem 2.1.1 alone is not invoked, because its stated
aperiodicity hypothesis excludes this SRW. The elementary
Gaussian tail arguments are written above rather than assumed from an

body:
[Proposition prop:tailrl-closed-form-weights of arXiv:2609.02987, 'Tail Likelihood Reinforcement Learning'] For every $i=1,\ldots,N$,
\begin{equation}
\omega\bigl(r_{(i)}\bigr)
=
\sum_{k=1}^{i}
\frac{r_{(k)}-r_{(k-1)}}{N-k+1}.

\end{equation}
Equivalently, all weights follow the recurrence
\begin{equation}
\omega\bigl(r_{(i)}\bigr)
=
\omega\bigl(r_{(i-1)}\bigr)
+
\frac{r_{(i)}-r_{(i-1)}}{N-i+1},
\qquad
\omega\bigl(r_{(0)}\bigr)=0.

\end{equation}
title: Closed-form empirical weights

For a d-regular Cayley graph, if rho is the normalized simple-random-walk spectral radius, the Benjamini-Schramm sufficient criterion is d*rho*p_c<1. The earlier C0047 attempt's p_c<1/rho drops d; when 0<rho<1 this inequality is automatic because p_c<=1<1/rho, so it cannot certify p_c<p_u. The corrected criterion is only sufficient: on the four-regular tree p_c=1/3, rho=sqrt(3)/2 and d*rho*p_c=2sqrt(3)/3>1 although p_u=1.

Thus Uprime=-grad F(UU^T)U is exactly the asymmetric gradient flow Bprime=-GA^T, Aprime=-B^T G; the Gram matrix solves Zprime=-Z grad F(Z)-grad F(Z)Z. No whitening, data commutation, or initial balance is required. With a simple positive top residual singular value s, the conditional Gram escape theorem uses rate 2s and requires (v^T Zalpha v)/||Zalpha-Zbar||_F to have a strictly positive liminf; nonzero projection alone is insufficient. Section 3 of arXiv:2012.09839, PDF p.3 explicitly gives the square asymmetric-to-symmetric reduction; these formulas spell out arbitrary rectangular block sizes and the exact gradient-flow normalization. Applying Theorem G.2 requires all its hypotheses; for quadratic regression its all-real-time convention requires a local complete extension, since quadratic flow need not be backward complete. This is an existing reduction and conditional local theorem, not an unconditional Gaussian second-step result.
Compatible factor dimensions and differentiable convex loss C
Conditional escape application additionally requires the full hypotheses of Theorem G.2
title: Li-Luo-Lyu asymmetric matrix factorization: symmetric PSD block lift

[Cor 190 (quenched first moment bounds on $Q^\sigma$ and $Q^{\sigma,\frozen}$) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For $Q$ as in Definition~\ref{d:Q}, we have
	$\bE[\Delta Q^\RomI(q_d)]
	\le L^{O(1)}(\MAX_N)^2\delta^2$
with $\MAX_N$ as in Proposition~\ref{p:Y.kolmogorov}. We also have
	\[
	\sum_{\sigma\in\{\RomII,\RomIII,\Ising\}}
	\bE\Delta Q^\sigma(q_d)
	\le L^{O(1)}\bigg\{
	(\MAX_N)^2
	+ \frac{(\SMAX_N)^2 \BUCKETS}{N}
	\bigg\} \delta
	\]
with $\SMAX_N$ as in Proposition~\ref{p:drift.quenched}. The same bound holds for the $Q^{\frozen,\sigma}$ processes.
	
\begin{proof}
Recall that $Q^\sigma=E^\sigma+\tilde{Q}^\sigma$. It follows from Lemma~\ref{l:qv.simplification} that
	\[
	\Big|\Delta E^\sigma(q_d)\Big| 
	\le O\bigg(
	\eta^2
	+\eta\Big(\Delta\tilde{Q}^\sigma(q_d)\Big)^{1/2}
	+\Big( \Delta \bar{D}^\sigma(q_d)\Big)^2\bigg)\,.
	\]
For $\sigma=\RomI$, it follows by combining Lemma~\ref{l:barD.I.second.quenched} with Lemma~\ref{l:tQ.first.quenched} that
	\[
	\bE\Delta Q^\RomI(q_d)
	\le \bE\Delta \tilde{Q}^\RomI(q_d)
		+\bE\Big|\Delta E^\RomI(q_d)\Big|
	\le
	L^{O(1)} \bigg\{
	\eta^2 + (\MAX_N)^2\delta^2 \bigg\}\,.
	\]
For $\sigma\in\{\RomII,\RomIII,\Ising\}$,
it follows by combining Lemmas~\ref{l:barD.II.second.quenched}--\ref{l:barD.Ising.second.quenched} with Lemma~\ref{l:tQ.first.quenched} that
	\[
	\bE\Delta Q^\sigma(q_d)
	\le\bE\Delta \tilde{Q}^\sigma(q_d)+ \bE\Big|\Delta E^\sigma(q_d)\Big| 
	\le L^{O(1)}\bigg\{
	\eta^2
	+(\MAX_N)^2\delta
	+ \frac{(\SMAX_N)^2 \BUCKETS\delta}{N}
	\bigg\}\,.\]
This proves the claim for the $Q^\sigma$ processes,
using that $\MAX_N\ge1$ and $\eta\ll\delta$. The analogous bound for the $Q^{\frozen,\sigma}$ processes follows by the same argument.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: quenched first moment bounds on $Q^\sigma$ and $Q^{\sigma,\frozen}$

[Lemma 14 of arXiv:2607.04193, 'Onsager--Machlup Functionals for Generalized Newtonian Equations of Motion with Time-Varyi'] Let $\frac14<H<\frac12$ and set $\alpha=\frac12-H\in(0,\frac14)$. Let
$f\in C^{1+\beta}_0([0,1];\mathbb R^d)$ with
\[

\[

\]

\begin{equation}
    \left\|
        s^{-2\alpha}I_{0^+}^{\alpha}(s^\alpha f_s)
    \right\|_{C^1([0,1];\mathbb R^d)}
    \le C\|f\|_{1+\beta}.
\end{equation}

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2511.14740, 'Marking and re-marking'] Let $X$ be a random variable taking values in $\mathbb N$, $\mathbf a \in [0,1]^c$ with $|\mathbf a| \leq 1$, and let $\mathbf Y = \mathbf a \circ X$ be the multinomial marking of $X$ with parameters $\mathbf a$. Then we have the following.
\begin{enumerate}

\item $\mathbb EY_i = a_i \, \mathbb EX$.
\item $\Disp(Y_i) = a_i^2 \Disp(X)$.
\item $\Cov(Y_i, Y_j) = a_i a_j \Disp(X)$ for $i \neq j$.
\item ${\displaystyle \operatorname{\mathbb E} \mathbf Y^{\ff{\mathbf k}} = \left(\prod_{i=1}^d a_i^{k_i}\!\right) \operatorname{\mathbb E} X^{\ff{| \mathbf k|}}}$.
\item $\Phi_{\mathbf Y}(\mathbf t) = \Phi_X\big(\mathbf a ^\top \mathbf t\big)$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 2 of arXiv:2511.14740

\[

=
p_{n}^{[\kappa]}\boxast_n^{(\kappa)} \left( p_{n}^{[\kappa-1]}\boxast_n^{(\kappa-1)}\left(\cdots p_n^{[2]}\boxast_n^{(2)}\left( p_{n}^{[1]}\boxast_n^{(1)} p_n^{[0]}\right)\cdots \right)\right),
\]
where \(p_m^{[i]}\in \pols_m(\R_{\geq 0})\) for \(i=0,\ldots,\kappa\) and for $m\in\N$, 
\[
\boxast_m^{(i)} =
\begin{cases}
  \boxtimes_m,       & \text{if } i \in\mathcal{I}, \\
  \boxplus_m,      & \text{if } i \notin \mathcal{I}.
\end{cases}
\]
Assume that
\[
\meas{p_n^{[i]}}\weak \mu_i, \qquad i=0,\ldots,\kappa,
\]
for some \(\mu_i\in \MM(\R_{\geq 0})\). Then
\[
\meas{q_n}\weak \mu_\kappa\boxast^{(\kappa)} \left( \mu_{\kappa-1}\boxast^{(\kappa-1)}\left(\cdots \mu_2 \boxast^{(2)}\left( \mu_1\boxast^{(1)} \mu_0\right)\cdots \right)\right),
\]
where
\[
\boxast^{(i)} =
\begin{cases}
  \boxtimes,       & \text{if } i \in\mathcal{I}, \\
  \boxplus,      & \text{if } i \notin \mathcal{I}.
\end{cases}
\]

gradient-slice defects in (equation eq:Gamma-plus of the paper)--(equation eq:Gamma-minus of the paper)
and the near-zero resolvent defect \(\Sigma_{L,0}\).  Prove also the two
nonbulk branch bounds in (equation eq:exact-three-branch-formula of the paper); under
(equation eq:sparse-rate-compatible of the paper), only the mixed-profile bound remains.
By
(thm:conditional-transfer,prop:primitive-dereg,prop:bulk-sparse-reduction of the paper),
these estimates would establish exact universality.  No remote
spectral-tail estimate is needed.  The counterexample shows that finite
moment matching, even through order \(2p\), cannot replace spatial
branch control.
(thm:bounded-block-counterexample of the paper) further shows that a deterministic
entry bound or a fixed \(N^{1/2-\varepsilon}\) cutoff with
\(0\le\varepsilon<1/2\) cannot replace control of collective coherent
deviations. (Stated as a problem by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)

body: In mathematics, the axiom of choice, abbreviated AC or AoC, is an axiom of set theory. Informally put, the axiom of choice says that given any collection of non-empty sets, one can identify another set containing one element chosen from each set, even if the collection is infinite. Formally, the axiom establishes existence rather than a construction; it states that for every set and every -indexed family of nonempty sets, there exists an -indexed set of elements of such that for every . The axiom of choice was formulated in 1904 by Ernst Zermelo in order to formalize his proof of the well-ordering theorem.

Ren-Nichani-Wu-Lee population MSE identity. Let X~N(0,I_d), let v_star,1,...,v_star,P be orthonormal, and let a_p>=0 with sum_p a_p^2=1. Let sigma be a real even link with sigma=sum_{i>=I} c_2i h_2i in L2(N(0,1)), I>=1, and sum_i c_2i^2=1, in the normalized probabilists Hermite basis. Let all student vectors v_k be nonzero and finite in number, and set f_v(x)=sum_k b_k sigma(u_k dot x), u_k=v_k/||v_k||_2, b_k=||v_k||_2^2, and f_star(x)=sum_p a_p sigma(v_star,p dot x). Define C(r)=sum_{i>=I} c_2i^2*r^(2i), -1<=r<=1. Then L=(1/2)E[(f_star(X)-f_v(X))^2]=(1/2)sum_p a_p^2-sum_{p,k}a_p*b_k*C(v_star,p dot u_k)+(1/2)sum_{k,l}b_k*b_l*C(u_k dot u_l). Equivalently, L=(1/2)sum_{i>=I}c_2i^2*||sum_p a_p*v_star,p^(tensor 2i)-sum_k b_k*u_k^(tensor 2i)||_F^2. Both series are finite-valued and converge absolutely. This deterministic identity is the source equation4; it needs no SGD convergence, sample independence across training steps, or neuron-initialization assumption. It is valid under the weaker link hypotheses displayed here, in particular without the differentiability assumptions needed to run SGD.
Finite orthonormal teacher family and finitely many nonzero student vectors.

body: [Proposition 16 of arXiv:2506.15736, 'Coming down from infinity for coordinated particle systems'] Let $D(dz)$ be an arbitrary measure that controls death with no atom at $1$. If a migration measure $M(dz)$ or reproduction measure $R_{uv}(dz)$ is $\Lambda$-strong then an infinite number of particles migrate or reproduce out of a site with coalescence according to $\Lambda(dz)$ and death according to $D(dz)$ before time $t$ for all $t > 0$.

body:
[Prob 112 of arXiv:2507.08909, 'Annealed almost periodic entropy'] When $\phi$ is unital, Theorem~\ref{thm:pre-LDP} says that the value $E_n$ gives the rate function in the large deviations principle obeyed by the random element
\[(\Phi^\pi_V)[B_n] \in \S^\rm{u}_k(B_n).\]
The values $E_n'$ should have an analogous interpretation, but this time for the random $S$-tuples
\begin{equation}
\big((\Phi^\pi_V)[B_n\cup sB_n]:\ s \in S\big)
\end{equation}
taking values in the space
\[\Big\{(Q_s:\ s \in S) \in \prod_{s \in S}\S^\rm{u}_k(B_n\cup sB_n):\ (Q_s)[B_n]\ \hbox{is the same for all $s$}\Big\}.\]
If this is true, then both inequalities in Lemma~\ref{lem:1-2-ineqs} become instances of the contraction principle.

I believe one can prove this along the same lines as Theorem~\ref{thm:pre-LDP} without any really new ideas, but working with the the tuples in~\eqref{eq:tuple-of-Phis} is sure to be more complicated than working with $(\Phi^\pi_V)[B_n$ alone. (Stated as a problem by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Problem 112 of arXiv:2507.08909

[Defn of arXiv:2603.17858, 'Decay of correlations and zeros for the hard-core model'] A family of holomorphic functions $\mathcal{F}$ is normal at $\lambda\in\mathbb{C}$,

    sequence $(g_{n})_{n}$ in $\mathcal{F}$ there exists a subsequence
    $(g_{n_{k}})_{k}$ that converges uniformly on $U$ to a holomorphic
    map $g:U\to\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$.

[Lemma 13 (Uniform boundary decay) of arXiv:2608.30211, '2608.30211'] Let $G_j$ be domains whose boundaries in $B_{2r}(p_j)$ are given by
uniformly $C^{1,1}$ graphs, and let
$h_j\in L^\infty(G_j\cap B_{2r}(p_j))$.  Suppose that
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 w_j\in H^1(G_j\cap B_{2r}(p_j))
 \cap C(\overline{G_j\cap B_{2r}(p_j)}),\\
 -\Delta w_j=h_j\quad\hbox{in }G_j\cap B_{2r}(p_j),\\
 \|w_j\|_\infty\leq M,\qquad \|h_j\|_\infty\leq M_1.
 \end{gathered}
\]
There are $\eta\in(0,1)$ and $C>0$, depending only on the dimension and
the uniform graph bounds, such that, for $0<\delta<r/8$,
\begin{align}
 \sup_{\substack{x\in G_j\cap B_{r/2}(p_j)\\
                  \dist(x,\partial G_j)\leq\delta}}
 |w_j(x)|
 &\leq \sup_{\partial G_j\cap B_r(p_j)}|w_j|
 \notag\\
 &\quad+C(M+M_1r^2)\left(\frac{\delta}{r}\right)^\eta .
 
\end{align}
The constants are uniform over the family $G_j$.

body: The Fourier entropy-influence conjecture is equivalent to its restriction to Boolean functions all of whose influences are below any fixed tau: a coordinate of influence at least tau has restriction drop Delta_i <= (2/ln 2 + log2(e/tau)) Inf_i, so a violation localizes to a subcube on which every influence is small and the restriction step fails at every coordinate. On self-compositions of Numaro's record function the restriction-step constant rho_0 = min_i Delta_i/Inf_i is 6.3290, 6.8901 and 7.0519 at 324, 5832 and 104976 variables (limit about 7.1116), so no potential-free coordinate induction can give a constant below 7.05. The XOR gate inequality is certified, so read-once formulas over AND, OR, XOR and NOT satisfy H <= 6.4573 I; a prime monotone 7-input gate breaks the read-once potential behind that bound; the five prime 3-input classes (one-hot, MAJ3, EQ3, MUX, Q3) are proved, while fan-in 3 at 6.4573 in general is numerical only. Per-coordinate erasure bounds fail even for monotone functions (majority with one flipped point gives ratio at least (n - 3 log2 n)/2). The full conjecture remains open.

[Definition 6 of arXiv:2608.05931, 'Effective Lagrangian regularity and the uniqueness threshold for random H\"older velocity '] Let $U : \T^d \to \R^d$ with $U \in C^0(\T^d)$ and $y \in \T^d$. Define
    \[R_t(y) := \sup_{X^1,\ X^2 \text{ solutions to~\eqref{eq:main ODE autonomous data}}}  d_{\T^d}(X^1_t, X^2_t).\]
    If, for some $t_0 >0,$ $R_t(y) = 0$ for all $t \in [0,t_0]$, then we say that $U$ is \textit{effectively regular at $y$}.
    Otherwise, we define
    \[E(y) := 1-\limsup_{t \to 0^+} \frac{\log t}{\log R_t(y)}.\]
    We then say that $U$ has \textit{effective Lagrangian regularity} $E(y)$ at $y$.

Put g=-A/(chi^2 xi^3). For any nonempty finite block B, let M=|B|, S=sum_{x in B}sigma_x, V=E S^2>0 and R=3-E S^4/V^2. Then -g>=R V^2/(M chi^2 xi^3). Thus along beta_n increasing to beta_c, bounds R_n>=r>0 and V_n/[chi_n sqrt(M_n xi_n^3)]>=b>0 imply -g(beta_n)>=r b^2>0. These near-critical premises have not been proved for C0052.

[Lem 38 of arXiv:2609.03821, 'Condensation and Metastability in the Supercritical Two-Species Zero-Range Process via Res'] Fix positive real numbers $x_{1},y_{1},\dots,x_{k},y_{k}>0$.
Then for any integers $N,n,p_{1},\dots,p_{k}\ge0$ such that $p_{1}+\cdots+p_{k}=N$
and $0\le n\le N$,
\[
\frac{1}{\binom{N}{n}}\sum_{\substack{q_{1},\dots,q_{k}\ge0:\\
q_{1}+\cdots+q_{k}=n
}
}\prod^{k}_{j=1}\left[{p_{j} \choose q_{j}}x^{q_{j}}_{j}y^{p_{j}-q_{j}}_{j}\right]\le c\prod^{k}_{j=1}\left(\frac{nx_{j}+(N-n)y_{j}}{N}\right)^{p_{j}},
\]
where $c>0$ depends only on the fixed constants $x_{1},y_{1},\dots,x_{k},y_{k}$.

body:
[Definition 7 of arXiv:2606.31287, '\bf Heat kernel lower bound estimates for symmetric pure jump processes via averaged jump '] \begin{enumerate}
\item[\rm (i)]  We say that ${\rm J}_{\phi, \leq}$ holds if there is some constant $c_{\ref{e:1.2}} > 0$ so that 
\be 
  J(x, y) \le \frac{c_{\ref{e:1.2}}}{V(x,d(x, y)) \phi (d(x, y))}
\ee 
for any $x, y \in \sX$.
 

 \item[\rm (ii)]\,\,Let $D$ be an open subset of $\sX$. Define
\[
\sF_D := \{ u : u \in \sF, u = 0 \,\,\text{for $\sE$-quasi everywhere on $D^c$}\}
\]
and
\[
\lambda_1(D) = \inf \left\{ \sE(f,f):  \,  f \in \sF_D \hbox{ with }  \|f\|_2 =1 \right\},
\]
where $\| u\|_2$ is the $L^2$-norm of $u \in L^2(K, \mu)$. Note that $\lambda_1(D)$ is the bottom of the Dirichlet spectrum for the generator of the subprocess $X^D$ of $X$ killed upon leaving $D$.

\item[\rm (iii)]\,\,
 We say that an MMD space $(\sX,d,m,\sE, \sF)$  satisfies the {\em Faber-Krahn
inequality} ${\rm FK}(\phi)$, if there exist constants $c_{\ref{e:fki}} > 0$, $\sigma_{\ref{e:fki}} \in (0, 1/2)$ and
$\theta > 0$ such that for any $r \in (0, {\sigma_{\ref{e:fki}}}\,\diam{\sX})$, any ball $B(x, r)$ and any open set $D \subseteq B(x, r)$, 
\be 
 \lambda_1(D) \ge \frac{c_{\ref{e:fki}}}{\phi(r)} \Big(\frac{V(x,r)}{m(D)}\Big)^{\theta}.
\ee

 \item[\rm (iv)]\,\, Let $\sF_b = \sF\cap L^\infty(\sX, m)$. We say that an MMD space $(\sX,d,m,\sE, \sF)$   satisfies the 
 {\em weak Poincar\'e inequality}
(${\rm PI} (\phi)$)
  if there exist constants $c_{\ref{eq:PIn}} > 0 $, $\sigma_{\ref{eq:PIn}} \in (0, 1/2)$ and $\delta \ge 1$ such that
for any $r \in (0, \sigma_{\ref{eq:PIn}}\,\diam{\sX})$, any $x \in \sX$ and $f \in \sF_b$,
\begin{equation}
\int_{B_r} (f(x) - \bar{f}_{B_r})^2m(dx) \le c_{\ref{eq:PIn}}\phi(r)\int_{{B_{\delta r}}\times {B_{\delta r}}} (f(y)-f(x))^2\,J(dx,dy),
\end{equation}
 where $B_r = B(x, r)$ and $\bar{f}_{B_r}= \frac{1}{m({B_r})}\int_{B_r} f(x)m(dx)$ is the average value of $f$ on $B_r$.
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem thm:monoStartTree of arXiv:2607.29409, 'The Zombie Infection Model'] Let $G=(V,E)$ be a tree and $\lambda \in (0,\infty)$.
		Then, if $\Delta_{1} \subseteq \Lambda \subseteq \Delta_{2} \Subset V$ with $\Lambda$
		connected, there is a coupling $\widehat{\BP}$ of
		$\big(\eta_{t}^{(1)}\big)\sim\BP^{\ZIM}_{\lambda,G,\Delta_1}$ and
		$\big(\eta_{t}^{(2)}\big)\sim\BP^{\ZIM}_{\lambda,G,\Delta_2}$ such that
		\begin{equation}
			\widehat{\BP}\!\left( \eta_{t}^{(1)}\leq \eta_{t}^{(2)}\: \forall \: t\in [0,
			\infty) \right) =1.
		\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Monotonicity in starting configuration on trees

body: [Proposition 12 (Bernoulli--Laplace Continuity) of arXiv:2605.19084, 'Limit Profiles for Separation Distance'] Let $\Omega_n:=\{0,1,\ldots,n/2\}$, and let $P_n$ be the Bernoulli--Laplace diffusion model on $\Omega_n$, where the state records the number of red balls in the left urn. If, along a subsequence, $s_{n,n/2}(\frac{n}{4}(\ln n+c))$ converges pointwise for every $c\in\mathbb R$ to a profile $\Phi(c)$, then $\Phi$ is continuous. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Bernoulli--Laplace Continuity

[Proposition prop:basic of arXiv:2411.08295, 'Improving the convergence of Markov chains via permutations and projections'] Let $P \in \mathcal{S}(\pi)$ and $Q \in \mathcal{I}(\pi) \cap \mathcal{L}$ be an isometric involution transition matrix. For $L \in \mathcal{L}(\pi,Q)$, we then have
	\begin{align}
		{}^Q D_{KL}(P \| L) &= {}^Q D_{KL}(P \| \overline{P}) + {}^Q D_{KL}(\overline{P} \| L), \\
		D_{KL}^Q(P \| L) &= D_{KL}^Q(P \| \overline{P}) +  D_{KL}^Q(\overline{P} \| L). 
	\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:basic of arXiv:2411.08295

[Lem 31 (Well-posedness of the controlled stochastic equation) of arXiv:2607.28238, 'Well-posedness and large deviations for the obstacle problem of first-order stochastic con'] Assume \textbf{Hypotheses (H1) and (H2)$'$}. 
For every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ and $h^\varepsilon\in\mathcal A_M$, \eqref{rs-1} admits a unique kinetic solution $(\bar u^\varepsilon,\bar\nu^\varepsilon)$, with an associated
kinetic measure $\bar q^\varepsilon$. 
Moreover, for every $p\geq2$,
\begin{align}
\sup_{0<\varepsilon<1}\mathbb E\bigg[&\underset{0\leq t\leq T}{\operatorname{ess\,sup}}\|\bar u^\varepsilon(t)\|_{L^p(\mathbb T^N)}^p+\bar\nu^\varepsilon(\mathbb T^N\times[0,T))\notag\\
&\quad+\int_{\mathbb T^N\times[0,T]\times\mathbb R}(1+|\xi|^p)\,\dd\bar q^\varepsilon(x,t,\xi)\bigg]\leq C_{p,M},
\end{align}
where $C_{p,M}$ depends only on $p$, $M$, $T$, $D_0$, the initial datum, and the obstacle, and is independent of $\varepsilon$ and of the chosen family
$(h^\varepsilon)_{\varepsilon\in(0,1)}\subset\mathcal A_M$.

[Lemma lem:four-point-prime-energy-stability of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] The four-point seed is a shift-stable $3$-chart of depth $\gamma_0h$.
For every fixed $t\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}$ and every fixed system of prime
windows satisfying (equation eq:prime-window-constants of the paper),
the suspended four-point chart satisfies, uniformly in the prime tuple,
\begin{equation}
 N_h\gg_t h^4,
 \qquad
 E_h\leq h^5\exp\!\left(O_t\!\left(
  \frac{\log h}{\log\log h}\right)\right).
\end{equation}
In particular it is prime-energy stable with exponents $(a,\mu)=(4,5)$.

set $t\coloneqq k/r_{\star}$. For $\delta\ge\delta_{\mathrm{sharp}}(t)+1/r_{\star}$, choose
\[
q\coloneqq\left\lfloor \mathsf{C}(t)r_{\star}\right\rfloor ,\;\alpha\coloneqq\frac{1}{\mathsf{C}(t)}\sqrt{\frac{\delta_{\mathrm{sharp}}(t)}{\delta-\varepsilon}},\;\varepsilon\coloneqq\mathsf{C}(t)-\frac{\left\lfloor \mathsf{C}(t)r_{\star}\right\rfloor }{r_{\star}},
\]
where $\mathsf{C}(t)$ is defined in ((eq:Cdef of the paper)). Then, $0<\alpha<r_{\star}/q$
holds, and the map $\mathcal{A}$ in ((eq:Adef of the paper)) satisfies $\mathcal{A}\in\operatorname{RIP}(\delta,k)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma lem:invariant-selected-column of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Let $V$ be a real orthogonal space of dimension $d$, with
\[
 \Omega_V=d^{-1/2}\sum_{\mu=1}^d e_\mu\otimes e_\mu.
\]
Let $R_i:L\to M_i$ and orthogonal projections $P_{i,m}$ satisfy
\[
 \sum_iR_i^*R_i\preceq I_L,
 \qquad [P_{i,m},R_i^*R_i]=0.
\tag{3.3.1w$_{12p_7}$}
\]
Let $T:V\to L\otimes E$ be fixed, let $S_{i,\theta}$ be contractions
on the passive factors, and let $\rho_i(\theta)$ be orthogonal on $V$.
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_i\int
 \|(R_iP_{i,m}\otimes S_{i,\theta})
       (T\rho_i(\theta)\otimes I)\Omega_V\|^2
 \frac{d\theta}{2\pi}
 \le \frac1d\|T\|_2^2
 \le\|T\|_{\rm op}^2.}
\tag{3.3.1w$_{12p_8}$}
\]
The same assertion holds if an own-circle output rotation is placed
between $T$ and $R_iP_{i,m}$, provided the latter intertwines that
rotation.  It is stable under passive Hilbert amplification, adjunction,
full transpose, and orthogonal rail permutation.

body: In number theory, Ostrowski's theorem, due to Alexander Ostrowski (1916), states that every non-trivial absolute value on the rational numbers $\mathbb {Q}$ is equivalent to either the usual real absolute value or a p-adic absolute value.

body:
Fix depth l+1 and a fully connected scalar-output ReLU network with input dimension d and hidden widths d_1,...,d_l. All weight matrices are independent with independent Gaussian entries of variance 1/d_previous. Put b=min(d,d_1,...,d_l) and D=max(d,d_1,...,d_l); the scalar output width is not included. There are positive constants c_1,c_2,c_3 depending only on l such that, for D sufficiently large and 0<delta<=1/2, b>=c_1*(log D)^c_2*log(1/delta) implies: for each fixed deterministic x!=0, with probability at least 1-delta there is a scalar eta, allowed to depend on the sampled network and x, for which f(x+eta*grad f(x)) has the opposite sign from f(x), and ||eta*grad f(x)||/||x||<=c_3*sqrt(log(1/delta)/d). No hidden layer is required to be comparable to the input dimension. For l=2, w=floor(d^c), 0<c<1, and w<=m<=d^A for fixed A>=c, delta=w^(-p), p>0 fixed, satisfies the condition for all sufficiently large d. At ||x||=sqrt(d), the radius is then O(sqrt(log w)).
Fixed depth l+1
Independent Gaussian entries with inverse incoming-width variance
ReLU activation
Fixed deterministic nonzero input
D sufficiently large, 0<delta<=1/2, and the stated quantitative minimum-width condition
Adaptive scalar eta along the initial gradient is permitted

body: Kuratowski's theorem: A finite graph G is planar if and only if G contains no subgraph that is a subdivision of K_5 (the complete graph on 5 vertices) and no subgraph that is a subdivision of K_{3,3} (the complete bipartite graph with parts of size 3 and 3). Here a subdivision of a graph H is any graph obtained from H by replacing its edges with internally disjoint paths.
title: Kuratowski's theorem

Own-work draft; proof (unaudited); independent review pending. # Positive-budget global risk differs from expected conditional minimax risk

T379-C014 v2: proof (unaudited), exact rational checks PASS. Target 2;
route-failure of a tempting extension, not a new exact global frontier.

Use the full-verifier, untagged experiment of C013 with d=3,K=2,r=1,
n=1,N>=7. Write lambda=1/(2N), kappa=1/2 and choose robust calibration
budget c=2lambda=1/N. The three pairs are numbered 0,1,2. Conditional
on the verifier output, relabel each certified candidate as 0. Each A
therefore has only candidate 0 true; S has both candidates true. This
relabeling preserves all factual probabilities. Fixed S contexts are
6,...,N-1. The verifier supplies no orientation labels.

One factual sample outside the certified sets resolves exactly one
pair; otherwise all three are unresolved. Thus P(U=3)=1-3lambda and
P(U=2)=3lambda, uniformly in every fixed world and verifier output.
C013's conditional worst-world frontier is zero at U=2 and lambda/2
at U=3. Its expectation is

 E V(c,U)=lambda/2-3lambda^2/2.                         (1)

## Feasible asymmetric algorithm

On U=2, use C013's attainer, removing all posterior mass 2lambda from
the unresolved outside-certificate atoms and adding it to fixed S.
This has zero false mass in every compatible world and Mis<=2lambda.

On U=3, leave pair 0 balanced. For each of pairs 1 and 2, if the factual
sample is a certified candidate in that pair, predict that its context
is A. Otherwise predict either orientation by an independent fair coin.
This is a rule using observed data only. Form two sets of outside-
certificate atoms:

* B1: both atoms of pair 0 and the predicted-S atom of pairs 1 and 2;
* B2: the predicted-A atom of pairs 1 and 2.

Assign g=lambda/4 to each of B1's four atoms, g=0 to B2's two atoms,
g=3lambda/2 to each of the six certified atoms, and
g=lambda+lambda/(N-6) to each of the 2(N-6) fixed S atoms.
These masses sum to lambda+9lambda+2(N-6)lambda+2lambda=1.

For ANY compatible orientation let t be the number of true S atoms
in B1 from pairs 1 and 2. The source mass of B1 is lambda(1+t),
that of B2 is lambda(2-t), and that of the six certified atoms is
9lambda, all with the latter group assigned equal g. The fixed S
group receives exactly 2lambda extra g mass. Uniformly coarsening p
within these four groups gives TV to g equal to

 [t lambda+(2-t)lambda+2lambda]/2=2lambda.

Each group has constant g; the exact score partition can only merge
groups. Uniform averaging is TV-contractive and fixes g, so actual
source Mis_infinity<=2lambda even at N=8 where two scores coincide.
This verifies robust feasibility for every orientation and every coin
realization, without assuming that the orientation predictions are right.

Let E be the number of wrong orientation predictions in pairs 1 and 2.
Exactly one atom of pair 0 is false. Therefore on U=3 the ACTUAL false
mass is

 H=(lambda/4)(1+E).                                   (2)

For example, if both predictions happen to be right, H=lambda/4 is
strictly below the conditional minimax value lambda/2. For the opposite
orientations the same generator has H=3lambda/4. Thus a conditional
worst-world lower bound is not a lower bound in each actual world.

## Expectation in each fixed world

The one-sample categories below are disjoint. Each expected H averages
only the algorithm's independent fair tie coins; their probabilities
are factual sampling probabilities in a fixed actual world.

| Observation | Probability | Expected H |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Outside certificate in any S of the three pairs | 3lambda | 0 |
| Certified atom in pair 0 | 3lambda | lambda/2 |
| Certified atom in true A of pair 1 or 2 | 4lambda | 3lambda/8 |
| Certified atom in true S of pair 1 or 2 | 2lambda | 5lambda/8 |
| Fixed S context | 1-12lambda | lambda/2 |

Multiplying and summing gives, in EVERY fixed world and conditional
on EVERY verifier realization,

 E H=lambda/2-7lambda^2/4
     < lambda/2-3lambda^2/2=E V(c,U),                  (3)

with strict gap lambda^2/4=1/(16N^2). Thus the global minimax expected
value is at most the left expression and is strictly below the expected
conditional worst-world value. For N=7 these values are 3/112 versus
11/392, separated by 1/784. No optimality of this algorithm is asserted.

This does not contradict C013, whose exact GLOBAL value was asserted
only at c=0; its positive-budget conditional statement and global bracket
remain intact. This auxiliary-route counterexample is not claimed to
score as a target narrowing. Source calibration definition: Kalai--
Vempala 2311.14648v3, Definitions 1--2 pp.8--9. All other work here is
an own-work unaudited draft. Priority and independent audit pending.

Exact verification: logs/positive_budget_separation_check.json records
13824 compatible-world feasibility checks, 1920 sample/coin outcomes,
32 fixed-world expectation checks and 384 pointwise negative controls.
The runs include N=7,8,9,12; N=8 checks the merged-score case directly.
The construction and expectation derivation above cover every N>=7.
Full-support verification in every variable context including paired S, without orientations
Independent fair algorithmic orientation tie coins; robust source Mis_infinity<=c on every data/coin outcome
All other hypotheses and sample protocol exactly as C013, specialized as stated

body:
Author-proved exact counterexample, independent audit pending. V independent fair signs have Z_V(h)=(2cosh(beta h))^V and limiting pressure beta^(-1)log(2cosh(beta h)); the response tanh(beta h) is positive at each h>0 but the zero-source right slope is zero. A collective two-state model instead has Z_V(h)=2cosh(beta Vh), pressure tending to |h|, and finite-volume zero-field derivative zero. For that model h_V=1/(beta V^2) gives response tending to zero while h_V=1/sqrt(V) gives response tending to one. These exact toy models show that neither fixed positive pinning nor an arbitrary diagonal proves spontaneous order; they are not Riesz phase results.
beta>0
V positive integer
Exact toy systems only
title: Draft: positive pinned response is insufficient for spontaneous order

[Conj 2 of arXiv:2604.12233, 'An upper bound on the smallest singular value of dense random combinatorial matrices'] For every $\ve, \delta >0$ there is a constant $C=C(\ve, \de)$ 
    depending only on $\ve$, $\de$ such that the following holds. 
     Let $d\le n$ be integers that satisfy $\min(d,n-d) \geq (1+\ve) \log n$. Let $M$ be a random $n\times n$  matrix uniformly drawn from  $\cM_{n,d}$.

  Then   
     \[\P\lr{s_n(M) > C\, \frac{\sqrt{d}}{ n}} \leq \delta.
    \] (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)

[Lem MainSeriesKeyLem of arXiv:2506.18207, 'Cartan's Path Development, the Logarithmic Signature and a Conjecture of Lyons-Sidorova'] Let $L_{1},\cdots,L_{r}$ be given vectors
of positive integers and let $n_{0}\geqslant1$. Suppose that $|L_{1}|+\cdots+|L_{r}|+n_{0}=k\leqslant N.$
Then one has 
\begin{align}
 & \sum_{\xi_{0}+\xi_{1}+\cdots+\xi_{r}=l-r}{\rm ad}_{A}^{\xi_{r}}\circ{\rm ad}_{\hat{F}_{w}(H_{L_{r}})}\circ\cdots\circ{\rm ad}_{A}^{\xi_{1}}\circ{\rm ad}_{\hat{F}_{w}(H_{L_{1}})}\circ{\rm ad}_{A}^{\xi_{0}}\big(\hat{F}_{w}(D_{n_{0}}\tilde{L})\big)\nonumber \\
 & =\sum_{i}\sum_{\mu=1}^{r+1}\Theta_{L_{\mu-1},\cdots,L_{1},n_{0}}^{i}\cdot(b_{i}^{i+n_{0}^{\mu-1}-1})^{l+1-\mu}\nonumber \\
 & \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \sum_{I\in{\cal W}_{\mu,r}}\frac{(-1)^{\varepsilon(I)}\Psi_{I,n_{0}^{\mu-1}}^{{\bf L}_{{\bf p},{\bf q}}^{\mu,r}}\cdot}{b_{(i_{\mu}),n_{0}^{\mu-1}}^{{\bf n}_{{\bf p},{\bf q}}^{\mu,r}}b_{(i_{\mu},i_{\mu+1}),n_{0}^{\mu-1}}^{{\bf n}_{{\bf p},{\bf q}}^{\mu,r}}\cdots b_{I,n_{0}^{\mu-1}}^{{\bf n}_{{\bf p},{\bf q}}^{\mu,r}}}E_{i-|{\bf n}_{{\bf p}}^{\mu,r}|,i+n_{0}^{\mu-1}+|{\bf n}_{{\bf q}}^{\mu,r}|}.
\end{align}
Here \textcolor{black}{$\mathcal{W}_{\mu,r}$} denotes the set of words $I=(i_{\mu},i_{\mu+1},\cdots,i_{r})\in\{\pm1\}^{r-\mu+1}$. Given such a word $I$, the vector $\mathbf{p}$
denotes the subword of $(\mu,\cdots,r)$ which records the locations
of $-1$'s in $I$ and ${\bf q}\triangleq(\mu,\cdots,r)\backslash{\bf p}$.
The quantity $\varepsilon(I)$ denotes the length of ${\bf p}$ (i.e.
number of $-1$'s in $I$). The function $\Theta_{L_{\mu-1},\cdots,L_{1},n_{0}}^{i}$
is defined by 
\[
\Theta_{L_{\mu-1},\cdots,L_{1},n_{0}}^{i}\triangleq\Theta_{L_{\mu-1},\cdots,L_{1},n_{0},i}(b_{i},b_{i+1},\cdots,b_{i+k-1}),
\]
where $\Theta_{L_{\mu-1},\cdots,L_{1},n_{0},i}$ is a suitable meromorphic
function in $m$ complex variables ($m\triangleq n_{0}+|L_{1}|+\cdots+|L_{\mu-1}|$)
whose shape depends on $(L_{1},\cdots,L_{\mu-1}),n_{0}$ and $i$.
The family $\{\Theta_{L_{1},\cdots,L_{\mu-1},n_{0}}^{i}\}$ of functions
satisfy the following property: for any integer $i$, $1\leqslant\nu\leqslant r$
and any sequence of vectors ${\bf V}=(V_{1},\cdots,V_{r})$, under
the one-dimensional reduction $b_{j}\triangleq b_{j}^{*}+w$ the function
\begin{equation}
w\mapsto\sum_{\sigma\in{\cal S}_{\nu}}\Theta_{V_{\sigma(\nu)},\cdots,V_{\sigma(1)},n_{0}}^{i}
\end{equation}
is analytic near $w=0$ and vanishes at $w=0$. When $\mu=1,$ the
function $\Theta_{L_{\mu-1},\cdots,L_{1},n_{0}}^{i}$ depends only
on $n_{0}$ and $i$. As a convention, if $\mu=r+1$ the summation
$\sum_{I\in{\cal W}(\mu,r)}$ in ((lem:MainSeriesKeyLem of the paper)) is
set to be one and $|{\bf n}_{{\bf p}}^{\mu,r}|=|{\bf n}_{{\bf q}}^{\mu,r}|\triangleq0$
. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem MainSeriesKeyLem of arXiv:2506.18207

[Theorem thm:long_range_cluster of arXiv:2607.04002, 'Collisions of random walks in unimodular random graphs: applications to the random geometr'] For each regime, we assume that the percolation model with edge probabilities~$\mathsf P_{\beta,s}$ admits a unique infinite connected component~$\mathcal C_\infty$ almost surely.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item For~$d = 1$ with~$s =2$, and~$d=2$ with~$s \ge 4$, the long-range percolation cluster~$\mathcal C_\infty$ has the discrete and continuous infinite collision property almost surely.
    \item For~$d = 1$ with~$s \in (1,2)$, and~$d \ge 2$ with~$s \in (d,d+2)$, the long-range percolation cluster~$\mathcal C_\infty$ has the discrete and continuous finite collision property almost surely.
    \item [BenjaminiCurien2012] For~$d \ge 1$ with~$s \in (d,2d)$, the tail~$\sigma$-algebra~$\mathcal T_\mathrm{rw}(\mathcal C_\infty)$ is trivial almost surely.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Rouché's theorem, named after Eugène Rouché, states that for any two complex-valued functions f and g holomorphic inside some region K with closed contour partial K (the boundary of K), if |g(z)| < |f(z)| on partial K, then f and f + g have the same number of zeros inside K, where each zero is counted as many times as its multiplicity. This theorem assumes that the contour is simple, that is, without self-intersections. Rouché's theorem is an easy consequence of a stronger symmetric form of Rouché's theorem, in which the strict inequality |f(z) - g(z)| < |f(z)| + |g(z)| on the contour implies that f and g have the same number of zeros inside.

[Thm t:normalform of arXiv:2607.24640, 'The Yang-Mills measure on surfaces via Morse theory'] For any $A\in\Omega^1(\Sigma,\mathfrak{g})$, there exist $\mathrm{g}_\infty\in L^{\infty}(\Sigma,G)$ such that the following holds: 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F(A_T)$ converges (in the sense of currents) to $F_\infty:=\mathrm{g}_\infty^{-1}F(A)\mathrm{g}_\infty$  as $T\rightarrow\infty$ and 
$$
\mathcal{S}_{\operatorname{YM}}(A)=\int_{\Sigma}\|\star_hF_\infty\|_{\mathfrak{g}}^2\upsilon,
$$
\item there exists $\beta_\infty\in\mathcal{D}^\prime(\Sigma,T^*\Sigma\otimes\mathfrak{g})\cap\ker(\iota_V)$ such that $\int_0^T\varphi_f^{-t*}(\iota_V(F_\infty)dt$ converges (in the sense of currents) to $\beta_\infty$ and $A_T$ converges (in the sense of currents) to
\begin{equation}
A_\infty:=\sum_{j=2}^{2g+1}\mathfrak{b}_j[W^u(a_j)]+\beta_\infty,
\end{equation}
where $\mathfrak{b}_j:=\int_{W^s(a_j)}A\in\mathfrak{g}$;
\item $\beta_\infty$ and $\mathrm{g}_\infty$ are smooth on $W^u(a_1):=\Sigma\setminus\cup_{j=2}^{2g+1}\overline{W^u(a_j)}$ and, for every $1\leq q< 2$, $\beta_\infty$ belongs to $L^q(\Sigma,T^*\Sigma\otimes\mathfrak{g})$;
\item one has\footnote{Here, $[a]$ denotes the current of integration on the point $a$.} $dA_\infty=F_\infty-\left(\int_\Sigma F_\infty\right)[a_{2g+2}]$;

\item for any $\gamma:[0,1]\rightarrow\Sigma$ of class $\mathcal{C}^1$ such that $\gamma(0),\gamma(1)\in W^u(a_1)$, one has 
$$
\lim_{T\rightarrow +\infty}\operatorname{Hol}_{\gamma}(A_T)=\mathrm{g}_\infty(\gamma(1))^{-1}\operatorname{Hol}_{\gamma}(A)\mathrm{g}_\infty(\gamma(0));
$$
\item for any gauge equivalent $A_1,A_2 \in \Omega^1(\Sigma,\mathfrak{g})$, i.e. $A_2=\mathrm{g}^{-1}d\mathrm{g}+\mathrm{g}^{-1}A_1\mathrm{g}$ for some $\mathrm{g}\in C^\infty(\Sigma,G)$, the limiting 
connections $A_{1,\infty},A_{2,\infty}$ satisfy
$$A_{2,\infty}=\mathrm{g}(a_1)^{-1}A_{1,\infty} \mathrm{g}(a_1)\quad\text{on}\quad W^u(a_1),$$
and, under the assumption of the previous item, 
$$
\lim_{T\rightarrow +\infty}\operatorname{Hol}_{\gamma}(A_{2,T})=\lim_{T\rightarrow +\infty}\mathrm{g}(a_1)^{-1}\operatorname{Hol}_{\gamma}(A_{1,T})\mathrm{g}(a_1).
$$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Use the source's tanh implementation of GeLU, g(u)=(u/2)(1+tanh(c(u+a u^3))), where c=sqrt(2/pi) and a=0.044715. For fixed real x,y, as nonzero delta tends to zero, [g(delta(x+y))-g(delta x)-g(delta y)]/(c delta^2) tends to x y. The convergence is uniform for (x,y) in any fixed bounded subset of R^2. Thus three GeLU evaluations and a linear rescaling approximate a scalar product to arbitrary accuracy on a fixed bounded input domain. This is a limiting approximation, not an exact finite-delta product identity.

Let (P_t) be the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semigroup on L^p of the standard Gaussian measure on R^n. For 1 < p <= q < infinity, || P_t f ||_q <= || f ||_p for every f, PROVIDED e^{-t} <= sqrt( (p-1)/(q-1) ). The constant is exactly 1 - the semigroup is a contraction from L^p to the strictly larger L^q, not merely bounded - and the condition on t is sharp. Two consequences used constantly: taking p = 2 gives || P_t f ||_q <= || f ||_2 for e^{-t} = 1/sqrt(q-1); and restricting to the n-th Wiener chaos, where P_t acts as multiplication by e^{-nt}, gives the MOMENT COMPARISON || F ||_q <= (q-1)^{n/2} || F ||_2 for every F in the n-th chaos and every q >= 2. That comparison is dimension-free and is the reason all L^q norms on a fixed chaos are equivalent, with a constant depending only on the chaos order and q. GROSS'S THEOREM: hypercontractivity of (P_t) with these exponents is EQUIVALENT to the logarithmic Sobolev inequality Ent(f^2) <= 2 E|grad f|^2 for the same measure; each implies the other by differentiating or integrating the relation at q = q(t). The discrete-cube analogue with the noise operator is the Bonami-Beckner inequality, and the Gaussian case follows from it by the central limit theorem. [Nelson (1966, 1973); Gross (1975); see Bakry, Gentil and Ledoux, Analysis and Geometry of Markov Diffusion Operators, Chapter 5]
1 < p <= q < infinity and e^{-t} <= sqrt((p-1)/(q-1))

body:
Bubeck and Sellke (2021): let (x_i, y_i), i = 1..n, be data with covariates x_i in R^d drawn from a distribution satisfying isoperimetry (Lipschitz functions of x concentrate like they do for a Gaussian; a mixture of such distributions is allowed) and labels y_i carrying genuine noise (conditional variance sigma^2 > 0 that no function of x can remove). Let F be a class of functions parametrized by p real parameters (more precisely, with log covering number of order p). Then with high probability every f in F that fits the data to within a constant fraction of the noise level (a fraction of the sum of the y_i's conditional variances remains unexplained) has Lipschitz constant at least of order sqrt(n d / p), up to logarithmic factors. Consequence: interpolating n noisy points in dimension d smoothly (Lipschitz constant O(1)) needs p of order n d parameters, a factor d beyond the n needed merely to memorize. The bound is vacuous without noise (a smooth interpolant can exist) and without the isoperimetry hypothesis on the covariates.

labels have irreducible noise of variance sigma^2 > 0
the model class has p parameters in the sense of a log covering number of order p
the model fits the data below the noise floor (an interpolation-type condition)

AUTHOR PROOF DRAFT, unaudited; novelty is unestablished. Cycle-flow rank lemma for a double edge cover of a connected loopless multigraph B. Every edge bears two distinct labels, the label multigraph G is connected and remains connected after any label is deleted, and each label subgraph B_t is nonempty, connected and bridgeless. If B has q vertices,e edges and v labels, then q-e+v<=2; if any B_t has cycle rank at least2, then q-e+v<=1. In raw cumulant diagrams with bridgeless local row-column graphs this gives the required strict suppression of all higher blocks, including odd blocks. General local graphs may have bridges, so the full asymmetric coefficient theorem and uniform remainder remain open. Supporting proof draft; novelty unestablished.
Finite loopless multigraph B, connected, with distinct parallel edges
Every edge has exactly two distinct labels, v>=2
Connected label graph G, with G-t connected for every label
Every label subgraph nonempty, connected and bridgeless
Real cycle spaces; for the strict bound at least one has dimension>=2

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:70f30bc77c3f6327d58902cbda49680b8fa9430d465a9be9f2b051d63e74a5b9","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/70/70f30bc77c3f6327d58902cbda49680b8fa9430d465a9be9f2b051d63e74a5b9.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:5b9f7179ba2c2e22072cbab7d7a8a73d7ac24334eed12464811cabe7931b35f8","bundle_entry_key":"odd-cumulants-bridgeless-double-cover-cycle-flow-rank-w718","bundle_id":"population.t287-odd-cumulant-cycle-flow-rank-v1","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Graph cycle spaces and extensive-rank matrix inference","draft":"w718/bundle_010.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.gaussian_channels:odd-cumulants-bridgeless-double-cover-cycle-flow-rank-w718","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# A cycle-flow rank lemma for the odd-cumulant route

Target 1 supporting route lemma. Proof draft, UNAUDITED. Novelty is
unestablished. This does not prove the full asymmetric coefficient theorem,
and it does not supply a dimension-uniform Taylor remainder.

## Statement

Let B be a finite connected undirected loopless multigraph with e edges
and q vertices. Every edge has two distinct labels from a set of v>=2
labels. Let G be the multigraph on labels with one edge for each edge of
B, joining that edge's two labels. For label t let B_t be the subgraph
formed by all edges bearing t, retaining their endpoints. Assume:

1. G is connected, and G-t is connected for every label t (a single
   vertex is connected).
2. Every B_t is connected and bridgeless, with at least one edge.

Then q-e+v<=2. Moreover, if some B_t has cycle-space dimension at least
two, then q-e+v<=1.

Parallel edges are distinct edges throughout. Orient the edges of B
arbitrarily, once and for all. All vector spaces below are over R.

## Proof of the weak bound

The cycle space Z(B), the kernel of the oriented vertex-edge incidence
matrix, has dimension b=e-q+1. Since B_t is bridgeless, every edge of B_t
belongs to a cycle. Thus for each of its edges its coordinate functional
is nonzero on Z(B_t). A finite union of proper linear hyperplanes cannot
cover a real vector space. We may therefore choose f_t in Z(B_t) nonzero
on every edge of B_t, and extend it by zero outside B_t. Its extension
lies in Z(B).

Form the v by e matrix F with rows f_t. A column indexed by edge a of G,
with endpoints t,u, has precisely two nonzero entries f_t(a),f_u(a).
If lambda is in the left kernel of F, it satisfies

    lambda_t f_t(a) + lambda_u f_u(a) = 0.

Consequently one coordinate of lambda determines all the others along
paths in connected G. In particular the kernel dimension is at most
one, and any nonzero kernel vector has every coordinate nonzero.
Therefore rank F>=v-1. Since its rows lie in Z(B), b>=v-1, proving the
weak inequality.

## Strictness

Suppose b=v-1. For every choice of full-support flows, F then has rank
exactly v-1 and a one-dimensional left kernel with all coordinates
nonzero. Fix one such choice and a nonzero kernel vector lambda.

Fix a label t and replace only its flow by any other full-support flow
h in Z(B_t). The new matrix again has a nonzero left-kernel vector mu
whose coordinates are all nonzero. On every edge joining labels other
than t, the old and new equations give

    mu_u/lambda_u = mu_w/lambda_w.

Connectivity of G-t makes this ratio a common nonzero constant c for
all labels other than t. On each edge a joining t and u, subtracting
the two kernel equations now gives

    mu_t h(a) = c lambda_t f_t(a).

All edges of B_t bear a second label other than t. Hence h is a scalar
multiple of f_t on its entire support. Every full-support flow in
Z(B_t) is therefore on one fixed line. Full-support flows are the
complement of finitely many proper hyperplanes, a nonempty open dense
subset of Z(B_t). This is possible only if dim Z(B_t)=1. As t was
arbitrary, equality forces this dimension to be one for every label.
If any label has dimension at least two, the integer b must be at least
v, proving strictness. QED.

## Translation to the cumulant diagrams

In a Wick contraction, B has one vertex for each global row equality
class and each global column equality class, and one edge for each
Wick pair. It is bipartite and loopless, including when several edges
have the same endpoints. Its label graph is the tensor contraction
graph G. Thus q=c_i+c_j, and q-e+v is exactly the index exponent.
Connected local raw row/column graphs and connected G imply connected B.

Let H_t be the local graph before global equality identifications.
Each of its edges maps to a distinct edge of B_t. If H_t is bridgeless,
then B_t is bridgeless: an edge on a cycle maps to an edge on a closed
trail, so cannot become a bridge. Vertex identifications preserve or
increase cycle-space dimension, since they preserve edge count and
cannot increase the vertex count of a connected graph.

Every raw block has size at least two. Thus H_t has minimum degree two.
If any raw block has size at least three, its connected graph has
cycle rank at least two: writing d for its edge count and h for its
vertex count, 2d>=2h+1 implies d>=h+1 and d-h+1>=2. This applies to odd
degrees without an Euler circuit. The strict exponent bound therefore
holds for all diagrams whose local graphs are bridgeless and which
contain a higher raw block.

## The remaining bridge obstruction

Minimum degree two DOES NOT imply bridgeless. A connected bipartite
local graph can consist of two length-two parallel-edge cycles joined
by a single edge. It has five edges, degree sequence (3,2,3,2), and a
bridge. All cycle flows vanish on that bridge. The full-support choice
used in the proof is then impossible; the associated column of F can
have zero entries, so the kernel-propagation proof cannot be invoked.
Some global identifications can remove such bridges, but this is not
guaranteed term by term by the current assumptions.

The general route must either remove these bridge terms through an
additional exact entropy cancellation or control their missing flow
constraints by a separate graph argument. Neither has been proved here.
Even that extension would address fixed-order coefficients only.

Least trusted step for review: whether the global quotient diagrams
indeed have precisely the B and G incidence representation stated in
the translation. The abstract graph lemma itself uses only the stated
support, rank and connectivity conditions.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:301e329545fb9cbce0c61e9c86ce36ea4e49997d0ea2cebdf0dbce18c63eb19b","revision_digest":"sha256:d1d8b8da18a72cdf1fea56d6242b4fc19bbae7b328bd1e53b2d44073088268f5","source_id":"owner:w718:T287:odd-cumulants-bridgeless-double-cover-cycle-flow-rank-w718","source_revision":"2026-10-21-v1","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

Method: Optimal spectra of random symmetric-group Cayley graphs structural calculation Result: The sign obstruction has an exact positive probability: when all r generator signs agree, the corresponding adjacency eigenvalue has absolute value2r, above2*sqrt(2r-1) for r>=2. This event has probability2^(1-r). After removing it, pointwise convergence for each selected irrep still cannot justify the supremum over all irreps: in a triangular array with one uniformly chosen bad coordinate per row, every coordinate is bad with probability1/m_N tending to0, yet the row maximum is bad surely. Check: The sign variables are independent fair signs for uniform permutations. The array example verifies the quantifier failure exactly and indicates the need for uniform probability bounds, rather than just increasing the range of an individual representation theorem. Obstruction: No uniform tail estimate over the high-dimensional irreducible representations is proved.

body: Let X be a square-integrable function of independent coordinates and X^L its value after an independent resampling of a block L, and suppose the pair (X, X^L) is exchangeable (automatic for independent block resampling). Then E[((X^L - X)^+)^2] = Var(X) - Cov(X, X^L). Proof in two lines from facts that hold separately: exchangeability gives E[(X - X^L)^2] = 2 Var(X) - 2 Cov(X, X^L), and the symmetry of X^L - X gives E[(X - X^L)^2] = 2 E[((X^L - X)^+)^2]; equate. Consequences: Cov(X, X^L) <= Var(X) always; summing over a partition of blocks turns Efron-Stein into the exact statement Sum_L E[((X^L - X)^+)^2] = Sum_L (Var(X) - Cov(X, X^L)), so bounding the positive-part functionals a resampling engine consumes is EXACTLY the problem of lower-bounding the block covariances. Numerically checked on a nonlinear functional (relative difference 0.008 at 200,000 samples).

body: In mathematics, the operator norm measures the "size" of certain linear operators by assigning each a real number called its operator norm. Formally, it is a norm defined on the space of bounded linear operators between two given normed vector spaces. Informally, the operator norm of a linear map is the maximum factor by which it "lengthens" vectors. It is also called the bound norm.

[Thm 2 of arXiv:2609.02686, 'The Bonnet-Myers theorem on Finsler manifolds with integral weighted Ricci curvature bound'] Let $(M, F, m)$ be an $n$-dimensional Finsler metric measure manifold. Assume that $\mathbf{S}\geq -\vartheta$ for some $\vartheta \geq 0$. Then for $p>\frac{n}{2}$, $K>0$ and $0 < r <\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{K}}$, we have
\be
\sin ^{4 p-n-1}(\sqrt{K} r) \varphi(r, \theta)^{2 p-1} e^{-\vartheta r} \sigma(r, \theta) \leq (2 p-1)^{p}\left(\frac{n-1}{2 p-n}\right)^{p-1} \int_{0}^{r}\left({\rm{Ric}}_{\infty}^{K}\right)^{p} e^{-\vartheta t} \sigma(t, \theta) d t. 
\ee

body:
[Lemma 18 (Insertions leading to absorption) of arXiv:2608.16752, 'Absorption Probabilities for Random Convex Hulls: Distribution-Freeness via the Wall-Cross'] Let $u\in \R^d$, $u\neq 0$ and let $\pi: \R^d \to u^{\perp}$ be the orthogonal projection  onto the hyperplane $u^{\perp}$. Suppose that $0\notin \partial_{u^{\perp}}(\pi K)$, where the boundary is taken in $u^{\perp}$.
Then, for all sufficiently small $\delta>0$, the
number of admissible insertions of $\delta u$ (including the sign choice in the Wendel and walk models) for which $0\in \overline K$ equals
\[
    (T_n-1)\,\mathbb{1}_{\{0\in K\}}+\mathbb{1}_{\{0\in\pi K\}}.
\]
title: Insertions leading to absorption

Own-work draft, proof (unaudited), claim w744-T368-wu-lemma9-missing-positive-part v2. Let n>=1 data (x_i,y_i) in R^d times {-1,+1} satisfy ||x_i||_2<=1. Assume a unit vector w_star and a fixed gamma>0 satisfy y_i <x_i,w_star> >= gamma for every i. Define ell(q)=log(1+exp(-q)), L(w)=(1/n)sum_i ell(y_i<x_i,w>), and full-batch GD w_{k+1}=w_k-eta grad L(w_k) with constant eta>0. Assume w_0=0. Put G(w)=(1/n)sum_i 1/(1+exp(y_i<x_i,w>)) and log_+(a)=max(0,log(a)) for a>0. For every integer t>=1, (1/t)sum_{k=0}^{t-1}G(w_k)<=[sqrt(2)+2log_+(gamma^2 eta t)+eta]/(gamma^2 eta t). The corresponding norm bound is ||w_t||<=[sqrt(2)+2log_+(gamma^2 eta t)+eta]/gamma. This corrects the printed unrestricted Lemma 9, which omits the positive part: n=d=1,x=y=w_star=gamma=1,eta=1/16,t=1 has left side 1/2 but its printed numerator sqrt(2)-8log(2)+1/16 is strictly below -181/48. The printed bound is therefore false at allowed small times. The replacement agrees with the original whenever gamma^2 eta t>=1, including the source phase-transition argument. No new optimization rate or refutation of source Theorem 1 is claimed.
Finite nonempty binary-labeled data with Euclidean feature norms <=1
Unit separating vector w_star and margin gamma>0
Averaged logistic risk and full-batch constant-step gradient descent
Zero initialization
Integer t>=1; log_+ argument gamma^2 eta t>0

Status: PROOF (UNAUDITED); source text and PDF p20 formula visually confirmed. This is a
source-statement correction, not a new optimization-rate result and not a solution
of the nonhomogeneous-network frontier target.

The primary arXiv:2402.15926 PDF p20 prints, under zero initialization and every
eta>0, for t>=1,

    mean_{k<t} G(w_k) <= [sqrt(2)+2 log(gamma^2 eta t)+eta]/(gamma^2 eta t).

Here G(w)=mean_i 1/(1+exp(y_i x_i dot w)). Take n=d=1, x=y=w_star=gamma=1,
w_0=0, t=1 and eta=1/16. These satisfy every boundedness/separability/initialization
hypothesis. The left side is exactly 1/2. The numerator on the right is
sqrt(2)-8log(2)+1/16 < 3/2-16/3+1/16 = -181/48 <0.
Use sqrt(2)<3/2 (squaring positive numbers) and log(2)>2/3, obtained by integrating
1/x >=4/3-4x/9 on [1,2], strictly except at x=3/2. The denominator is 1/16>0.
Thus the printed unrestricted small-time statement is false. No floating-point
estimate is used. The rendered formula in renders/arxiv2402.15926_p20.png was
inspected and confirms both the numerator and its unrestricted eta>0,t>=1 range.

A correct universal version replaces log(a) by log_+(a)=max(0,log(a)).
The data hypotheses, arbitrary eta>0 and t>=1 remain unchanged. Proof:

Write z_i=y_i x_i, p_i(w)=1/(1+exp(z_i dot w)), G=mean_i p_i, and
g=grad L=-mean_i p_i z_i. Source Lemma 7 uses u=u_1+u_2, where
u_2=eta w_star/(2gamma), and gives

    ||w_t-u||^2/(2 eta t)+mean_{k<t} L(w_k)
      <= L(u_1)+||w_0-u||^2/(2 eta t).

Indeed ||g||<=G<=1, g dot w_star<=-gamma G, so
2eta g dot u_2+eta^2||g||^2<=0. Convexity of L controls the u_1 term;
sum the squared-distance recursion over k. This holds for any u_1 and w_0.

For w_0=0 set a=gamma^2 eta t and u_1=log_+(a) w_star/gamma.
If a>=1, separability and log(1+exp(-q))<=exp(-q) give L(u_1)<=1/a.
If a<1 then u_1=0 and L(u_1)=log(2)<1<1/a. Consequently

    ||w_t-u||^2 <= ||u||^2+2/gamma^2,
    ||w_t|| <=2||u||+sqrt(2)/gamma
             =[2log_+(a)+eta+sqrt(2)]/gamma.

Finally z_i dot w_star>=gamma gives the perceptron progress inequality
(w_{k+1}-w_k) dot w_star>=eta gamma G(w_k). Telescope from w_0=0 and use
||w_star||=1, obtaining mean G<=||w_t||/(eta gamma t), exactly the corrected
bound. All divisions use eta,gamma,t>0. The logarithm's argument a is positive.
When a>=1, this reproduces the printed expression unchanged; in particular this
is the regime used in the source's finite phase-transition proof (Lemma 12).

Indeed, if eta>=1, tau>=60eta/gamma^2 implies gamma^2 eta tau>=60.
If eta<1, n>=1 gives (eta+n)/eta>2, so the logarithmic term in tau gives
gamma^2 eta tau>=60(eta+n)log((eta+n)/eta)>60log(2)>40>1.

The same positive-part choice also justifies the all-time parameter and averaged
risk estimates without using a negative comparator radius in a margin inequality.
It does not refute Theorem 1 or its acceleration corollary.

Dependency: Use the split-comparator potential bound. [Definition of arXiv:2411.13030, 'Classification of the limit shape for 1+1-dimensional FPP'] Let $p$ be a semi-directed path from the origin to a point $(n,m)$. For $k=0,...,n$ let $f_p(k)\in \mathbb Z$ be such that $(k, f_p(k)) \in \mathbb Z^2$ is the first intersection of $p$ with the vertical line $\{k\}\times \mathbb Z$. In particular, $f_p(0)=0$. The points $(k, f_p(k)) \in \mathbb Z^2$ are referred to as \emph{pioneer points}. 
We also introduce the convention $f_p(n+1)=m$ (even though $(n+1,m) \not \in p$).
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2411.13030, 'Classification of the limit shape for 1+1-dimensional FPP'

[Lemma lem.densite.1 of arXiv:2411.19145, 'On the intersection of critical percolation clusters and other tree-like random graphs'] There exists a constant $C>0$, such that for any $\rho>0$, any $r\ge 1$, and any finite set $\Lambda\subset V$ satisfying 
$$|\Lambda\cap B(x,r)|\le \rho \cdot |B(x,r)|,\quad \textrm{for all }x\in \Lambda,$$  
one has for any $R\ge r$, and any $x\in V$, 
$$|\Lambda\cap B(x,R)|\le C \cdot \rho R^d. $$

[Proposition pr:hextension of arXiv:2604.21142, 'Gaussian fluctuations for Internal DLA on cylinders'] For $2 \leq k \leq N$, let $q_k > 0$ be the positive real number defined by
	\begin{equation}
	 \cosh(q_k) = 2 - \l_k\,.
	 \end{equation}
(By irreducibility and laziness, $\l_k \in [0, 1)$ for $k \geq 2$, so $2 - \l_k \in (1, 2]$ and $q_k > 0$.) Then, for every $h \in {\ensuremath{\mathbb Z}} $ and every sequence $(\a_k(h))_{2 \leq k \leq N}$ of real numbers, the function
	\[ \psi(x, y) = \sum_{k=2}^N \a_k(h)\, f_k^N(x)\, e^{q_k(y - h)} \]
is discrete harmonic on ${\ensuremath{\mathbb G}} _N$, decays exponentially as $y \to -\infty$, and satisfies $\psi(x, h) = \sum_{k=2}^N \a_k(h)\,f_k^N(x)$ on the line $\{(x, h) : x \in V_N\}$.

[Theorem thm:fullI of arXiv:2607.01463, 'Two Multi--Draw Coupon Collector models with different retention rules'] The full asymptotic expansion of the average of the random variable $T_{N,d}$ in the $d$ coupon collector's problem (d--CCP) is given by  
\begin{align}
\mathbb {E}\left[T_{N,d}\right]=&\frac{H_N}{A_N}+\frac{B_N}{A_N^2}\nonumber \\
\sim& \frac{N}{d}\log N+\frac{\gamma}{d}N
+\sum_{m=0}^{\infty}\bigl(\lambda_m(d)\log N+\nu_m(d)\bigr)N^{-m},\quad N\rightarrow \infty,

\end{align}
where the coefficients $\lambda_m(d)$ and $\nu_m(d)$ are defined in relations ((33a of the paper))-((38 of the paper)). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:fullI of arXiv:2607.01463

body: [Definition of arXiv:2411.13505, 'Capacity of loop-erased random walk'] We define the two-sided loop-erased random walk $\hat\eta$ as the random variable on two-sided infinite paths in $\Omega$ such that $\hat\eta[0,\infty)$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $\eta$ with Radon-Nikodym derivative given by $\frac{X_\infty}{\mathbb{E}[X_\infty]}$. It was shown in [lawler19fourdimensional] that $(T\hat\eta)[0,\infty)\stackrel{d}{=}\hat\eta[0,\infty)$. Thus, we can extend $\hat\eta$ to the space of two-sided infinite paths by defining $\hat\eta[-a,b]\stackrel{d}{=}\hat\eta[0,a+b]-\hat\eta(a)$.
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2411.13505, 'Capacity of loop-erased random walk'

[Lem zygmundwithlogs of arXiv:2412.00593, 'A new approach to strong convergence II.\\The classical ensembles'] Fix $k,l\in\mathbb{Z}_+$ and $u>0$, and let $s := \lceil k+ul\rceil$.
Let $h\in\mathcal{P}_q$ with Chebyshev expansion
$h(x) = \sum_{j=0}^q a_j T_j(K^{-1}x)$, and let
$f(\theta):= h(K \cos(\theta))$.  Then
$$
	\sum_{j=1}^q j^k (1+\log j)^l  
	|a_j| \lesssim
	\bigg(\frac{e^u}{u}\bigg)^l
	\sobnorm{f^{(s+1)}}{0}{[0, 2\pi]}.
$$

body:
[Proposition 2 of arXiv:2608.23989, 'Collision Properties in Discrete and Continuous Time on Bounded-Degree Graphs'] The following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item Let~$P$ be an irreducible Markov kernel on $\mathsf S$, reversible with respect to a measure $\pi$ satisfying
    \[ \sup_{x \in \mathsf S}\pi(x) <\infty.\]
    Then~$\Pp(\mathcal E^P_\mathrm{disc}) \in \{0,1\}$ for every common starting state.  
    \item Let~$Q$ be an irreducible~$Q$-matrix on~$\mathsf S$, reversible with respect to a measure~$\pi$ satisfying
    \[ \sup_{x \in \mathsf S} \pi(x) <\infty \qquad \text{and} \qquad \sup_{x \in \mathsf S}q(x) <\infty .\]
    Then~$\Pp(\mathcal E^Q_\mathrm{cont}) \in \{0,1\}$ for every common starting state. 
\end{enumerate}
title: Proposition 2 of arXiv:2608.23989

[Lemma 8 (Campbell--Palm intensity identity) of arXiv:2608.20101, '\bfseries Largest bulk gap of the complex Ginibre ensemble'] For every Borel set \(A\subset D_1\),
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E\mathcal E_n(r)(A)
 =\int_AK_n(a,a)q_n(a,r)\dd^2a.
\end{equation}
More generally, the same formula holds with \(r\) replaced by a measurable
location-dependent radius \(r(a)\).  In particular, the adaptive process in
\Cref{prop:LO} has intensity measure exactly
\(\kappa\dd^2z\) in unit-disk coordinates.
