body:
[Lem 46 of arXiv:2510.22783, 'Universality of Cutoff for Riffle Shuffling'] Consider the set $\mathcal M$ of $(N-i+\iota(p)+y_{p,i}-1)\times K$ matrices with entries in $[k]_0$ such that:
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item The first $n^{\rem}$ rows start with $\p$.
            \item The first $n^{\rem}$ rows are lexicographically greater than or equal to $s_i$.
            \item Among the first $n^{\rem}$ rows, at least $y_{p,i}$ are equal to $s_i$.
            \item For every $t\in [K]$ and $j\in [k]_0$, the number of $j$-digits in the $t$-th column is exactly $n_j^{(t),\rem}$ .
        \end{enumerate}
        We then select uniformly at random a matrix from $\widehat{\mathcal{M}}$.
        For each\footnote{Note the fourth condition above with $t=1$ and $j=\p$ implies that \emph{only} the first $n^{\rem}$ rows begin with $\p$; recall $n^{\rem}=n^{(1),\rem}_{\p}$.} $j \in [n^{\rem}]$, denote by $\widehat{s}_j$ the $j$-th row of the selected matrix. 
        If we sort $\{\widehat{s}_j\}_{j \in [n^{\rem}]}$ into increasing lexicographic order, writing the result as $(\overline{s}'_j)_{j \in [n^{\rem}]}$, then we have
        \[
            (\overline s'_{1}, \ldots, \overline s'_{n^{\rem}}) \overset{\mathrm{law.}}{=} (s_{i-y_{p,i}+1},s_{i-y_{p,i}+2},\ldots,s_{\tau(p)})
            \text{\emph{ conditioned on $\mathbf a_i$,}}
        \]
        which gives a natural coupling between the two sequences of strings with $\overline{s}'_{j}=s_{j+i-y_{p,i}}$ for each $j \in [n^{\rem}]$, and thereby between the set $\{\widehat{s}_j\}_{j \in [n^{\rem}]}$ and the sequence $(\overline{s}_{j+i-y_{p,i}})_{j \in [n^{\rem}]}$. 
        We denote this natural coupling by $Q$.
        In particular, the distribution of $\left|\cI(B_x)\right|$ conditioned on $\mathbf a_i$ coincides with that of $\left|\{j \in [n^{\rem}] : \widehat{s}_j \in B_{x}\}\right|$.

[Definition Measure-theoretic upper expectation of arXiv:2512.21026, 'Minimax Duality in Game-Theoretic Probability\thanks{Work in progress: mistakes are likely'] Let $(\Omega,\mathcal{Z})$ be a gamble space, and $X:\Omega\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ a measurable variable.
  Then we define
  \begin{align}
    \overline{\mathbb{E}} X &:= \sup_{P\in\Delta(\Omega)} \inf_{Z\in\mathrm{mdcl}(\mathcal{Z})} \mathbb{E}_P [X-Z]~,
  \end{align}
  and $\underline{\mathbb{E}} X := -\overline{\mathbb{E}}(-X)$.
  If $\mathbb{E}_P[X-Z]$ is not defined, we define it to be $\infty$.
title: Measure-theoretic upper expectation

[Definition defi:interface of arXiv:2511.01851, 'Percolation on graphs of polynomial growth is local:\\analyticity, supercritical sharpness'] Let $\mathscr{I}\subset V$ be a finite set of vertices. We say that $\mathscr{I}$ is an \textit{interface} if it is $t$-coarse connected and either $o\in \mathscr{I}$ or $o$ lies in a finite connected components of $\mathscr{G}\setminus \mathscr{I}$. Let $\overline{\mathscr{I}}$ denote the set of vertices $x$ such that $d_{\mathscr{G}}(x,\mathscr{I})\leqslant 10N$. We say that an interface $\mathscr{I}$ \textit{occurs in $\omega$ at scale $N$} if
\begin{enumerate}
    \item every $x\in \mathscr{I}$ is bad,
    \item every $x\in V\setminus \mathscr{I}$ such that $d_{\mathscr{G}}(x,\mathscr{I})\leqslant t$ is good,
    \item the closed edges of $\overline{\mathscr{I}}$ form a bond-cutset between $o$ and $\infty$.
\end{enumerate}
When clear from context, we simply write that $\mathscr{I}$ occurs.
title: Definition defi:interface of arXiv:2511.01851

[Proposition eq:finite_size_criterion_1 of arXiv:2607.18011, 'From local giants to locality in long-range percolation'] \thlabel{prop:finite_size_criterion}
    Let $G$ be a transitive graph of polynomial growth with $d \geq 2$ and let $J : V \times V \to \mathbf{R}_+$ be a transitive kernel.
    
    Suppose that $G$ admits $A$-controlled nets for some $A \geq 1$.
    
    Let $\delta > 0$ and let $\beta \in \mathbf{R}_+$.
    
    Suppose that there exists $\nu > 0$ such that  for some $R \in \mathbf{N}$ we have
    
    \begin{equation}
    
        \mathbf{P}_{\beta}
        \left(
            \# 
            K_{R}^{\scriptscriptstyle (1)}
            \geq
            \nu
            \# B(R)
        \right) 
        \geq 
        1
        -
        \delta,
    \end{equation}
    
    and for any two sets $S_1, S_2 \subseteq B(10AR)$ with $d_G(S_1,S_2) \geq 2R$ and $\#S_1, \#S_2 \geq \nu \# B(R)$, 
    
    \begin{equation}
    
        \mathbf{P}_\beta
        \left(
            S_1 
            \sim 
            S_2 
        \right) 
        \geq 
        1
        -
        \delta
        .
    \end{equation}      
    
    If $\delta = c_G/(18 (8A)^d C_G)$ then $\beta > \beta_c(G,J)$.
    
    Further, $\mathbf{P}_{\beta} \left(K_{R}^{\scriptscriptstyle (1)} \leftrightarrow \infty \right) \to 1$ as $\delta \to 0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Finite-size criterion for $d \geq 2$

[Cor Thom-space-po of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] The diagram $((diag:thom-space-spectrum of the paper))$ is a pushout of presentably symmetric monoidal global $\infty$-categories. 
\begin{proof} 
    By Corollaries~(cor:global-spectra-smash of the paper) and (cor:gl-pointed of the paper) and the construction of the various maps, $((diag:thom-space-spectrum of the paper))$ is a commutative square in $\CAlg(\textup{Pr}^\textup{Glo}_\textup{Glo})$.
    It therefore suffices to show that for every presentably symmetric monoidal global $\infty$-category ${\mathcal{C}}$, 
    the square $((diag:thom-space-spectrum of the paper))$ induces an equivalence \[{\textup{Hom}}({\mathpalette\ulhelper{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_{\textup{gl}}^{\otimes},{\mathcal{C}})\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}  {\textup{Hom}}(\ul{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_{\textup{gl},*}^{\otimes},{\mathcal{C}})\times_{{\textup{Hom}}({\ul\Spc_{\textup{Glo}/\ul\textup{Rep}^{\oplus}}},{\mathcal{C}})}{\textup{Hom}}(\ul\Spc_{\textup{Glo}/\ul\textup{VRep}^{\oplus}},{\mathcal{C}}),\] where ${\textup{Hom}}({-},{-})\coloneqq {\textup{Hom}}_{\CAlg(\textup{Pr}^{\textup{Glo}}_{\textup{Glo}})}({-},{-})$ denotes the $\infty$-groupoid of symmetric monoidal left adjoints.  
  
    Fix a presentably symmetric monoidal global $\infty$-category ${\mathcal{C}}$.
    It follows from Proposition~(prop:slice-sym-mon-is-universal of the paper) and the universal property of group completion that restriction along ${\mathpalette\ulhelper{\Spc}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_{\textup{Glo}/\ul\textup{Rep}^{\oplus}}\to \ul\Spc_{\textup{Glo}/\ul\textup{VRep}^{\oplus}}$ yields an inclusion of path components \[ {\textup{Hom}}({\mathpalette\ulhelper{\Spc}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_{\textup{Glo}/\ul\textup{VRep}^{\oplus}},{\mathcal{C}})\hookrightarrow {\textup{Hom}}({\mathpalette\ulhelper{\Spc}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_{\textup{Glo}/\ul\textup{Rep}^{\oplus}},{\mathcal{C}})\] with image those globally cocontinuous symmetric monoidal functors ${\mathpalette\ulhelper{\Spc}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_{\textup{Glo}/\ul\textup{Rep}^{\oplus}}\to {\mathcal{C}}$ which send elements in the Yoneda image of $\smash{\ul\textup{Rep}^{\oplus}}$ to invertible objects.   
    By construction of the Thom space functor $\ul{\textup{th}}_\textup{gl}^\otimes$, this implies that the projection \begin{align*}{\textup{Hom}}(\ul{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_{\textup{gl},*}^{\otimes},{\mathcal{C}})\times_{{\textup{Hom}}(\ul\Spc_{\textup{Glo}/\ul\textup{Rep}^{\oplus}},{\mathcal{C}})}{\textup{Hom}}(\ul\Spc_{\textup{Glo}/\ul\textup{VRep}^{\oplus}},{\mathcal{C}}) \to {\textup{Hom}}(\ul{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_{\textup{gl},*}^{\otimes},{\mathcal{C}})\end{align*} is the inclusion of the components consisting of those globally cocontinuous symmetric monoidal functors which in every degree $G$ send all representation spheres to invertible objects. The map ${\textup{Hom}}(\Sigma^\bullet,{\mathcal{C}})\colon{\textup{Hom}}({\mathpalette\ulhelper{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_\textup{gl}^\otimes,{\mathcal{C}})\to{\textup{Hom}}(\ul{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_{\textup{gl},*},{\mathcal{C}})$ admits the same description by the universal property of global spectra (Corollary~(cor:global-spectra-smash of the paper)) and Corollary~(cor:SpR-sym-mon-univ-prop of the paper),  finishing the proof.

Let $K$ be symmetric positive definite with eigenvalues $w_1 \le \dots \le w_n$ and eigenvectors $U$, and let $G$ be symmetric positive semidefinite. The exact identity $V = \mathrm{Tr}(K^{-1} G K^{-1}) = \sum_k \tilde G_{kk} / w_k^2$ with $\tilde G = U^\top G U$ holds, but if $G$ is replaced by $G + E$ with $\|E\|_2 \le \varepsilon \|G\|_2$ (rounding of relative size $\varepsilon$ in the entries of $G$), the computed value changes by at most $\varepsilon \|G\|_2 \sum_k w_k^{-2} \le \varepsilon\, n\, \|G\|_2 / w_1^2$. When $\|G\|_2$ is comparable to $\|K\|_2^2 = w_n^2$ (as for $G = \Phi D \Phi^\top$ built from the same features as $K = \Phi\Phi^\top$), this is an absolute error of order $\varepsilon\, \kappa(K)^2$ per eigendirection, so the trace form is not a usable number once $\varepsilon \kappa(K)^2 \gtrsim 1$. If instead $G = \Phi D \Phi^\top$ and $K = \Phi \Phi^\top$ share a factor $\Phi$ with $D$ diagonal nonnegative, then $V = \sum_j D_{jj} \|K^{-1} \Phi_{\cdot j}\|^2$, and a perturbation $\Delta$ of $\Phi$ with $\|\Delta\|_F \le \delta$ changes $V$ to first order by at most $2 \sqrt{V}\, \sqrt{D_{\max}}\, \delta / w_1$: one inverse, and the error enters through a single factor of $1/w_1$ rather than $1/w_1^2$. Measured instance: Gaussian kernel on the sphere, $d=12$, $n=4096$, $\kappa(K) = 1.3\times 10^{10}$, $\varepsilon \kappa^2 = 4\times 10^4$: the trace form reads $3.09$, a factored form through an eigendecomposition of $G$ alone reads $25.7$ (the rounding directions of $G$ still divided by $w_k^2$), the shared-factor form reads $2.653$, and a Monte-Carlo evaluation of the same quantity reads $2.657 \pm 0.003$.
K symmetric positive definite
G symmetric positive semidefinite
rounding modelled as a symmetric perturbation E of G with spectral norm at most epsilon times the spectral norm of G

[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2609.02019, '2609.02019'] Let $s>5/2$. Let  $J_n$ be the Friedrichs mollifier defined in \eqref{Define Jn}.
		Then we have
		\begin{equation*}
			\left|\IP{\mathcal{H} u\partial_x u, u}_{H^{s}}\right|
			\lesssim  (\|u_x\|_{L^\infty}+\|\mathcal{H} u_x\|_{L^\infty})\|u\|^2_{H^{s}},\quad u\in H^{s+1}.
		\end{equation*}
		and
		\begin{equation*}
			\sup_{n\ge1}\left|\bIP{J_n (\mathcal{H} u\partial_x u), J_n u}_{H^{s}}\right|
			\lesssim  (\|u_x\|_{L^\infty}+\|\mathcal{H} u_x\|_{L^\infty})\|u\|^2_{H^{s}},\quad u\in H^{s}.

			\lesssim  \Big(1+\|u\|^4_{H^s}+\|v\|^4_{H^s}\Big)
			\left((n\wedge m)^{-2(s-1-\theta)}+\|u-v\|^2_{H^\theta}\right).

[Theorem scheme case of arXiv:2609.04023, 'Characterizing Contractions and Weighted Blowdowns'] Suppose $X$ and $Z$ are smooth connected separated schemes of finite type over $\mathbb{C}$ of dimension $n$, and there is a projective contraction morphism $f : X \to Z$ where the exceptional divisor $E$ is a smooth irreducible Cartier divisor. Moreover, suppose there is a smooth closed irreducible subscheme $Y \subseteq Z$ such that $E \simeq f^{-1}(Y)$ set-theoretically, and $f : X \setminus E \xrightarrow{\sim} Z \setminus Y$. 
    
    Then, $f$ is the blowup of $Z$ along smooth center $Y$, i.e., $X \simeq \operatorname{Bl}_Y Z$. In particular, there is a vector bundle $V \to Y$ of rank $r := \operatorname{codim}(Y, Z)$ such that $(E, \mathcal{O}_{E}(-E)) \simeq (\mathbb{P}(V), \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}(V)}(1))$ where $\mathbb{P}(V)$ is the projectivization of $V$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

PRIVATE AUTHOR-CHECKED PARTIAL CANDIDATE; no independent review or novelty certification. For n FIFO queues, Poisson jobs at rate n*lambda/k choosing uniform k-subsets, and independent task marks, let r(T) be a stationary marginal M/G/1 emptying tail. The tagged k-workload law differs from its marginal product by at most 2*k*r(T)+3*lambda*T*k*(k-1)^2/(2*(n-1)) in total variation. Exponential services of rate mu>lambda give r(T)<=(1+sqrt(lambda/mu))*exp(-(sqrt(mu)-sqrt(lambda))^2*T), hence sufficient k=o((n/log(n))^(1/3)). A conditional polynomial tail T^(-p) instead gives sufficient exponent p/(3*p+1). Credits the prior finite-time coupling method; general service, optimal exponents and novelty remain unresolved.

Status: private author-checked partial result for P0429. No independent review or novelty certification. The general finite-second-moment service question is not solved. The basic collision and empty-start coupling method is already in Wang et al., *Delay Asymptotics and Bounds for Multi-Task Parallel Jobs*, Sections 3-5, archived as `queues_limited_forkjoin_2018`. We credit that method and its $k=o(n^{1/4})$ theorem. This packet sharpens the marginal emptying-time step under an additional exponential-service assumption and restores thinned arrival rates explicitly.

## Model and candidate bound

There are $n\ge2$ FIFO servers. Jobs arrive as a Poisson process of rate $\Lambda=n\lambda/k$, independently select uniform $k$-subsets of servers, and place one task in each selected queue. Service requirements of all tasks, including different tasks of the same job, are independent and identically distributed, independent of routing and arrivals. Fix the marginal rate $0<\lambda<\mu$, with mean service $1/\mu$. Let $\pi_{n,k}$ be the stationary joint workload law at any specified $k$ servers, and let $\nu_k$ be the product of their marginal stationary workload laws. Total variation uses $\sup_A|\pi(A)-\nu(A)|$.

Write $r(T)$ for the probability that a stationary marginal M/G/1 workload has not hit zero by time $T$. The modular coupling bound is

$$d_{\rm TV}(\pi_{n,k},\nu_k)\le 2k r(T)+\frac{3\lambda T k(k-1)^2}{2(n-1)},\qquad T>0.$$

With exponential service of rate $\mu$, put $\rho=\lambda/\mu$ and $c=(\sqrt\mu-\sqrt\lambda)^2>0$. Then

$$r(T)\le(1+\sqrt\rho)e^{-cT},$$

so the candidate explicit stationary bound is

$$d_{\rm TV}(\pi_{n,k},\nu_k)\le 2k(1+\sqrt\rho)e^{-cT}+\frac{3\lambda T k(k-1)^2}{2(n-1)}.$$

Either right-hand side may also be capped at one. The constants are uniform in $n,k$ at fixed $\lambda,\mu$.

## Step 1: independent arrivals with exactly restored marginal rates

Fix the tagged set $K$ with $|K|=k$. For one job let $N$ count selected servers in $K$. Counting ordered pairs gives

$$\mathbb E[N(N-1)]=\frac{k^2(k-1)^2}{n(n-1)}.$$

Poisson marking decomposes the arrival stream into independent streams indexed by its selected tagged subset. Retain every singleton-tagged arrival, discard all arrivals hitting two or more tagged queues, and add independent Poisson arrivals to each tagged queue at the marginal rate removed from that queue. The resulting $k$ arrival processes are independent Poisson processes of rate exactly $\lambda$. Give added tasks independent service requirements with the original law, and use identical marks on shared singleton arrivals.

Over $[0,T]$, the probability of any discrepancy is bounded by the expected number of discarded job events plus the expected total number of added task events. These are bounded by

$$\Lambda T\left(\mathbb P(N\ge2)+\mathbb E[N\mathbf1_{N\ge2}]\right)\le\frac32\Lambda T\mathbb E[N(N-1)].$$

Here $1\le N(N-1)/2$ and $N\le N(N-1)$ when $N\ge2$. Substitution of $\Lambda=n\lambda/k$ yields the collision term in the stated bound. This argument is nonasymptotic and does not require $2k\le n$.

Start the original and modified queues empty. Until the first discrepancy their tagged workload paths agree, because they have identical tagged arrival times and task marks. Thus the same bound controls total variation at time $T$.

## Step 2: couple empty starts to stationary starts

For the original system, couple one copy with stationary workloads at time zero to a copy with empty workloads, using the same future routing, arrivals and service marks. The stationary workload is coordinatewise above the empty-start workload. Whenever a stationary coordinate hits zero, both copies have zero workload there and then agree forever at that coordinate.

Each stationary coordinate is a marginal M/G/1 queue with the same $\lambda$ and service law, even though coordinates are dependent. By a union bound, the probability that any of the $k$ coordinates has failed to couple by $T$ is at most $kr(T)$. The independent comparison system has the same marginal law, so its own stationary-versus-empty coupling has the same bound. The triangle inequality between these two comparisons and Step 1 proves the modular estimate. Independence of the original stationary coordinates is neither assumed nor required.

## Step 3: exponential-service emptying tail

Consider the marginal M/M/1 queue count $Q$ until its first hit $\tau_0$ of zero. For $q\ge1$, its generator applied to $h(q)=a^q$, with $a=\sqrt{\mu/\lambda}>1$, is

$$\frac{{\cal L}h(q)}{h(q)}=\lambda(a-1)+\mu(a^{-1}-1)=-(\sqrt\mu-\sqrt\lambda)^2=-c.$$

Stopping first at zero and at a finite upper count level makes the standard exponential generator martingale legitimate. Nonnegativity and Fatou's lemma upon removal of the upper stopping level give

$$\mathbb E_q\left[e^{c(T\wedge\tau_0)}a^{Q(T\wedge\tau_0)}\right]\le a^q.$$

On $\{\tau_0>T\}$ the integrand is at least $e^{cT}$, so $\mathbb P_q(\tau_0>T)\le a^qe^{-cT}$. Averaging over the stationary geometric queue count yields

$$\mathbb E[a^{Q(0)}]=\frac{1-\rho}{1-\rho a}=\frac{1-\rho}{1-\sqrt\rho}=1+\sqrt\rho.$$

A marginal workload is zero exactly when its queue count is zero. The count process here is used only to bound this marginal stopping time; the pathwise workload coupling in Step 2 remains driven by shared task marks. No erroneous identification of arbitrary coupled count and workload paths is needed.

## Consequences and limits

Taking $T=2\log n/c$ gives

$$d_{\rm TV}(\pi_{n,k},\nu_k)\le\frac{2k(1+\sqrt\rho)}{n^2}+\frac{3\lambda k(k-1)^2\log n}{c(n-1)}.$$

Hence the distance tends to zero when $k=o((n/\log n)^{1/3})$ under exponential service. This is a sufficient regime, not an optimal threshold, and says nothing at the boundary $k\asymp n^{1/3}$ by itself. Poisson arrivals see the stationary pre-arrival workload law by PASTA. The arriving job selects its uniform target set independently of that law; exchangeability makes its selected workloads have the law of the specified tagged set. Appending independent tagged-job service requirements and taking a maximum is a Markov kernel, so total variation contracts; the same error controls the job-delay distribution against the independent comparison.

More generally, if $r(T)\le C T^{-p}$ for some fixed $p>0$, the modular estimate gives an error of order $k/T^p+Tk^3/n$. Balancing at $T\asymp(n/k^2)^{1/(p+1)}$ gives the sufficient regime $k=o(n^{p/(3p+1)})$. This conclusion is conditional on the stated emptying-tail bound; no unproved implication from a service moment is used. For $p=1$, the source's finite-second-moment estimate recovers the known exponent $1/4$.

## Attempts to break the argument

The vulnerable points are the growing number of tagged queues, simultaneous multi-hit arrivals, the marginal rate after removing those arrivals, and the passage to stationarity. The proof restores lost marginal rates rather than silently comparing to lower-load queues. It uses a union bound over all $k$ queues and retains both empty-start errors. The exponential tail constant tends to zero as load approaches one, so this packet does not claim a uniform heavy-traffic result. Correlated within-job service marks are excluded. Exponential control of the stationary emptying time has not been proved here for general service laws.

The original paper already has the same broad finite-time/emptying-time proof structure and numerical experiments at larger exponents. The observation here could be a known or straightforward corollary; bounded search is not a novelty certificate. No full original open-problem solution is promoted. Arithmetic controls are in `check_forkjoin_stationary.py` and `forkjoin_stationary_checks.json`.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:a619d7dacb1a00e81c0fd7880a8238307c0094169dc2d53c70b64cc661abaf09","revision_digest":"sha256:d253e2e3cbdb2c0e440a7f9838e7636022d4551fd8fbbf029c6fec68ce834cac","source_id":"owner-probability-exposition-20260907:fork","source_revision":"author-checked-private-20260907-v1","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

satisfying:

\smallskip
 $(i)$ for every $i\!\in \{1,\ldots,n\}$,
\[

C_i(x) \subset  \bigcap_{j=1}^n \big \{\xi\!\in U: \phi_{_F}(\xi,x_i) \le  \phi_{_F}(\xi,x_j)\big\},
\]

 $(ii)$ if $C_i(x)\neq \varnothing$ and $x_j=x_i$, then $C_j(x)= \varnothing$,

\smallskip
 \noindent is called an {\em $F$-Bregman--Voronoi partition} (or more simply a {\em Bregman--Voronoi partition}) induced by the $n$-tuple $x$.

Let (X, Sigma, mu) be a measure space, 0 < p_0 < p_1 <= infinity, 0 < theta < 1, and define p by 1/p = (1-theta)/p_0 + theta/p_1. Then for every measurable f, ||f||_p <= ||f||_{p_0}^{1-theta} ||f||_{p_1}^{theta} (convention 0 * infinity = 0). Consequently L^{p_0} intersect L^{p_1} is contained in L^p for every intermediate p, and t -> log ||f||_{1/t} is a convex function of t in [0, 1/p_0] where finite. This is the 'trivial' (one-function) interpolation inequality; the operator analogue is the Riesz-Thorin theorem.

body:
Let (X,d) be a metric space and let f : X -> (-infinity, +infinity] be lower semicontinuous and bounded below. For each n define f_n(x) = inf over y in X of ( f(y) + n d(x,y) ). Then each f_n is real-valued and n-Lipschitz, the sequence is nondecreasing, f_n <= f for every n, and f_n(x) increases to f(x) at every x. So a lower semicontinuous function bounded below is the pointwise increasing limit of Lipschitz functions. On a Hilbert space with the quadratic kernel (1/(2t))||x-y||^2 in place of n d(x,y) the same construction gives the Moreau envelope of a convex f, which is convex, differentiable with Lipschitz gradient, and increases to f as t decreases to 0.
f lower semicontinuous AND bounded below (boundedness below can be relaxed to a linear minorant);
the approximation is from BELOW and increasing.
For an upper semicontinuous f bounded above the dual sup-convolution gives a decreasing sequence of Lipschitz functions.

The classical Aizenman-Burchard condition establishes tightness of random curves confined to a compact region (planar or spatial) under uniform power bounds P(N_{r, R}^x(gamma_n) >= N) <= K_N (r/R)^{lambda_N} with lambda_N -> infinity. Sequential tightness relaxes this by eliminating the requirement of power decay uniform over all moduli r/R: precompactness holds, for curves in a compact (geodesic) metric space X, under non-uniform regularity lim_{N -> infinity} sup_n P(N_{r, R}^x >= N) = 0 for each fixed annulus (compactness is needed: constant curves escaping to infinity cross no annulus yet are not tight), accommodating pathological curves (such as logarithmic spirals) where scale-invariant power bounds fail.

body: [Definition 5 (Iterative directed graph process) of arXiv:2608.07239, 'Unified framework for asymptotically uniform iterative construction of generalised random '] Consider the vertex set $V=\{v_1,\ldots,v_n\}$, consider degree sequences $\d=(d_1,\ldots,d_n)$ and $\d'=(d_1',\ldots,d_{n}')$ of non-negative integers with $m:=d_1+\ldots+d_n=d_1'+\ldots+d_{n}'>0$, and consider a set $X$ of forbidden arcs. We define $\widetilde{V}:=A \cup B$ with $A=\{w_1,\ldots,w_n\}$ and $B=\{w_1',\ldots,w_n'\}$ disjoint, and $$\widetilde{X}:=\{(w_i,w_j'):(v_i,v_j)\in X\}\cup\{(w_i,w_i'):i=1,\ldots,n\}.$$ Consider sampling a bipartite graph from the iterative bipartite graph process on $\widetilde{V}$, $\d$, $\d'$, and $\widetilde{X}$. Identify any pair $w_i$, $w_i'$ with the vertex $v_i$ and any edge $(w_i,w_j')$ with an arc from $v_i$ to $v_j$. This results in a simple directed graph with out- and in- degree sequences $\d$ and $\d'$ and with no arcs from $X$.
title: Iterative directed graph process

[Lemma lem:a6 of arXiv:2607.24164, 'The KLS constant is $O(\log^{1/4} n)$'] Under the regularity assumptions of (lem:a1 of the paper),
every bounded smooth function $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfies
\[
  \Var_{Y\sim\nu}(f(Y))
  \leqslant
  \mathbb{E}_{Y\sim\nu}\!\left[
    \varphi^{ab}(Y)(\partial_af)(Y)(\partial_bf)(Y)
  \right],
\]
where the right-hand side is allowed to be infinite.

body:
[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2609.03495, 'Spectral Characteristics of Autoencoder Parameters as a Vector Representation of Data'] Suppose that assumptions (B1)--(B6) hold. We introduce the notation ${\Delta_r := \|\boldsymbol{\sigma}_{1:r}^{data}(\mathbf{X}_1)-\boldsymbol{\sigma}_{1:r}^{data}(\mathbf{X}_2)\|_2,}$ where $\boldsymbol{\sigma}^{data}_{1:r}(\cdot)$ denotes the singular values of the data matrices $\mathbf{X}_c$ from the first to the $r$-th.

\noindent Then there exist constants \({C_0>0}\) and \({c_*>0}\) such that, for any \({\delta\in(0;\frac{1}{2})}\), for a sample size \(n\), with probability at least \({1-2\delta}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\big\|\boldsymbol{\sigma}_{1:r}^{model}(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\psi}}_n(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_1))-
\boldsymbol{\sigma}_{1:r}^{model}(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\psi}}_n(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_2))\big\|_2
\ge c_*\Delta_r - C_0\Bigl(\sqrt{\tfrac{\log(1/\delta)}{n^2}} + \sqrt{\eta_n} + \tau_n\Bigr),
\end{aligned}
\]
where \({\tau_n := \max(\tau_n^1, \tau_n^2)}\) is the maximum of the optimization errors for models trained on samples of size $n$ using $\mathbf{X}_1$ and $\mathbf{X}_2$.

In particular, if \({\Delta_r>0}\) and \({\eta_n,\tau_n \to 0}\), then as \({n \to \infty}\), the right-hand side remains positive, and the vectors of the first \(r\) singular values remain separated by a nonzero gap with probability tending to 1. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 5 of arXiv:2609.03495

[Lemma lem:lower_bound_gaussian_lim of arXiv:2411.03609, 'Asymptotically optimal Wasserstein couplings for the small-time stable domain of attractio'] Let $\bm{X}$ be a L\'evy process on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with 
the characteristic triplet $(\bm{\gamma_X},\bm{\Sigma_X}\bm{\Sigma_X}^{\scalebox{0.6}{$\top$}},\nu_{\bm{X}})$.
For $t\in (0,1]$, denote
$\bm{X}^t=(\bm{X}_{st}/\sqrt{t})_{s\in[0,1]}$. Moreover, let $\bm{\Sigma_X}\bm{B}$ be the
Gaussian component of $\bm{X}$ in its L\'evy--It\^o decomposition~(equation eq:levy_ito_decomp of the paper) and define 
  $\bm{S}\coloneqq \bm{X}-\bm{\Sigma_X}\bm{B}$ with L\'evy--Khintchine exponent $\psi_{\bm{S}}$.\\
{\normalfont(a)} Pick any $\bm{u}_*\in\mathbb{R}^d_{\bm{0}}$ and define $C_*\coloneqq |\bm{u}_*|^{-1}|\psi_{\bm{S}_1}(\bm{u}_*)|>0$. Then, we have 
\begin{align*}
\mathcal{W}_1(\bm{X}^t_1,\bm{\Sigma}_{\bm{X}}\bm{B}_1)
    \geqslant C_*\sqrt{t}+ \mathcal{O}(t^{3/2}),
\quad\text{as }t \downarrow 0.
\end{align*}
{\normalfont(b)} Let $\lambda$ be the largest eigenvalue of $\bm{\Sigma}_{\bm{X}}\bm{\Sigma}^{\scalebox{0.6}{$\top$}}_{\bm{X}}$. Suppose there exist $\delta\in[1,2)$ and vectors  $(\bm{u}_r)_{r\in(0,\infty)}$ on $\mathbb{R}^d_{\bm{0}}$ satisfying $|\bm{u}_r|=r$ and $c:=\inf_{r>1}r^{-\delta}|\psi_{\bm{S}}(\bm{u}_r)|>0$. Then for any $C_*\in(0,ce^{-\lambda/2})$ we have
\[
\mathcal{W}_1(\bm{X}^t_1,\bm{\Sigma}_{\bm{X}}\bm{B}_1) \geqslant C_* t^{1-\delta/2}
\qquad\text{for all sufficiently small }t>0.
\]
title: Lemma lem:lower_bound_gaussian_lim of arXiv:2411.03609

body:
[Definition def:pseudo of arXiv:2608.01253, 'The pseudo-quantum representation of \\finite reversible Markov chains'] For an initial law $\pi_0$, $\widehat\pi_0:=\binom{\pi_0}{0}$, set $\Phi_0:=B\widehat\pi_0$ and, for $z\in\mathbb{C}$,

\[
\Phi_z:=W_z\Phi_0\in\mathbb{C}^{2M}\quad(\text{the \emph{pseudo-wave}}),\qquad
\rho_z:=\Phi_z\Phi_z^{T}\in\operatorname{Sym}_{2M}(\mathbb{C})\quad(\text{the \emph{pseudo-density}}).
\]

The superscript $T$ is the plain transpose, with no complex conjugation, so
$\rho_z$ is complex symmetric and in general not Hermitian.
title: Pseudo-wave and pseudo-density

[Lemma lem:deriveSPDE of arXiv:2608.27828, 'Scaling limit of the 3D abelian Yang--Mills Langevin dynamics'] On the time interval $t<\tau_\varepsilon$ where $\tau_\varepsilon$ is as in (equation e:def-tau of the paper), the DeTurck-gauge-fixed Langevin dynamics (equation eq:NParaDisc of the paper) can be written as
\begin{equ}

\partial_t \theta^\varepsilon(e)  
 = \Delta_\varepsilon \theta^\varepsilon
+ a_3 \, \varepsilon^4 \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}_\varepsilon^* \,(\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}_\varepsilon \theta^\varepsilon)^3(e)

+ \varepsilon^{-2} \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}_\varepsilon^* (\mathfrak{R}(\varepsilon^2 \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}_\varepsilon \theta^\varepsilon))(e)
+\xi^\varepsilon
\end{equ}
where  $a_3 = -\frac16 h^{(4)}(0)$ and $\mathfrak{R}(z):=
    z-a_{3}z^3-h'(z)$.

Moreover, there exists $C>0$, independent of $\eps$, such that, for all $z\in [-\rho_0,\rho_0]$,
\begin{equ}[e:coeff-bounds]
|a_3|\le C,
\qquad
|\mathfrak R(z)|\le C|z|^5.
\end{equ} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:deriveSPDE of arXiv:2608.27828

[Theorem thm:radial-ig of arXiv:2411.19810, 'Radial conformal welding in Liouville quantum gravity'] Let $\beta,\rho_1,...,\rho_n\in\mathbb{R}$, define $\alpha$ as in~(equation eq:radial-alpha of the paper),  and let $h$ be the GFF on $\mathbb{D}$ described  above. Then there exists a unique coupling between $h+\alpha\arg(\cdot)+\beta\log|\cdot|$ and a radial $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa^\beta(\underline\rho)$ process in $\mathbb{D}$ from $-i$ targeted at 0 with force points $x_1,...,x_n$ such that the following holds. For every $\eta$-stopping time $\tau$, the conditional law of $h+\alpha\arg(\cdot)+\beta\log|\cdot|$ given $\eta|_{[0,\tau]}$ is that of $\tilde h+\alpha\arg(\cdot)+\beta\log|\cdot|$ where $\tilde h$ is a GFF on $\mathbb{D}\backslash\eta([0,\tau])$ such that $\tilde h+\alpha\arg(\cdot)+\beta\log|\cdot|$ has the same boundary conditions as $h+\alpha\arg(\cdot)+\beta\log|\cdot|$ on $\partial \mathbb D$. If $\kappa\in(0,4)$, then $\tilde h+\alpha\arg(\cdot)+\beta\log|\cdot|$ has $-\alpha$-flow line boundary conditions on $\eta([0,\tau])$. If $\kappa'>4$, then $\tilde h+\alpha\arg(\cdot)+\beta\log|\cdot|$ has $-\alpha$-flow line boundary conditions with angle $\frac{\pi}{2}$ (resp.\ $-\frac{\pi}{2}$) on the left (resp.\ right) side of $\eta([0,\tau])$. 
	
	    In this coupling, $\eta([0,\tau])$ is a local set of $h$, and $\eta$ is measurable with respect to $h$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:radial-ig of arXiv:2411.19810

for every $t>0$.

\item
For $\cV=\cV_{\max}$, let $e\in\{\ell,r\}$ and suppose that $\mu$ has
finite mass near $e$. Then, for every $t>0$,
\[
  \lim_{x\to e}
  \frac{\partial_xu(t,x)}{\rho(x)}

where the limit is taken within $I$. If, in addition, $\rho$ is bounded
near $e$, then
$
  \lim_{x\to e}\partial_xu(t,x)=0.
$
\end{enumerate}

For n>=64 let R_n be symmetric +/-1 and B_n an independent Bernoulli variable with p_n=exp(-sqrt(n)). Set X_n=n^{1/3}R_n+(n/4)(B_n-p_n), Y_n=3n/2+X_n. Then EX_n=0, n<=Y_n<=2n, and Var X_n=n^{2/3}+(n^2/16)p_n(1-p_n)~n^{2/3}. For this family define chi_a=inf{a: for some alpha>0, sup_n E exp(alpha|X_n|/n^a)<infinity} and chi_b=sup{b: for some c>0,N, Var X_n>=c n^{2b} for all n>=N}. One has chi_a=1/2 and chi_b=1/3. Thus a pure variance power law and uniform square-root exponential concentration do not by themselves identify the two fluctuation thresholds. Indexing by lattice endpoints with n=ceil(|v|) preserves the gap. This is an abstract random-variable family, not an FPP metric or iid-edge construction, and it does not refute P0110.

[Lemma 13 of arXiv:2606.09691, '\textsc{Degenerate Diffusions on Continuum Percolation and Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman Equatio'] Let $U\subsetneq \mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty open set, and let
\[
d_U(x):=\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial U),\qquad x\in U.
\]
Then there exists a construction 
\[
U \mapsto \rho_U \qquad\mbox{with} \qquad \rho_U\in C^\infty(U),\qquad \rho>0 \text{ in }U,
\]
such that for every $x\in U$, we have
\begin{equation}
c\, d_U(x)\le \rho_U(x)\le C\, d_U(x), \qquad\text{and}\qquad 
|D^\alpha \rho_U|\leq C_{|\alpha|} d_U(x)^{1-|\alpha|} 
 \text{ for }\alpha \in \mathbb N_0^d,  
\end{equation}
where the constant  $ C_{|\alpha|}$  depends only on $d$ and 
 $|\alpha|=\sum_1^d \alpha_i$. In particular, $|\nabla \rho_U(x)|\le C_1$ and $\rho_U$ is globally Lipschitz on $U$, and its extension by $0$ on $\mathbb R^d\setminus U$ is globally Lipschitz on $\mathbb R^d$.

Moreover, the construction is translation-covariant in the sense 
\begin{equation}
\rho_{U+z}(x+z)=\rho_U(x) \qquad\forall x\in U.
\end{equation}

[Theorem th 4.3 of arXiv:2511.07173, '\bf Mean-field backward stochastic Volterra integral equations: well-posedness and related'] \rm
	Under (ass4.1 of the paper), BSVIE ((1.1 of the paper))  admits a unique global adapted solution
	$(Y(\cdot), Z(\cdot,\cdot))\in L^\infty_{\mathbb{F}}[0,T]\times  {\cal Z}^2_{\mathbb{F}}(\Delta[0,T];\mathbb{R}^d).$  Moreover, there exist two positive constants
	$M_1$ and $M_2$  depending on  $K_1,K_3, T,\tilde{\gamma},\gamma_0, \beta,\beta_0,\alpha$ such that
	\begin{equation*}
		\|Y(\cdot)\|_{L_{\mathbb{F}}^\infty[0,T]}\leqslant M_1\quad\hbox{and}\quad\ \|Z(\cdot,\cdot)\|^2_{{\cal Z}^2_{\mathbb{F}}(\Delta[0,T])}\leqslant M_2.
	\end{equation*}
title: Theorem th 4.3 of arXiv:2511.07173

[Proposition 3 of arXiv:2605.05388, 'The Efron-Stein inequality for identically distributed pairs'] Let \(\epsilon\in \mathbb R\), let \(X_i\) be uniform on \([0,2\pi]\) and let \(Y_i\) equal \(X_i+2\epsilon\) mod \(2\pi\). Then \(X_i\stackrel{d}{=}Y_i\). Assume that the pairs \((X_i,Y_i)\) are independent as \(i\) varies. Let \(f(x_1,\ldots x_n)=\sin(x_1+\ldots +x_n)\), and let \(Z_i=f(X_1,\ldots X_{i},Y_{i+1},\ldots Y_n)\). Then the random variables \(Z_i\) (and hence the ratio on the left-hand side of \eqref{e}) depend on \(\epsilon\), and we have
\begin{equation}
\lim_{\epsilon\to 0} \frac
{E(Z_n-Z_0)^2}{\sum_{i=1}^n E(Z_i-Z_{i-1})^2}=n.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

also called the relative entropy, of $\mu$ relative to $\nu$ is
\[
  \KL(\mu\|\nu)
  :=\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}
     \mu(\omega)\log\frac{\mu(\omega)}{\nu(\omega)},
\]
with the conventions
$0\log\frac0y=0$ for $y\geq 0$ and $x\log\frac x0=+\infty$ for $x>0$.

Let $T>0$ and $u\in C^2_1(\mathbb R^n\times(0,T])\cap C(\mathbb R^n\times[0,T])$ satisfy $u_t-\Delta u=0$ in $\mathbb R^n\times(0,T)$ and $u(\cdot,0)=g$. If there are constants $A,a>0$ with $u(x,t)\le Ae^{a|x|^2}$ for all $x\in\mathbb R^n$, $0\le t\le T$, then $\sup_{\mathbb R^n\times[0,T]}u=\sup_{\mathbb R^n}g$ (maximum principle for the Cauchy problem). Consequently, for continuous $f$ and $g$, the problem $u_t-\Delta u=f$ in $\mathbb R^n\times(0,T)$, $u(\cdot,0)=g$, has at most one solution in $C^2_1(\mathbb R^n\times(0,T])\cap C(\mathbb R^n\times[0,T])$ satisfying $|u(x,t)|\le Ae^{a|x|^2}$ on $\mathbb R^n\times[0,T]$ with $A,a$ independent of $t$. The growth hypothesis cannot be dropped (Tychonoff's example).

body:
Backward uniqueness says the map from $u(\cdot,T)$ to $u(\cdot,0)$ is injective; it says nothing about continuity of that map or about its range, and both fail badly -- the backward heat problem is the standard ill-posed problem of Hadamard. (1) No stability: on $U=(0,\pi)$ with Dirichlet data, $u_k(x,t)=e^{-k^2t}\sin(kx)$ has $\|u_k(\cdot,T)\|_{C^m}\le k^me^{-k^2T}\to0$ for every $m$ while $\|u_k(\cdot,0)\|_{L^2}=\sqrt{\pi/2}$ is fixed. Hence there is no estimate $\|u(\cdot,0)\|\le C\|u(\cdot,T)\|$ in any pair of norms, and numerical backward continuation must be regularized. (2) No solvability: $e^{T\Delta_D}$ has range $\{\psi=\sum_kc_k\sin(kx):\sum_k e^{2k^2T}c_k^2<\infty\}$, a dense but meagre subspace of $L^2$; for instance $\psi(x)=\sum_{k\ge1}k^{-2}\sin(kx)\in L^2$ is not $u(\cdot,T)$ for any solution with $u(\cdot,0)\in L^2$, since that would require coefficients $e^{k^2T}k^{-2}$ at time $0$. Backward-in-time data must be analytic-like (exponentially decaying spectral coefficients). (3) What does survive is conditional stability of logarithmic or Holder type: under the a priori bound $\|u(\cdot,0)\|_{L^2}\le M$, log-convexity gives $\|u(\cdot,t)\|_{L^2}\le M^{1-t/T}\|u(\cdot,T)\|_{L^2}^{t/T}$ for $0<t<T$, with the estimate degenerating exactly as $t\downarrow0$. An auditor should flag any argument that uses backward uniqueness to produce a bound at the earlier time without such an a priori bound.
Injectivity of the solution map does not imply continuity of its inverse
The range of the forward solution operator is a proper dense subspace
Conditional (Holder) stability requires an a priori bound at the initial time and degenerates as t tends to 0
title: Pitfall: Backward uniqueness is not backward stability or backward solvability

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2605.11279, 'Flocking with Multiple Types: Competition, Fluid Limits and Traveling Waves'] We have the following:
    \begin{enumerate}[label = (\alph*)]
        \item  Suppose that Assumptions \ref{assumption0} and \ref{assumption2} hold. Then the sequence $\{\mu_n(\cdot)\!: n\in\nat\}$ is $\mathscr{C}$-tight in the space $\mathscr{D}\big([0, \infty), \mathscr{P}_1(\real\times \{+,-\})\big)$. 

        \item  In addition, suppose that Assumptions \ref{assumption3} and \ref{assumption4} hold. Then any subsequential weak limit point $\mu(\cdot)$ of $\{\mu_n(\cdot)\!: n\in\nat\}$ in $\DDD\big([0, \infty), \PPP_1(\real \times \{+, -\})\big)$ satisfies \eqref{originalMVE}, the McKean-Vlasov equation, for $t \ge 0$ and $f \in \HHH$. Moreover, there exists a $B_0 \in (0,\infty)$, depending only on $C_0$ in Assumption \ref{assumption3} and the jump distribution $J$ such that, almost surely, $\mu \in \TTT_{B_0}$.

        \item  Furthermore, if $\mu_n(0) \cpinf{n} \nu$ in $\PPP_1\bigparens{\real \times \{+, -\}}$, where $\nu$ is deterministic, then $\mu_n(\cdot) \cpinf{n} \mu(\cdot)$ in $\DDD\big([0, \infty), \PPP_1(\real \times \{+, -\})\big)$, where $\mu(\cdot)$ is the unique and deterministic solution to \eqref{originalMVE} in $\TTT_{B_0}$ with initial condition $\mu(0) = \nu$. 
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Defn 7 of arXiv:2609.00723, 'An integral Hyodo--Kato isomorphism'] Let $\sA=(A,\alpha:L\to A)\in \mathrm{PreLog}_{\sR}$. Note that we have $\widehat{\omega}_{\sA/\sR}^* /p \simeq {\omega}_{\sA/p/\sR/p}^*$.

body:
[Corollary 4 (Exact posterior--prior reverse-path relative entropy) of arXiv:2608.21709, 'Posterior Information Dynamics of Diffusion Models for Linear Inverse Problems'] Fix $T>t>0$.  On the reverse clock $u\in[0,T-t]$, let
$\mathbb Q^{r,\mathrm{rev}}_{[t,T]}$ and
$\mathbb P^{\mathrm{rev}}_{[t,T]}$ be the time-reversal pushforwards of the
forward OU path laws initialized from $q_t^r$ and $p_t$, respectively.
When the noised marginals are smooth and positive, they coincide with the
reverse processes \eqref{eq:posterior-reverse-sde} and
\eqref{eq:prior-reverse-sde}, initialized from $q_T^r$ and $p_T$.
Assume the hypotheses of
Theorem~\ref{thm:fixed-r-entropy-dissipation} on \([t,T]\).  Then
\begin{equation}

\KL\!\left(
\mathbb Q^{r,\mathrm{rev}}_{[t,T]}
\middle\|
\mathbb P^{\mathrm{rev}}_{[t,T]}
\right)
=
\mathcal K_t(r)
=
\mathcal K_T(r)+
\int_t^T\E_{X_u\mid r}\|g_u(X_u,r)\|^2\,\dd u.
\end{equation}
Under the normalization $\dd X_t=-X_t\dd t+\sqrt2\dd W_t$, the coefficient of
the integral is one: the two reverse drifts differ by $2g_t$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Exact posterior--prior reverse-path relative entropy

  \end{enumerate}

body: [Definition Jordan curve of arXiv:2604.04672, 'Connected components and topological ends of stationary planar forests'] A subset $J\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ is called a Jordan curve if there exists a continuous bijection $\mathbb S^1\to J$. By the Jordan curve theorem (see [topology_book]), $\mathbb{R}^2\setminus J$ then consists of exactly two open connected components, one bounded and one unbounded, denoted $\mathrm{Int} J$ and $\mathrm{Ext} J$, respectively, both having boundary $J$. The closures of $\mathrm{Int} J$ and $\mathrm{Ext} J$ are denoted by $\overline{\mathrm{Int}} J$ and $\overline{\mathrm{Ext}} J$, respectively.
title: Jordan curve

[Lemme 59 (Principle of Domination) of arXiv:2604.00635, 'Large deviations of the periodic Toda chain'] Let $\mu \in \mathcal{M}_1(\mathbb{R})$ be  compactly supported and such that

$$\Int{\mathbb{R}^2}{} \ln \frac{1}{|x-y|}\, \mathrm{d}\mu(x) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) < +\infty \,. $$

Suppose there exists a constant $C$ such that

$$ \Int{\mathbb{R}}{} \ln|x-y| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \geq C \qquad \dd \mu(x)-\e{a.e.} \; on \;\;  \mathrm{supp}[\mu] \;. $$

Then, in fact,

$$ \Int{\mathbb{R}}{} \ln|x-y| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \geq C  \qquad \text{for every} \quad  x \in \mathbb{R} \, .$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Principle of Domination

Every elliptic curve E over Q is modular: if N is its conductor, its L-function is the L-function of a weight-2 newform of level N; equivalently, E admits a nonconstant morphism from the modular curve X_0(N). Wiles and Taylor-Wiles proved the semistable case, which with Frey's construction and Ribet's theorem implies Fermat's Last Theorem, and Breuil, Conrad, Diamond and Taylor completed the theorem for all elliptic curves over Q (2001). It is the GL_2 case of the bridge the Langlands program predicts between arithmetic and automorphic forms.
E is an elliptic curve over Q
N is the conductor of E

[Prop cA of arXiv:2609.01501, 'Singularities of star cluster algebras'] Let the situation be as in Def.~(Def:cA of the paper).
	Set $ \alpha := \# \{ a \in \{ 1, \ldots, n \} \mid q_a = 1 \} $.
	For $ j \in \{ 0, \ldots, n - 2 \} $,
	we have 
	\[
		\mathcal{A} (n;\boldsymbol{q}; j) 
		\ = \ 
		\sum_{k=0}^{n-j} 
		\binom{n-\alpha}{n-j-k} \binom{\alpha}{k} 2^{\alpha - k}
	\]

	and
	\[
	\mathcal{A} (n;\boldsymbol{q}) 
	\ = \ 
	3^\alpha 2^{n-\alpha}  
	- ( n + 1) 2^{\alpha} 
	+ \alpha 2^{\alpha - 1}
	\ .
	\]

[2 7 of arXiv:2506.08874, 'On Limiting Probability Distributions of Higher Order Markov Chains'] Let $X=\{X_t : t=1, 2, \ldots\}$ be an $(m-1)$th order Markov chain on state space $S$ whose transition tensor is $\cal P$. If there exists a nonnegative $\pi \in \mathbb R^n$ such that $\ds \sum_{i=1}^n \pi_i = 1$ and 
$\ds{\lim_{k \rightarrow \infty} {\cal P}^{(k)}=\pi \otimes \underbrace{e \otimes \cdots \otimes e}_{m-1}}$, then 
$$
\lim_{t \rightarrow \infty}\Pr(X_t=i)=\pi_i
$$
for each $i \in S$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2609.03495, 'Spectral Characteristics of Autoencoder Parameters as a Vector Representation of Data'] Let three datasets be given: ${\mathbf{X}_1 \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times d}}$, ${\mathbf{X}_2 \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times d}}$, and ${\mathbf{X}_3 \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times d}}$; let their singular values be positive: ${\sigma_i^{\text{data}}(\mathbf{X}_c) > 0 ~~~ \forall i \in \overline{1, d}}$.

Let two new datasets be obtained by mixing vectors from the third dataset into each of the first two datasets: ${\tilde{\mathbf{X}}_c = [\mathbf{X}_c, \mathbf{X}_3] \in \mathbb{R}^{(n+m) \times d}, ~~~ c \in \{1, 2\}}$.

Suppose that an autoencoder model with fully connected layers without nonlinear activation functions and latent dimension $k$ is trained on each dataset, minimizing the loss function
${\min_{\boldsymbol{\psi}_c}(\mathcal{L}(\boldsymbol{\psi}_c)) = \min_{\boldsymbol{\psi}_c} \|\tilde{\mathbf{X}}_c - \tilde{\mathbf{X}}_c\mathbf{W}_{c}^{enc}\mathbf{W}_{c}^{dec\top}\|_F^2}$
with a regularization term of the form ${\|\text{cov}(\mathbf{h}) - \mathbf{I}\|^2}$, which decorrelates the vectors $\mathbf{h}$ in the latent space, i.e., ${\text{cov}(\mathbf{h}) \sim I}$.

Then the mean squared difference between the singular values of the parameters of the autoencoders with parameters $\mathbf{W}^{enc}_1$, $\mathbf{W}^{dec}_1$, $\mathbf{W}^{enc}_2$, $\mathbf{W}^{dec}_2$ decreases as $m$ increases:
\[
\|\sigma_i^{\text{model}}(\mathbf{W}^{enc}_1) - \sigma_i^{\text{model}}(\mathbf{W}^{enc}_2)\|_2 \underset{m \to \infty}{\longrightarrow} 0,
\]
Consequently, as the datasets converge, both their singular values and the singular values of the parameters of the autoencoders trained on these datasets converge as the number of rows $m$ tends to infinity. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 3 of arXiv:2609.03495

$$ 
\lim_{t \to \infty} \inf_{\|x\| \leq t^{\sigma}} \frac{p_t^{y_1-x}}{p_t^{y_2-x}} = \lim_{t \to \infty} \sup_{\|x\| \leq t^{\sigma}} \frac{p_t^{y_1-x}}{p_t^{y_2-x}} = 1. 
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

If $\mathcal{W}$ is a joint stationary distribution of an $(m-1)$th order Markov chain  $\{X_t\}_{t=1}^{\infty}$ on state space $S$, then $\pi \in \mathbb{R}^n$
defined by
\be

\pi_i = \sum_{i_2,\ldots, i_{m-1} \in S} w_{i i_2 \ldots i_{m-1}}
\ee
is called a marginal stationary distribution of the chain.
}
title: Definition 7 of arXiv:2607.12303

[Theorem thm:cluster_expansion of arXiv:2604.18558, 'Uniform analyticity of local observables in FK-percolation and analyticity of the Ising sp'] Assume that for $\epsilon > 0$ small enough, there exists a constant $C_\epsilon > 0$, going to 0 when $\epsilon$ tends to 0, such that for any $|z| < \epsilon$, for every polymer $\gamma \in \mathsf{P}^L_N$, 
\[
|\mathsf{w}_z(\gamma)| \leq C_\epsilon \exp( - |\gamma|(1 + c(d))).
\]
Then, there exists $\epsilon > 0$ such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item For all $|z| < \epsilon$, the following equality is true, and the sum appearing in the right-hand side converges absolutely:
\[
\Xi(\mathsf{w}_z) = \exp\big( \sum_{n\geq 1}\sum_{\gamma_1, \cdots, \gamma_n \in \mathsf{P}_N^L} \varphi_n(\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_n) \prod_{k = 1}^{n} \mathsf{w}_z(\gamma_k) \big). 
\]
We then say that $\Xi(\mathsf{w}_z)$ admits a \textit{convergent cluster expansion}.
\item Moreover, there exists $c_\epsilon > 0$, going to 0 when $\epsilon$ goes to 0 such that for any $|z| < \epsilon$, and all $N \in \mathbb N$,
\[
\sum_{n\geq 1}\sum_{\gamma_1, \cdots, \gamma_n \in \mathsf{P}_N^L} \big|\varphi_n(\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_n)\big| \prod_{k = 1}^{n} \big|\mathsf{w}_z(\gamma_k)\big| \leq c_{\epsilon} |\mathbb T_N^L| . 
\]
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:cluster_expansion of arXiv:2604.18558

[Thm 4 (Sharp $\frac{\pi}{2}$ Theorem) of arXiv:2608.29703, 'A Sharp Small-Coefficient Variant of Khintchine's Inequality and the Sharp $\pi/2$ Theorem'] There exists a universal constant $C>0$ such that
for every Boolean function $f:\{\pm1\}^{n}\to\{\pm1\}$ with sufficiently
small $\theta=\max_{i}|\widehat{f}_{\{i\}}|$, 
\[
W_{1}(f)=\sum^{n}_{i=1}\widehat{f}^{2}_{\{i\}}\le\frac{2}{\pi}+C\theta^{2}.
\]
Moreover, the quadratic rate is attained by majority functions  in the sense of order, and
thus, is optimal in the order. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Sharp $\frac{\pi}{2}$ Theorem

[Thm 12 (Partial Fraction Decomposition, {\cite[Theorem 2) of arXiv:2609.00974, 'On Algebraic Integrability\\ of Vector Fields \\ with Rational Function Coefficients\\ tha'] {PFD_euclidean_1989}}]
    Let $k$ be a field of any characteristic.
    Let $f\in k(x)$ be a rational function. Let $f=\frac{a}{b}$ be a presentation of $f$, where $a,b\in k[x]$ and $(a,b)=1$. Let $b=\prod_{i=1}^n p_i^{m_i}$ be a decomposition into pairwise distinct irreducible factors. Then, there exists the \textbf{partial fraction decomposition} (PFD) of $f$:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item A polynomial $Q\in k[x]$.
        \item For each $1\le i\le n$ and $1\le j\le m_i$ a polynomial $s_{ij}\in k[x]$ with $\op{deg}(s_{ij})<\op{deg}(p_i)$.
    \end{itemize}
    These polynomials are\textbf{ unique} such that the following equality holds:
    \[
    f=Q+\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{j=1}^{m_i} \frac{s_{ij}}{p_i^j}.
    \]
    In particular, if $k$ is algebraically closed, then, without any loss of generality, we can assume that $p_i=x-a_i$, so $s_{ij}\in k$ and we define:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item Polynomial Part: $P(f)=Q$
        \item Logarithmic Part: $L(f)=\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{s_{i1}}{x-a_i}$, and we call $s_{i1}$ the residue of $f$ at $a_i$.
        \item Higher Part: $H(f)=\sum_{i>1}^n\sum_{j=1}^{m_i} \frac{s_{ij}}{{(x-a_i)}^j}$
    \end{enumerate}
    In total, we have $f=PFD(f)=P(f)+L(f)+H(f)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:l345 of arXiv:2608.28007, 'Exact Risk Ratios for Weighted Data Selection in Linear Regression'] Let $V=\{v_1,\dots,v_p\}$ positively span $\mathbb{R}^m$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item There are coefficients $\lambda_i>0$ with $\sum_i\lambda_iv_i=0$.
\item If $p=m+1$ then $V$ spans linearly, its kernel is one-dimensional, and
the kernel is generated by a strictly positive vector; so $V$ is a positive
circuit of rank $m$.
\item Let $K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p$ be a linear subspace and let $\lambda$ generate an
extreme ray of $K\cap\mathbb{R}^p_{+}$. Then the columns indexed by
$S=\operatorname{supp}(\lambda)$ carry a one-dimensional dependence space; if $K$ is the
kernel of a matrix with columns $v_i$, the support $S$ is a positive circuit.
\end{enumerate}

[Lemma lem:RBJ-kernel of arXiv:2608.02772, 'Non-Abelian Hirota-Miwa Equations for the KPZ Universality Class'] We have
\[
\mathbb{P}_y\Bigl(\bigcap_{i=1}^m
\{Y_{n_i}(t) > a_i\}\Bigr)
= \det(I - K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}})_{\ell^2(\mathbb{Z})},
\]
where
\[
K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}(x, x')
= \sum_{1 \le j \le i \le m}
  \sum_{r \le a_i} \sum_{r' \le a_j}
   \psi_{t, r, n_i}(x)
  \bigl[\delta_{ij}\delta_{r,r'}
  + [B_{\mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}]_{ij}(r, r')\bigr]
  \phi_{t, r', n_j}(x').
\]
This identifies $K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}$ with the
kernel~(equation eq:K-def of the paper) on the product graph
$\mathcal{G}^m$, with $\psi, \phi$ as the seed data and
$B_{\mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}$ as the propagator.

More precisely, this is the quantum cut point measure of the thin quantum disk defining $(\phi, \eta)$ (Definition~(def-thin-wedge of the paper)) restricted to the set of cut points $\eta ((0, \sigma)) \cap \mathbb{R}$.
	     Weight the law of $(\phi, \eta)$ by $|\mathcal{QCP}_{\phi, \eta((0, \sigma))\cap \mathbb{R}}|$ and sample a point $p \sim \mathcal{QCP}_{\phi, \eta((0, \sigma))\cap \mathbb{R}}^\#$. 
	
	
	    
	    Define $(\mathcal{D}_1,\mathcal{D}_2, \tilde \mathcal{D})$ as in Lemma~(lem-resample-infty-1 of the paper). Let $\mathcal{D}_3$ (resp.\ $\mathcal{D}_4$) be the ordered subset of $\tilde \mathcal{D}$ corresponding to two-pointed quantum surfaces disconnected after (resp.\ before) $\eta$ hits $p$. Then the law of $(\mathcal{D}_1, \mathcal{D}_2, \mathcal{D}_3, \mathcal{D}_4)$ is
        \begin{align*}
           C\int 1_{r_1+r_2+r_3+r_4> \ell_2, r_4 < \ell_2}  \Big( &{\mathcal{M}}^\mathrm{disk}_{0,2}(W; r_1+r_2+r_3+r_4 - \ell_2, r_1) \times {\mathcal{M}}^\mathrm{disk}_{0,2, \bullet}(\gamma^2-W; \ell_2, \cdot, r_2) \\
           &\times {\mathcal{M}}^\mathrm{disk}_{0,2}(W; \cdot, r_3) \times {\mathcal{M}}^\mathrm{disk}_{0,2}(W; \cdot, r_4) \Big), 
        \end{align*}
	    where the integral is taken over $(\ell_2, r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4)$ with respect to Lebesgue measure on $(0,\infty)^5$, and $C = (1-\frac2{\gamma^2}W)^4$.

[Theorem 14 (Free-boundary integral equation) of arXiv:2608.12291, 'When should one stop the most exciting game?\\ {\tiny Sequential Inference for win-marting'] The optimal boundary $b_T$ solves
\begin{equation}
    \begin{aligned}
        g(x)=\mathbb{E}\Bigg[g(X^x_{T-t})&+\int_0^{T-t}c(t+u)\ind{X^x_{u}\in(1-b_T(t+u),b_T(t+u))}\,du\\
        &-\int_0^{T-t}\mathcal{L}g(X^x_{u})\ind{X^x_{u}\not\in(1-b_T(t+u),b_T(t+u))}\,du\Bigg],
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
for $x=b_T(t)$ and $x=1-b_T(t)$ with $t<T$. For $T=\infty$, the integral is interpreted as the monotone limit as the integration domain expands and $g(X^x_{T-t})=0$ since $X^x_{\infty}\in\{0,1\}$, almost surely.

Moreover, this equation characterizes the optimal boundary uniquely in the following sense. 
If $\beta:[0,T)\to(1/2,1)$ is a continuous function satisfying
\[
    \gamma(t)<\beta(t)<1
\]
and solves \eqref{eq:main_boundary_integral} with $b_T(t)$ replaced by $\beta(t)$ for all $t<T$, then $\beta(t)=b_T(t)$ for all $t<T$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 23 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] Assume $q\equiv c>0$ and $a\equiv a_0$. Define $H_d(c)=\sup_{s\in\R}\{cs-d(M(s)-1)\}$.
Let $s_c>0$ be the unique solution of $dM'(s_c)=c$. There exist $R_0>0$ and $C>0$, depending only on $J,d,c$, such that for $R\ge R_0$,
\[
H_d(c)-a_0\le\Lp((-R,R))\le H_d(c)-a_0+\frac{C}{R^2}.
\]
Consequently $\Lp((-R,R))\downarrow H_d(c)-a_0$

body:
[Prop ldp+zn of arXiv:2609.02682, 'LDP for tensor forms'] Suppose $\{Q_n\}_{n\ge 1}$ is a sequence of symmetric, zero-diagonal $v$-tensors, such that (equation eq:cut of the paper) holds. Then the following conclusions hold:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[(i)] Suppose ${\bf{X}}=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ where $X_i \overset{\text{i.i.d.}}{\sim} \mu$ defined in (equation mu of the paper). Then for any ${\boldsymbol\alpha}\in \mathbb{R}^c$, $\boldsymbol{\alpha}^\top\boldsymbol N_n(Q_n, \bf{X})$ (see (equation defNinGPT2 of the paper)) satisfies an LDP  with speed $n$ and the good rate function 
        
\begin{equation}
I_{W_\infty,\boldsymbol{\alpha}}({t}):=\underset{\substack{{\boldsymbol f}\in \mathcal{F}_c: \\ \ \boldsymbol{\alpha}^\top {\boldsymbol G}_{W_{\infty}}({\boldsymbol f})=t}}{\inf} \Big\{ \int_0^1\sum_{r=1}^c f_{r}(u)\log f_{r}(u)du-\sum_{r=1}^{c}h_r \int_0^1 f_r(u)du\Big\}+\log \sum_{s=1}^c e^{h_s},
\end{equation}
where ${\boldsymbol G}_{W_{\infty}}({\boldsymbol f}):= \Big(G_{W_{\infty},\mathbf{1}_1}(\boldsymbol f), \ldots, G_{{W_{\infty}},\mathbf{1}_c}(\boldsymbol f)\Big)$, see (def:g2 of the paper). 

\item[(ii)] For the scaled log partition function $\mathcal{Z}_{Q_n}({\boldsymbol\alpha},\boldsymbol h)$ as in (equation logpf of the paper), we have
\begin{align}
\lim\limits_{n\rightarrow \infty} \mathcal{Z}_{Q_n}({\boldsymbol\alpha},\boldsymbol h)= \sup_{{\boldsymbol f}\in \mathcal{F}_c}\left\{{\boldsymbol\alpha}^\top {\boldsymbol G}_{W_\infty}({\boldsymbol f})
+\sum_{r=1}^c h_r\int_0^1 f_r(u)\,du
-\int_0^1\sum_{r=1}^c f_r(u)\log f_r(u)\,du\right\}-\log c.
		\end{align}   
        Moreover, the maximizers of the above optimization problem are attained.
        

\item [(iii)] Let $\mathcal{A}\subseteq \mathcal{F}_c$ denote the set of optimizers in (equation eq:potts_unconstrained_opt of the paper). Then, for every $\varepsilon>0$ we have 
\begin{equation}

\mathcal R_{Q_n,{ {\boldsymbol\alpha}},\boldsymbol h}\left(
\operatorname{dist}({\boldsymbol m}_n({\bf X}),\mathcal S)>\varepsilon
\right)
\xrightarrow{n\to\infty}0,
\end{equation}

where
\[
\mathcal S
:=\Big\{\Big(\int_0^1 f_1(u)\,du,\ldots,\int_0^1 f_c(u)\,du\Big):\, {\boldsymbol f}=(f_1,\ldots,f_c)\in\mathcal{A}\Big\}.
\]
In particular, if $\mathcal{A}=\{{\boldsymbol f}^*\}$, then
\[
{\boldsymbol m}_n({\bf X})\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{\mathcal R_{Q_n,{ {\boldsymbol\alpha}},\boldsymbol h}\text{-prob.}}
\Big(\int_0^1 f_1^*(u)\,du,\ldots,\int_0^1 f_c^*(u)\,du\Big).
\]
    \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop ldp+zn of arXiv:2609.02682

[Definition 14 of arXiv:2607.10486, 'Weak martingale solutions to stochastic Navier-Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard system with transport '] Let $(\Omega ,\mathscr{F}, \mathbb{F}, \mathbb{P})$ be a filtered probability space with the filtration 
$\mathbb{F}=(\mathscr{F}_t)_{t\in [0,T]}$
and $\rK$ be a real separable Hilbert space. By an  $\mathbb{F}$-adapted cylindrical Wiener process on $\rK$, we understand a family $W(t)$, $t\ge 0$, of bounded linear
operators from ${\rK}$ into  $L^2(\Omega,{\mathcal F},\mathbb{P})$ such that:
\begin{trivlist}
\item[(i)] for all $t \in [0,T]$, and $\psi,\varphi \in {\rK}$,
\[
\mathbb{E} \left[W(t)\psi W(t)\varphi \right]=t \langle\psi,\varphi \rangle _{\rK}\;;
\]
\item[(ii)] 
for each $\psi\in \rK$, $W(t)\psi$, $t \in [0,T]$ is a real valued
$\mathbb{F}$-adapted Wiener process.
\end{trivlist}

body: Three hubs, any remainder (bounded-density quadratic-form conjecture). Let X_H in R^3 and X' be independent, all coordinates independent with densities <= 1, L = M X' in R^3 with singular values s_1 >= s_2 >= s_3 > 0, B any real symmetric 3 x 3 matrix, beta in R^3 and R(X') any real quadratic polynomial. Then Q = X_H^T B X_H + 2 <X_H, L + beta> + R(X') satisfies |phi_Q(eta)| <= 2^{3/4} (s_1 s_2 s_3)^{-1/2} (pi/|eta|)^{3/2} and ||p_Q||_inf <= 3 sqrt2 (s_1 s_2 s_3)^{-1/3}. Proof: phi_Q pairs h_eta(l) = E e^{i eta (X_H^T B X_H + 2 <X_H, l + beta>)} with the slice transforms of E[e^{i eta R}; L in dl]; Plancherel in the three-dimensional partner gives int |h_eta|^2 <= (pi/|eta|)^3 for every B (the chirp is unimodular), and |mu^_l| <= rho_L(l) <= 2^{3/2}/(s_1 s_2 s_3). So any three coordinates whose off-diagonal block to the rest has s_1 s_2 s_3 bounded below give a bounded density, whatever else the matrix is.

[Definition of arXiv:2507.08757, 'Strong existence and uniqueness of the tilt-indexed Busemann process in the planar corner '] A \emph{system of random geodesics} is a family of random geodesics 
$\{\widehat\pi^u({\widehat\omega}):u\in\mathbb{Z}^2\}$ such that for each $u\in\mathbb{Z}^2$, $\widehat\pi^u$ is a random geodesic out of $u$.

The system is \emph{coalescing} if 
    \[\widehat\mathbb{P}\bigl\{\forall u,v\in\mathbb{Z}^2:  \widehat\pi^u({\widehat\omega})\curlywedgeuparrow\widehat\pi^v({\widehat\omega})\bigr\}=1.\]

The system is \emph{shift-covariant} if, $\widehat\mathbb{P}$-almost surely,
\[\widehat\pi^u({\widehat\omega})=u+\widehat\pi^0(\widehat{T}_u{\widehat\omega})\quad \text{ for }  u\in\mathbb{Z}^2. \]

${\widehat{\mathbbold\Pi}_c}$ denotes the set of shift-covariant coalescing systems of random geodesics. \qedhere

[Defi def: degree of arXiv:2605.03151, 'Giants through Higher-Order paths in Random Simplicial Complexes'] Let $X$ be a $d$-dimensional simplicial complex and $\sigma$ be a $k$-dimensional simplex in $X$, $0 \leq k < d$. For $k \leq \ell \leq d$, the $\ell$-degree of $\sigma$ is defined to be the number of $\ell$-dimensional simplices in $X$ that contain $\sigma$, i.e., 
\[  \tag{3.2.1}
\deg_{k, \ell}^X(\sigma) := \left| \{ \tau \in X \: : \: \dim (\tau) = \ell, \sigma \subseteq \tau \} \right|.
\]
In other words, $\deg_{k, \ell}$ is equal to the cardinality of the $(\ell - k)$-dimensional link of $\sigma$ in $X$.
title: Degree of simplices

[Theorem 11 of arXiv:2608.30549, '\vspace{-1cm}Maximally Spread Out Measures and Implications\\{} for Phase Transitions in A'] Let $(\XX, d)$ be a quasi-metric space and let $\emptyset \neq \SC \subset \XX$ be bounded.
  Then, writing $\AR^\ast := (\umd(\SC))^{-1}$, the following holds:
  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item (A suitable family of controlled complexity achieves every rate below $\AR^\ast$)
          There exists a family $(\CalA_n^\ast)_{n \in \N}$ of subsets
          $\emptyset \neq \CalA_n^\ast \subset \XX$
          of controlled complexity in $\XX$ such that for every $0 \leq \AR < \AR^\ast$,
          there exists $C(\AR) > 0$ satisfying
          \[
            \sup_{x \in \SC} \,\, \dist(x, \CalA_n^\ast) \leq C(\AR) \cdot n^{-\AR}
            \qquad \forall \, n \in \N.
          \]

    \item (No family of controlled complexity can achieve a rate above $\AR^\ast$
          uniformly over $\SC$)
          Let $(\CalA_n)_{n \in \N}$ be a family of controlled complexity in $\XX$.
          If
          \begin{equation}
            \sup_{x \in \SC} \,\, \dist(x, \CalA_n) \leq C(\AR) \cdot n^{-\AR}
            \qquad \forall \, n \in \N
            
          \end{equation}
          holds for some $\AR \geq 0$ and some constant $C(\AR) > 0$, then $\AR \leq \AR^\ast$.
  \end{enumerate}
  Now, set $\AR^\sharp := \bigl( \lmd (\SC) \bigr)^{-1}$ and
  assume that $\mu$ is a probability measure on $\XX$ that is critical for $\SC$.
  Then the following holds:
  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),resume]
    \item (Any rate above $\AR^\sharp$ is only achievable on a $\mu$-null set)
          For every $\AR > \AR^\sharp$ and every family $(\CalA_n)_{n \in \N}$
          of subsets $\emptyset \neq \CalA_n \subset \XX$ of controlled complexity in $\XX$,
          the set
          \[
            \CalR^\AR \bigl( (\CalA_n)_{n \in \N}, \SC, \XX\bigr)
            := \Bigl\{
                 x \in \SC
                 \,\,:\,\,
                 \sup_{n \in \N}
                 \bigl(
                   n^\AR \cdot \dist (x, \CalA_n)
                 \bigr)
                 < \infty
               \Bigr\}
          \]
          is a $\mu$-null set, i.e.,
          $\mu^\ast \bigl( \CalR^\AR \bigl( (\CalA_n)_{n \in \N}, \SC, \XX\bigr) \bigr) = 0$.
          In fact, we even have
          \[
            \mu^\ast
            \biggl(\,\,
              \bigcup_{\AR \in (\AR^\sharp, \infty)}
                \CalR^\AR \bigl( (\CalA_n)_{n \in \N}, \SC, \XX\bigr)
            \biggr)
            = 0
            .
          \]
  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 11 of arXiv:2608.30549

[Prop 13 of arXiv:2603.28702, 'Distribution of the magnetization of the critical Ising model on sparse random graphs'] \begin{enumerate}
\item
For each $i\ge3$,
$$\tilde{Y}_{i,n}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{(d)}\tilde{C}_i\sim\text{Pois}\left(\frac{d^i}{2i}\right).$$
These convergences hold jointly, and the limits $C_i$ are independent.
\item 
For any $\ell\in\N$,
$$\widehat{X}_{\ell,n}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{(d)}X_\ell\sim N\left(0,1+\gamma_\ell^{(2)}\right),$$
where $$\gamma_\ell^{(2)}:=\dfrac{d-1}{\ell^2}\SL{k=1}^\ell\left[(\ell-k+1)^2\cdot d^{-k}\right]-1\xrightarrow[\ell\to\infty]{}0.$$ 
Also, this convergence holds jointly with the convergences in \ref{pois-cycle-ER} and the limits are independent.
\item
Let $m$ be as in Lemma \ref{Zm-ER-mom}. Under the planted measure $\PR_m^*$, for any $i\ge3$
$$\tilde{Y}_{i,n}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{(d)}\tilde{C}_i'\sim\text{Pois}\left(\frac{d^i+1}{2i}\right).$$
As before, these convergences hold jointly, and the limits are independent.
\item 
Let $m$ be as in Lemma \ref{Zm-ER-mom}, moreover satisfying the condition that $m\cdot n^{-3/4}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}x$. Under the planted measure $\PR_m^*$, for any $\ell\in\N$
$$\widehat{X}_{\ell,n}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{(d)}X_\ell'\sim N\left(\dfrac{x^2}{\sqrt{2(d-1)}}\left(1+\gamma_\ell^{(1)}\right),1+\gamma_\ell^{(2)}\right),$$
where
$$\gamma_\ell^{(1)}:=\dfrac{d-1}{\ell}\SL{k=1}^\ell\left[(\ell-k+1)\cdot d^{-k}\right]-1\xrightarrow[\ell\to\infty]{}0.$$
Also, this convergence holds jointly with the convergences in \ref{pois-cycle-pl-ER} and the limits are independent.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem of arXiv:2506.09364, 'A collection of results relating the geometry of plane domains and the exit time of planar'] Let $\{U\}_{j\in \mathbb{N}}$ be a collection of domains which contain the origin. Let $C =\{c_j\}_{j\in \mathbb{N}}$ be a discrete subset of $\mathbb{C}$ such that for all $i, j$ 
with $i\neq j$ it holds that $(U_i + c_i)\cap (U_j + c_j) = \emptyset$. Consider the domain $D$ given by,
$$
    D = \mathbb{C} \setminus \bigcup_{j\in\mathbb{N}} (U_j + c_j).
$$
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a graph embedded in $\mathbb{C}$ whose vertices are a subset of $C$, let $L$ be the union of all the edges in $\mathcal{L}$.
If for $p\in\mathbb{R}^+$ there exists some $\delta < 1$ and $N$ such that for every edge $e\in\mathcal{L}$, the following conditions hold.
\begin{itemize}
    \item Define $\tau = \inf_{t>0}\{t: B_t \in L \setminus e\}$, it holds that $\sup_{a\in e\cap D} P_a(\tau < T(D)) \leq \delta$.
    \\
\item Let $U$ be the component of $\mathbb{C}\setminus (L\setminus e)$   
containing $e$, it holds that $\sup_{a\in e\cap D} E_a[\tau_U^p] \leq N$.
\end{itemize}
Then $bh(D) \geq p$.

[Proposition prop_new_concentration of arXiv:2411.02046, 'Speed of Convergence and Moderate Deviations of FPP on Random Geometric Graphs'] There exists~$C_{\mathrm{dev}}>0$ such that the following holds. Let~$x \in \R^d$ be such that~$\|x\|$ is large enough,~$t \in [1,\|x\|$ and~$s > 0$. Then,
\begin{equation}
	\p\big(|Y_{t,x} - \E[Y_{t,x}]| > s \big) \le 2 \inf_{\alpha \in \left(0,~1/(4\K t)\right)} \exp\left\{ C_{\mathrm{dev}} \alpha^2 t~\|x\| - s \alpha\right\}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 5 of arXiv:2605.02430, '\textbf{Scaling limit of the range of tree-valued branching random walks in random environ'] (\textbf{GW trees and forests}) Let $\mu\eqo (\mu(k))_{k\in \bbN}$ 
be a probability measure on $\bbN$. 

\smallskip

\noi
$(\textbf{a})\, $ A \textit{GW tree with offspring distribution $\mu$} (a \textit{GW($\mu$)-tree}, for short) is a random tree $\tau$  that satisfies the following. 
\begin{compactenum}
\item[] \textbf{(1):} $k_\varnothing (\tau)$ has law $\mu$. \textbf{(2):} For all $k\ino \bbN^*$ such that $\mu(k)\! >\! 0$, the subtrees $\theta_{(1)} \tau, \ldots , \theta_{(k)} \tau$ under $\bP (\, \cdot \, | k_\varnothing (\tau)\! = \! k)$ are independent with the same law as $\tau$ under $\bP$. 
\end{compactenum}

\smallskip

\noi
$(\textbf{b})\, $ Let $(\tau^{_{(k)}}_{^{\!}})_{k\in \bbN^*}$ be i.i.d.~GW($\mu$)-trees. We generically denote by $\tau_\infty$ the tree associated with the forest $(\tau^{_{(k)}}_{^{\!}})_{k\in \bbN^*}$. We call $\tau_\infty$ a GW($\mu$)-forest. 

\smallskip

\noi
$(\textbf{c})\, $ We say that $\tau$ is a \emph{grafted GW($\mu$)-tree} if $k_\varnothing (\tau)\eqo 1$ and if $\theta_{(1)}\tau$ is a GW($\mu$)-tree. \cq

[Thm Thm_Mat_Gar_1 of arXiv:2606.22183, 'Expected loss of quasi-arithmetic means of exchangeable random variables'] Let $I\subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be a nonempty open interval and $(\xi_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of exchangeable random variables with values in $I$.
If $L:I\to\mathbb{R}$ is a convex (loss) function such that $\operatorname{\mathbb{E}}(\vert L(\xi_1)\vert)<\infty$, then
 $\operatorname{\mathbb{E}}(L(\frac{\xi_1+\cdots+\xi_n}{n}))\in[-\infty,\infty)$, $n\in\mathbb{N}$, and the sequence $\big(\operatorname{\mathbb{E}}(L(\frac{\xi_1+\cdots+\xi_n}{n}))\big)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is decreasing. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 29 of arXiv:2608.25785, 'Proper Actions on Homogeneous Spaces of the Upper Triangular Matrix Group via Coarse Geome'] Let $(S,\mathcal{E}),(T,\mathcal{F})$ be coarse spaces and 
    $f$ a map from $S$ to $T$.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item If $f$ is coarse, the map $f$ reflects asymptotic disjointness.
        That is, for $A,D\subset S$, if $f(A)\pitchfork_{\mathcal{F}}f(D)$, then $A\pitchfork_\mathcal{E} D$.
        \item If $f$ is a coarse embedding, the map $f$  both preserves and reflects  asymptotic disjointness.
        That is, for $A,D\subset S$, $A\pitchfork_\mathcal{E} D$ if and only if $f(A)\pitchfork_{\mathcal{F}} f(D)$. 
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Dfn of arXiv:2603.13873, '{Solvability of BSDEs with possibly unbounded stochastic coefficients \\ on a general weig'] A continuous function $u(t,x):[0,T]\times {\mathbb R}^n\rightarrow {\mathbb R}^k$ with $u(T,\cdot)=h(\cdot)$ is a viscosity sub-solution (super-solution) of PDE (equation PDE' of the paper) if for any $1\leq i\leq k$ and any function $\phi\in C^{1,2}([0,T]\times {\mathbb R}^n;{\mathbb R})$, it holds that
$$
\frac{\partial \phi(t_0,x_0)}{\partial t}+\mathcal{L}\phi(t_0,x_0)+g_i(t_0,x_0,u(t_0,x_0),
(\nabla_x\phi\sigma)(t_0,x_0))\geq 0\  (\leq 0),
$$
as long as the function $u_i-\phi$ has a local maximum (minimum) at the point $(t_0,x_0)\in [0,T)\times {\mathbb R}^n$. A viscosity solution of PDE (equation PDE' of the paper) is both a viscosity sub-solution and viscosity super-solution.

[Proposition t:clt_linear_marks_new of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] Let $\tilde{\mathcal{P}}$ be a marked point process on $\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{K}$ having
 summable exponential $\mathbb{B} $-mixing correlations, as in Definition~(def.A2 of the paper) and let $\xi: \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{K} \times
  {\mathcal{N}}_{\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{K}} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a marking function on $\tilde{\mathcal{P}}$.
   \begin{enumerate}[wide,label=(\roman*),labelindent=0pt]
\item 
Let $\xi$ be fast \textnormal{BL}-localizing on $\tilde{\mathcal{P}}$
  as in Definition~(def.Lp-stabilizing_marking of the paper)~(i.BL-localizing of the paper),~(i.BL-localizing-fast of the paper),
and assume it satisfies the $p$-moment
  condition 
  \begin{equation}

\sup_{1 \leq q \leq p} \sup_{x_1,\ldots,
  x_{q} \in \mathbb{R}^d} \mathbb {E} _{\bk x1{q}}[ \max(1,|\xi( \tilde{x}_1, \tilde{\mathcal{P}} )|^p)]
\leq M_p^{\xi} < \infty
\end{equation}
for all $p>1$. 
   If $f \in \mathbb{B} (W_1)$ satisfies
 ${\rm Var} \,\hat\mu_{n}^{\xi}(f)  = \Omega(n^{\nu})$ for some $\nu > 0$,
   then as $n \to \infty$, 
 \begin{equation}  ({\rm Var} \,\hat\mu_{n}^{\xi}(f))^{-1/2}\Big( \hat\mu_{n}^{\xi}(f) - \mathbb {E}  \hat\mu_{n}^{\xi}(f) \Big) \stackrel{d}{\Rightarrow} Z,
\end{equation}
where $Z$ denotes a standard normal random variable.
\item 
If  moreover $\mathcal{P}$ is stationary and $\xi$ is translation invariant then the analogs of 
expectation,  variance asymptotics and multivariate central limit
theorems (as in Proposition~(expvar of the paper) and Theorem (t:multcltmarkedpp of the paper))
hold for $(\hat\mu_{n}^{\xi})_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ where
\(\mathbb{E} _{\0}[\xi(\tilde\0,\tilde{\mathcal{P}})]\), \(\mathbb{E} _{\0}[\xi^2(\tilde\0,\tilde{\mathcal{P}})]\) and \(\mathbb{E} _{\0,x}[\xi(\tilde{\0},\tilde{\mathcal{P}})\xi(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}})]\) can be used in place of \(\mathbb{E} [\Upsilon_{\0}]\), \(\mathbb {E} [\Upsilon_{\0}^2]\) and \(\mathbb {E} \bigl[\Upsilon_{(\0,z)}[1]\Upsilon_{(\0,z)}[2]\bigr]\), respectively, under a $p=(1+\epsilon)-$ or $p=(2+\epsilon)-$ moment condition~(equation e:xinpmomcopied-infty of the paper).
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Dy 15 of arXiv:2606.26496, 'Homeomorphism of the Revuz correspondence under Dynkin class assumptions'] A numerical function ${\sf A}_t(\omega)$, $t\geq0$, $\omega\in\Omega$ is a positive continuous additive functional if the following conditions hold:
		\begin{itemize}
			\item[(i)] For each $t\geq 0$, ${\sf A}_t(\cdot)$ is $\mathscr{F}_t$-measurable.
			\item[(ii)] There exists a set $\Lambda\in\mathscr{F}_\infty$ and $N\subset E$ with ${\rm Cap}(N)=0$ such that $\mathbb{P}_x(\Lambda)=1$ for any $x \in E\setminus N$ and $\theta_t \Lambda \subset \Lambda $ for any $t>0$. Moreover, for each $\omega \in \Lambda$, ${\sf A}_0(\omega)=0$, $|{\sf A}_t(\omega)|<\infty$ for any $t<\zeta(\omega)$, ${\sf A}_t(\omega)={\sf A}_{\zeta(\omega)}(\omega)$ for any $t\geq\zeta(\omega)$ and
			\[
			{\sf A}_{t+s}(\omega)={\sf A}_s(\omega)+{\sf A}_t(\theta_s\omega),\quad\text{for all}\quad t,s\geq0.
			\]
			\item[(iii)] For each $\omega \in \Lambda$, the map $t \mapsto {\sf A}_t(\omega)$ is nonnegative and continuous on $[0,+\infty)$.
		\end{itemize}
title: Definition 15 of arXiv:2606.26496

body:
[Lem 5 of arXiv:2605.21638, 'Markov renewal theory for transfer operators and point processes on the line'] Let $P$ be the transition kernel of a positive Harris chain with state space $\R^k$ and invariant probability measure $\pi$. Suppose that the minorisation condition~\eqref{eq:minor} holds with $r=1$. Then there exists a tuple 
	\[
		\Bigl( \Omega,\F, (\P_{\mu^\ast})_{\mu \in \mathcal M_1(\R^k)}, (M_n^\ast)_{n\in \N_0}, (\tilde \tau_j)_{j\in \N_0} \Bigr) 
	\] 	
	in which $(\Omega,\F)$ is a measurable space, each $\P_{\mu^\ast}$ is a probability measure on $(\Omega,\F)$, and:
	\begin{enumerate} [(i)]
		\item Under $\P_{\mu^\ast}$, $(M_n^\ast)_{n\in \N_0}$ is a time-homogeneous Markov chain with initial law $\mu^\ast$.
		\item $0< \tilde \tau_1< \cdots $ is a sequence of  $\P_{\mu^\ast}$-almost surely finite stopping times  (with respect to the natural filtration $(\F_n)_{n\in\N_0}$ of $(M_n^\ast)_{n\in \N_0}$).
		\item For all measurable sets $A\subset \R^k$, and every probabilty measure $\mu$ on $\R^k$,
                \begin{equation} 
            		\P_{\mu^\ast}\Bigl( M_{\Tilde{\tau}_j}^\ast  \in A\times \{0,1\} \, \Big|\, \F_{\tilde \tau_j -1} \Bigr) = \nu(A),
            	\end{equation}
            	$\P_{\mu^\ast}$-almost surely.
        \item   The driving chain $(M_n)_{n\in \N_0}$ with initial law $\mu$ is the marginal of $(M^\ast_n)$ with initial law $\mu^\ast$, i.e.\ for every probability measure $\mu$ on $\R^k$ and $n\in\N$ and all measurable $A \in \R^k$,
            	\begin{equation} 
 			\P_{\mu^\ast}(M^\ast_n \in A \times \{ 0,1 \}) = P^n(\mu,A).
            	\end{equation}
	\end{enumerate}
title: Lem 5 of arXiv:2605.21638

body:
[Theorem 2 (Fixed-measurement posterior information budget) of arXiv:2608.21709, 'Posterior Information Dynamics of Diffusion Models for Linear Inverse Problems'] Fix a measurement value $r$ with $0<p_R(r)<\infty$ and define
\[
q_t^r(x):=p_t(x\mid r),
\qquad
\mathcal K_t(r):=\KL(q_t^r\|p_t).
\]
Let $0<s<t<\infty$.  Assume $\mathcal K_s(r)<\infty$, the relative Fisher
information
\[
\int q_u^r(x)
\left\|\nabla\log\frac{q_u^r(x)}{p_u(x)}\right\|^2\dd x
\]
is integrable over $u\in[s,t]$, and the integration-by-parts boundary terms
vanish.  Then
\begin{equation}

\mathcal K_s(r)-\mathcal K_t(r)
=
\int_s^t
\E_{X_u\mid r}\|g_u(X_u,r)\|^2\,\dd u.
\end{equation}
Consequently, for almost every $t>0$ (and at every differentiability point),
\begin{equation}

-\frac{\dd}{\dd t}\mathcal K_t(r)
=
\E_{X_t\mid r}\|g_t(X_t,r)\|^2.
\end{equation}
Averaging over the measurement gives
\begin{equation}

\MI(R;X_s)-\MI(R;X_t)
=
\int_s^t\E\|g_u(X_u,R)\|^2\,\dd u,
\qquad
-\frac{\dd}{\dd t}\MI(R;X_t)
=
\E\|g_t(X_t,R)\|^2
\end{equation}
whenever the derivative exists.  Thus force energy is the forward-time
dissipation rate of posterior--prior relative entropy, or the corresponding
reverse-time assimilation rate. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Fixed-measurement posterior information budget

[Lemma lem:SSL of arXiv:2412.05142, 'Strong convergence of the Euler scheme for singular kinetic SDEs driven by $\alpha$-stable'] [BDG-Levy] 
Let $(S,T)\in[0,1]^2$. Let $p\in[2,\infty)$.   Let
$(A_{s,t})_{(s,t)\in \Delta_{[S,T]}}$ be a family of ${\mathbb R}^d$-valued random variables in $L_p(\Omega)$
such that $A_{s,t}$ is $\mathcal{F}_t$-measurable for all $(s,t)\in \Delta_{[S,T]}$.   Let ${\mathcal G}\subset{\mathcal F}_S$ be an $\sigma$-algebra. Suppose that there exist constants $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2>0$ and constants $K_1, K_2\in[0,\infty)$,  such that the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
   \item $\|A_{s,t}\|_{L_p(\Omega)|{\mathcal G}}\leqslant K_1|t-s|^{\frac{1}{2}+\epsilon_1}$, $(s,t)\in\Delta_{[S,T]}$,
   \item $\|{\mathbb E}^{s-(t-s)}\delta A_{s,u,t}\|_{L_p(\Omega)|{\mathcal G}}\leqslant K_2|t-s|^{1+\epsilon_2}$, $(s,t)\in\Delta_{[S,T]}$ and $u=\frac{s+t}{2}$,
   \item there exists a  process $\mathcal{A}:[S,T]\mapsto L^p(\Omega;{\mathbb R}^d)$  such that  for any $(s,t)\in [S,T]_\leqslant^2$ one has
   \begin{align}
       
       {\mathcal A}_t-{\mathcal A}_s=\lim_{m\rightarrow\infty}\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}A_{s+i\frac{t-s}{m},s+(i+1)\frac{t-s}{m}} \quad\text{ in probability}.
   \end{align}
\end{enumerate}
 Then there exists constants $\hat K_1,\hat K_2>0$ which depend only on $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3, d,p$ so that for any $(s,t)\in[S,T]_{\leqslant}^2$,
  \begin{align}
       
       \|{\mathcal A}_{t}-{\mathcal A}_{s}\|_{L_p(\Omega)|{\mathcal G}}\leqslant K_1\hat K_1|t-s|^{\frac{1}{2}+\epsilon_1}+K_2\hat K_2|t-s|^{1+\epsilon_2}.
   \end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:SSL of arXiv:2412.05142

[Definition of arXiv:2609.00233, 'A survey on mapping class groups of 3-manifolds'] Let $M$ be a compact, orientable 3-manifold.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item We say that $M$ is \emph{irreducible} if and only if every 2-sphere in $M$ bounds a copy of $D^3$ in $M$.
    \item We say that an orientable embedded surface $F$ in $M$ with $\partial F \subseteq \partial M$ is \emph{compressible} if either
    \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
        \item there exists a curve $k \subseteq \mathring{F}$, homotopically essential in $F$, and a disc $D \subseteq M$ with $\mathring{D} \subseteq \mathring{M}$ and $D \cap F = \partial D =k$; or
        \item there exists a 3-ball $E \subseteq M$ with $E \cap F = \partial E$.
    \end{enumerate}
    If an orientable, embedded surface $F$ is not compressible, we say that $F$ is \emph{incompressible}.
    \item We say that $M$ is \emph{boundary irreducible} if and only if $\partial M$ is incompressible.
    \item We say that $M$ is \emph{Haken} (or sufficiently large) if it contains an incompressible surface.
\end{enumerate}
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2609.00233, 'A survey on mapping class groups of 3-manifolds'

body: In topology and related areas of mathematics, a product space is the Cartesian product of a family of topological spaces equipped with a natural topology called the product topology. This topology differs from another, perhaps more natural-seeming, topology called the box topology, which can also be given to a product space and which agrees with the product topology when the product is over only finitely many spaces. However, the product topology is "correct" in that it makes the product space a categorical product of its factors, whereas the box topology is too fine; in that sense the product topology is the natural topology on the Cartesian product.
title: Product topology

[Proposition 41 of arXiv:2608.05931, 'Effective Lagrangian regularity and the uniqueness threshold for random H\"older velocity '] Suppose $U=\sum_{j=0}^\infty u^j$ satisfies Assumption~\ref{asmp:main for autonomous}. Additionally, suppose that for some $\alpha\in(0,1)$ and $p>1$, we have a constant $K\geq 1$ such that for $n\in\{0,1,2\}$ and all $j\in\N$,
\begin{equation}
\|\nabla^n u^j\|_{L^p_\omega \mathcal{C}^0_{x}}\leq K 2^{(n-\alpha)j}.
\end{equation}
    Then for all $\eps>\frac{d}{p}$ and $A\geq 1$ there exist vector fields $\{u^{j,A}\}_{j \geq 0}$ (on possibly a larger probability space, though coupled to the original $u^j$) also satisfying Assumption~\ref{asmp:main for autonomous} such that for all $j\geq 0$, $n\in\{0,1,2\}$,
\[\|\nabla^n u^{j,A}\|_{\mathcal{C}^0_{x}} \leq A K 2^{(n-\alpha+\eps)j},
\]
and, letting $U^A:=\sum_{j=0}^\infty u^{j,A}$, there exists $C(d,p,\eps)>0$ such that
\[\P(U^A\neq U)\leq C A^{1-p}.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
