[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2512.01483, 'Scaling Limits of Line Models in Degenerate Environment'] Let $\alpha \in (0,1)$ and $Z_k$, $k \in \mathbb{Z}$, be a collection of i.i.d. random variables defined on the same probability space $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{P})$ with tail behavior  $\mathbb{P}(Z_k > t) = t^{-\alpha + o(1)}$ as $t \to \infty$. Let $\alpha^{-} \in (0, \alpha) $. Then, for $\mathbb{P}$-a.e. $\omega$, there exists $C(\omega)>0$, such that, for all $k \geq 1$,
\[\max_{-k \leq i \leq k} Z_i \leq C(\omega) (1+ k^{\frac{1}{\alpha^{-}}}). \]

[Proposition 2 (Linear error equation) of arXiv:2608.16256, 'Error Distribution of the Local Linearization Method for Stochastic Differential Equations'] \label[proposition]{prop:ll_exact_linear_reduction}
The scaled error satisfies
\begin{equation}
    \hat U_t^{n,i}
    =
    Z_t^{n,i}
    +
    \int_0^t
    f^i_j(\hat X_{\varphi_n(s)}^n)
    \hat U_s^{n,j}\,ds,
    \qquad
    0\le t\le1,
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
    Z^n
    \coloneqq
    \bar M^n
    +
    \sum_{\ell=1}^5 R^{(\ell),n}.
\end{equation}
Here
\begin{align}
    \bar M_t^{n,i}
    &\coloneqq
    \frac{n\sqrt n}{2}
    \int_0^t
    f^i_{jk}(\hat X_{\varphi_n(s)}^n)
    \sigma^j_\alpha\sigma^k_\beta
    \\
    &\quad\times
    \biggl[
        \bigl(
            B_s^\alpha-B_{\varphi_n(s)}^\alpha
        \bigr)
        \bigl(
            B_s^\beta-B_{\varphi_n(s)}^\beta
        \bigr)
        -
        \delta^{\alpha\beta}
        \bigl(s-\varphi_n(s)\bigr)
    \biggr] ds,
    \\
    R_t^{(1),n,i}
    &\coloneqq
    n\sqrt n
    \int_0^t
    \widetilde R_s^{n,i}\,ds,
    \\
    R_t^{(2),n,i}
    &\coloneqq
    n\sqrt n
    \int_0^t
    f^i_{jk}(\hat X_{\varphi_n(s)}^n)
    \bigl(
        \hat X_s^{n,j}
        -
        \hat X_{\varphi_n(s)}^{n,j}
    \bigr)
    \bigl(
        X_s^k-\hat X_s^{n,k}
    \bigr) ds,
    \\
    R_t^{(3),n,i}
    &\coloneqq
    \frac{n\sqrt n}{2}
    \int_0^t
    f^i_{jk}(\hat X_{\varphi_n(s)}^n)
    \bigl(
        X_s^j-\hat X_s^{n,j}
    \bigr)
    \bigl(
        X_s^k-\hat X_s^{n,k}
    \bigr) ds,
    \\
    R_t^{(4),n,i}
    &\coloneqq
    \frac{n\sqrt n}{2}
    \int_0^t
    f^i_{jk}(\hat X_{\varphi_n(s)}^n)
    \theta_s^{n,j}\theta_s^{n,k}\,ds,
    \\
    R_t^{(5),n,i}
    &\coloneqq
    n\sqrt n
    \int_0^t
    f^i_{jk}(\hat X_{\varphi_n(s)}^n)
    \theta_s^{n,j}\eta_s^{n,k}\,ds.
\end{align}

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2605.30121, 'Improved Survival Results for the One-Dimensional Renewal Contact Process'] Let $\mu$ be an interarrival distribution and let $U = \sum_{n\ge 0} \mu^{*n}$
be its renewal measure. If there exist $\kappa>0$ such that
\[
   \sup_{a\ge 0} U_{\mathrm{at}}\big( (a,a+\kappa] \big) \;<\; \eta/2,
\]
then $\lambda_c(\mu) \;<\; +\infty$. In particular, the conclusion holds for every non-atomic interarrival distribution. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 2 of arXiv:2605.30121

[Thm t1-tightening of arXiv:2411.14236, 'Size of chaos for Gibbs measures\\of mean field interacting diffusions'] Let $\mu \in \mathcal P_1(\mathcal X)$
and let $\rho > 0$, $\delta \geqslant 0$.
Suppose that for all $\nu \in \mathcal P_1(\mathcal X)$,
\begin{equation}

W_1^2(\nu, \mu) \leqslant \frac 2\rho
\bigl(H(\nu | \mu) + \delta\bigr).
\end{equation}
Then for all $\nu \in \mathcal P_1(\mathcal X)$,
\begin{equation}

W_1^2(\nu, \mu) \leqslant \frac 8\rho (2+\delta)^2 H(\nu|\mu).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm t1-tightening of arXiv:2411.14236

[Definition item:WB1 of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] In the VEB setting, we say that $V$ is \emph{well-behaved} if the following properties hold:
\begin{enumerate}[(WB1)]
\item For all $t \ge \tau_0$, $\textup{type}^{\Psi(t)} \ne \textup{failure}$.
\item For all $j \ge j_0$, there is a positive integer $t \le \tau_0 + (4/\lambda)^{2(j-1)}$ such that $\Psi(t)$ is $j$-filling or $j$-advancing.
\item For all $g \ge 0$ with $\textup{type}^{\Psi(\tau_g)} \in \{\textup{refilling}, \textup{stabilising}\}$, there is a positive integer $g'$ with $g+1 \le g' \le g+2j$ such that $\textup{type}^{\Psi(\tau_{g'})} = \textup{filling}$.
\item For all $g \ge 0$ with $\textup{type}^{\Psi(\tau_g)} = \textup{refilling}$, $\tau_{g+1} \le \tau_g + (j^{\Psi(\tau_g)})^{\phi+46}$.
\item For all $g \ge 0$ with $\textup{type}^{\Psi(\tau_g)} = \textup{stabilising}$, $\tau_{g+1} \le \tau_g + (j^{\Psi(\tau_g)})^{\phi+72}$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Definition item:WB1 of arXiv:2602.21315

body: In algebraic geometry, a projective variety is an algebraic variety that is a closed subvariety of a projective space. That is, it is the zero-locus in of some finite family of homogeneous polynomials that generate a prime ideal, the defining ideal of the variety.

body:
[Lem 124 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Recall the definition \eqref{e:bad.times.J}. 
If $(p^N)'$ converges to $p'$ in the L\'evy--Prohorov metric in the sense of Definition~\ref{d:levy.prohorov.derivs}, then  we have
	\[
	J^N\equiv
	J(p^N,\tep,\lambda)
		\subseteq 
		J\bigg(p,2\tep,\frac{\lambda}{2}\bigg)
	\equiv J
	\] for all $N$ large enough. 

\begin{proof}
The function $(p^N)'$ is nonincreasing, so there exists a nonnegative measure $\nu_N$ on $[q_0,1]$ with
	\[
	\nu_N( (s,t]) = -\Big[(p^N)'(t)-(p^N)'(s)\Big]
	\]
for all $q_0 \le s\le t\le1$, and with $\nu_N(\{0\})=0$. Define analogously the measure $\nu$ corresponding to the limiting function $p$.
The L\'evy--Prohorov convergence assumption implies that for all $N\ge N(\tep)$ we have
	\[
	\nu_N(A) \le \nu(A^{\tep})+\tep
	\]
where $A\subseteq[q_0,1]$ is any Borel set, and $A^{\tep}$ is the $\tep$-fattening of $A$. (The same inequality also holds with $\nu$ and $\nu_N$ exchanged.) It follows that
	\begin{align*}
	&-\Big[(p^N)'(t+\tep)-(p^N)'(t-\tep)\Big]
	= \nu_N([t-\tep,t+\tep])\\
	&\qquad\le \nu([t-2\tep,t+2\tep]) + \tep
	=-\Big[p'(t+2\tep)-p'(t-2\tep)\Big]+ \tep
	\le \frac{\lambda}{2}+\tep\,,
	\end{align*}
where the last bound holds provided $t\notin J$. Since $\tep\ll\lambda$ by Assumption~\ref{a:params}, this shows that if $t\notin J$ then $t\notin J^N$, as claimed.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 124 of arXiv:2608.29416

[Corollary 2 of arXiv:2605.23817, '\bfseries Visibility in the Boolean Model \\ on Harmonic Manifolds'] Let \(M\) be a simply connected non-compact homogeneous harmonic manifold
	with volume entropy \(h\geq 0\). Consider the Boolean model on \(M\) with
	intensity \(\lambda>0\) and fixed ball grains of radius \(\rho>0\), and let
	\(a_\rho\) be the tube coefficient from \eqref{eq:arho}. If \(h=0\), then $\EE[\vol_M(V_o)\mid o\notin Z]<\infty$ for every $\lambda>0$.
	If \(h>0\), then
	\[
	\EE[\vol_M(V_o)\mid o\notin Z]<\infty
	\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad
	\lambda>\lambda_c(M,\rho):={h\over a_\rho}.
	\]

[Theorem main_theorem of arXiv:2607.13302, 'Extending an Order-Statistic Characterization of the Exponential Distribution'] Let $\mathcal{F}$ denote the family of continuous cumulative distribution functions $F$ satisfying $F(0) = 0$, where the corresponding probability density function $f$, {such that $f(0)>0$,} admits a Maclaurin series expansion for every $x > 0$. Let $X_1, X_2, \dots, X_n$ be a random sample from the distribution $F$ that belongs to $\mathcal{F}$. Let $j$ and $k$ be fixed numbers such that {$1 \leq j < k < (n+j)/2 < n$} and let $X_{01}, X_{02}, ..., X_{0j}$ be independent random variables, each of them independent from sample $X_1, \dots, X_n$ and each from the distribution $F$. If
\[ X_{(k-j;n)} + \sum_{i=1}^j \frac{1}{n-k+i}X_{0i} \overset{d}{=} X_{(k;n)}, \]
then $F \sim \mathcal{E}(\lambda)$, for some $\lambda > 0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition defn:sub-stop of arXiv:2601.07045, 'From Continuous to Discrete: \\ a No-U-Turn Sampler for Permutations'] Let $\mathcal{O}$ be an orbit of length $2^j$, and let

(Definition~(def:dyadic-suborbit of the paper)). We say that $\mathcal{O}$ satisfies the \emph{sub-stopping condition}
(\textsc{SubStop}) if at least one dyadic sub-orbit satisfies the
\textsc{Stop} condition:
\[
\textsc{SubStop}(\mathcal{O},\varepsilon,w)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists\, s\in\{0,\dots,j\},\; t\in\{1,\dots,2^s\}
\text{ such that }
\textsc{Stop}\bigl(\mathcal{O}_{s,t},\varepsilon,w\bigr).
\]
title: \textsc{SubStop} condition

body: In probability theory, statistics and related fields, a Poisson point process is a type of mathematical object that consists of points randomly located on a mathematical space with the essential feature that the points occur independently of one another. The process's name derives from the fact that the number of points in any given finite region follows a Poisson distribution. The process and the distribution are named after French mathematician Siméon Denis Poisson. The process itself was discovered independently and repeatedly in several settings, including experiments on radioactive decay, telephone call arrivals and actuarial science.

Method: Source-specific calculation, conditional implication or exact obstruction Result: Finite-volume integration by parts produces the force sum over other particles of1/(x-y). At unit density, the absolute far-field integral is integral from1 toR of dy/y=log R. Thus a bound obtained by taking absolute values before the infinite-volume limit cannot be uniform. A symmetric principal value may cancel the mean term, but then fluctuations and truncated correlations must be controlled. Check: The two-sided integral of |1/y| doubles the logarithmic divergence; the symmetric integral of1/y itself is zero. This exhibits exactly the cancellation destroyed by an absolute-value estimate. Obstruction: The missing step is uniform integrability of the renormalized force and justification of differentiation under the infinite conditional law. Existence of a DLR density does not alone justify that interchange. No general BBGKY identity is established here.

body: [Definition Dual graph of arXiv:2604.24743, 'The impact of disorder and non-convex interactions on delocalisation of height functions'] Consider the graph $(\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^2)^*$ defined to be the copy of $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^2$ translated by the vector $(1/2, 1/2)$. We refer to this graph as the dual lattice and denote by $E((\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^2)^*)$ its edge set. Each edge $e^* \in E((\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^2)^*)$ is naturally associated with an edge of $e$ of $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^2$ (which is the only edge of $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^2$ intersecting the edge~$e^*$). We refer to Figure~(fig:duallattice of the paper) for an illustration.

\begin{equation}
\text{there is $\theta_0>0$ such that}\quad

\vmarklaw(\dd \pmark) \vmarklaw(\dd \qmark)
\emarklaw(\dd \rmark)<\infty.
\end{equation}
For each $i\geq 1$, consider the solution $\bX^i=(\bX^i_t)_{t\geq 0}$ to the nonlinear SDE corresponding to
$\vmark_i$ and $B^i$. For $i,j\geq 1$ with $i\neq j$, consider the pathwise unique solution $\bU^{ij}=(\bU^{ij}_t)_{t\geq 0}$ to
\begin{equation}
\bU^{ij}_t=G(\vmark_i,\vmark_j ,\emark_{ij})
+ \int_0^t \alpha(\bX^i_s,\bX^j_s,\bU^{ij}_s)\dd s + \int_0^t \beta(\bX^i_s,\bX^j_s,\bU^{ij}_s)\dd W_s^{ij}.
\end{equation}

(i) If $\phi$ is bounded, then for all $T>0$, there is a constant $C_T>0$ such that
for all $N\geq 2$,
$$
\E\Big[\sup_{t\in[0,T]}(|X^{1,N}_t-\bX^1_t|^2+|U^{12,N}_t-\bU^{12}_t|^2)\Big] \leq \frac{C_T}N.
$$

(ii) If~\eqref{m2c} and~\eqref{meu} hold, then
for all $T>0$, there is  $C_{T}>0$ such that
for all $N\geq 2$,
$$
\E\Big[\sup_{t\in[0,T]}(|X^{1,N}_t-\bX^1_t|+|U^{12,N}_t-\bU^{12}_t|)\Big] \leq \frac{C_T\exp(C_T\sqrt{\log N})}{N^{\frac 12}}.
$$

(iii) In either case above, introduce
$f_t=\mathrm{Law}(\bX^1_t,\bX^2_t,\bU^{12}_t)$.
For all $T>0$, there is  $C_T>0$ such that for all $N\geq 3$,
$$
\sup_{t\in [0,T]}\E\Big[\cW_1\Big(\frac1{N(N-1)}\sum_{i,j \in I_N,i\neq j}\delta_{(X^{i,N}_t,X^{j,N}_t,U^{ij,N}_t)},f_t\Big)\Big]
\leq \frac{C_T}{N^{\frac 1{2d+1}}}.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Corollary 11 (Parseval-type identity and intrinsic reconstruction) of arXiv:2608.30589, 'Vector-Valued Wavelet Bases as Hilbert $\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})$-Module Bases: A Construc'] Assume that the family $\{\Psi_{j,k}\}_{(j,k)\in\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}^d}\subset L^2(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbb{R}^m)$
is a Parseval $\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})$-module frame, i.e.\ for every $f\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbb{R}^m)$ one has the reconstruction
\begin{equation}
f=\sum_{(j,k)\in\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}^d}\langle f,\Psi_{j,k}\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})}\,\Psi_{j,k},
\end{equation}
with convergence in the Hilbert-module norm. For $f\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbb{R}^m)$ define
\[
C_{j,k}:=\langle f,\Psi_{j,k}\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})}\in\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R}).
\]
Then:
\[
\sum_{(j,k)\in\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}^d}\langle f,\Psi_{j,k}\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})}\,
\langle \Psi_{j,k},f\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})}
=\langle f,f\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})},
\]
and
\[
f=\sum_{(j,k)\in\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}^d} C_{j,k}\,\Psi_{j,k},
\]
with convergence in the Hilbert-module norm. In particular, the coefficient family $\{C_{j,k}\}$ uniquely determines $f$.

body:
[Lemma 55 of arXiv:2608.30059, 'Multihomogeneous Measures and Stochastic Polar Representations'] Let \(\nu\in M_{\chi,\sigma}(E)\) and consider:
\begin{enumerate}[\rm(i)]
\item
\(\nu=\nu_Z\) for some \(E\)-valued random element \(Z\).

\item
There is a finite-valued measurable \(h:E\to[0,\infty)\) such that
\[
L_h=1\quad\nu\text{-almost everywhere}.
\]

\item
There is a finite-valued measurable \(f:E\to(0,\infty)\) such that
\[
0<K_f<\infty\quad\nu\text{-almost everywhere}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Conditions \textup{(ii)} and \textup{(iii)} are always equivalent.
If \(\rho\not\equiv1\), all three conditions are equivalent.

If \(\rho\equiv1\), condition \textup{(i)} holds if and only if
there is an \(h\) as in \textup{(ii)} satisfying
\[
\int_Eh(x)\,d\nu(x)=1.
\]
Whenever positive representing measures exist, they have a common
total mass, and a probability representing measure exists precisely
when this common mass is one.

body:
Let U be an open subset of C and f holomorphic on U. If gamma is a closed piecewise smooth curve in U that is null-homotopic in U - in particular, any closed curve when U is simply connected - then the integral of f over gamma is zero. Homology form: the integral of f over a cycle gamma in U vanishes for every holomorphic f on U if and only if the winding number n(gamma, a) is zero for every point a outside U. Consequently, on a simply connected domain every holomorphic function has a holomorphic primitive.
f holomorphic on all of U (a single pole inside the curve breaks the conclusion)
gamma null-homotopic in U, or U simply connected

body:
[Proposition prop:morse-count of arXiv:2609.00336, 'Critical points of point charge potentials along lines'] Let $p>0$, locations $x_1 , \ldots , x_m \in \mathbb{R}$ be pairwise distinct, and $q_1, \ldots , q_m$ all nonzero, and satisfying $Q:=\sum_{r=1}^m q_r\neq0$. Further suppose that all critical points of the potential 
		\[
		U(a,b)=\sum_{r=1}^m \frac{ q_r}{\big((a-x_r)^2+b^2\big)^{p/2}},
		\]
		are nondegenerate. Then, $U$ has exactly $m-1$ critical points, all of which are saddles.
title: Proposition prop:morse-count of arXiv:2609.00336

[Definition 8 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] Let \(U\subset Y^{\rm rv}\) be open.  We say that
\((\mathrm S)_U\) holds if there are \(t_U<T\) and \(c_U>0\), independent
of \(x\in\pi^{-1}(U)\) and \(t\in[t_U,T)\), such that
\begin{equation}
 S_{t,x}\ge c_U\eta,
 \qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad
 Q_{t,x}\le c_U^{-1}\eta^{-1}.
\end{equation}
We say that \((\mathrm Q)_U\) holds if there are \(t_U<T\) and
\(C_U<\infty\), with the same uniformity, such that
\begin{equation}
 S_{t,x}\le C_U\eta,
 \qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad
 Q_{t,x}\ge C_U^{-1}\eta^{-1}.
\end{equation}
When an estimate holds for all \(0\le t<T\), as will be the case for
the estimates proved below, we use the same notation.  Condition
\((\mathrm S)_U\) supplies the upper differential bound for pulled-back
base coordinates, whereas \((\mathrm Q)_U\) is the lower differential
bound that prevents loss of base rank.
title: Definition 8 of arXiv:2609.02878

body:
[Theorem thm:d_thin_dom_attract of arXiv:2411.03609, 'Asymptotically optimal Wasserstein couplings for the small-time stable domain of attractio'] Let $\alpha \in (0,2)\setminus\{1\}$ and Assumption~(\nameref{asm:T}) hold for some $p>0$. Then, for any $q\in(0,1]$ satisfying the condition $\int_{\mathbb{R}^d\setminus B_{\bm{0}}(1)}|\bm{w}|^q\nu_{\bm{X}}^{\mathrm{d}}(\mathrm{d} \bm{w})<\infty$, we have $\mathds{E}\big[\sup_{s\in[0,1]} |\bm{R}_{st}/t^{1/\alpha}|^q\big] 
    = \mathcal{O} \big(t^{1-q/\alpha}\big)$ as $t \downarrow 0$. Moreover, for any real number $q\in(0,\alpha)\cap(0,1]$, we let $\kappa(t)\coloneqq t^r$ for $t\in(0,1]$ and some $r\geqslant -1/\alpha$. Then, as $t \downarrow 0$, we have
\begin{align}
\mathcal{W}_q\big(\bm{J}^{\bm{S}^t,\kappa(t)},\bm{J}^{\bm{Z},\kappa(t)}\big)
    &=\begin{dcases}
    \mathcal{O}\big(t^{1-q/\alpha}\big(1+\log(1/t)\1_{\{p+q=\alpha,\,r\ne -1/\alpha\}}\big)\big), & \text{for }p+q\geqslant\alpha,\\
    \mathcal{O}\big(t^{p/\alpha + r(p+q-\alpha)}\big), & \text{for }p+q< \alpha. 
    \end{dcases} 
\\
\mathcal{W}_2\big(\bm{D}^{\bm{S}^t,\kappa(t)},\bm{D}^{\bm{Z},\kappa(t)}\big)^2
    &=\mathcal{O}\big(t^{p/\alpha+r(p-\alpha+2)}\big), \\

    |\bm{\gamma}_{\bm{S}^t,\kappa(t)}-\bm{\gamma}_{\bm{Z},\kappa(t)}| 
&=\begin{dcases}
    \mathcal{O}\big(t^{1-1/\alpha}(1+\1_{\{p+1=\alpha,\,r\ne-1/\alpha\}}\log(1/t))\big),
    &p\geqslant \alpha-1>0,\\
    \mathcal{O}(t^{p/\alpha+ r(p-\alpha+1)}),&p<\alpha-1\text{ or }\alpha\in(0,1).
\end{dcases}
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:d_thin_dom_attract of arXiv:2411.03609

body:
[Lemma lem:sepstatdetcon of arXiv:2606.02472, 'Correlated uniform attachment trees'] From two sequences $(X_j^{i})_{j\geq 1}$, $i=1,2$ with $X_j^{i} \in \{0,1,\ldots, j-1\}$, generate a paired tree sequence $(T_k^{1}, T_k^{2})_{k\geq 1}$, where the edges of $T_k^{i}$ are $\{\{j, X_j^{i}\}\}_{j=0}^k$.
    Fix a sequence of time steps $0<K_0<K_1<\cdots< K_\ell< m<n$, and assume  $(X_j^{1},X_{j}^{2})_{j\geq 1}$  are such that the following hold. 
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
        \item For all $j=0,\ldots, \ell$, the $K_j$ most central nodes of $(T_k^{i})_{k\geq 1}$, $i=1,2$, do not change after step $m$, meaning
        \[
        A_{K_j}^{i}(N) = A_{K_j}^{i}(m) \text{ for all } N \geq m, \, i=1,2, \, \text{and } j=0,\ldots, \ell.
        \]
        \item After time step $m$, the differences in the number of nodes connecting to $A_{K_j}^{i}$ in each of the two trees has the following uniform bound
        \ba{
         \max_{j \in \{0,\ldots, \ell \}} \left| \sum_{k=m+1}^{n} \mathbbm{1}_{ \left\{ X_k^{1} \in A_{K_j}^{1}(m) \right\} }  - \sum_{k=m+1}^{n} \mathbbm{1}_{ \left\{ X_k^{2} \in A_{K_j}^{2}(m)\right\} } \right| \leq \log(n)^{2/3}.
        }
         \item After time step $m$, the weighted sum of squares of the differences in the number of nodes connecting to $A_{K_j}^{i}(m)$ in each of the two trees satisfies the bound
        \[
        \frac{1}{\ell + 1} \sum_{j=0}^{\ell} \frac{1}{K_j} \bbbclr{  \sum_{k=m+1}^{n} \mathbbm{1}_{ \left\{ X_k^{1} \in A_{K_j}^{1}(m) \right\} }  - \sum_{k=m+1}^{n} \mathbbm{1}_{ \left\{ X_k^{2} \in A_{K_j}^{2}(m) \right\} } }^2 > C\log(n),
       \]
       for some fixed  $C>0$.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then
    \ban{
        \frac{1}{(\ell + 1)\log(n)} \sum_{j=0}^{\ell} \frac{1}{K_j} &\bbbclr{ \sum_{x \in A_{K_j}^{1}(n)} \deg_{T_n^{1}}(x) -  \sum_{x \in A_{K_j}^{2}(n)} \deg_{T_n^{2}}(x)  }^2
            \\
         &> C  - \frac{1}{(\ell + 1)\log(n)} \sum_{j=0}^{\ell} \frac{2(m+1) \log(n)^{2/3} + (m+1)^2}{K_j}. \notag
    } (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:sepstatdetcon of arXiv:2606.02472

body:
For any formal series E in power sum symmetric functions, the plethystic exponential satisfies Exp(E + F) = Exp(E) * Exp(F), and Exp(sum_{k=1}^infinity p_k / k) = prod_{i} (1 - x_i)^(-1). The boundary Cauchy-Littlewood identity is equivalent to evaluating Exp on the specialized difference of alphabets representing boundary reflection charges.
Formal power series in symmetric function algebra

body:
[Theorem thm:funkan of arXiv:2507.22011, 'Random Lozenge Waterfall:\\Dimensional Collapse of Gibbs Measures'] {reed1972}}]
	
	Assume that $A_N$ and $A$ are self-adjoint operators on the same Hilbert space $H$,
	and they have a common essential domain $H_0\subset H$.
	Assume that $A_N\varphi\to A\varphi$ as $N\to +\infty$ for all $\varphi\in H_0$.\footnote{The
	convergence on the common essential domain implies that $A_N\to A$ in the strong resolvent sense.}
	Let $a,b\in \mathbb{R}\cup\{\pm\infty\}$, $a<b$, be such that $a,b$ are not eigenvalues of $A$.
	Then
	\begin{equation*}
		P_{(a,b)}(A_N)\hspace{1pt}\varphi \to P_{(a,b)}(A)\hspace{1pt}\varphi\quad \textnormal{as $N\to+\infty$\quad for all
		$\varphi\in H$},
	\end{equation*}

[Corollary cor:random-four-set-first-order of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Fix $h\geq2$.  As $q\to\infty$, a uniformly random

\[
 \mathbb P(|hA|=M_h-M_{h-r})
 =\frac{24\kappa_r}{q}+O_h(q^{-2})

\]
and
\[
 \mathbb P(|hA|=M_h)
 =1-\frac{24K_h}{q}+O_h(q^{-2}).
\]
Every other attainable cardinality has probability
$\Theta_{h,n}(q^{-2})$.  In particular,
\[
 \mathbb P(A\text{ is not }B_h)
 =\frac{24K_h}{q}+O_h(q^{-2}),
 \qquad K_h\asymp h^2.
\]

[Definition 10 of arXiv:2506.10494, 'Geometric Jensen-Shannon Divergence Between Gaussian Measures On Hilbert Space'] [\textbf{Regularized Kullback-Leibler divergence between Gaussian measures on Hilbert spaces}\cite{Minh:LogDet2016,Minh:2020regularizedDiv}]
			
			Let $\Ncal(m_1,C_1), \Ncal(m_2,C_2) \in \Gauss(\Hcal)$,
			
			
			
			with corresponding mean vectors $m_1,m_2 \in \H$  
			and
			
			covariance operators $C_1, C_2 \in \Sym^{+}(\H) \cap \Tr(\H)$. 
			For any 
			
			fixed $\gamma \in \R$, 
			$\gamma > 0$, 
			the regularized 
			
			KL divergence, denoted by ${\KL}^{\gamma}(\Ncal(m_1, C_1)|| \Ncal(m_2, C_2))$, 
			
			is defined to be
			\begin{align}
				
				{\KL}^{\gamma}(\Ncal(m_1, C_1)|| \Ncal(m_2, C_2)) 
				
				&=\frac{1}{2}\la m_1 - m_2, (C_2 + \gamma I)^{-1}(m_1 - m_2)\ra 
				\nonumber
				\\
				&\quad + \frac{1}{2}d^1_{\logdet}[(C_1 + \gamma I), (C_2 + \gamma I)].
			\end{align}
title: Definition 10 of arXiv:2506.10494

Every bounded sequence of real numbers has a convergent subsequence. More generally, every bounded sequence in R^n has a convergent subsequence.

For any subset A of R^n, sequential compactness (every sequence in A has a subsequence converging to a point of A) is equivalent to A being closed and bounded. In every infinite-dimensional normed space, the closed unit ball is closed and bounded but not sequentially compact, so neither finite-dimensional formulation extends to all normed spaces.

[Theorem deg_7_cubature_formula of arXiv:2411.13707, 'High-degree cubature on Wiener space \\ through unshuffle expansions'] Let $(z_i,\lambda)$, $(z_{ij},\mu)$ and $(z,\eta)$ be independent Gaussian cubature formulae of $(\text{deg}=7, \text{dim}=d)$, $(\text{deg}=3, \text{dim}=d^2)$ and $(\text{deg}=2, \text{dim}=1)$ respectively. Define,
\begin{align*}
\mathcal{L}^{(n,m,r)} \coloneqq{}& \epsilon_0 + \sum_{i}\Big (z_i^{(n)}\epsilon_i+\frac{1}{\sqrt 3}z_{ii}^{(m)}\mathrm{e}(\epsilon_0\epsilon_i)+\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{e}(\epsilon_0\epsilon_i\epsilon_i)\Big ) +\sum_{i,j}\Big[ \Big( \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}z_i^{(n)} z_{jj}^{(m)}+ \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}z_{ij}^{(m)}\Big) \mathrm{e}(\epsilon_i\epsilon_j)\\
&+\frac{1}{2} z_i^{(n)}\mathrm{e}(\epsilon_i\epsilon_j\epsilon_j)+\frac{1}{12}\mathrm{e}(\epsilon_0\epsilon_i\epsilon_i\epsilon_j\epsilon_j)+\frac{1}{24}\mathrm{e}(\epsilon_i\epsilon_i\epsilon_0\epsilon_j\epsilon_j)\Big] +\sum_{i,j,k} \Big (\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} z_{ij}^{(m)}z_k^{(n)}z^{(r)}\mathrm{e}(\epsilon_i\epsilon_j\epsilon_k)\\
&+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}z_{i}^{(n)}z_{jj}^{(m)}\mathrm{e}(\epsilon_i\epsilon_j\epsilon_k\epsilon_k)+\frac{1}{4\sqrt{3}}z_{i}^{(n)}z_{kk}^{(m)}\mathrm{e}(\epsilon_i\epsilon_j\epsilon_j\epsilon_k)+\frac{1}{12}z_i^{(n)} \mathrm{e}(\epsilon_i\epsilon_j\epsilon_j\epsilon_k\epsilon_k)\\
&+\frac{1}{24}z_j^{(n)} \mathrm{e}(\epsilon_i\epsilon_i\epsilon_j\epsilon_k\epsilon_k)\Big ).
\end{align*}
and $\theta_{n,m,r} = \lambda_n\mu_m\eta_r$ for each $(n,m,r)$ that indexes the product measure $(z_i,\lambda)\times (z_{ij},\mu)\times (z,\eta)$. Then
$\mathcal{L}^{(n,m,r)}$ and $\theta_{n,m,r}$ define the Lie polynomials and weights respectively of a degree-\(7\) cubature formula on \(d\)-dimensional Wiener space with drift. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:mixingtime of arXiv:2411.18563, 'Lower tails for triangles inside the critical window'] In the setting of Theorem~(thm:barbour2019longterm of the paper),
let $y_0\in\Omega_{\text{typ}}$ and let  $P=(Y_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ where we set $Y_0=y_0$.
Let $\nu$ denote the stationary distribution of $P$. For $k \geq 1$, we have
\[
W_1(\nu,Y_k) \leq \textup{diam}(\Omega)\left((1 - \rho)^{k} + 2k e_k + \nu(\Omega\setminus \Omega_{\text{typ}})\right).
\]
As a consequence, we have
\[
\left|\nu(f) - \mathbb{E}\left[f(Y_k)\right]\right| \leq L\cdot \textup{diam}(\Omega)\left((1 - \rho)^{k} + 2k e_k + \nu(\Omega\setminus \Omega_{\text{typ}}\right)\, ,
\]
where $\nu(f)$ denotes the expectation of $f$ with respect to $\nu$.
title: Lemma lem:mixingtime of arXiv:2411.18563

[Definition def:waterfall_region of arXiv:2507.22011, 'Random Lozenge Waterfall:\\Dimensional Collapse of Gibbs Measures'] Fix the scaled dimensions
	$\mathsf{T},\mathsf{S},\mathsf{N}$
	of the hexagon, and let $(\mathsf{t},\mathsf{x})$ be the scaled
	coordinates. Denote by $\mathcal{H}$ the scaled hexagon, that is,
	\begin{equation}
		
		\mathcal{H}\coloneqq \left\{
		(\mathsf{t},\mathsf{x})\colon 0< \mathsf{t}<\mathsf{T},\
		\max(0,\mathsf{t}-\mathsf{T}+\mathsf{S})< \mathsf{x}<
		\min(\mathsf{S}+\mathsf{N},\mathsf{t}+\mathsf{N})\right\}.
	\end{equation}
	Let
	\begin{equation}
		
		\mathsf{t}_l\coloneqq
		|\mathsf{N}-\mathsf{S}|
		,
		\qquad
		\mathsf{t}_r\coloneqq
		\min(\mathsf{N}+\mathsf{S},2\mathsf{T}-\mathsf{N}-\mathsf{S}).
	\end{equation}
	Denote the \emph{waterfall region} by
	\begin{equation}
		
		\mathcal{W}\coloneqq \left\{ (\mathsf{t},\mathsf{x})\in \mathcal{H}\colon
			\mathsf{t}_l< \mathsf{t}< \mathsf{t}_r,
			\
			|2\mathsf{x}-\mathsf{S}-\mathsf{t}|< \mathsf{N}
		\right\}.
	\end{equation}
	Also, let the \emph{center line} be the following line segment of slope $\frac{1}{2}$:
	\begin{equation}
		
		\mathcal{C}\coloneqq
		\left\{ (\mathsf{t},\mathsf{x})\in \mathcal{H}\colon
		\mathsf{t}_l< \mathsf{t}< \mathsf{t}_r,\
		\mathsf{x}=\tfrac12(\mathsf{t}+\mathsf{S})
		\right\}
		\subset \mathcal{W}.
	\end{equation}
	See (fig:waterfall_region of the paper) for illustrations of the waterfall
	region and the corresponding exact samples
	from the $q$-Racah measure generated by the
	shuffling algorithm of [borodin-gr2009q].

[Corollary 5 (Convergence to the dynamical $ \Phi^{\kk+1}$ model) of arXiv:2605.28677, 'Weak universality for stochastic reaction-diffusion models\\ with long-range correlated no'] Let the random field $\zeta$ satisfy Assumption~\ref{ass_zeta}, 
and assume that its rescaling $\xi_\ve$ defined in \eqref{rescaled_noise} converges in law in the sense of Schwartz distributions to a random field $\xi$. 
Then 

\begin{itemize}
\item the smooth model $(\Pi^\ve,\Pi^{-,\ve},\Gamma^\ve)$ of Theorem~\ref{prop_main_reg} 
converges in law to a model $(\Pi,\Pi^-,\Gamma)$ with respect to the distance induced by

\begin{equation}
\max_{|\beta|\leq2} \big\{\|\Pi\|_\beta+\|\Pi^-\|_\beta+\|\Gamma\|_\beta\big\} \, ,
\end{equation}

\item $\Pi$ and $\Pi^-$ satisfy almost surely \eqref{pde_Pi} for $[\beta]\geq0$.
\end{itemize}
The convergence in the first item also holds in probability (respectively in $L^p$ for all $p<\infty$), provided the underlying sequence of random fields $\xi_\ve$ converges in probability (respectively in $L^p$ for all $p<\infty$) to a random field $\xi$.

Moreover, if we repeat the construction of $(\Pi^\ve,\Pi^{-,\ve},\Gamma^\ve)$ in Theorem~\ref{prop_main_reg} with multiindices only over $\{\kk\}\cup\NN^{1+d}$ 
(in particular all sums and products over $k\geq\kk$ collapse to $k=\kk$)
to obtain a model $(\Pi^\ve_{\kk},\Pi^{-,\ve}_{\kk},\Gamma^\ve_{\kk})$ for \eqref{eq_limit}, 
then $(\Pi^\ve_{\kk},\Pi^{-,\ve}_{\kk},\Gamma^\ve_{\kk})$ converges to a limiting model $(\Pi_{\kk},\Pi^-_{\kk},\Gamma_{\kk})$ which coincides with 
$(\Pi,\Pi^-,\Gamma|_{\RR[\![z_{\kk},z_\n]\!]})$ in the following sense:
For multiindices $\beta$ with $\sum_{k>\kk}\beta(k) = 0$ it holds 

\begin{equation}
\Pi_\beta=\Pi_{\kk,\beta} \, , \quad
\Pi^-_\beta=\Pi^-_{\kk,\beta} \, , \quad
\textnormal{and}\quad (\Gamma)_\beta^\gamma = (\Gamma_{\kk})_\beta^\gamma 
\quad\textnormal{for all $\gamma$ with $\sum_{k>\kk}\gamma(k)=0$} \, , 
\end{equation}

while for $\beta$ satisfying $\sum_{k>\kk}\beta(k)>0$ it holds

\begin{equation}
\Pi_\beta=0 \, , \quad
\Pi^-_\beta=0 \, , \quad
\textnormal{and}\quad (\Gamma)_\beta^\gamma=0 
\quad\textnormal{for all $\gamma$ with $\sum_{k>\kk}\gamma(k)=0$} \, .
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Convergence to the dynamical $ \Phi^{\kk+1}$ model

[Lemma 2q:moment of arXiv:2510.09818, 'On the Fourier dimension of fractional Brownian graphs'] [LL25].
Let $B$ be a fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H \in (0,1)$, and recall that the Fourier transform of $\mu_{G}$ is given by~(equation b1 of the paper). Then for any $q\in \mathbb N_+$ and $\xi_1, \xi_2 \in \mathbb R \setminus\{0\}$, we have
\begin{align}
	\mathbb E\left[ |\hat{\mu}_G(\xi_1,\xi_2)|^{2q} \right]
	= \frac{(q!)^2}{|\xi_2|^{2q/H}} \sum_{\varepsilon\in \mathcal{A}_{2q}} \mathcal{I}_{T}^{\lambda}[\varepsilon, G_\varepsilon],
\end{align}
where the parameters $\lambda, T$ and the function $G_{\varepsilon}$ are chosen as
\begin{align}
	\lambda = \frac{\xi_1}{|\xi_2|^{1/H}}, \qquad
	T = |\xi_2|^{1/H} ,\quad \text{ and }\quad
	G_\varepsilon(u) = e^{-\pi\mathrm{Var}(\sum_{i=1}^{2q} \varepsilon_i B_{u_i})}.
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 2q:moment of arXiv:2510.09818

For 0 < p < 1 the functional ||f||_p = (int |f|^p)^{1/p} is NOT a norm and the triangle inequality is false. Counterexample: on [0,1] with Lebesgue measure take f = 1_{[0,1/2]} and g = 1_{(1/2,1]}. Then ||f+g||_p = ||1_{[0,1]}||_p = 1, while ||f||_p + ||g||_p = 2 * (1/2)^{1/p} = 2^{1 - 1/p} < 1 for every p < 1 (e.g. 2^{-1} = 0.5 at p = 1/2). What survives: (i) the reverse inequality ||f+g||_p >= ||f||_p + ||g||_p for nonnegative f, g when 0 < p < 1; (ii) the quasi-triangle inequality ||f+g||_p <= 2^{1/p - 1}(||f||_p + ||g||_p); (iii) the p-th power is subadditive, int |f+g|^p <= int |f|^p + int |g|^p, so d(f,g) = ||f - g||_p^p is a complete translation-invariant metric and L^p (0 < p < 1) is a complete metric topological vector space - but it is not locally convex on a nonatomic space, and its dual is {0}. Related trap: the generalized Hölder inequality with 1/r = sum 1/p_i remains valid for r < 1, but the TWO-exponent Hölder inequality with a negative conjugate exponent (0 < p < 1, q = p/(p-1) < 0) points the other way under the appropriate positivity and finiteness hypotheses, so the standard direction may not be quoted when p < 1.

[Defn of arXiv:2505.14762, 'Multiple radial SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Sutherland system'] The conformal group \( \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{D}) \) satisfies the following properties, see [S85]:
\begin{itemize}
    \item \( \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{D}) \) is isomorphic to \( PSL_2(\mathbb{R}) \). Each element \( \tau \in \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{D}) \) can be written as:
    \[
    \tau(z) = T_v \circ \rho_{\theta}(z),
    \]
    where \( \rho_\theta(z) = e^{i\theta} z \) and \( T_v(z) = \frac{z - v}{1 - \overline{v} z} \).

    Geometrically, \( \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{D}) \) is an \( S^1 \)-bundle over \( \mathbb{H} \), and it naturally acts on \( \partial \mathbb{D} \cong S^1 \) by extending the conformal maps to the boundary.

    \item The universal cover \( \widetilde{\mathrm{Aut}}(\mathbb{D}) \) is isomorphic to \( \widetilde{SL}_2(\mathbb{R}) \). Each element \( \tau \in \widetilde{\mathrm{Aut}}(\mathbb{D}) \) can be decomposed as:
    \[
    \tau = T_v \circ A_\theta,
    \]
    where \( \theta \in \mathbb{R} \), and \( A_\theta \) represents addition by \( \theta \) on \( \mathbb{R} \).

    Geometrically, \( \widetilde{\mathrm{Aut}}(\mathbb{D}) \) is an \( \mathbb{R} \)-bundle over \( \mathbb{H} \), and it naturally acts on \( \mathbb{R} \), the universal cover of \( S^1 \).

    \begin{itemize}
        \item For \( x \in \mathbb{R} \), \( A_\theta(x) = x + \theta \).
        \item For \( v \in \mathbb{D} \), there exists a unique \( |y - x| < \pi \) such that \( e^{iy} = T_v(e^{ix}) \).
    \end{itemize}
\end{itemize}
title: Unnumbered defn of arXiv:2505.14762, 'Multiple radial SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Sutherlan'

For iid weights equal to a>0 with probability p in (0,1) and b>a otherwise, suppose northeast directed bond percolation on the a-edges has positive forward survival probability theta(p). Then almost surely some global bi-infinite FPP geodesic exists. At the origin, forward and backward surviving-ray events depend on disjoint edge time levels and intersect with probability theta(p)^2. Their concatenation is monotone and every finite segment has Manhattan distance many a-edges, the minimum possible cost. Translation ergodicity upgrades positive probability of existence to probability one. This is a boundary obstruction to dropping nonatomicity, not a counterexample to the nonatomic-law target.

Hasebe, Ueda and Wang, Log-unimodality for free positive multiplicative Brownian motion (arXiv:2009.13848), Problem 4.7 asks: if nu is a probability measure supported on [alpha, beta] with 0 < alpha < beta, must there be a number D >= 0 (depending on nu) such that sigma_t (free multiplicative convolution) nu is log-unimodal for all t >= D? Our result (id P0193, 2026-09-08): NO. For nu = (delta_{1/10} + delta_{10})/2 on [1/10, 10] the convolution is log-unimodal for no t >= 5 pi. Using the authors' own Lemma 4.1(3) criterion with r = e^u and atoms e^{+-a}, a = log 10, the relevant integral equals F_R(u) = (K_R(u-a) + K_R(u+a))/2 with K_R(s) = 1/(2(cosh s - cos R)); choosing the unique R in [pi/2, pi) with R / sin R = t/10 (which exists exactly for t >= 5 pi) gives F_R(0) <= 1/(2 cosh a) = 10/101 < 1/10 while F_R(+-a) >= 1/8 > 1/10 and F_R tends to 0 at +- infinity, so the level set has four roots against the criterion's at most two. Verification as the source words it: both bounds are uniform over the whole admissible range of R (measured max F(0) = 0.099010, min F(a) = 0.129901), so this is a proof and not a numerical observation; and a control both ways - on the three cases where the authors' Theorem 4.4 applies (alpha = 1, beta = 1.1 / 1.2 / 1.3) the same root counter returns at most 2 roots at t = 1.01 D and t = 10 D, agreeing with their proved theorem. Prior art not cleared.
nu = (delta_{1/10} + delta_{10})/2, supported on [1/10, 10]
sigma_t the free positive multiplicative Brownian motion

body:
[Theorem 11 of arXiv:2506.10856, 'The space of multifurcating ranked tree shapes: enumeration, lattice structure, and Markov'] The space $\mathcal{T}_{N,K}$ of ranked tree shapes with $N$ leaves and $K$ internal nodes is in bijection with the space $\mathcal{F}_{N,K}$ of $K\times K$ lower triangular matrices with non-negative integer entries that obey the
following constraints:
\begin{enumerate}[label={F\arabic*.}]
    \item The diagonal elements $F_{i,i}$ are strictly increasing: $F_{1,1}< F_{2,2}<...<F_{K,K}$ with $F_{K,K}=N$. The subdiagonal elements satisfy $F_{i+1,i} = F_{i,i}-1$ for all $i=1,...,K-1$.
    \item The elements $F_{i,1}, i=3,...,K$ in the first column satisfy \[ \max\{0, F_{i-1,1}- 1\} \leq F_{i,1} \leq F_{i-1,1}\] This just implies the column elements are decreasing by at most 1 if $F_{i-1,1}$ is non-zero. 
    \item All other elements $F_{i,j}, i=4,...,K, j=2,...,i-2$ satisfy these three conditions. 
    \begin{enumerate}[label={\alph*.}]
        \item $\max\{0, F_{i,j-1} \} \leq F_{i,j}$: Row-wise non-decreasing. 
        \item $F_{i-1, j}-1 \leq F_{i,j} \leq F_{i-1, j}$: Column-wise change is either 1 or 0.
        \item $0\leq (F_{i-1, j} - F_{i,j}) - (F_{i-1, j-1}- F_{i,j-1}) \leq 1$: in any $2\times 2$ grid, sum of off-diagonal elements minus sum of on-diagonal elements is 1 or 0. 
    \end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
The space of such matrices is denoted $\mathcal{F}_{N,K}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 11 of arXiv:2506.10856

body:
[Lem 21 of arXiv:2609.00723, 'An integral Hyodo--Kato isomorphism'] Let $\sR=(R,\alpha_R\colon N\to R)$ be as in \eqref{eq;SN} and write $\sR/p=(R/p,N)$. The restriction on the subcategory $\mathrm{lSm}^{\rm Cart}_{\sR/p}$ of affine fine log-smooth algebras of Cartier type of the log-crystalline cohomology functor
      	\[
      	R\Gamma_{crys}(-/\sR) \colon \PreLog_{\sR/p} \to \mathcal{D}(R)^\wedge_p
      	\]
      	is the left Kan extension of its restriction to $\mathrm{lPoly}_{\sR/p}$. In particular, derived log crystalline cohomology and underived crystalline cohomology coincide for log smooth algebras of Cartier type.  
         Moreover, the algebra structure of $R\Gamma_{crys}(X/\sR)$ for $X\in \mathrm{lSm}^{\rm Cart}_{\sR/p}$ is left Kan extended from that for polynomial objects. 
     	\begin{proof}This is basically well-known, and follows the same argument of the non-logarithmic counterpart. We give a proof for the convenience of the reader. 
      		Considering the restriction of $R\Gamma_{crys}(-/\sR)$ to  polynomial pre-log algebras and the resulting left Kan extension, (here, we use the fact that $\mathcal{D}(R)^\wedge_p$ admits colimits)
      		we obtain a natural comparison map from derived log crystalline cohomology $dR\Gamma_{crys}(-/\sR)$ to $R\Gamma_{crys}(-/\sR)$. Both functors satisfy étale descent: this is clear for the underived version. As for derived log crystalline cohomology, it is enough to note that, since $dR\Gamma_{crys}(-/\sR)$ takes value in $p$-complete $\sR$-modules, we can check descent by reduction modulo $p$. Since by construction derived log crystalline cohomology is obtained by Kan extension from polynomials pre-log algebras over $\sR/p$, on any such algebra 
      		$\sP$,  we can choose a polynomial algebra $\widetilde{\sP}$ over $\sR$ as its smooth lift. Then, the derived log crystalline cohomology $R\Gamma_{\text{crys}}(\sP/\sR)$ is exactly computed by the $p$-completion of $\omega_{\widetilde{\sP}/\sR}^{*}$ as \eqref{eq;omegalogcryscomparison}. 
      		Reducing modulo $p$ again, this is precisely $\omega_{\sP/(\sR/p)}^{*}$, thus $dR\Gamma_{crys}(-/\sR)/p$ is $L\omega^*_{-/(\sR/p)}$, which satisfies étale descent. At this point, the claim of the Lemma follows again from the fact that         for log smooth pre-log algebras $\sA$ of Cartier type over $\sR/p$,
      		the comparison map 
      		$L\omega^*_{\sA/(\sR/p)}\to \omega^*_{\sA/(\sR/p)}$ is an equivalence (see for example \cite[Proposition 4.6]{BLPO-HKR}).
            Finally, the last statement follows from Remark \ref{rmk;multiplicativity}). 
                 	\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 21 of arXiv:2609.00723

[Proposition prop:multiport-closed of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Fix a scalar rooted centered orthogonal-Weingarten ribbon map $\Gamma$ and
remove passive singleton color components by centering.  Before estimating
anything, cut simultaneously every row or trace wire joining distinct
coefficient components, record every resulting port, choose a maximizing
smoothing and all prime tags, and record one base on each original
$p\vee r$ circuit.  This declares $\tau$.  For every pure-Weyl component
$P$ with $m_P\ge2$, discard the forbidden-pair zero terms and apply
(lem:two-carrier-packet of the paper); hence $c^{\!*}(P)\ge2$ and
(thm:packet of the paper) gives a presentation
$\zeta_{P,\tau}$ satisfying
\[
 \|\zeta_{P,\tau}\|_{\mathscr P_\tau}
 \le A^{m_P}n^{c^{\!*}(P)-2}
 \|C_P\|_2^2\|C_P\|_\mathrm{op}^{m_P-2}.
\tag{2.6.14a}
\]
All cut interfaces can be reclosed at once by a normalized scalar
projective contraction $\mathcal G_\Gamma$ with
\[
 \mathcal A_\Gamma
 =\omega_\Gamma\,
 \mathcal G_\Gamma\!\left(
   \widehat\bigotimes_P\zeta_{P,\tau}\right),
 \quad
 \|\mathcal G_\Gamma\|_\pi\le1,
 \quad
 |\omega_\Gamma|
 \le C^m n^{F-4m+\ell_\Gamma-g_{\rm Wg}}.
\tag{2.6.14b}
\]
No component is estimated inside a gap of another component and no
component token is split.

Own-work draft, proof (unaudited), T280-w716-C2 v2, independent review pending; novelty not asserted. Let input be uniform probability measure on S2 and let the neuron feature be a ReLU(w.x+b). Train all Euclidean parameters including bias. Suppose the initial law is invariant under (a,w,b)->(a,Qw,b) for every Q in O(3), with E[a^2+|w|^2+b^2]<infinity; use derivative zero at ReLU zero. Its population tangent operator has harmonic eigenvalues mu_k. Put r=|w|, s=-b/r only on {r>0, |b|<r}. Then mu_2-mu_3=E[1_{r>0,|b|<r}(1-s^2)^3{r^2(1-s^2)^2+a^2(28s^4+14s^2+6)}/256], with integrand defined as zero elsewhere, including r=0. Hence mu_2>=mu_3, strictly iff the crossing event has positive probability. The coefficient formula uses q_2(s)=(1-s^2)^2/16 and q_3(s)=s q_2(s) and conditional eigenvalue r^2 q_k^2+a^2[(q_k-s q_k_prime)^2+q_k_prime^2+k(k+1)q_k^2]. The q_k_prime^2 term is the trained-bias contribution. Symbolic Legendre integration and polynomial identities plus 1,365 exact rational/boundary cases passed. The harmonic-analysis argument remains unaudited; no Lean certificate is asserted. This excludes initial bias/radius tuning as a route to degree-3-before-degree-2 learning under rotational initialization; it does not exclude a later anisotropic feature-learning reversal or settle T280 Target 2.
Draft: proof (unaudited), not independently checked
All model, measure, metric and moment conditions are stated in the statement
title: Draft: biased ReLU Legendre degree-2 versus degree-3 tangent eigenvalue gap on S2 (T280 w716)

body: Publication record. S. Bubeck, Y. Li and D. Nagaraj conjectured that, for generic data, any two-layer neural network with m neurons that fits n noisy labels must have Lipschitz constant at least of order sqrt(n/m), with no restriction on the size of the weights; Bubeck and Sellke proved a universal version for Lipschitz-parameterized classes under a polynomial bound on the parameters. Y. Shmalo, A law of robustness for two-layer neural networks with arbitrary weights (arXiv:2607.07778, July 2026) proves the conjectured law up to one logarithmic factor for every continuous piecewise-linear activation, ReLU in particular, for data uniform on S^{d-1} (d >= 3) or drawn from N(0, I_d/d), labels in [-1, 1] with noise level sigma^2 > 0, and width-m two-layer networks with arbitrary real weights, biases and an affine skip connection. ResearchGate record 408594034. Not refereed.
title: Bubeck-Li-Nagaraj law of robustness conjecture proved up to one logarithmic factor for two-layer neural networks with arbitrary weights (Shmalo 2026, arXiv:2607.07778)

[Lem lem-1d-reduction of arXiv:2608.30807, 'Isodiametric-type upper bounds for Steklov eigenvalues'] Let $0\leq \gamma<1$. Then there exists a constant $C(\gamma)>0$ such that, for every positive function $a\in L^1(0,1)$ satisfying
\[
\int_0^1a(t)dt=1,
\]
there exists $f\in H_0^1(0,1)\setminus\{0\}$ such that
\[
\frac{\int_0^1a(t)|f'(t)|^2dt}{\int_0^1a(t)^{\gamma}f(t)^2dt}\leq C(\gamma).
\]

body:
[Proposition proposition-upperbound of arXiv:2411.04500, '\LARGE Probabilistic Approaches to The Energy Equality in Forced Surface Quasi-Geostrophic'] For every $\varepsilon,\delta(\varepsilon)>0$ and $m(\varepsilon)\in\mathbb{N}_+$, let $\theta_{\varepsilon,\delta(\varepsilon)}$ be a stochastic generalized Leray solution of (equation SPDE-SQG of the paper) in the sense of Definition (def-stochastic-leray of the paper) with initial data $ \theta_{\varepsilon, \delta(\varepsilon)}(0)$ satisfying Assumption (Gaussian-initial-data of the paper),  and let $\theta_{\varepsilon,m(\varepsilon)}$ be the solution of (equation Galerkin approximation equations-delta=0 of the paper) with initial data $ \theta_{\varepsilon, m(\varepsilon)}(0)\sim \mathcal{G}(0,\varepsilon P_{m(\varepsilon)}/2)$.  
	\item	(i) Let $\mu_{\varepsilon}=\mu_{\varepsilon,\delta(\varepsilon)}$ be the laws of $\theta_{\varepsilon,\delta(\varepsilon)}$ on $\mathbb{X}_{\alpha,\beta}$. Assume that the scaling regime (equation scaling-delta of the paper) holds for $(\varepsilon,\delta(\varepsilon))$, 
	then for any closed set $F\subset\mathbb{X}_{\alpha,\beta}$, 
	\begin{equation}
		\limsup_{\varepsilon\rightarrow0}\varepsilon\log\mu_{\varepsilon}(F)\leqslant-\inf_{\theta\in F}\mathcal{I}(\theta). 	
	\end{equation}
	\item(ii)  Let $\mu_{\varepsilon}=\mu_{\varepsilon,m(\varepsilon)}$ be the laws of $\theta_{\varepsilon,m(\varepsilon)}$ on $\mathbb{X}_{\alpha,\beta}$. Assume that the scaling regime (equation scaling-m of the paper) holds for $(\varepsilon,m(\varepsilon))$, then for any closed set $F\subset\mathbb{X}_{\alpha,\beta}$, the upper bound (equation upper-bound of the paper) holds as well.
title: Upper bound

body:
[Cor nmlinfinf of arXiv:2412.00822, '\textsc{Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations \\ beyond hyperbolic spaces}'] Let $(\theta_{1},\phi_{1},r_{1})$ and $(\theta,\phi,r)$ be two corona points.
In the model of $\mathcal{M}$ given by the product of upper-half planes $\mathbb{U}_{2} \times \mathbb{U}_{2}$:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] If $(\theta_{1},\phi_{1})$ is sent at $(\infty,\infty)$,

$$
\emph{\text{NML}}((\infty,\infty, r_{1}),(\theta,\phi, r)) = \left \lbrace (z_{1},z_{2})\in \mathcal{M}\,;\;  |z_{1}-\theta|^{2} \cdot |z_{2}-\phi|^{2}=\frac{r_{1}}{r}\left(1+|\theta|^{2} \right)\left(1+|\phi|^{2} \right)\right \rbrace \; ;
$$
\item[(ii)] If $(\theta_{1},\phi_{1})$ is sent at $(\infty,y)$, for $y\in \mathbb{R}$,
{
$$
\emph{\text{NML}}((\infty,y, r_{1}),(\theta,\phi, r)) = \left \lbrace (z_{1},z_{2})\in \mathcal{M} \,;\;  \frac{|z_{1}-\theta|^{2} \cdot |z_{2}-\phi|^{2}}{|z_{2}-y|^{2}}=\frac{r_{1}}{r}\frac{\left(1+|\theta|^{2} \right)\left(1+|\phi|^{2} \right)}{1+|y|^{2}}\right \rbrace \;.
$$
}

\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \textsc{Geometry of the no man's land in the product of upper-half planes}

[Theorem Thm:compactness_thm_1 of arXiv:2604.07497, 'The Three-Dimensional Stochastic EMHD System: Local Well-Posedness and Maximal Pathwise So'] Let $X \subset Y \subset Z$ be Banach spaces such that $X$ and $Z$ are reflexive and the embedding $X \subset \subset Y$ is compact and $Y \hookrightarrow Z$ is continuous. L^p(0,T;X) \cap W^{\gamma,p}(0,T;Z) \subset \subset L^p (0,T;Y).
\]

[Proposition 12 of arXiv:2605.16560, 'Seasonal Statistics of Shannon Rate in a Dynamical Poisson-Voronoi Cellular Network'] For any $\beta, \gamma\geq 0$, the joint distribution of $H^2_{\sst \Ical}$ and $R^2_{\sst \Ical}$ is given by the joint Laplace transform 

\[
\E^0_{\Vcal_{\sst \Ical}}\left[e^{-\g H_{\sst \Ical}^2-\b R_{\sst \Ical}^2}\right]
{=}\frac{2\la\pi}{3\beta}\!\!\left[\!\left(1+\frac{\g}{\la\pi}\right)^{-\frac{3}{2}}\hspace{-0.17in} - \left(1+\frac{\g+\beta}{\la\pi}\right)^{-\frac{3}{2}}\right].
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 12 of arXiv:2605.16560

[Proposition Prop.LowerBound of arXiv:2411.15485, '\bf\Large Stochastic Volterra Equations for Local Times of Spectrally Positive L\'evy Proc'] For each $\beta>\beta_0$, there exist constants $n_0\geq 1$ and $C\geq 0$ such that for any $z\in \mathbb{R}$, 
 \begin{eqnarray}
  \inf_{n\geq n_0} \bigg|1-\int_0^\infty e^{\mathtt{i}zt -\frac{\beta}{n}  t} \cdot \gamma_n \overline\varPi_n(t)\, dt\bigg| \geq C  \cdot \big( |z|\wedge 1 \big).
 \end{eqnarray} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 3 of arXiv:2506.22040, '\vspace{-3em} Khinchin inequalities for uniforms on spheres with a deficit'] Let $\Psi$ be a smooth function on $\R^d$. For a fixed vector $v \in \R^d$, define
\[ 
f(t) = \int_{S^{d-1}} \Psi\big(v + t^{1/2}x\big) \dd x, \qquad t > 0.
 \]
Then
\begin{align}

f'(t) &= \frac{1}{2}\int_{B_2^d}\Delta\Psi\big(v + t^{1/2}x\big) \dd x, \\
f''(t) &= \frac{1}{4}\int_0^1r^{d+1}\left(\int_{B_2^d}\Delta\Delta\Psi\big(v + t^{1/2}rx\big) \dd x\right)\dd r.
\end{align}

[Definition 7 of arXiv:2609.03875, 'Measure theory without infinities'] Let $\mf A$ be a monoid. A map $\mu$ is said to be an $\mf A$-valued additive function if $\im\mu\subset \mf A$ and 
  $\mu(A) = \finsum \mu\circ\mb A$ for every $A\in D_\mu$ and every finite partition $\mb A$ of $A$ into elements of $D_\mu$. A map $\mu$ is called an $\mf A$-valued content if $\mu$ is an $\mf A$-valued additive function and $D_\mu$ is a ring.
title: Definition 7 of arXiv:2609.03875

body:
[Proposition 7 of arXiv:2608.26565, 'A Horizon-Free Extrinsic Penrose Inequality'] For every $t\in(0,t_0)$, the following assertions hold.
\begin{enumerate}
 \item[(i)] If $G\subset\Omega(\Gamma_1)$ has finite perimeter and finite
 measure and contains a one-sided neighborhood of $\Gamma_1$ in
 $\Omega(\Gamma_1)$, then adjoining $K_0$ does not increase $\mathscr F_t$:
 \begin{equation}
  \mathscr F_t(G\cup K_0)\leq\mathscr F_t(G).
  
 \end{equation}
 Equality holds if and only if $K_0\subset G$ almost everywhere.

 \item[(ii)] If $F$ is an inner end region, then truncation at
 either fixed leaf does not increase $\mathfrak J_t$:
 \begin{equation}
  \mathfrak J_t\bigl(F\cap\Omega(\Gamma_i)\bigr)
  \leq\mathfrak J_t(F),\qquad i=0,1.
  
 \end{equation}
 For each $i$, equality holds if and only if
 $F\setminus\Omega(\Gamma_i)$ has measure zero.

 \item[(iii)] Every $\mathscr F_t$-minimizer $G$ among finite-perimeter sets
 $G'$ satisfying
 \[
  K_0\subset G'\subset\Omega(\Gamma_1),
  \qquad |G'|<\infty,
 \]
 contains a slab extending across $\Gamma_0$: there is a minimal leaf
 $\Gamma_-\prec\Gamma_0$ in the extension across $\Gamma_0$ such that
 \[
  \Omega(\Gamma_1)\setminus\Omega(\Gamma_-)\subset G
  \quad\text{almost everywhere}.
 \]
\end{enumerate}
title: Proposition 7 of arXiv:2608.26565

body:
[Theorem 14 (Aligned anisotropic Gaussian allocation) of arXiv:2608.21709, 'Posterior Information Dynamics of Diffusion Models for Linear Inverse Problems'] Let $X_0\sim\calN(0,\Sigma)$, where
\[
\Sigma=V\diag(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d)V^\top,
\qquad \lambda_i>0.
\]
Let $A\in\R^{d_y\times d}$ have full row rank and suppose the measurement
is aligned with the prior eigenbasis,
\[
A=U\begin{bmatrix}\diag(s_1,\ldots,s_{d_y})&0\end{bmatrix}V^\top,
\qquad
\Gamma=\sigma_y^2\Id_{d_y},
\]
with $s_i=0$ for $i>d_y$.  Define
\begin{equation}

B_{i,t}=a_t^2\lambda_i+\Delta_t,
\qquad
v_{i,t}=\frac{\lambda_i\Delta_t}{B_{i,t}},
\qquad
\tau_i^2=\left(\lambda_i^{-1}+s_i^2/\sigma_y^2\right)^{-1},
\qquad
\widetilde B_{i,t}=a_t^2\tau_i^2+\Delta_t,
\end{equation}
where $\tau_i^2=\lambda_i$ when $s_i=0$.  Under the joint law of $(X_t,R)$,
\begin{equation}

\E|s_{t,i}^{\rm prior}(X_t)|^2=\frac1{B_{i,t}},
\qquad
\E|g_{t,i}(X_t,R)|^2
=
\frac{a_t^2s_i^2\lambda_i^2}
{B_{i,t}^2(s_i^2v_{i,t}+\sigma_y^2)},
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}

\rho_i(t)
=
\frac{a_t^2s_i^2\lambda_i^2}
{B_{i,t}(s_i^2v_{i,t}+\sigma_y^2)}
=
\frac{B_{i,t}}{\widetilde B_{i,t}}-1.
\end{equation}
Consequently:
\begin{enumerate}
\item As $a_t\to0$,
\[
\rho_i(t)=
\frac{a_t^2s_i^2\lambda_i^2}{s_i^2\lambda_i+\sigma_y^2}+O(a_t^4).
\]
\item For $s_i>0$, $\rho_i(t)$ is strictly increasing along the reverse
trajectory, with low-noise limit $s_i^2\lambda_i/\sigma_y^2$, and
\begin{equation}

\rho_i(t)=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\widetilde B_{i,t}=\frac12B_{i,t}.
\end{equation}
Thus, within this aligned linear-Gaussian model, $\rho_i=1$ is a
variance-halving, equal-Fisher-energy reference level.  It is crossed at a
unique interior noise level iff $s_i^2\lambda_i>\sigma_y^2$; when
$s_i^2\lambda_i=\sigma_y^2$, it is attained only at the clean endpoint.
\item Since the exact force is null on unmeasured aligned coordinates,
\begin{equation}

\rho_t^{\rm global}=\omega_t\rho_t^{\rm row},
\qquad
\omega_t=
\frac{\sum_{i:s_i>0}B_{i,t}^{-1}}{\sum_{i=1}^dB_{i,t}^{-1}}.
\end{equation}
For an isotropic prior, $\omega_t=d_y/d$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem lA4cor of arXiv:2504.07255, 'A Tail-Respecting Splitting Numerical Scheme\\ for L\'evy-Driven SDEs With Superlinear Dri'] For any $q\in(0,p)$
\begin{equation}\begin{aligned}
\sup_{t\in[t_k, t_{k+1})}\mathbf{E}^{(N)}_{t_1,\dots,t_N}\Big[\|\Delta_t^n\|^q\Big|\mathcal{F}_{t_k-}\Big]
&\leq_C \|\Delta_{t_k-}^n\|^q\\
&+h_n^{\frac{p-q}{\chi}\wedge q}(1+\|X_{t_k-}^{(n)}\|^p)
+ h_n^{\frac{p-q}{\chi}\wedge q}(1+\|X_{t_k-}^n\|^{p})\\
&+ (U^n_{t_k-})^q
+h_n^{1\wedge \frac{q}2}(U_{t_k-}^n)^{(p-q)\wedge (q\chi)}+h_n^{1\wedge \frac{q}2}
\end{aligned}\end{equation}
for $n$ large enough uniformly over
$N\in\mathbb{N}$, partitions $\{t_1,\dots, t_N\}$,  and $k=1, \dots, N$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem lA4cor of arXiv:2504.07255

[Corollary cor:root-comparison of arXiv:2607.08551, 'Weighted-threshold Coupon Collection'] Let $(\delta_N)_{N \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a positive sequence such that $\delta_N<t_{N,\theta}$ for all sufficiently large $N$ and
\[
\frac{\Delta_{N,\theta}(\delta_N)^2}{w_N^\ast}\xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{}\infty.
\]
Then
\[
\lim_{N \to \infty} \mathbb{P}(|\tau_{N,\theta}-t_{N,\theta}| > \delta_N) = 0.
\]
title: Corollary cor:root-comparison of arXiv:2607.08551

body: Publication record. Y. Shmalo, Correlation of leaf heights at mesoscopic separation in the critical beta-splitting tree (October 2026). In the critical beta-splitting random tree on n leaves, closed into a cycle, take a uniformly random leaf and the leaf r places further round the cycle. Aldous and Janson (The critical beta-splitting random tree II: overview and open problems, arXiv:2303.02529, Section 3.9, Open Problem 1) asked for a proof that the correlation of the two leaf heights tends to 1 - alpha when log r_n / log n tends to alpha in [0, 1]. The paper proves that, uniformly in 1 <= r <= n/2, the covariance of the two heights is sigma^2 log(n/r) + O(sqrt(log n)) and the variance of one height is sigma^2 log n + O(sqrt(log n)), with sigma^2 = 2 zeta(3)/zeta(2)^3, so the correlation equals 1 - log r / log n + O((log n)^(-1/2)). The proof uses a potential of each leaf's position in its clade that decreases at rate zeta(2) up to square-integrable errors, and compares the two martingales it produces up to the cut that separates the two leaves. Exact rational checks, a Monte Carlo simulation and a Lean 4 file accompany the paper. Paper and code: https://github.com/yspennstate/beta-splitting-leaf-correlation (commit e337fd88d00f). Not refereed.
title: Correlation of leaf heights at mesoscopic separation in the critical beta-splitting tree tends to 1 - alpha, answering Aldous-Janson Open Problem 1 (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/beta-splitting-leaf-correlation)

[Lem l1-contraction of arXiv:2604.20629, 'Rates of forgetting for the sequentially Markov coalescent'] Let $q(t\mid x)$ be a probability distribution
in $t$ and assume that it is stochastically monotone, i.e.
\[
F_{x}(y):=\int^{y}_{0}q(t|x) dt
\]
is non-increasing in $x$ for fixed $y>0$. Further define the mean
map 
\[
m(x):=\int^{\infty}_{0}t q(t|x) dt.
\]
If there exists $0<r<1$ such that 
\begin{equation}
|m(a)-m(b)|\le r |a-b|,\qquad a,b>0,
\end{equation}
then the quantile coupling 
\[
X_{n+1}=F^{-1}_{X_{n}}(U_{n}),\qquad Y_{n+1}=F^{-1}_{Y_{n}}(U_{n}),\qquad U_{n}\sim\mathrm{Unif}(0,1),
\]
satisfies ((eq:contractive-coupling of the paper)).

[Thm 4 of arXiv:2506.20146, 'Parabolic Anderson Model in the Hyperbolic Space. Part I: Annealed Asymptotics'] For any $p\geqslant1$, the following second order
asymptotics holds true for the solution $u(t,x)$ to the PAM (\ref{eq:GlobalPAM}):
\begin{equation}
\lim_{t\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{\beta(pt)}\log\big(e^{-H(pt)}\langle u(t,o)^{p}\rangle\big)=-\sqrt{-\frac{Q''(0)}{2}}d,
\end{equation}
where $H(t)$, $\beta(t)$ are defined by (\ref{eq:CGF}), (\ref{eq:BetaScale})
respectively and $\langle\cdot\rangle$ means taking expectation with
respect to the $\xi$-randomness. In other words, the $p$-th moment
of $u(t,o)$ satisfies the asymptotics
\begin{equation}
\langle u(t,o)^{p}\rangle=\exp\Big(\frac{1}{2}\sigma^{2}p^{2}t^{2}-d\sqrt{-\frac{Q''(0)}{2}}p^{3/2}t^{3/2}(1+o(1))\Big)\ \ \ \text{as }t\rightarrow\infty.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 4 of arXiv:2506.20146

Unreviewed draft reduction. Let T be a stopping time for a discrete process and B a deterministic finite set of M>=1 states. At every kth visit to any x in B before T, assume conditional probability at least h, 0<h<1, of no further visit to x before T, using that visit's sigma-field. Then for integer t>=M, P(T>t and all pre-exit states lie in B)<=M(1-h)^(floor(t/M)-1). Iterate conditional next-visit bounds and use a union bound over B. This controls time only after the visit hazard and confinement are proved.

[Lem 93 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Recalling Definitions \ref{d:SDE.classification.sym}--\ref{d:measure.classes.sym}, we have
\begin{align*}
\sM^{\svi,\sym}(\alpha,0) 
&\subseteq \sM^{\svii,\sym}(\alpha,0)\,,\\
\sM^{\sideal,\sym}(\alpha,0) &\subseteq \sM^{\sx,\sym}(\alpha,0)\,.\end{align*}

\begin{proof}
We repeat the most relevant part of Definition~\ref{d:SDE.classification.sym} for the first assertion: 
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}[h]{r|cccccccc}
\MSRheader\\
\hline
\GREATdefn{sy}\\
\SPRdefn{sy}
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
The $\svi$ and $\svii$ classes
 differ only in the constraint on $p$: the $\svi$ class satisfies condition~\ref{it:3.6} (i.e. $p(\epsilon) \ge 1-\epsilon$, among other conditions) while the $\svii$ class satisfies condition~\ref{it:3.7} (i.e. $p\equiv 1$). Consider any
	\[\mu = \mu^\sym(q_*=0,b,\sigma,p,\zeta=\zeta_0)
	 \in \cM^{\svi,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)\,,\]
corresponding to controls
	\[(q_*=0,b,\sigma,w,p,\zeta=\delta_0,\zeta^\Ising=\delta_0) \in \Adm^{\svi,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)\,.\]
In particular, $p$ satisfies condition~\ref{it:3.6}.
Recall the notation of Definition~\ref{d:X.adm}: 
we have $(b,\sigma) \in \Adm(0;p,f)$
for budget function $f(t) = (\bbE w_t)^2 / \alpha$, so
    \[
        \acute\mu = \mu(q_*=0,b,\sigma,p,\zeta=\zeta_0) \in \cM(0;p,f)\,.
    \]
Note that $\mu = \sym(\acute\mu)$.
Now consider the functions $\tilde p, \hat p \in \incr([0,1];[0,1])$ given by $\tilde p \equiv 1$ and
    \[
        \hat p(t) = \begin{cases}
            p(\epsilon) & t\in [0,\epsilon) \,, \\
            p(t) & t \in [\epsilon,1]\,.
        \end{cases}
    \]
    Since the restrictions of $p$ and $\hat p$ to $[\epsilon,1]$ agree, Proposition~\ref{p:continuity.in.p.near.0} implies
    \beq
        d_\cH\Big(\cM(0;p,f),\cM(0;\hat p,f)\Big) 
        \le \Big(9(1+1/\alpha) \epsilon\Big)^{1/2}\,,
    \eeq
    for $\cM(0;p,f)$ specified in Definition~\ref{d:X.adm}.
    Since $p$ satisfies condition~\ref{it:3.6}, we have $p(\epsilon) \ge 1-\epsilon$, and so
    \[
        \|\hat p' - \tilde p'\|_1
        =\|\hat p' \|_1 
        = \hat p(1) - \hat p(\epsilon)
        = p(1) - p(\epsilon)
        \le \epsilon\,.
    \]
    Then Proposition~\ref{p:continuity.in.p} implies
    \beq
        d_\cH\Big(\cM(0;\hat p,f),\cM(0;\tilde p,f)\Big) 
        \le \Big(6(1+1/\alpha) \epsilon\Big)^{1/2}\,.
    \eeq
    For some $\tilde\epsilon = \tilde\epsilon(\epsilon)$ tending to $0$ as $\epsilon \rightarrow 0$, \eqref{e:grt.in.spr.hausdorff1} and \eqref{e:grt.in.spr.hausdorff2} imply the existence of $\tilde \mu \in \cM(0;\tilde p,f)$ such that
    (since $\sym$ is a contraction)
    \beq
        \bbW_2\Big(
        \mu=\sym(\acute{\mu}), 
        \sym(\tilde \mu)
        \Big) 
        \le \bbW_2(\acute \mu,\tilde \mu)
        \le \tilde\epsilon\,.
    \eeq
    Let $\tilde\mu$ be attained by controls $(\tilde b,\tilde \sigma) \in \Adm(0;\tilde p,f)$, i.e.,
    \[
        \tilde\mu = \mu(q_*=0,\tilde b,\tilde \sigma,\tilde p,\zeta=\zeta_0)\,.
    \]
Since $\tilde{p}\equiv1$ satisfies condition~\ref{it:3.7}, we have 
    \[
        (q_*=0,\tilde b,\tilde \sigma,w,\tilde p,\zeta=\delta_0,\zeta^\Ising=\delta_0) 
        \in \Adm^{\svii,\sym}(\alpha,0;\epsilon)\,,
    \]
    and therefore $\sym(\tilde\mu) \in \cM^{\svii,\sym}(\alpha,0;\epsilon)$. 
    Since for all $\mu \in \cM^{\svi,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)$ we can find such $\sym(\tilde\mu)$ satisfying \eqref{e:great.in.spr.sym.W2}, we conclude
    \[
        \cM^{\svi,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon) 
        \subseteq 
        \cB_{\tilde\epsilon}\Big( \sM^{\svii,\sym}(\alpha,0;\epsilon) \Big)\,.
    \]
Adjusting $\tilde\epsilon$ gives
    \[
        \cB_\epsilon\Big( \cM^{\svi,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon) \Big)
        \subseteq 
        \cB_{\tilde\epsilon}\Big( \sM^{\svii,\sym}(\alpha,0;\tilde\epsilon) \Big)\,.
    \]
Recalling Definition~\ref{d:measure.classes.sym}, 
taking a union over $L$ and an intersection over $\epsilon$ proves the first assertion.

We now repeat the most relevant part of Definition~ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:arithmetic of arXiv:2609.02041, 'Sparse $k$-AP Covering Sets and the Arithmetic Kakeya Conjecture'] There exists a constant $c>0$ 
such that for all sufficiently large $k$,
there exists a positive integer $Q$, $N$ and a subset 
$B\subseteq \{0,1,\dots,N-1\}$ such that 
$$|B| < N^{1-\frac{c}{\log\log k}}$$
and for every $x\in\{0,1,\dots,N-1\}$,
there exists a nonnegative integer $d$ such that 
$x-d$, $x-2d$, \dots, $x-(k-1)d$ are all in $B$.

\]

[Lemma lem:factorial-box-divisibility of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Let $d,t\geq0$ be integers, let $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_t$ be positive
integers, put $R=\ell_1\cdots\ell_t$, and, for an indeterminate $x$, set
\[
 \Psi_{\boldsymbol\ell,d}(x)
 =\sum_{0\leq j_i<\ell_i}
   \binom{x-j_1-\cdots-j_t+d}{d}.
\]
Here $\binom{X}{d}=X(X-1)\cdots(X-d+1)/d!$ is the generalized binomial
polynomial (with $\binom{X}{0}=1$).
There is a universal polynomial
\[
 F_{d,t}(X,L_1,\ldots,L_t)
 \in\mathbb Z[X,L_1,\ldots,L_t]
\]
of degree $d$ in $X$ such that, after the specialization
$X=x$ and $L_i=\ell_i$,
\begin{equation}
 (d+t)!\,\Psi_{\boldsymbol\ell,d}(x)
 =R F_{d,t}(x,\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_t).
\end{equation}
Its leading coefficient in $X$ is $(d+t)!/d!$.

Owner campaign draft, literature-based proof (unaudited), no novelty claim. Let P be the uniform Euclidean probability on [0,1]^2 and P_n the empirical measure of n iid P draws. Ambrosio, Stra and Trevisan, arXiv:1611.04960v1 Theorem 1.1 PDF p.3, prove lim_(n->infinity) (n/log n) E W2^2(P_n,P)=1/(4 pi); this is empirical-to-uniform, whereas their bipartite constant is 1/(2 pi). For Q_n=P_n*N(0,h_n^2 I_2), the explicit Gaussian coupling yields |sqrt(E W2^2(Q_n,P))-sqrt(E W2^2(P_n,P))|<=sqrt(2)h_n. Thus if h_n^2=o(log n/n), the smoothed expected squared-W2 cost has the same 1/(4 pi) limit after multiplication by n/log n. Taking h_n=1/n and fresh fraction r=1 contradicts a bound C(n^(-1)+h_n^2) with C independent of n,h. Hence the unqualified all-bandwidth T356 Target 1 fails in ambient dimension two even for a connected full-dimensional constant density on its compact domain. A logarithmic sampling term, a bandwidth regime that absorbs it, or a restricted law class is necessary. This does not refute the Lipschitz-curve law theorem: a Lipschitz image of an interval cannot carry uniform square probability. The local Gaussian transfer is the draft being checked, not a new claim to the established matching theorem. Evidence: w703 T356 C008 v1, with primary PDF and hash in SOURCES.jsonl.

[Theorem 9 (Covering-to-measure principle, \cite{dadush2022matrix} Lemma 3.3) of arXiv:2606.16005, '\bfseries An Algebraic Matrix Spencer Theorem'] Let $K\subset\R^s$ be symmetric and convex.  The following are equivalent,
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[\textup{(1)}] $N\!\left(K^\circ,\frac1sB_\infty^s\right)\le 2^{O(s)}$,
    \item[\textup{(2)}] $N\left(K^\circ,\frac{1}{\sqrt s}B_2^s\right)\le 2^{O(s)}$,
    \item[\textup{(3)}] $\gamma_s(K)\ge 2^{-O(s)}$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, we will use the following parameterized form of the implication \(\textup{(2)}\Rightarrow\textup{(3)}\). If \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^s\) is a symmetric convex body, and for some $r\ge s$, $N\left(K^\circ,\frac{1}{\sqrt s}B_2^s\right)\le 2^{Cr}$, then $\gamma_s(cK)\ge 2^{-C'r}$, where $c,C'>0$ depend only on $C$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Covering-to-measure principle, \cite{dadush2022matrix} Lemma 3.3

body:
[Corollary cor:time-change-transport of arXiv:2604.05941, 'Banach spaces of continuous paths with finite $p$-th variation'] Let $q\ge2$, let $\mathbb P$ be a dense $q$-refining partition sequence, and let $\phi$ be the associated homeomorphism from Proposition~(prop:q-refining-homeomorphism of the paper). If $x\in V_{\mathbb{T}_q}^p$ satisfies
    \[
        [x]_{\mathbb{T}_q}^{(p)}(t)=h(t),\qquad t\in[0,1],
    \]
    for some continuous non-decreasing function $h$ with $h(0)=0$, then $y:=x\circ\phi\in V_\mathbb P^p$ and
    \[
        [y]_\mathbb P^{(p)}(t)=h(\phi(t)),\qquad t\in[0,1].
    \]
    Equivalently, if $H:[0,1]\to[0,\infty)$ is continuous, non-decreasing, and $x\in V_{\mathbb{T}_q}^p$ satisfies
    \[
        [x]_{\mathbb{T}_q}^{(p)} \equiv H\circ\phi^{-1},
    \]
    then $x\circ\phi\in V_\mathbb P^p$ and $[x\circ\phi]_\mathbb P^{(p)} \equiv H$.

body:
[1 16 of arXiv:2606.10058, 'Mean First Passage Times and Fundamental Tensors of Higher Order Markov Chains'] Let ${\cal A}=[a_{i_1i_2\ldots i_m}] \in \mathbb R^{u \times w \times n \times \cdots \times n}$, where $w \le n$, be an $m$th order tensor and ${\cal E} \in \mathbb R^{1 \times u \times n \times \cdots \times n}$ be an $m$th order tensor of all ones. Then, ${\cal E} \boxtimes {\cal A} \in \mathbb R^{1 \times w \times n \times \cdots \times n}$ is an $m$th order tensor such that 
$${\cal E} \boxtimes {\cal A}=\left[\sum_{j=1}^u a_{ji_2\ldots i_m}\right],$$
i.e., it effects a summation operation over the first index of $\cal A$. In particular, for an $m$th order identity tensor ${\cal I} \in \mathbb R^{u \times u \times n \times \cdots \times n}$, where $u \le n$, 
\be

{\cal E} \boxtimes {\cal I}={\cal E}.
\ee
Moreover, if ${\cal B} \in \mathbb R^{w \times v \times n \times \cdots \times n}$, where $v \le n$, is an $m$th order tensor too, then 
\be

({\cal E} \boxtimes {\cal A}) \boxtimes {\cal B}={\cal E} \boxtimes ({\cal A} \boxtimes {\cal B}),
\ee
i.e., there is associativity for such a special case of $\boxtimes$ multiplication. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: 1 16 of arXiv:2606.10058

[Corollary 11 (Positive exponential moments) of arXiv:2605.14511, 'Clumsy and Careless:\\ Stationary-Entry Flux in Non-monotone Coupon Collectors'] Assume the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:reset-rare-success}.  If, for a fixed $a\in(0,1)$,
\begin{equation}
        \frac{\phi_n(q_ne^{a\rho_ns_n})}{s_n}\longrightarrow1,
\end{equation}
then
\[
        \Ebb e^{a\rho_ns_nT_n}\longrightarrow\frac1{1-a}.
\]

[Lemma lem:CBess of arXiv:2605.15545, 'Crossover from subcritical to critical decay: \\ random walk, self-avoiding walk, percolat'] Let $d\ge 1$ and $\nu = (d-2)/2$.
Let $x,\eta\in\mathbb{R}^d$ with $x\neq 0$,
and also $\eta \neq 0$ if $d\le 2$.
Let $\Lambda \in \mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ be symmetric and positive-definite.
Then
\begin{equation} 
\mathbb{C}(x; \eta, \Lambda)
= \frac { 2} { (2\pi)^{d/2}   \sqrt{\det \Lambda }  }
\left( \frac ab \right)^\nu
K_\nu(ab)  e^{ x \cdot \Lambda^{-1} \eta }.
\end{equation}
In particular, for $d=1$ and $d=3$ we have
\begin{alignat}2
\mathbb{C}(x; \eta, \Lambda)
&=
\frac{ 1 } { |\eta| }
	e^{ x \cdot \Lambda^{-1} \eta -ab},
   &&(d=1),
    \\
    \mathbb{C}(x; \eta, \Lambda)
&= \frac { 1} { 2\pi \sqrt{\det \Lambda } }
\frac{ 1 } {\sqrt{x \cdot \Lambda^{-1} x} }  e^{ x \cdot \Lambda^{-1} \eta -ab}
    \qquad&& (d=3).
\end{alignat}
title: Lemma lem:CBess of arXiv:2605.15545

body:
[Proposition 21 of arXiv:2607.11756, 'Full replica symmetry breaking in the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model'] Suppose that
\[
 0<a<b\le1,
 \qquad
 \alpha(s)=m\in(0,1)
 \quad(a<s<b).
\]
Set
\[
 T=\beta^2(b-a),
 \qquad
 \sigma(t)=a+\frac{t}{\beta^2},
 \qquad
 U(t,x)=u(\sigma(t),x),
 \qquad 0\le t<T.
\]
Let $\widehat X_t=X_{\sigma(t)}$, denote its density by $p(t,\cdot)$,
and define
\begin{equation}
 f(t,x)=p(t,x)\e^{-mU(t,x)},
 \qquad
 V(t,x)=-\log f(t,x).
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 U_t=-\frac12(U_{xx}+mU_x^2),
 \qquad
 f_t=\frac12f_{xx}
\end{equation}
on $(0,T)\times\R$, and
\begin{equation}
 V_x\ge0,
 \qquad V_{xx}\ge0,
 \qquad V_{xxx}\le0
 \qquad\text{on }(0,T)\times(0,\infty).
\end{equation}

For $0\le B<1$, let $x=x(t,B)\ge0$ be the inverse slope coordinate
\[
 B=U_x(t,x),
\]
and set
\[
 C(t,B)=U_{xx}(t,x(t,B)).
\]
Define
\begin{align}
 z&=-\frac12C_B=(m+K)B,
 &J&=K+BK_B,                                      \\
 \Phi&=2z^2-mC,
 &N&=V_x+KB,                                      \\
 R_1&=KBV_x+\frac12(KB)^2,
 &R_V&=\frac12(V_x^2-V_{xx}),                     \\
 R_0&=2CJ-\frac m2C-\frac12z^2,
 &G&=2Cz(3zJ-CJ_B),                               \\
 L&=CJ-z(N+z),                                    \\
 w(t,B)&=2p(t,x(t,B))C(t,B).                      
\end{align}
Every derivative of $V$ appearing in slope coordinates is evaluated at
$(t,x(t,B))$.

Fix a compact interval $I\subset[0,T)$, so that $\max I<T$. There are constants
$c_I,C_I>0$ such that, for every $t\in I$ and $x\in\R$,
\begin{align}
 c_I\e^{-C_Ix^2}
 &\le f(t,x)\le C_I\e^{-c_Ix^2},                 \\
 p(t,x)&\le C_I\e^{-c_Ix^2},                     \\
 |V_x(t,x)|&\le C_I(1+|x|),                      \\
 0\le V_{xx}(t,x)&\le C_I,                       \\
 |V_{xxx}(t,x)|&\le C_I.                         
\end{align}
Consequently, for every $A\ge0$ and integer $k\ge0$, there are
constants $c_{I,A,k},C_{I,A,k}>0$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{t\in I}\int_R^\infty
 p(t,x)(1+x)^k\e^{Ax}\dd x
 \le C_{I,A,k}\e^{-c_{I,A,k}R^2},
 \qquad R\ge0.
\end{equation}

There are constants $A_I,C_I'<\infty$ such that, for $t\in I$ and
$0\le B<1$,
\begin{align}
 &|N|+|\Phi|+|G|+|R_0|+|(R_0)_B|
 +|R_1|+|(R_1)_B|\notag\\
 &\qquad
 +|R_V|+|(R_V)_B|+|L|+|L_B|
 \le C_I'\e^{A_Ix(t,B)}.                         
\end{align}
If $I\Subset(0,T)$, then, with the time derivative taken at fixed
$B$,
\begin{equation}
 \left|\frac{\partial_t(w\Phi)}w\right|
 \le C_I'\e^{A_Ix(t,B)}.
\end{equation}

More generally, suppose $Q$ is continuous on $I\times[0,1)$ and
satisfies
\begin{equation}
 |Q(t,B)|\le C\e^{Ax(t,B)}
\end{equation}
for some $A,C<\infty$. Then
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{t\in I}\int_0^1w(t,B)|Q(t,B)|\dd B<\infty.
\end{equation}
If
\[
 B_I(R)=\sup_{t\in I}U_x(t,R),
\]
then
\[
 B_I(R)<1,
 \qquad
 B_I(R)\uparrow1
 \quad(R\to\infty),
\]
and
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{t\in I}\int_{B_I(R)}^1w(t,B)|Q(t,B)|\dd B
 \le C_{I,Q}\e^{-c_{I,Q}R^2}.
\end{equation}

Define
\begin{equation}
 F(t,B)=\int_B^1w(t,D)\Phi(t,D)\dd D.
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 |F(t,B)|\le C_I\e^{-c_Ix(t,B)^2}.
\end{equation}
In particular, if $Q$ satisfies \eqref{eq:admissible-Q}, then
\begin{equation}
 F(t,B)Q(t,B)\longrightarrow0
 \qquad(B\uparrow1),
\end{equation}
uniformly for $t\in I$, and
\begin{equation}
 w(t,B)C(t,B)z(t,B)\longrightarrow0
 \qquad(B\uparrow1)
\end{equation}
uniformly for $t\in I$.

If $I\Subset(0,T)$, the function
\begin{equation}
 H(t)=\int_0^1w(t,B)\Phi(t,B)\dd B
\end{equation}
belongs to $C^1(I)$, with
\begin{equation}
 H'(t)=\int_0^1\partial_t(w\Phi)(t,B)\dd B.
\end{equation}
At any $t\in(0,T)$ for which $H(t)=0$, one has $F(t,0)=0$ and
\begin{equation}
 \int_0^1w\Phi R_0\dd B
 =\int_0^1F(R_0)_B\dd B
 =\int_0^1w\tau(R_0)_B\dd B,
 \qquad \tau=\frac Fw.
\end{equation}
At such a centered time, the function
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal H(B)=w(B)C(B)z(B)-F(B)
\end{equation}
extends to an absolutely continuous function on $[0,1]$, satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal H_B=wL
 \qquad\text{a.e.\ on }(0,1),
\end{equation}
and has
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal H(0)=\mathcal H(1)=0.
\end{equation}

[Lemma 9 (Universal-cover noncollapsing for torus bundles) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Fix \(B\geq1\).  There is a number \(i_B>0\) with the following property.  Let
\(M\) be the total space of a \(\TT^2\)-bundle over \(S^1\), let \(h\) be an
invariant metric for that bundle structure, and let \(g\) be
another metric satisfying
\[
        B^{-1}h\leq g\leq Bh.
\]
If \(|\sec_g|\leq\Lambda\) for some \(\Lambda>0\), then the universal cover
satisfies
\[
        \inf_{\widetilde x\in\widetilde M}
        \inj_{\widetilde g}(\widetilde x)
        \geq i_B\Lambda^{-1/2}.
\]

For security parameter lambda, a secret-key zero-bit pseudorandom code for a channel C consists of polynomial-time KeyGen, randomized Enc and Dec, with polynomial block length n(lambda). There is only one message, denoted 1. For k generated by KeyGen and fresh x=Enc(k), Dec(k,C(x))=1 except with negligible probability. For every fixed string y independent of k, Dec(k,y)=bottom except with negligible probability (a bound uniform over y). Any polynomial-time adversary with oracle access to fresh encodings under one fixed k has negligible advantage over an oracle returning fresh independent uniform n-bit strings. The decoder is secret; public-key encoding is an additional property, not part of this definition.
The channel and all algorithm interfaces are fixed
Negligibility is in lambda; fresh encoder coins on every call

[Lemma 6 ({\cite[Lemma 4.1) of arXiv:2605.05864, 'Classification and Metrization of Classes of Smooth measures'] {AM92}}] 
For a smooth measure \(\mu \in \mathcal{S}\) and its corresponding PCAF \(A^\mu\), the following equalities hold:
\[
\|R_\alpha \mu\|_{\infty, q} = \|R_\alpha \mu\|_{\infty} \quad \text{for any } \alpha > 0,
\]
and
\[
\|\mathbb{E}_{\cdot}[A_t^{\mu}]\|_{\infty, q} = \|\mathbb{E}_{\cdot}[A_t^{\mu}]\|_{\infty} \quad \text{for any } t > 0.
\]
Here, $\|\cdot\|_{\infty}$ denotes the essential supremum norm with respect to the underlying measure $m$.

body:
Load-bearing hypothesis: Re a(u, u) ≥ α‖u‖² for all u in the Hilbert space H, with a fixed α > 0 and the norm of H itself (the trial and test space). What fails: strict positivity a(u, u) > 0 for u ≠ 0, or injectivity of the associated operator, is not enough - the solution operator need not be bounded and the problem need not be solvable. Counterexample 1: H = ℓ², a(u, v) = Σ_{n ≥ 1} n^{-1} u_n conj(v_n). Then a is bounded (C = 1), Hermitian, and a(u, u) > 0 for every u ≠ 0, but the associated operator is the injective compact diagonal operator with entries 1/n, whose range is not closed. For f = (1/n)_n ∈ ℓ², the equation a(u, v) = ⟨f, v⟩ for all v forces u_n = 1 for all n, which is not in ℓ²: no solution exists. Counterexample 2 (the practical one): on a bounded connected Lipschitz domain Ω, a(u, v) = ∫_Ω ∇u·∇v̄ on H = H¹(Ω) is bounded and positive semidefinite but not coercive, since a(1, 1) = 0; the Neumann problem −Δu = f, ∂_ν u = 0 is solvable only under the compatibility condition ∫_Ω f = 0, and is never uniquely solvable in H¹(Ω) (constants can be added). Coercivity is recovered only on the subspace {u ∈ H¹(Ω) : ∫_Ω u = 0} via the Poincaré-Wirtinger inequality; on H_0^1(Ω) it is recovered via the Poincaré inequality, which is why the Dirichlet problem is the easy case. Other silent hypotheses: H must be complete (a coercive bounded form on a dense non-closed subspace gives no existence), and the coercivity constant α must be uniform, not depending on u. Note a is not assumed symmetric - that part is genuinely unnecessary. For non-coercive but well-posed problems (e.g. mixed or saddle point formulations, convection dominated problems, different trial and test spaces), the correct replacement is the Banach-Necas-Babuska inf-sup theorem: an inf-sup condition on a plus injectivity of the adjoint form, of which coercivity is only a sufficient condition.
H is a Hilbert space
a is bounded sesquilinear on H × H
the claimed coercivity constant α > 0 must hold on all of H

with $\theta(x) := \int_{\XX}k(y \mid x)\pi(\dd y)$ and $r := 1-\theta$, one has
$\theta \le 1$ and

$\pi$ is invariant for $T$, i.e.\ \hyp{A3}{A3} holds, and $T$ is reversible with respect to
$\pi$.

body: Let X and Y be Banach spaces, U a subset of X open in the norm topology, and F: U -> Y. F is Frechet differentiable at a point x in U if there exists a bounded linear operator A: X -> Y such that the limit, as h in X tends to 0, of ||F(x+h) - F(x) - A h||_Y / ||h||_X equals 0. The operator A, when it exists, is unique and is called the Frechet derivative of F at x, denoted DF(x). [standard, e.g. Brezis, Functional Analysis, Sobolev Spaces and PDEs]
title: Frechet Derivative of a Map Between Banach Spaces

[Definition def: good_connectivity of arXiv:2608.00399, 'The Heavy-tailed Frog Model'] Let $a>0$. A subset $S \subseteq \mathbb{T}^d_m$ is \textup{QC}$(a)$ (quickly connected) if
\[
    \max_{x,y\in S} D(x,y)\ \le\ (\log m)^{a}.
\]
Equivalently, for every ordered pair $x,y\in S$ there exists a directed path from $x$ to $y$ of length at most $(\log m)^a$. (In particular, this implies $D(x,y)<\infty$ for all $x,y\in S$.)
title: Quick Connectivity
