body:
[Lem 164 ($\bar{\bx}$ is Lipschitz) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Take $\bar{\bx}\equiv \bar{\bx}(q_d)$
 as in \eqref{e:normalized.vectors.x}, so it is measurable with respect to
 $\cG(q_d)$. Then
		\[
		\|\E\bar{\bx}\|^2
		\le \frac{Nq_0}{q_d} \le N\,.\]
and the centered random vector $\bar{\bx}  -\E\bar{\bx}$ is subgaussian with variance proxy $L^{O(1)}$.

\begin{proof} 
Recall $\chi(p)=\E R(p)$ with $R(p)$ as in \eqref{e:p.corr.overlap}, and $q_d=\chi(p_d)$. Note that
	\[
	\frac{\|\E\bar{\bx}\|^2}{N}
	= \frac{\|\E\cA(\bG)\|^2}{Nq_d}
	= \frac{\chi(0)}{q_d} 
	\le \frac{\chi(p_0)}{q_d} = \frac{q_0}{q_d}\le1\,,
	\]
which proves the first claim. Next note that we can write
	\[
	\sqrt{q_d}\bar{\bx}
	\stackrel{\eqref{e:normalized.vectors.x}}{=}
	\E\bigg( \cA
	\Big(\sqrt{p_d}\bar{\bG} +\sqrt{1-p_d}\bG'\Big)
	\,\bigg|\,\bar{\bG}\bigg)\,,
	\]
where $\bar{\bG} = \bG(q_d)/\sqrt{p_d}$ and $\bG'$ are independent $M\times N$ matrices, each with i.i.d.\ standard gaussian entries. Since $\cA$ is $L$-Lipschitz, and $p_d/q_d \le L^{O(1)}$ by \eqref{e:deriv.p.bound}, it follows that $\bar{\bx}$ is $L^{O(1)}$-Lipschitz with respect to $\bar{\bG}$. The claim then follows using Lemma~\ref{l:lip.subgaus}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Rough paths of mixed regularity

body:
[Definition 7 (Hive) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] Let $ H_n(\lambda_n, \mu_n;  \nu_n)$ denote the set of all discrete concave functions $h_n:T_n \ra \R,$ (which,  following Knutson and Tao \cite{KT1},  we call hives)
such that \ben \item $\forall i \in [n]\cup\{0\},\quad h_n(0,  i) = \sum_{j = 1}^i \la_n(j).$
\item $\forall i \in [n]\cup\{0\},\quad h_n(i,  n) = \sum_{j = 1}^n \la_n(j) + \sum_{j = 1}^i \mu_n(j).$
\item $\forall i \in [n]\cup\{0\},\quad h_n(i,  i) = \sum_{j = 1}^i \nu_n(j).$
\een
Let $|H_n(\lambda_n, \mu_n;  \nu_n)|$ denote the ${n-1 \choose 2}-$dimensional Lebesgue measure of this hive polytope.
title: Hive

body:
[Theorem thm:correlation of arXiv:2608.05089, 'Correlation decay in area-tilted line ensembles'] There are some $\lambda_0 > 1$ and $C, \gamma > 0$ such that for all $\lambda \geqslant \lambda_0$
    and all $i, j \in \mathbb{N}$,
    if $\mathbf{X}$ denotes the $\lambda$-tilted stationary line ensemble
    then for all $t > 0$, we have
    \begin{equation}
        
        0 \leqslant \operatorname{Cov}[X^i(0), X^j(t)] \leqslant C e^{-\gamma t} \lambda^{-(i+j-2)/3}.
    \end{equation}
    The same bound holds if $\mathbf{X}$ is replaced by the stationary
    $n$-line $\lambda$-tilted ensemble $\mathbf{X}_n \sim \mathcal{L}_n^\lambda$, for any $n$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Exponential decay of correlations

[Proposition prop:normal_domain_comonotonic of arXiv:2411.03609, 'Asymptotically optimal Wasserstein couplings for the small-time stable domain of attractio'] Let $\bm{Z}$ be $\alpha$-stable with $\alpha \in (0,2)$ and $\bm{X}$ be in its domain of normal attraction. Let Assumption~(\nameref{asm:C}) (with constant $H\equiv G$ and $Q\equiv 1$) hold for some $p\in(0,\infty)\setminus\{\alpha-1\}$. Then, for any $q\in(0,1]\cap(0,\alpha)$ with $\mathds{E}[|\bm{X}_1|^q]<\infty$, we have, as $t \downarrow 0$, 
\[
\mathcal{W}_q\big(\bm{X}^t,\bm{Z}\big)
=\begin{dcases}
\mathcal{O}\big(t^{\min\{pq/\alpha,1-q/\alpha\}}\big),&\alpha\in(0,1),\\
\mathcal{O}\big(t^{q\min\{p/\alpha,1-1/\alpha\}}\big),&\alpha\in(1,2).
\end{dcases}
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:normal_domain_comonotonic of arXiv:2411.03609

[Theorem th:mom-cum-high of arXiv:2412.09290, 'Asymptotics of Harish-Chandra transform and infinitesimal freeness'] Let $\Psi_0, \ldots, \Psi_n$ be infinitely differentiable functions at $0$
  and consider the sequences $(c_m^{(0)})_{m \in \mathbb{N}}$, $\ldots$,
  $(c^{(n)}_m)_{m \in \mathbb{N}}$, where for every $i = 0, \ldots, n$,
  \[ c_m^{(i)} := \frac{i! \Psi_i^{(m)} (0)}{(m - 1) !}, \text{\quad for
     every } m \in \mathbb{N}. \]
  Then, for the sequence $(\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_k^{(n)})_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ defined
  in ((tavradiamouleipis of the paper)) we have, for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the equality
  \begin{equation}
    \ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_k^{(n)} = \sum_{\underset{\pi = \{V_1, \ldots, V_l \}}{\pi
    \in \ensuremath{\operatorname{NC}} (k)}} \sum_{\lambda_1 + \cdots + \lambda_l = n}
    \frac{1}{\lambda_1 ! \ldots \lambda_l !} c_{|V_1 |}^{(\lambda_1)} \ldots
    c_{|V_l |}^{(\lambda_l)}. 
  \end{equation}
title: Theorem th:mom-cum-high of arXiv:2412.09290

[Theorem 4 (Behavior of geodesics) of arXiv:2609.04139, 'The conformally invariant metric on CLE$_4$ II:\\ existence of geodesics'] Let $D$ be a weak geodesic CLE$_4$ metric coupling in the sense of \Cref{def:weak_axioms}. Let $U \subsetneq \BC$ be a deterministic simply connected domain. Then:
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item Almost surely, for each $\SCL_1, \SCL_2 \in \Gamma_U$, every $D_{\Gamma_U}^U$-geodesic $P$ connecting $\SCL_1$ and $\SCL_2$ is such that $\{D_{\Gamma_{U}}^{U}(\SCL_1,\SCL): \SCL \in \Gamma, \ \SCL\cap P([0,1]) \neq \emptyset\}$ forms a dense subset of the interval $[0, D_{\Gamma_{U}}^{U}(\SCL_1, \SCL_2)]$.
			\item Almost surely, for each $\SCL_1, \SCL_2 \in \Gamma_U$, every $D_{\Gamma_U}^U$-geodesic $P$ connecting $\SCL_1$ and $\SCL_2$ has the property that the subset $\{P(t) : t \in [0,1],\ P(t) \notin \bigcup_{\SCL \in \Gamma_U} \SCL\}$ of $\overline U$ is of Hausdorff dimension zero. 
			\item Almost surely, for each $\SCL_1, \SCL_2 \in \Gamma_U$, no $D_{\Gamma_U}^U$-geodesic connecting $\SCL_1$ and $\SCL_2$ touches $\partial U$. 
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Behavior of geodesics

[Theorem 12 of arXiv:2605.03182, 'Exponential integrability of the solution to the stochastic Burgers equation driven by whi'] The semigroup $P_t$ is Lipschitz improving, in the sense that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a constant $L_{T,\varepsilon}>0$ such that, for any $\varphi \in {B}_b(H)$, for every $t\in(0,T]$, and for every $x,x'\in H$ we have
\begin{equation}
	|P_t\varphi(x)-P_t\varphi(x')|\leqslant\frac{L_{T,\varepsilon}\exp\left(\varepsilon\left(\|x\|_{L^2_{\xi}}^2+\|x'\|_{L^2_{\xi}}^2\right)\right)}{\sqrt{t}}\|\varphi\|_{L^{\infty}} \|x-x'\|_{L^2_{\xi}}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\[
\inf_{\Gamma} P_{z}\bigl(S[0,\tau(\partial B(z,br))]\cap \Gamma\neq\varnothing\bigr)\geq \frac{c}{\log r},
\]
where the infimum is over all nearest-neighbour paths $\Gamma\subseteq B(z,br)$ connecting $\partial B(z,ar)$ to $\partial B(z,br)$.

[Lemma 1l of arXiv:2411.05204, '\Large\bf Sample Path Properties of the Fractional Wiener--Weierstrass Bridge'] Fix $N\in\mathbb N$ and suppose that $K\in(2H-1,H)$. Define
\begin{align}
    T_N:=\{x\in[0,1]:\text{ for all }k\in\mathbb N_0,\ \{b^kx\}\in[b^{-N},1-b^{-N}]\}.
\end{align}
Then for all $t,s\in T_N$ with $|t-s|<b^{-L}$, 
\[{\mathbb E}[|Y(t)-Y(s)|^2]\geq \frac{1}{L}|t-s|^{2K}.\]
Here, $L$ may depend on $N$.
